Let Xīng (興) be the Marquis of Línxiāng (臨湘),
Dé (得) be the Marquis of Zhēndìng (真定),
Shào (邵) be the Marquis of Lèchéng (樂成),
and Mào (茂) be the Marquis of Dānfù (單父)."
Among the imperial clan members and those from abolished states enfeoffed as marquises, there were a total of one hundred and thirty-seven people.
On the *dīngsì* day,
Zhào (趙) King Liáng (良) was demoted to Duke of Zhào (趙公),
Tàiyuán (太原) King Zhāng (章) to Duke of Qí (齊公),
and Lǔ (魯) King Xīng (興) to Duke of Lǔ (魯公).
On the *gēngwǔ* day,
Kǒng Ān (孔安), the Duke Who Continues the Line of Yīn (殷紹嘉公), was made Duke of Sòng (宋公),
and Jī Wǔ (姬武), the Duke Who Continues the Line of Zhōu (周承休公), was made Duke of Wèi (衞公).
Thirteen kingdoms in the Western Capital region were abolished and consolidated: Guǎngpíng (廣平) into Jùlù (鉅鹿),
Zhēndìng (真定) into Chángshān (常山),
Héjiān (河閒) into Xìndū (信都),
Chéngyáng (城陽) into Lángyá (琅邪),
Sìshuǐ (泗水) into Guǎnglíng (廣陵),
Zīchuān (淄川) into Gāomì (高密),
Jiāodōng (膠東) into Běihǎi (北海),
Lù'ān (六安) into Lújiāng (廬江),
and Guǎngyáng (廣陽) into Shànggǔ (上谷).
In the third month, on the *xīnwèi* day,
Hán Xīn (韓歆), Administrator of Pèijùn (沛郡), became Grand Minister of Works.
On the *bǐngzǐ* day,
Acting Grand Minister of Works Mǎ Chéng (馬成) was dismissed.
In summer, the fourth month,
Grand Marshal Wú Hàn (吳漢) returned to the capital from Shǔ (蜀).
Thereupon, a great banquet was held for the generals and soldiers,
rewards were distributed, and meritorious deeds were recorded.
Meritorious officials received increased fiefs and new enfeoffments,
totaling three hundred and sixty-five people.
Among the imperial relatives who were enfeoffed due to imperial favor, there were forty-five people.
The offices of Left and Right Generals were abolished.
General-in-chief Who Establishes Awe, Gěng Yǎn (耿弇), was dismissed.

Yìzhōu (益州) transmitted Gōngsūn Shù's (公孫述) blind musicians, instruments for suburban and ancestral temple music, ceremonial chariots, and palanquins, whereupon the ritual objects were first complete.
At this time, military campaigns had ceased,
and there were few affairs in the empire.
Official documents and corvée labor
were made as simple and minimal as possible,
to the extent that only one in ten remained.
On the *jiǎyín* day,
Dòu Róng (竇融), Shepherd of Jìzhōu (冀州), became Grand Minister of Works.
In the fifth month,
the Xiōngnú (匈奴) plundered Hédōng (河東).
In autumn, the seventh month,
the Mán Yí (蠻夷) people from beyond the borders of Guǎnghàn (廣漢), led by Yùláng Chìxīn Yǐtán (孕桹赤妡迆v), submitted.
In the ninth month,
barbarians from beyond the borders of Rìnán (日南) presented white pheasants and white rabbits.
In winter, the twelfth month, on the *jiǎyín* day,
an imperial edict stated that all people from Yìzhōu (益州) who had been captured and made slaves since the eighth year
should all be emancipated as commoners;
or if they were living as secondary wives,
and wished to leave,
they were to be allowed to do so freely;
those who dared to detain them
would be dealt with according to the law for capturing people, as in Qīng (青) and Xú (徐) provinces.
Jīnchéng (金城) Commandery was reestablished.
In the fourteenth year, spring, the first month,
construction began on the front hall of the Southern Palace.
The Xiōngnú (匈奴) sent envoys to present tribute,
and a middle-ranking general was sent to reciprocate the mission.
In summer, the fourth month, on the *xīnsì* day,
Kǒng Zhì (孔志), a descendant of Kǒngzǐ (孔子), was enfeoffed as Marquis of Bāochéng (襃成).
Rèn Guì (任貴) from Yuèsuī (越巂) claimed to be the Administrator
and sent an envoy to present a report.
In the ninth month of autumn,
Jiǎ Dān (賈丹) of Píngchéng (平城) killed Lú Fāng's (盧芳) general Yǐn Yóu (尹由) and surrendered.
That year,
Kuàijī (會稽) suffered a great epidemic.
The kingdoms of Shāchē (莎車) and Shànshàn (鄯善) sent envoys to offer tribute.
On the Guǐmǎo (癸卯) day of the twelfth month,
an edict ordered that slaves in Yì (益) and Liáng (涼) provinces
who had petitioned local officials since the eighth year
were all to be emancipated as commoners (shùrén 庶人),
and those who had been sold would not have their price returned.
In the first month of spring of the fifteenth year, on the Xīnchǒu (辛丑) day,
Grand Minister of Works Hán Xīn (韓歆) was dismissed
and committed suicide.
On the Dīngwèi (丁未) day,
a comet appeared in昴 (Mǎo, the Pleiades).
Ōuyáng Shè (歐陽歙), Administrator of Rǔnán (汝南), became Grand Minister of Works.
Grand General who Establishes Righteousness Zhū Yòu (朱祐) was dismissed.
On the Dīngwèi (丁未) day,
a comet appeared in Yíngshì (營室).
In the second month,
the people of the three commanderies of Yànmén (鴈門), Dàijùn (代郡), and Shànggǔ (上谷) were relocated
to areas east of Chángshān (常山) Pass and Jūyōng (居庸) Pass.
Initially,
after Bā (巴) and Shǔ (蜀) were pacified,
Grand Marshal Wú Hàn (吳漢) submitted a memorial requesting the enfeoffment of the imperial princes,
but this was not permitted.
He repeatedly submitted memorials for several years.
In the third month,
an edict finally ordered the ministers to deliberate.

Grand Minister of Education Róng (融), Marquis of Gùshǐ (固始) Tōng (通), Marquis of Jiāodōng (膠東) Fù (復), Marquis of Gāomì (高密) Yǔ (禹), Grand Master of Ceremonies Dēng (登), and others submitted their deliberation, stating:
"In ancient times, feudal lords were enfeoffed
to serve as screens for the capital.
The Zhōu (周) enfeoffed eight hundred, with members of the same surname, the various Jī (姬) clans, establishing states
to assist the royal house,
revere and serve the Son of Heaven,
enjoy long reigns,
and serve as a model for later generations.
Hence, the *Book of Odes* says: 'Greatly enlarge your dwellings,
to be supports for the House of Zhōu.'
Emperor Gāozǔ (高祖), with his sagely virtue,
brought the world under his sway,
and also focused on cherishing kin,
enfeoffing his brothers and sons,
without deviating from old statutes.
Your Majesty's virtue spans heaven and earth,
reviving the imperial lineage.
You commend virtue and reward merit,
and maintain close relations with the nine clans.
Meritorious officials and imperial kinsmen
have all received enfeoffment and peerage,
many receiving vast territories,
some even encompassing contiguous counties.
Now the imperial princes, by the grace of Heaven,
are able to dress themselves and perform obeisance.
Yet Your Majesty, being humble and modest,
has suppressed discussion and not yet deliberated on this,
which has led to disappointment among all ministers and common people.
It is fitting, taking advantage of the auspicious time of mid-summer,
to establish their titles and ranks,
to broaden the number of supporting vassals,
clarify affection for kin,
revere the ancestral temples,
give weight to the altars of soil and grain,
accord with the ancients and conform to old customs,
and satisfy the hearts of the multitude.
Your servants request that the Grand Minister of Education submit maps of the land,
and the Grand Master of Ceremonies select an auspicious day and
prepare the ceremonies."
The imperial decree stated:
"Granted."
In the fourth month of summer, on the Wùshēn (戊申) day,
a grand sacrificial ox was offered at the ancestral temples.
On the Dīngsì (丁巳) day,
Grand Minister of Education Róng (融) was sent to announce to the temple,
and Imperial Prince Fǔ (輔) was enfeoffed as Right-Flank Duke,
Yīng (英) as Duke of Chǔ (楚),
Yáng (陽) as Duke of Dōnghǎi (東海),
Kāng (康) as Duke of Jìnán (濟南),
Cāng (蒼) as Duke of Dōngpíng (東平),
Yán (延) as Duke of Huáiyáng (淮陽),
Jīng (荊) as Duke of Shānyáng (山陽),
Héng (衡) as Duke of Línhuái (臨淮),
Yān (焉) as Left-Flank Duke,
and Jīng (京) as Duke of Lángyé (琅邪).
On the Guǐchǒu (癸丑) day,
posthumous titles were conferred upon his elder brother Bóshēng (伯升) as Duke Wǔ (武) of Qí (齊),
and his second elder brother Zhòng (仲) as Duke Āi (哀) of Lǔ (魯).
In the sixth month, on the Gēngwǔ (庚午) day,
the offices of Commander of the屯騎 (Túnqí), Chángshuǐ (長水), and Shèshēng (射聲) Regiments were reestablished;
the Left Commander of the Qīngjīn (青巾) was renamed Commander of the Yuèqí (越騎) Regiment.
An edict was sent to the provinces and commanderies to inspect and verify the acreage of cultivated land
and the household population and their ages.
It also investigated two-thousand-bushel officials and chief magistrates who were partial or unfair.
In the eleventh month of winter, on the Jiǎxū (甲戌) day,
Grand Minister of Works Ōuyáng Shè (歐陽歙) was imprisoned and died.
In the twelfth month, on the Gēngwǔ (庚午) day,
Dài Shè (戴涉), Marquis Within the Passes, became Grand Minister of Works.
Lú Fāng (盧芳) entered from Xiongnú (匈奴) and resided in Gāoliǔ (高柳).
That year,
General of Cavalry Dù Mào (杜茂) was dismissed.
General of Tiger's Teeth Gài Yán (蓋延) passed away.
In the second month of spring of the sixteenth year,
Zhēng Cè (徵側), a woman from Jiāozhǐ (交阯), rebelled
and seized many cities and towns.
On the last day of the third month, Xīnchǒu (辛丑),
there was a solar eclipse.
In the ninth month of autumn,
Zhāng Jí (張伋), Prefect of Hénán (河南), and over ten other commandery administrators,
were imprisoned and died for failing to accurately survey fields.
Powerful families in commanderies and states, as well as bandit leaders and various brigands, rose up everywhere,
attacking and plundering their localities,
and harming and killing chief magistrates.
When commanderies and counties pursued them,
they would disperse upon arrival,
but regroup after the pursuit left.
This was especially severe in the four provinces of Qīng (青), Xú (徐), Yōu (幽), and Jì (冀).
In the tenth month of winter,
envoys were sent to the commanderies and states,
allowing the brigands to expose each other:
if five people together captured and executed one person,
their crimes would be remitted.
Even if officials lingered, avoided, or deliberately let them go,
they would not be questioned,
but their effectiveness would be judged solely by the number of bandits captured and killed.
Governors, administrators, magistrates, and chiefs who were responsible for bandits within their jurisdiction but failed to apprehend them,
or who abandoned their cities and posts out of fear,
would not be held accountable.
Instead, their performance would be ranked solely by the number of bandits captured,
and only those who concealed them would be punished.
Thereupon, people began to pursue and capture each other,
and the bandits largely dispersed.
Their leaders were relocated to other commanderies,
given land and provisions,
and enabled to live a peaceful life.
From then on, cattle and horses roamed freely,
and city gates were not closed.
Lú Fāng (盧芳) sent an envoy to request surrender.
In the twelfth month, on the Jiǎchén (甲辰) day,
Fāng (芳) was enfeoffed as King of Dài (代).
Initially,
after Wáng Mǎng's (王莽) chaos,
cloth, silk, gold, and grain were used as currency.
That year,
five-zhū (五銖) coins began to circulate.
In the first month of spring of the seventeenth year,
Duke Liáng (良) of Zhào (趙) passed away.
On the last day of the second month, Yǐwèi (乙未),
there was a solar eclipse.
In the fourth month of summer, on the Yǐmǎo (乙卯) day,
the emperor made a southern tour.
The Crown Prince, Right-Flank Duke Fǔ (輔), Duke Yīng (英) of Chǔ (楚), Duke Yáng (陽) of Dōnghǎi (東海), Duke Kāng (康) of Jìnán (濟南), and Duke Cāng (蒼) of Dōngpíng (東平) accompanied him.
He visited Yǐngchuān (潁川),
then proceeded to Yè (葉) and Zhānglíng (章陵).
In the fifth month, on the Yǐmǎo (乙卯) day,
the imperial carriage returned to the palace.
In the sixth month, on the Guǐsì (癸巳) day,
Duke Héng (衡) of Línhuái (臨淮) passed away.
In the seventh month of autumn,
the sorcerer Lǐ Guǎng (李廣) and his group rose up and occupied Wǎnchéng (皖城).
Colonel of the Tiger's Teeth Guards Mǎ Yuán (馬援) and General of Cavalry Duàn Zhì (段志) were sent to suppress them.
In the ninth month,
Wǎnchéng (皖城) was captured,
and Lǐ Guǎng (李廣) and his followers were executed.
In the tenth month of winter, on the Xīnsì (辛巳) day,
Empress Guō (郭) was deposed and made Empress Dowager of Zhōngshān (中山),
and Noble Lady Yīn (陰) was made empress.
Right-Flank Duke Fǔ (輔) was promoted to Prince of Zhōngshān (中山),
with Chángshān (常山) Commandery as his fief.
The other nine dukes
were all promoted to kings within their original enfeoffments.
On the Jiǎshēn (甲申) day,
the emperor visited Zhānglíng (章陵).
He repaired the garden temples,
offered sacrifices at his old residence,
inspected the fields and dwellings,
held banquets and musical performances,
and bestowed rewards.
At this time, his maternal relatives, the imperial uncles and aunts, in their drunken joy,
spoke among themselves, saying:
"Wénshú (文叔) was cautious and trustworthy when young,
not very amiable with others,
only straightforward and gentle.
Now he can do such things!"
The emperor heard this
and laughed heartily, saying:
"When I govern the world,
I also wish to do so with gentleness."
Thereupon, he had ancestral halls built for all the imperial kinsmen of Chōnglíng (舂陵).
Five phoenixes were seen in Jiá (郟) County of Yǐngchuān (潁川).
In the twelfth month,
he returned from Zhānglíng (章陵).
That year,
the kingdom of Shāchē (莎車) sent envoys to offer tribute.
In the spring, second month, of the eighteenth year (42 CE),
Shǔjùn Administrator Shǐ Xīn rebelled.
Grand Marshal Wú Hàn was dispatched with two generals to suppress him,
besieging Chéngdū.
On the jiǎyín day,
the Emperor made a western inspection tour,
arriving at Cháng'ān.
In the third month, on the rénwǔ day,
sacrifices were offered at Gāomiào,
followed by rites at the Eleven Mausoleums.
Passing through Féngyì territory,
he proceeded to Púbǎn,
where he sacrificed to Hòutǔ.
In summer, fourth month, (jiǎxū) 【guǐyǒu】, the imperial carriage returned to the palace.
(guǐyǒu) 【jiǎxū】 day,
an edict stated:
"Currently, in the border commanderies, stealing fifty hù of grain
is a capital offense,
opening the way for殘吏 (cánlì) to wantonly kill.
This law is hereby abolished
and shall be brought into line with the inner commanderies."
General Fúbō Mǎ Yuán was dispatched with General Lóuchuán Duàn Zhì and others to attack the Jiāozhǐ rebels under Zhēng Cè.
(wù) 【jiǎ】shēn day,
the Emperor visited Hénèi.
On the wùzǐ day,
he returned from Hénèi.
In the fifth month,
there was a drought.
Lú Fāng again fled into Xiongnú territory.
In autumn, seventh month,
Wú Hàn captured Chéngdū
and executed Shǐ Xīn and his followers.
On the rénxū day,
an amnesty was granted to those in Yìzhōu whose crimes were punishable by death or lesser penalties.
In winter, tenth month, on the gēngchén day,
the Emperor visited Yíchéng.
Upon his return,
he sacrificed at Zhānglíng.
In the twelfth month, on the yǐchǒu day,
the imperial carriage returned to the palace.
In this year,
the position of zhōumù was abolished,
and cìshǐ were established.
In the spring, first month, of the nineteenth year (43 CE), on the gēngzǐ day,
Emperor Xiàoxuān was posthumously honored as Zhōngzōng.
Sacrifices to Emperor Zhāo and Emperor Yuán began at Tàimiào,
to Emperor Chéng, Emperor Āi, and Emperor Píng at Cháng'ān,
and to Chōnglíng Jié Hóu and his four ancestors at Zhānglíng.
The demonic shamans Shàn Chén and Fù Zhèn rebelled,
occupying Yuánwǔ.
Grand Master Tàizhōng Zāng Gōng was dispatched to besiege them.
In summer, fourth month,
Yuánwǔ was captured,
and Shàn Chén, Fù Zhèn, and their followers were executed.
General Fúbō Mǎ Yuán defeated Jiāozhǐ,
executing Zhēng Cè and her followers.
Subsequently, he defeated the Jiǔzhēn rebels under Dū Yáng and others,
who surrendered.
In the intercalary month, on the wùshēn day,
the Dukes of Zhào, Qí, and Lǔ were promoted to Kings.
In the sixth month, on the wùshēn day,
an edict stated:
"According to the principles of the Spring and Autumn Annals,
the son of the noblest mother is established as heir.
Yáng, King of Dōnghǎi,
is the son of the Empress,
and should rightly inherit the great succession.
Crown Prince Qiáng,
with sincere humility and modesty,
wishes to serve as a prince of a feudal state.
It is difficult for a father
to long oppose the feelings of his son.
Therefore, Qiáng is made King of Dōnghǎi,
Yáng is established as Crown Prince,
and his name is changed to Zhuāng."
In autumn, ninth month,
the Emperor made a southern inspection tour.
On the rénshēn day,
he visited Nányáng,
then proceeded to the prefectural lodging in Nándùn, Rǔnán,
where he hosted a banquet,
bestowed gifts upon officials and common people,
and exempted Nándùn from land tax for a year.
The elders prostrated themselves and said:
"Your Imperial Father resided here for a long time,
and Your Majesty recognizes the temple and residence.
Each time you come, you bestow generous favor.
We wish for an exemption for ten more years."
The Emperor said:
"The empire is a heavy responsibility,
and I constantly fear I am not equal to it.
Day by day,
how can I dare to promise ten years into the distant future?"
The officials and common people then said:
"Your Majesty truly cherishes it,
why speak so humbly?"
The Emperor laughed heartily,
and added one more year to the exemption.
He then proceeded to Huáiyáng, Liáng, and Pèi.
The Southwestern Yi raided Yìzhōujùn.
General Wǔwēi Liú Shàng was dispatched to suppress them.
The Grand Administrator of Yuèsuī, Rèn Guì, plotted rebellion.
In the twelfth month,
Liú Shàng attacked and killed Rèn Guì.
In this year,
the Commandant of Hángǔ Pass was re-established.
The palaces of Xījīng were repaired.
In the spring, second month, of the twentieth year (44 CE), on the wùzǐ day,
the imperial carriage returned to the palace.
In summer, fourth month, on the gēngchén day,
Grand Minister of Works Dài Shè was imprisoned and died.
Grand Minister of Agriculture Dòu Róng was dismissed.
In the fifth month, on the xīnhài day,
Grand Marshal Wú Hàn passed away.
The Xiongnú raided Shàngdǎng and Tiānshuǐ,
then reached Fúfēng.
In the sixth month, on the gēngyín day,
Grand Administrator of Guǎnghàn Cài Mào was appointed Grand Minister of Works,
and Grand Coachman Zhū Fú was appointed Grand Minister of Agriculture.
On the rénchén day,
Left Commander of the Central Army Liú Lóng was appointed General of Agile Cavalry
and acted as Grand Marshal.
On the yǐwèi day,
Fǔ, King of Zhōngshān, was transferred to be King of Pèi.
In autumn,
people of the Korean Han state in Dōngyí led their populace to Lèlàng and submitted.
In winter, tenth month,
the Emperor made an eastern inspection tour.
On the jiǎwǔ day,
he visited Lǔ,
then proceeded to Dōnghǎi, Chǔ, and Pèiguó.
In the twelfth month,
the Xiongnú raided Tiānshuǐ.
On the rényín day,
the imperial carriage returned to the palace.
In this year,
Wǔyuán Commandery was abolished,
and its officials and people were relocated to Hédōng.
Jìyáng County was exempted from corvée labor for six years.
In the spring, first month, of the twenty-first year (45 CE),
General Wǔwēi Liú Shàng defeated the Yí of Yìzhōu,
pacifying them.
In summer, fourth month,
the Hú of Āndìng Subordinate State rebelled,
gathering at Qīngshān.
Chief Clerk for Leading Troops Chén Xīn was dispatched to suppress them.
In autumn,
the Xiānbēi raided Liáodōng.
Grand Administrator of Liáodōng Jì Róng severely defeated them.
In winter, tenth month,
General Fúbō Mǎ Yuán was dispatched beyond the frontier to attack the Wūhuán,
but was unsuccessful.
The Xiongnú raided Shànggǔ and Zhōngshān.
That winter,
the kings of Shànshàn, Chēshī, and sixteen other states all sent their sons to serve at court and offer tribute,
requesting a Dūhù.
The Emperor, considering that the Central Plains had just been pacified
and he had no time for external affairs,
returned their attendant sons
and generously bestowed rewards.
In the spring, intercalary month, of the twenty-second year (46 CE), on the bǐngxū day,
the Emperor visited Cháng'ān,
sacrificed at Gāomiào,
and then performed rites at the Eleven Mausoleums.
In the second month, on the jǐsì day,
he returned from Cháng'ān.
In summer, fifth month, on the last day of the month (yǐwèi),
there was a solar eclipse.
In autumn, seventh month,
Colonel Director of Retainers Sū Yè was imprisoned and died.
In the ninth month, on the day Wùchén,
there was an earthquake and the earth cracked.
An imperial edict stated:
"Recently, there was an earthquake,
especially severe in Nányáng.
Now, the earth
bears the heaviest of all things
and should be still and unmoving.
Yet now it has quaked and cracked;
the fault lies with the sovereign above.
If the spirits do not favor one who lacks virtue,
calamities will befall the officials and people.
I am greatly afraid.
Therefore, command Nányáng not to deliver this year's land tax and fodder.
Send an Yèzhě to inspect.
For those condemned to capital punishment who were imprisoned before the day Wùchén,
reduce their capital punishment by one degree.
All penal servitude convicts are to have their cangues and fetters removed,
and be given silk floss garments.
For residents in the commandery who were crushed to death, bestow coffin money,
three thousand (coins) per person.
For those whose poll tax and arrears are unpaid, and whose homes are especially ruined,
do not collect the debts.
If officials or people have died
beneath collapsed walls or destroyed houses,
and their families are too weak to collect their remains,
then use current money and grain to hire laborers
to search for them."
In winter, the tenth month, on the day Rénzǐ,
Dàsīkōng Zhū Fú was dismissed.
On the day Guǐchǒu,
Guānglùxūn Dù Lín became Dàsīkōng.
In this year,
Qí Wáng Zhāng died.
There were locusts in Qīngzhōu.
The Xiōngnú Yùjiàn Rìzhú Wáng Bǐ
sent an envoy to Yúyáng to request peace and kinship,
and sent Zhōngliángjiàng Lǐ Mào to report.
The Wūhuán attacked and defeated the Xiōngnú,
and the Xiōngnú migrated north,
leaving the land south of the desert empty.
An edict abolished the stationed officials and soldiers at the frontier commanderies' watchtowers.
In the 23rd year, in spring, the first month,
the Southern Mán in Nánjùn rebelled.
Wǔwēi Jiāngjūn Liú Shàng was sent to suppress and defeat them,
and their people were resettled in Jiāngxià.
In summer, the fifth month, on the day Dīngmǎo,
Dàsītú Cài Mào died.
In autumn, the eighth month, on the day Bǐngxū,
Dàsīkōng Dù Lín died.
In the ninth month, on the day Xīnwèi,
Chénliú Tàishǒu Yù Kuàng became Dàsītú.
In winter, the tenth month, on the day Bǐngshēn,
Tàipú Zhāng Chún became Dàsīkōng.
The Gāogōulì led their people to Lèlàng to submit.
In the twelfth month,
the Wǔlíng Mán rebelled,
plundering commanderies and counties.
Liú Shàng was sent to attack them,
and fought at Yuánshuǐ,
but Shàng's army was defeated and perished.
In this year,
the Xiōngnú Yùjiàn Rìzhú Wáng Bǐ led his tribes and sent envoys to Xīhé to submit.
In the 24th year, in spring, the first month, on the day Yǐhài,
there was a general amnesty throughout the empire.
The Xiōngnú Yùjiàn Rìzhú Wáng Bǐ sent envoys to the Wǔyuán frontier post
to request protection against the Northern Barbarians.
In autumn, the seventh month,
the Wǔlíng Mán attacked Línyuán.
Yèzhě Lǐ Sōng and Zhōngshān Tàishǒu Mǎ Chéng were sent to attack the Mán,
but were unsuccessful.
Thereupon, Fúbō Jiāngjūn Mǎ Yuán led four generals to attack them.
An edict ordered the relevant authorities to re-emphasize the old regulations concerning supporting vassal kings.
In winter, the tenth month,
the Xiōngnú Yùjiàn Rìzhú Wáng Bǐ declared himself the Southern Chányú,
and thus the Xiōngnú were divided into Southern and Northern.
In the 25th year, in spring, the first month,
the Mò people beyond the frontier of Liáodōng
attacked Yòuběipíng, Yúyáng, Shànggǔ, and Tàiyuán.
Liáodōng Tàishǒu Zhài Róng summoned and pacified them.
Wūhuán tribal chiefs came to court.
The Southern Chányú sent envoys to the imperial court with tribute,
pledging allegiance as a vassal;
he also sent his Zuǒxián Wáng to attack and defeat the Northern Xiōngnú,
reclaiming over a thousand *lǐ* of land.
In the third month,
the Southern Chányú sent his son to serve as a hostage.
On the last day of the month Wùshēn,
there was a solar eclipse.
Fúbō Jiāngjūn Mǎ Yuán and others defeated the Wǔlíng Mán at Línyuán.
In winter, the tenth month,
all the rebellious Mán surrendered.
The king of Fúyú sent envoys to present tribute.
In this year,
Wūhuán tribal chiefs led their people to submit,
coming to the imperial court to offer tribute.
In the 26th year, 【spring】the first month,
an edict ordered the relevant authorities to increase the salaries of all officials.
For those of one thousand *dàn* and above,
it was less than the old system of the Western Capital;
for those of six hundred *dàn* and below,
it was an increase from the old ranks.
The construction of the imperial tomb (Shòulíng) began.
Jiāngzuò Dàjiàng Dòu Róng reported on the vastness of the imperial garden and tomb,
without regard for the resources used.
The Emperor said:
"In ancient times, the burials of emperors and kings
all used earthenware figures and pottery vessels,
wooden carriages and straw horses,
so that later generations would not know their location.
Tàizōng understood the meaning of beginning and end,
and Jǐngdì was able to follow and uphold filial piety.
When the empire underwent reversals,
the Bālíng alone remained intact and received its blessing.
Is this not excellent?
The land now designated does not exceed two or three *qǐng*.
There is no need for a mountainous tomb;
the ponds are merely to allow water to flow."
Zhōngliángjiàng Duàn Chēn was sent to bestow the seal and ribbon upon the Southern Chányú,
ordering him to reside in Yúnzhōng.
An envoy for the Xiōngnú (Shǐ Xiōngnú Zhōngliángjiàng) was first established,
leading troops to guard him.
The Southern Chányú sent his son to serve as a hostage,
and presented a memorial to the imperial court.
Thereupon, the people of the eight commanderies of Yúnzhōng, Wǔyuán, Shuòfāng, Běidì, Dìngxiāng, Yànmén, Shànggǔ, and Dài returned to their native lands.
Yèzhě were sent to divide and lead, to carry out punishments and repair city walls.
Frontier residents who were in Zhōngguó were sent
back to their various counties,
all granted travel money,
and provided with transported provisions.
In the 27th year, in summer, the fourth month, on the day Wùwǔ,
Dàsītú Yù Kuàng died.
In the fifth month, on the day Dīngchǒu,
an edict stated:
"In the past, Qì served as Sītú,
and Yǔ served as Sīkōng,
neither had the character 'dà'
in their titles.
Therefore, order these two offices to remove 'dà'."
Also, Dàsīmǎ was changed to Tàiwèi.
Piàojí Dàjiāngjūn, acting Dàsīmǎ, Liú Lóng was dismissed on that very day.
Tàipú Zhào Xǐ became Tàiwèi,
and Dàsīnóng Féng Qín became Sītú.
Barbarians beyond the frontier of Yìzhōujùn led their people to submit.
The Northern Xiōngnú sent envoys to Wǔwēi to beg for peace and kinship.
In winter,
Lǔ Wáng Xìng and Qí Wáng Shí first took up their fiefdoms.
In the 28th year, in spring, the first month, on the day Jǐsì,
Lǔ Wáng Xìng was transferred to be Běihǎi Wáng,
and the state of Lǔ was added to Dōnghǎi.
Dōnghǎi Wáng Qiáng was granted the musical instruments of Hǔbēn, Máotóu, and Zhōngjù.
In summer, the sixth month, on the day Dīngmǎo,
Pèi Tàihòu Guō Shì died.
Thereupon, an edict ordered commanderies and counties to arrest the clients of kings and marquises,
and several thousand people were put to death.
In autumn, the eighth month, on the day Wùyín,
Dōnghǎi Wáng Qiáng, Pèi Wáng Fǔ, Chǔ Wáng Yīng, Jìnán Wáng Kāng, and Huáiyáng Wáng Yán first took up their fiefdoms.
In winter, the tenth month, on the day Guǐyǒu,
an edict ordered all male prisoners condemned to capital punishment to be recruited for the "silkworm chamber" (castration),
and their women to be confined.
The Northern Xiōngnú sent envoys to offer tribute,
begging for peace and kinship.
In the 29th year, in spring, the second month, on the first day Dīngsì,
there was a solar eclipse.
Envoys were sent to investigate wrongful imprisonments
and release prisoners.
On the day Gēngshēn,
all men in the empire were granted two ranks of nobility;
the widowed, solitary, orphaned, helpless, gravely ill, and poor who could not support themselves were granted five *hú* of grain per person.
In summer, the fourth month, on the day Yǐchǒu,
an edict ordered that all prisoners in the empire, from those deserving of death downwards, and all convicts, should have their original sentences reduced by one degree.
Others were allowed to atone for crimes by paying a fine or performing labor, with varying degrees.
In the 30th year, in spring, the first month,
Xiānbēi tribal chiefs submitted
and offered New Year's greetings at court.
In the second month,
the Emperor made an eastern inspection tour.
On the day Jiǎzǐ,
he arrived in Lǔ,
then proceeded to Jìnán.
In the intercalary month, on the day Guǐchǒu,
the imperial carriage returned to the palace.
A comet appeared in the Purple Palace constellation.
In summer, the fourth month, on the day Wùzǐ,
Zuǒyì Wáng Yān was transferred to be Zhōngshān Wáng.
In the fifth month,
there were great floods.
All men in the empire were granted two ranks of nobility;
the widowed, solitary, orphaned, helpless, gravely ill, and poor who could not support themselves were granted five *hú* of grain per person.
In autumn, the seventh month, on the day Dīngyǒu,
the Emperor visited the state of Lǔ.
The corvée labor for Jìyáng County for this year was remitted.
In winter, the eleventh month, on the day Dīngyǒu,
the Emperor returned from Lǔ.
In the thirty-first year, in summer, the fifth month,
there was a great flood.
On the day Wùchén,
titles of nobility were bestowed upon all men in the empire,
each receiving two ranks.
The widowed, lonely, orphaned, childless, seriously ill, and impoverished who could not sustain themselves were given grain,
six *hú* each.
On the last day of the month, Guǐyǒu,
there was a solar eclipse.
That summer,
there were locusts.
In autumn, the ninth month, on the day Jiǎchén,
an imperial edict ordered all death row prisoners to be conscripted into the *cánshì* (silkworm chamber),
and the women among them to be castrated.
That year,
in Chénliú, it rained grain,
shaped like foxtail millet seeds.
The Northern Xiōngnú sent envoys to present tribute.
In Zhōngyuán元年 (first year), in spring, the first month,
Wáng Qiáng (King of Dōnghǎi), Wáng Fǔ (King of Pèi), Wáng Yīng (King of Chǔ), Wáng Kāng (King of Jǐnán), Wáng Yán (King of Huáiyáng), and Wáng Xū (King of Zhào) all came to court.
On the day Dīngmǎo,
the emperor embarked on an Eastern Inspection Tour.
In the second month, on the day Jǐmǎo,
the emperor visited Lǔ,
and then proceeded to Tàishān.
Wáng Xīng (King of Běihǎi) and Wáng Shí (King of Qí) paid respects at Dōngyuè.
On the day Xīnmǎo,
sacrifices were offered to the mountains and rivers (*cháiwàng*) at Dàizōng (Tàishān),
and the *dēngfēng* ceremony was performed on Tàishān.
On the day Jiǎwǔ,
the *shàn* ceremony was performed at Liángfù.
In the third month, on the day Wùchén,
Sīkōng Zhāng Chún passed away.
In summer, the fourth month, on the day Guǐyǒu,
the imperial carriage returned to the palace.
On the day Jǐmǎo,
a great amnesty was declared throughout the empire.
Yíng, Bó, Liángfù, and Fènggāo were exempted
from this year's land tax and fodder contributions.
The reign title was changed to Zhōngyuán.
The emperor journeyed to Cháng'ān.
On the day Wùzǐ,
sacrifices were offered at Chánglíng.
In the fifth month, on the day Yǐchǒu,
the emperor returned from Cháng'ān.
In the sixth month, on the day Xīnmǎo,
Tàipú Féng Fáng was appointed Sīkōng.
On the day Yǐwèi,
Sītú Féng Qín passed away.
That summer,
a sweet spring emerged in the capital,
and those who drank from it were cured of all chronic illnesses,
except for the blind and the lame who were not healed.
Also, red grass grew along the water's edge.
Commandaries and kingdoms frequently reported the appearance of sweet dew.
The assembled officials submitted a memorial, stating:
"The spirits of the earth have responded with auspicious signs, and scarlet grass has sprouted.
Whenever Emperor Xiàoxuān had auspicious omens,
he would change the reign title,
such as Shénjué, Wǔfèng, Gānlù, and Huánglóng,
which were listed as era names,
presumably to evoke responses from the deities
and to manifest virtue and trustworthiness.
Thus, peace and prosperity were achieved,
and it was known as a 'restoration.'
Today, the empire is peaceful and tranquil,
and spiritual wonders continue to descend.
Your Majesty's sentiment is to humbly decline,
and to push away these honors rather than embrace them.
How can such auspicious signs and glorious blessings
be allowed to disappear without being recorded?
It is fitting to order the Grand Scribe to compile them
to be transmitted to future generations."
The emperor did not accept this.
He always humbly considered himself without virtue,
and whenever commandaries and kingdoms reported such things,
he would suppress them and not treat them as significant.
Therefore, the official historians rarely had the opportunity to record them.
In autumn,
there were three locust outbreaks in the commandaries and kingdoms.
In winter, the tenth month, on the day Xīnmèi,
Sīlì Xiàowèi Lǐ Xīn of Dōnglái was appointed Sītú.
On the day Jiǎshēn,
the Sīkōng was ordered to offer sacrifices and announce to the High Temple:
"Emperor Gāo and his officials made a covenant,
that none but those of the Liú clan should be made kings.
Empress Lü harmed and murdered the three Zhàos,
and exclusively enthroned members of the Lü clan.
Thanks to the spiritual protection of the altars of soil and grain,
Lù and Chǎn were executed,
the Mandate of Heaven nearly fell,
and a perilous dynasty was made safe again.
Empress Lü is not suitable to be worshipped alongside Emperor Gāo in the High Temple,
sharing the same ancestral hall as the supreme ancestor.
Empress Bó possessed maternal virtue and benevolence,
and Emperor Xiàowén governed the country with wisdom and sagacity.
Their descendants have benefited from their blessings,
and their fortune has extended to this day.
Therefore, confer the honorable title of Empress Gāo upon Empress Bó,
and let her be worshipped alongside the spirits of the earth.
Move Empress Lü's ancestral tablet to the imperial park,
and offer sacrifices to her four times a year."
In the eleventh month, on the last day of the month, Jiǎzǐ,
there was a solar eclipse.
That year,
the Míngtáng, Língtái, and Pìyōng were initially constructed,
as well as the sacrificial ground for the northern suburb.
Prophetic charts and texts (*túchèn*) were circulated throughout the empire.
Jìyáng and Nándùn were exempted from corvée labor.
The Cānláng Qiāng raided Wǔdū,
defeating the commandary troops.
Liú Xū, the Grand Administrator of Lǒngxī, dispatched troops to relieve them,
and together with the Wǔdū commandary troops, they suppressed the rebellious Qiāng,
defeating them all.
In the second year, in spring, the first month, on the day Xīnwèi,
the northern suburb altar was first established,
and sacrifices were offered to Hòutǔ (Empress Earth).
The king of the Wōnú Kingdom of the Eastern Yí sent envoys to present tribute.
In the second month, on the day Wùxū,
the emperor passed away in the front hall of the Southern Palace,
at the age of sixty-two.
His dying edict stated:
"I have been of no benefit to the common people.
Everything should follow the system of Emperor Xiàowén,
striving for simplicity and economy.
Inspectors and chief officials of two thousand *dàn* salary should not leave their cities,
nor should they dispatch officials or make reports through the postal system."
Initially,
the emperor had been involved in military affairs for a long time,
and was weary of warfare.
Moreover, he knew that the empire was exhausted and depleted,
and desired peace and rest.
After the pacification of Lǒng and Shǔ,
unless there was an urgent warning,
he never spoke of military campaigns again.
The crown prince once asked about matters of attack and battle,
and the emperor said:
"In the past, when Duke Líng of Wèi asked about battle formations,
Confucius did not answer.
This is not something you need to concern yourself with."
Every morning he held court,
and only dismissed it when the sun set.
He frequently summoned dukes, ministers, gentlemen, and generals to discuss governance and administration,
and did not sleep until after midnight.
The crown prince saw the emperor's diligent and tireless efforts,
and seizing an opportune moment, advised him, saying:
"Your Majesty possesses the wisdom of Yǔ and Tāng,
but has lost the blessings of nourishing one's nature according to Huáng-Lǎo principles.
I wish you would care for your spirit and energy,
and leisurely enjoy your peace."
The emperor said:
"I enjoy this myself; I do not feel tired."
Although he personally accomplished great deeds,
he remained cautious as if he had not yet succeeded.
Therefore, he was able to clearly and carefully manage the affairs of government,
and maintain control over all power and authority.
He assessed the times and measured his strength,
so that no action he took was erroneous.
He retired meritorious officials and promoted civil administrators,
sheathed his bows and arrows and dispersed his horses and cattle.
Although his Dao did not quite match that of ancient times,
this too was a form of martial achievement that ceased conflict.
A commentary states: The Imperial Ancestor, Nándùn Jūn (南頓君), was initially the Magistrate of Jìyáng (濟陽).
On the night of *jiǎzǐ* (甲子) in the twelfth month of the first year of Jiànpíng (建平) [9 BCE], Guāngwǔ (光武) was born in the county office.
A red light illuminated the room.
He was astonished and found it extraordinary,
so he sent the diviner Wáng Cháng (王長) to interpret it.
Wáng Cháng dismissed those around him
and said:
"This omen is too auspicious to be spoken of."
That year, auspicious grain grew in the county's borders,
with one stalk bearing nine ears.
Because of this, Guāngwǔ (光武) was named Xiù (秀).
The following year,
a *fāngshì* (方士) named Xià Hèliáng (夏賀良)
reported to Emperor Āi (哀帝),
saying that the Han (漢) dynasty's Mandate of Heaven was in decline
and that it was destined to receive a new mandate.
Thereupon, the era name was changed to Tàichū Yuánnián (太初元年),
and he was called
"Chén Shèng Liú Tàipíng Huángdì" (陳聖劉太平皇帝)
to avert misfortune.
When Wáng Mǎng (王莽) usurped the throne,
he resented and disliked the Liú (劉) clan.
Because the character for "gold" (金) and "knife" (刀) were present in the word for "money" (錢),
he changed it to *Huòquán* (貨泉).
Some interpreted the characters on the *Huòquán* (貨泉) coin as
"Báishuǐ Zhēnrén" (白水真人).
Later, Sū Bó'ē (蘇伯阿), a diviner who observed *qì* (氣), was sent by Wáng Mǎng (王莽) to Nányáng (南陽).
From afar, he saw the walls of Chōnglíng (舂陵)
and exclaimed:
"What splendid *qì*!
Luxuriant and verdant!"
When he first raised an army and returned to Chōnglíng (舂陵),
he saw from a distance to the south of his dwelling
a dazzling fire illuminating the sky,
which then disappeared shortly after.
Initially,
the Daoist masters Xīmén Jūnhuì (西門君惠) and Lǐ Shǒu (李守) also said that Liú Xiù (劉秀) was destined to become the Son of Heaven.
Is it true that a ruler's reception of the Mandate
is accompanied by such omens?
If not,
how could he have seized the timely dragon and controlled the heavens?
A eulogy states: The fiery virtue (of Han) was in decline,
and a great bandit usurped the state.
The nine provinces swirled,
and the three luminaries were shrouded in mist.
People grew weary of deceit and treachery;
gods longed for a return to virtue.
Guāngwǔ (光武) was born with the Mandate,
and spiritual blessings manifested themselves.
He discerned subtle changes before others,
and his profound strategy was intertwined with celestial patterns.
He gathered hundreds of thousands of followers,
like *píhǔ* (貔虎) forming a pack.
Long chariots thundered across the plains,
and high spears pierced the clouds like comets.
Once his heroic might was displayed,
the new capital (Wáng Mǎng's) burned itself.
He slaughtered the commoners and generations [of the usurper],
and disputes raged in Liáng (梁) and Zhào (趙).
The Three Rivers were not yet clear,
and the four passes were again disturbed.
Then the divine banner turned,
and heaven's retribution was meted out in succession.
[一０]Fortresses lost their defenses,
and chariots and books shared the same path.
[一一]Once auspicious omens were revealed,
human stratagems all concurred.
[一二]Bright and clear was the ancestral plan,
valiant and decisive was the heroic judgment.
[一三]Oh, how glorious was the Mandate,
which made our Han (漢) prosper!
[一四] Biography of Emperor Xiǎnzōng Xiàomíng (顯宗孝明帝紀) No. 2
Emperor Xiǎnzōng Xiàomíng (顯宗孝明皇帝), personal name Zhuāng (莊),
was Guāngwǔ's (光武) fourth son.
His mother was Empress Yīn (陰).
The Emperor was born with a broad lower jaw;
at the age of ten, he could comprehend the *Chūnqiū* (春秋).
Guāngwǔ (光武) found him extraordinary.
In the fifteenth year of Jiànwǔ (建武) [40 CE], he was enfeoffed as the Duke of Dōnghǎi (東海公).
In the seventeenth year, his noble rank was elevated to King.
In the nineteenth year, he was established as Crown Prince.
He studied under the *Bóshì* (博士) Huán Róng (桓榮)
and mastered the *Shàngshū* (尚書).
On the *wùxū* (戊戌) day of the second month of the second year of Zhōngyuán (中元) [57 CE],
he ascended the imperial throne
at the age of thirty.
He honored the Empress as the Empress Dowager.
On the *dīngmǎo* (丁卯) day of the third month,
Emperor Guāngwǔ (光武) was interred at Yuánlíng (原陵).
The officials concerned proposed that his ancestral temple be honored with the title Shìzǔ (世祖).
In the fourth month, on the *bǐngchén* (丙辰) day,
an imperial edict stated:
"I, a mere junior,
have received and inherited the sacred enterprise.
Night and day I tremble with reverence,
not daring to be idle or at ease.
The late emperor received the Mandate and brought about a restoration;
his virtue was equal to that of emperors and kings.
He harmonized all states
and was recognized by heaven and earth.
He pacified all spirits
and bestowed favor upon the masses and the vulnerable.
I have taken on this great destiny,
succeeding to the body and preserving the culture.
Unaware of the hardships of cultivation,
I fear that there may be failures and losses.
The sacred grace and last instructions
hold the world in great esteem,
considering the common people as paramount.
How will the *gōngqīng* (公卿) and all officials
assist me in my shortcomings?
Therefore, bestow upon all men in the empire two ranks of nobility;
the *sānlǎo* (三老), the filial and brotherly, and the diligent farmers, three ranks.
If the rank exceeds *gōngchéng* (公乘),
they may transfer it to a son, a sibling, or a sibling's son.
For refugees without registered names who wish to register themselves, one rank.
For the masses, widows, orphans, the solitary, and the severely ill,
ten *hú* (斛) of grain each.
As for those who suffered punishment and prisoners in commanderies and states
who committed offenses before the amnesty on the *jǐmǎo* (己卯) day of the fourth month of the first year of Zhōngyuán (中元) [56 CE] but were arrested and imprisoned thereafter,
all their punishments are to be remitted.
Furthermore, border people who suffered from unrest and became wives of people in inland commanderies,
if before the *jǐmǎo* (己卯) amnesty,
are all to be sent back to the border,
to do as they please.
Officials from the rank of *zhōng èrqiānshí* (中二千石) down to those with yellow seals
who were demoted in rank or paid redemption
are all to have their ranks restored and redemption returned.
At present, there is no Son of Heaven above,
and no regional governors below,
as if crossing deep waters without a boat or oar.
Indeed, the responsibility of the myriad chariots (the empire) is extremely heavy,
yet the vigorous (the young emperor) may be light-minded.
[一０]Truly, I rely on virtuous men to assist this young one.
[一一]Hú Yǔ (胡禹), Marquis of Gāomì (高密侯), is the foremost in great achievements.
Liú Cāng (劉蒼), King of Dōngpíng (東平王), is magnanimous and resourceful.
Both can be entrusted with the charge of a six-foot orphan
and remain unyielding in the face of great trials.
[一二]Therefore, make Hú Yǔ (胡禹) the Grand Tutor (太傅) and
Liú Cāng (劉蒼) the General of Agile Cavalry (驃騎將軍).
Let the Grand尉, Xǐ (憙), announce the posthumous title at the southern suburban altar.
[一三]Let the Grand Minister of Works, Xīn (訢), reverently escort the coffin for burial.
[一四]Let the Grand Minister of Agriculture, Fáng (魴), lead the troops to restore the earth.
[一五]Enfeoff Xǐ (憙) as the Marquis of Jiéxiāng (節鄉侯),
Xīn (訢) as the Marquis of Ānxiāng (安鄉侯),
and Fáng (魴) as the Marquis of Yángyì (楊邑侯)."
In the ninth month of autumn,
the Shāodāng Qiāng (燒當羌) raided Lǒngxī (隴西)
and defeated the commandery troops at Yǔnjiē (允街).
An amnesty was granted to prisoners in Lǒngxī (隴西),
reducing their sentences by one degree,
and they were not to be collected for this season's levies. The three thousand men conscripted from Tiānshuǐ (天水)
were also exempted from taxes for this year.
The Attendant Secretary (謁者) Zhāng Hóng (張鴻) was sent to suppress the rebellious Qiāng (羌) at Yǔnwú (允吾).
Zhāng Hóng's (張鴻) army was utterly defeated,
and he died in battle.
In the eleventh month of winter,
the Palace Commander (中郎將) Dòu Gù (竇固) was dispatched to oversee General of Capturing Barbarians (捕虜將軍) Mǎ Wǔ (馬武) and two other generals to attack the Shāodāng Qiāng (燒當羌).
On the *jiǎyín* (甲寅) day of the twelfth month,
an imperial edict stated:
"Spring is the time to observe the seasons;
people engage in farming and sericulture.
Order the relevant officials to diligently follow the seasonal *qì*
and not to cause trouble or disturbance.
For all fugitives in the empire sentenced to death or lesser penalties,
they are permitted to pay redemption:
for capital crimes, twenty bolts of fine silk;
for crimes from amputation of the right foot down to shaving the head, wearing a cangue, and working as a convict, ten bolts;
for complete convicts down to those serving as *sīkòu zuò* (司寇作), three bolts.
If the crime has not yet been discovered,
those who report themselves first upon the arrival of this edict
shall pay half the redemption.
Currently, selections (for office) are not genuine,
and wicked flatterers have not been removed.
Powerful families make requests and solicit favors,
and corrupt officials act recklessly.
The common people are distressed and resentful,
with no one to tell their grievances.
The relevant officials must clearly present the charges
and also correct those who made the recommendations.
Furthermore, whenever commanderies and counties impose levies,
they lightly commit fraud for profit,
wrongfully demand from the weak and frail,
and prioritize the poor.
They must strive for fairness and impartiality,
and not allow any wrongful impositions."
In the first month of spring of the first year of Yǒngpíng (永平) [58 CE],
the Emperor, leading the *gōngqīng* (公卿) and all officials below, held court at Yuánlíng (原陵),
following the protocol of the New Year's assembly.
In the fifth month of summer,
Grand Tutor Dèng Yǔ (鄧禹) passed away.
On the *wùyín* (戊寅) day,
Liú Qiáng (劉彊), King of Dōnghǎi (東海王), passed away.
The Grand Minister of Agriculture Fēng Fáng (馮魴) was sent with a credential to oversee the funeral arrangements,
and a "dragon-ascending banner" (升龍旄頭), imperial chariot (鑾輅), and dragon banner (龍旂) were bestowed.
On the *yǐmǎo* (乙卯) day of the sixth month,
Liú Qiáng (劉彊), King Gōng of Dōnghǎi (東海恭王), was interred.
In the seventh month of autumn,
General of the Captives Mǎ Wǔ and others fought against the Shāodāng Qiāng,
and greatly defeated them.
Soldiers were recruited to garrison Lǒngyòu,
and each person was granted 30,000 qián.
On the day of Wùzǐ in the eighth month,
Jīng, King of Shānyáng, was moved to become King of Guǎnglín,
and dispatched to his state.
In this year,
Jì Róng, Administrator of Liáodōng, sent the Xiānbēi to attack the Chìshān Wūhuán,
and greatly defeated them,
beheading their chieftains.
The Gūfù Yi of Yuèsuí rebelled,
and the provincial and commandery administrations suppressed them.
In the first month of spring in the second year, on the day of Xīnmò,
Emperor Guāngwǔ was worshipped in the Míngtáng as an ancestor.
The Emperor, the dukes, ministers, and marquises first wore crowns, robes, jade pendants, and embroidered shoes to conduct the ceremony.
After the rites were completed,
he ascended the Língtái.
The Director of the Secretariat, holding a staff of authority, issued an edict to the General of Agile Cavalry and the Three Dukes, saying:
"Today, on this propitious day of the auspicious month,
Emperor Guāngwǔ has been worshipped in the Míngtáng as an ancestor,
to be paired with the Five Emperors.
The rites are complete with all ceremonial objects,
the music harmonizes the eight tones,
the blessings are sung,
and the merits danced.
Timely decrees are issued,
and commands given to the various rulers.
After the ceremony,
we ascended the Língtái,
observed the primordial qi,
played the seasonal pitch pipes,
and contemplated the changes in things.
The various officials, regional aides,
descendants of the imperial clan,
the various commanderies presenting their accounts,
the hundred barbarian tribes offering their tributes,
the Wūhuán and Huìnà all came to assist in the sacrifice,
and the Xiongnu Shànyú's sons serving as hostages and the Gǔdōuhóu also attended.
This is indeed brought about by the merits and virtues of the Sacred Ancestor.
I, being ignorant and humble,
have inherited this great enterprise,
personally held the jade gui and bi,
and reverently sacrificed to Heaven and Earth.
Looking back, the late emperor received the Mandate and brought about a restoration,
restoring order from chaos,
thereby pacifying the world,
performed the Feng and Shan sacrifices on Mount Tài,
established the Míngtáng,
built the Pìyōng,
and erected the Língtái,
broadening and extending the Great Way,
which reached the eight extremes;
yet his descendant lacks the qualities of Chéng and Kāng,
and his ministers lack the strategies of Lǚ and Dàn.
〔一０〕As I wash and present the wine cups,
I am filled with shame and trepidation.
〔一一〕My nature is inherently dull and coarse,
and I become even more fearful when facing affairs.
Hence, 'The noble person is open and at ease;
the petty person is constantly anxious.'
〔一二〕Let an amnesty be granted to all in the empire, from those condemned to death downwards,
including those who plotted rebellion or committed great treason,
all are to be pardoned.
All officials and teachers,
strive to diligently fulfill your duties,
act in accordance with the seasonal decrees,
and be reverent like august Heaven,
to bring peace to the common people."
〔一三〕
In the third month,
he visited the Pìyōng,
and first performed the Grand Archery Ceremony.
In the ninth month of autumn,
Fǔ, King of Pèi; Yīng, King of Chǔ; Kāng, King of Jìnán; Yán, King of Huáiyáng; and Zhèng, King of Dōnghǎi, came to court.
On the day of Rénzǐ in the tenth month of winter,
he visited the Pìyōng,
and first performed the ceremony of nourishing the elderly.
An edict stated:
"Emperor Guāngwǔ established the rites of the Three Dynasties,
but had not yet been able to attend and partake.
I, a humble youth,
have come to inherit this sacred enterprise.
Recently, on an auspicious day in late spring,
I first performed the Grand Archery;
on the first day of this auspicious month,
I again trod the Pìyōng.
I revered the Three Elders as if serving them,
and treated the Five Venerables as elder brothers,
providing comfortable carriages and soft wheels,
assisting and offering.
The marquises and kings prepared sauces,
the dukes and ministers presented delicacies,
and I personally bared my arm to carve the meat,
holding the goblet and rinsing my mouth.
May they be blessed to swallow without choking,
and blessed to eat without getting stuck.
Above, the 'Lù Míng' was sung;
below, the 'Xīn Gōng' was played on wind instruments,
the eight rows of dancers were fully arranged,
and the myriad dances performed in the courtyard.
I am truly of meager virtue,
how can I possibly be worthy?
The *Yì* speaks of riding on a burden,
the *Shī* critiques comparing oneself to others.
I constantly remember my shame and regret,
never forgetting it in my heart.
The Three Elder Lǐ Gōng
is aged and learned.
The Five Venerable Huán Róng
taught me the *Shàngshū*.
The *Shī* says: 'No virtue goes unrewarded,
no word goes without a response.'
Therefore, grant Róng the noble title of Guānnèihóu,
with an enfeoffment of five thousand households.
The Three Elders and Five Venerables shall all be maintained with a salary equivalent to two thousand dàn for the rest of their lives.
Let each of the Three Elders in the empire be granted one dàn of wine
and forty jīn of meat.
The officials concerned shall care for the aged,
〔一０〕have compassion for orphans,
and show favor to widows,
thus fulfilling my intentions."
Yān, King of Zhōngshān, first went to his state.
On the day of Jiǎzǐ,
the Emperor made a western inspection tour,
visited Cháng'ān,
sacrificed at the Gāomiào,
and then performed rites at the eleven imperial tombs.
He traveled through and inspected the various mansions and cities,
met with officials from commanderies and counties,
and bestowed rewards and music.
On the day of Jiǎshēn in the eleventh month,
envoys were dispatched to sacrifice to Xiāo Hé and Huò Guāng with a middle-level offering.
The Emperor paid respects at the imperial tombs
and passed by their graves in a ceremonial procession.
He then proceeded to Hédōng,
and wherever he passed, he granted gifts to officials from the rank of two thousand dàn, magistrate, and chief down to clerks,
each according to their rank.
On the day of Guǐmǎo,
the imperial carriage returned to the palace.
In the twelfth month,
Dòu Lín, Colonel Protector of the Qiāng, was imprisoned and died.
In this year,
the welcoming of the qi was first performed in the Five Suburbs.
Fēng, son of Yīn Jiù, Lesser Controller of the Imperial Household, killed his wife, Princess Lìyì.
Jiù was implicated and committed suicide.
In the first month of spring in the third year, on the day of Guǐsì,
an edict stated:
"I performed the suburban sacrifices,
ascended the Língtái,
met with the imperial historians,
and rectified ceremonial standards.
Spring is
the beginning of the year.
If the beginning is correctly aligned,
then the three seasons will be accomplished.
Recently, floods and droughts have been irregular,
and border residents have little food.
Policies were amiss above,
and the people suffered the consequences.
Let the officials concerned strive to accord with the seasonal qi,
encourage and supervise agriculture and sericulture,
eliminate the cutworms and locusts,
as well as the insect pests;
carefully review punishments and be cautious with penalties,
clearly investigate single statements,
and work tirelessly day and night,
to fulfill my intentions."
On the day of Jiǎyín in the second month,
Zhào Xǐ, Grand Commandant, and Lǐ Xīn, Minister of Education, were dismissed.
On the day of Bǐngchén,
Guō Dān, Left Protector of Fēngyì, became Minister of Education.
On the day of Jǐwèi,
Yú Yán, Administrator of Nányáng, became Grand Commandant.
On the day of Jiǎzǐ,
the noble lady, Lady Mǎ, was established as empress,
and imperial prince Dá
was established as crown prince.
All men in the empire were granted two ranks of nobility;
the Three Elders, filial and fraternal individuals, and industrious farmers were granted three ranks;
rootless people without registered names who wished to register were granted one rank;
widows, orphans, the solitary, the severely ill, and the poor who could not support themselves were granted grain,
five dàn per person.
On the day of Xīnyǒu in the fourth month of summer,
imperial prince Jiàn was enfeoffed as King of Qiāncéng,
and Xiàn as King of Guǎngpíng.
On the day of Dīngmǎo in the sixth month,
a comet appeared north of Tiānchuán.
On the day of Wùchén in the eighth month of autumn,
the Grand Music was changed to Grand Performance Music.
On the last day of the Rénshēn [month],
there was a solar eclipse.
An imperial edict stated:
"I have received and carried on the ancestral enterprise,
but have no good governance.
The sun and moon suffer eclipses,
comets appear in the sky,
floods and droughts are irregular,
crops fail,
people have no stored provisions,
and those below suffer distress.
Although I diligently ponder day and night,
my wisdom and ability are insufficient.
In the past, King Zhuāng of Chǔ had no calamities,
yet he maintained vigilance and fear;
Duke Āi of Lǔ suffered great misfortune,
but Heaven did not send down condemnation.
The current celestial phenomena
are perhaps a warning for me to save the situation.
Let the officials conscientiously attend to their duties,
to assist one who is devoid of virtue.
In ancient times, high ministers offered poems,
and all artisans offered remonstrances.
Those who speak of affairs
should not conceal anything."
In the winter, tenth month,
a steaming sacrifice was offered at the temple of Guāngwǔ.
For the first time, the dances of Wénshǐ, Wǔxíng, and Wǔdé were performed.
On the Jiǎzǐ day,
the imperial carriage, accompanied by the Empress Dowager, visited Zhānglíng,
to view the old residence.
On the twelfth month Wùchén day,
they returned from Zhānglíng.
That year,
the Northern Palace and various government offices were constructed.
The capital and seven commanderies and kingdoms suffered great floods.
In the fourth year, spring, second month Xīnhài day,
an imperial edict stated:
"I personally plowed the sacrificial field,
to pray for agricultural affairs.
In the capital, there was no lingering snow in winter,
and no warm rain in spring;
the numerous officials toiled and prayed with utmost sincerity.
And recently, timely rain has fallen twice,
moistening the overwintering wheat.
Therefore, grant the dukes and ministers half their stipends.
Let the officials diligently follow current policies,
and strive to make punishments equitable."
In autumn, ninth month Wùyín day,
Jiàn, King of Qiānchéng, died.
In winter, tenth month Yǐmǎo day,
Sītú Guō Dān and Sīkōng Féng Fáng were dismissed.
On the Bǐngchén day,
Fàn Qiān, Yin of Hénán, was appointed Sītú,
and Fú Gōng, Grand Coachman, was appointed Sīkōng.
In the twelfth month,
Liáng Sōng, Marquis of Língxiāng, was imprisoned and died.
In the fifth year, spring, second month Gēngxū day,
Cāng, King of Dōngpíng and General of Agile Cavalry, was relieved and returned to his fief;
Jīng, King of Lángxié, proceeded to his state.
In winter, tenth month,
the imperial retinue went to Yè.
He met Xǔ, King of Zhào, at Yè.
The three elders of Chángshān said to the Emperor:
"Your Majesty was born in Yuánshì.
We wish to receive preferential remission."
An imperial edict stated:
"Fēng, Pèi, and Jìyáng
are where the Mandate originated from.
Bestowing grace and repaying virtue
is appropriate.
Now, under the administration of Yǒngpíng,
the common people are filled with resentment,
yet officials and commoners seek remission.
This causes me shame and ridicule.
Nonetheless, I cannot disregard the earnest plea of this county.
Therefore, remit the land tax and additional levies for Yuánshì county for six years,
and reward the county clerks
and the runners at the palace gates."
He returned from Yè.
In the eleventh month,
the Northern Xiōngnú raided Wǔyuán;
in the twelfth month,
they raided Yúnzhōng.
The Southern Chányú attacked and repelled them.
That year,
border residents who were in the inner commanderies were sent away,
and each was granted twenty thousand cash for travel expenses.
In the sixth year, spring, first month,

Fǔ, King of Pèi; Yīng, King of Chǔ; Cāng, King of Dōngpíng; Yán, King of Huáiyáng; Jīng, King of Lángxié; Zhèng, King of Dōnghǎi; Xū, King of Zhào; Xīng, King of Běihǎi; and Shí, King of Qí came to court.
In the second month,
a precious tripod emerged from Mount Luò.
The Administrator of Lújiāng presented it.
In summer, fourth month Jiǎzǐ day,
an imperial edict stated:
"In the past, Yǔ collected metal from the nine provinces,
and cast cauldrons to symbolize creatures,
allowing people to know the divine and the malevolent,
and avoid evil qi.
When virtue thrived,
the cauldrons passed to Shāng and Zhōu;
when Zhōu's virtue declined,
the cauldrons were lost.
Auspicious omens descend
in response to those with virtue.
At present, governance and transformation are fraught with many deviations.
How then could this have come about?
The Yì Jīng says the cauldrons symbolize the Three Dukes.
Could it be that the dukes and ministers perform their duties correctly?
Let the Grand Minister of Sacrifices, on the day of the spring sacrifice,
display the tripod in the temple,
to be used as an implement.
Grant the Three Dukes fifty rolls of silk each,
and the Nine Ministers and officials of two thousand dàns half of that.
Previous imperial edicts
forbade people from submitting memorials that spoke of 'sageliness,'
yet recently memorials and reports often contain excessive flattery.
From now on, if there are overly complimentary and hollow praises,
the Grand Scribes should suppress them and not review them,
to show that I do not tolerate flatterers and simpletons."
In winter, tenth month,
the imperial retinue traveled to Lǔ,
and sacrificed at the tomb of Gōng, King of Dōnghǎi;
he met with Fǔ, King of Pèi; Yīng, King of Chǔ; Kāng, King of Jìnán; Cāng, King of Dōngpíng; Yán, King of Huáiyáng; Jīng, King of Lángxié; and Zhèng, King of Dōnghǎi.
In the twelfth month,
he returned,
and visited Yángchéng,
sending envoys to sacrifice at Mount Zhōngyuè.
On the Rénwǔ day,
the imperial carriage returned to the palace.
Cāng, King of Dōngpíng, and Jīng, King of Lángxié, accompanied the carriage and came to pay respects to the Empress Dowager.
In the seventh year, spring, first month Guǐmǎo day,
Empress Dowager Yīn died.
In the second month Gēngshēn day,
Empress Guāngliè was buried.
In autumn, eighth month Wùchén day,
Xīng, King of Běihǎi, died.
That year,
the Northern Xiōngnú sent envoys to request peace and kinship.
In the eighth year, spring, first month Jǐmǎo day,
Sītú Fàn Qiān died.
In the third month Xīnmǎo day,
Tàiwèi Yú Yán was appointed Sītú,
and Zhào Xǐ, Wèiwei, acted as Tàiwèi.
Zhèng Zhòng, Mounted Commandant of the Yue Cavalry, was dispatched to reciprocate the envoy of the Northern Xiōngnú.
For the first time, the General who Pacifies the Liao was established,
stationed at Mánbǎi in Wǔyuán.
In autumn,
fourteen commanderies and kingdoms suffered from floods.
In winter, tenth month,
the Northern Palace was completed.
On the Bǐngzǐ day,
he presided over the Bìyōng,
and entertained the three elders and five venerable gentlemen.
After the ceremony,
an imperial edict instructed the Three Dukes to recruit death-row prisoners from the capital and commanderies and kingdoms,
reducing their sentences by one degree,
without flogging,
to be sent to the camp of the General who Pacifies the Liao,
and stationed in the border counties of Shuòfāng and Wǔyuán;
their wives and children could follow them,
and register in the border counties;
if parents or siblings wished to take their place,
they were free to do so.
As for those guilty of grave treason and heinous crimes punishable by a unique death,
all were to be recruited and sent to the silkworm chamber.
Runaways were allowed to redeem their crimes, each with different conditions.
All those who were relocated
were granted bows, crossbows, clothing, and rations.
On the last day of the Rén-yín [year],
there was a solar eclipse,
which was total.
An edict stated:
“I, with my lack of virtue,
have undertaken this great enterprise,
and below I have incurred the resentment of the people,
while above I have agitated the Three Luminaries.
The anomaly of the solar eclipse,
its calamity is especially great,
which the Spring and Autumn Annals and apocryphal texts declare to be a supreme condemnation.
I constantly reflect on this fault,
which lies with me alone.
Let all officials diligently perform their duties,
speaking plainly without concealment.”
Thereupon, those in office all submitted sealed memorials,
each speaking of gains and losses.
The emperor read the memorials,
deeply blamed himself,
and then circulated the memorials among all officials.
An edict stated:
“What all my officials have said
are all my faults.
The wrongs of the people I cannot rectify,
the cunning of officials I cannot restrain;
and I lightly employ manpower,
repairing palaces and residences,
my comings and goings are without moderation,
my joys and angers are excessive.
Formerly, the Yìng Mén (a part of the palace) was ill-guarded,
and the Guān Jū criticized the age;
flying thistles followed the wind,
which Wēi Zǐ lamented.
I forever behold these past warnings,
trembling with awe and fear.
I am merely afraid that my scant virtue,
over time, will lead to negligence.”
The Northern Xiōngnú raided various commanderies in Xīhé.
In the ninth year, spring, third month, on the Xīn-chǒu day,
an edict pardoned death-row prisoners in commanderies and states,
allowing them to go with their wives and children to Wǔyuán and Shuòfāng to settle;
wherever such a person died, their wife's father or brother, or their son or full brother, was granted lifelong exemption from service;
if their wife had no father or brother but only a mother,
her mother was granted sixty thousand coins,
and her household tax was also remitted.
Summer, fourth month, on the Jiǎ-chén day,
an edict ordered commanderies and states to grant public land to the poor, each according to their circumstances.

It was ordered that the Sīlì Xiàowèi and the regional Cìshǐ annually report one of the “ink-ribboned” chief officials who had served three years or more and whose administration was particularly outstanding,
submitting these reports together with the census.
And those whose administration was particularly poor
were also to be reported.
This year,
there was a great harvest.
Schools were established for the petty marquises of the Four Surnames,
and masters of the Five Classics were appointed.
In the tenth year, spring, second month,
Wáng Jīng, King of Guǎnglíng, committed a crime,
committed suicide,
and his state was abolished.
Summer, fourth month, on the Wù-zǐ day,
an edict stated:
“Last year, the five grains yielded abundantly,
and this year, silk and wheat had good harvests;
therefore, a great amnesty is granted to the empire.
At this flourishing time of summer growth,
let us cleanse old evils
to reward the farmers' efforts.
Let the people diligently cultivate mulberries and crops,
to prepare for disasters.
Let officials respect their duties,
and not allow any errors or neglect.”
In the intercalary month, on the Jiǎ-wǔ day,
the emperor made a southern tour,
went to Nányáng,
and offered sacrifices at Zhānglíng.
On the summer solstice (literally, "sun reached north"),
he also offered sacrifices at his old residence.
After the rituals,
he summoned students from the imperial academy to perform court music,
playing "Lù Míng."
The emperor himself played the xūn and chí (ancient wind instruments) to accompany them,
to entertain the honored guests.
Upon returning,
he went to Nándùn,
and feasted the Three Elders and his officials.
Winter, eleventh month,
Wáng Tíng, King of Huáiyáng, was summoned to a meeting at Píngyú;
Wáng Fǔ, King of Pèi, was summoned to a meeting at Suīyáng.
Twelfth month, on the Jiǎ-wǔ day,
the imperial carriage returned to the palace.
In the eleventh year, spring, first month,

Wáng Fǔ, King of Pèi; Wáng Yīng, King of Chǔ; Wáng Kāng, King of Jìnán; Wáng Cāng, King of Dōngpíng; Wáng Yán, King of Huáiyáng; Wáng Yān, King of Zhōngshān; Wáng Jīng, King of Lángyá; and Wáng Zhèng, King of Dōnghǎi, came to court.
Autumn, seventh month,
Guō Bà, Sīlì Xiàowèi, was imprisoned and died.
This year,
yellow gold was found in Cháohú,
which the Grand Administrator of Lújiāng presented.
At this time, qílín, white pheasants, sweet springs, and auspicious grains appeared in various places.
In the twelfth year, spring, first month,
the Ailáo King of the Yi people from outside Yìzhōu's frontier led his people to submit.
Thereupon, Yǒngchāng Commandery was established,
and the Western Commandant of Yìzhōu was abolished.
Summer, fourth month,
Jiàngzuò Yèzhě Wáng Wú was sent to repair the Bīqú canal,
from Xíngyáng to Qiānchéng Hǎikǒu.
Fifth month, on the Bǐng-chén day,
titles of nobility were granted to all men in the empire,
two ranks per person;
the Three Elders, filial and fraternal individuals, and diligent farmers received three ranks per person;
for transient people without registered names who wished to register, one rank per person;
widows, widowers, orphans, childless elderly, the seriously ill, and the poor who had no family and could not support themselves were granted grain,
three hú per person.
An edict stated:
“Formerly, Zēng and Mǐn served their parents,
exhausting themselves to provide for them;
Zhòngní (Confucius) buried his son,
with a coffin but no outer coffin.
Mourning values expressing grief,
while ritual preserves peace and frugality.
But now, the common people's customs for funerals
compete in extravagance and ostentation.
The living have no stone (small amount) of savings,
yet their wealth and resources are exhausted on grave mounds.
At New Year and Winter Solstice they have no dregs or husks (poor food),
yet sacrificial animals are lavishly prepared for a single offering.
They squander and ruin the accumulated wealth of generations,
to provide for the expenses of a single morning,
leaving their descendants hungry and cold,
ending their lives in this manner.
How can this be the intention of their ancestors?
Moreover, the systems for carriages and clothing
are indulged to the extreme.
Fields lie waste and uncultivated,
and those who roam and eat are numerous.
Let the relevant officials clearly reiterate the prohibitions,
and what is appropriate for the present,
let it be announced to the commanderies and states.”
Autumn, seventh month, on the Yǐ-hài day,
Fú Gōng, Sīkōng, was dismissed.
On the Yǐ-wèi day,
Móu Róng, Dàsīnóng, became Sīkōng.
Winter, tenth month,
Wáng Kāng, Sīlì Xiàowèi, was imprisoned and died.
This year,
the empire was peaceful and stable,
people were free from forced labor,
the harvests were abundant year after year,
the common people were prosperous,
millet cost thirty coins per hú,
and cattle and sheep covered the fields.
In the thirteenth year, spring, second month,
the emperor plowed the sacrificial field.
After the ritual,
food was granted to the spectators.
Third month,
Xuē Zhāo, Hénán Yǐn, was imprisoned and died.
In the summer, fourth month,
the Xiùqú was completed.
On the day Xīnsì,
the Emperor made an imperial tour to Xíngyáng,
inspecting the river and canals.
On the day Yǐyóu,
an imperial edict stated:
"Since the collapse of the Xiùqú,
more than sixty years ago,
and especially in recent years,
the rain has been unseasonal,
the Yellow River has flooded eastward,
growing worse day by day.
The original sites of the sluice gates
are all now in the middle of the river.
Vast and overflowing,
the banks cannot be discerned.
It stretches boundlessly to the horizon,
its course unknown.
Now, the people of Yǎn and Yù
suffer greatly from floods,
and they say that the government does not prioritize the people's urgent needs,
but prefers to undertake other projects.
Some also believe that the Yellow River's entry into the Xiùqú
benefits Yōu and Jì,
and thus they say, 'If the left embankment is strong, the right embankment is damaged;
if both left and right are strong, the downstream is damaged.'
It is better to let the water follow its natural course,
allowing people to settle on higher ground.
The government would save the cost of damming and blocking,
and the common people would avoid the suffering of drowning.
However, opinions differ,
and there are conflicting arguments from north and south.
I do not know which to follow,
and have long been unable to decide.
Now that embankments have been built, the canal dredged,
the water diverted and gates erected,
the Yellow River and the Xiùqú are separated,
restoring their old courses.
To the north of Táoqiū,
the land is gradually becoming mounds of earth.
Therefore, I offer splendid jade and pure sacrificial animals
to pay homage to the River God.
Passing eastward by Luòruì,
I marvel at Yǔ's accomplishments.
Now, the suitability of the five soils
has returned to its proper state.
The low-lying fields along the canal
shall be allocated to the poor,
so that the powerful and influential do not monopolize their benefits.
Thus, I hope to continue the work of Emperor Wǔ of the Hàn Dynasty at Hùzǐ."
Thereupon, he crossed the Yellow River,
ascended Tài Háng,
and advanced to Shàngdǎng.
On the day Rén Yín,
the imperial carriage returned to the palace.
In the winter, tenth month, on the last day, Rén Chén,
there was a solar eclipse.
The Three Excellencies removed their caps and impeached themselves.
The imperial command stated:
"Do not impeach yourselves for caps and shoes.
Calamities and anomalies repeatedly appear,
the fault lies with me.
Worried and anxious,
I do not know the proper course of action.
Could it be that officials, when reporting matters,
conceal and suppress much,
causing the ruler to be obstructed
and the common people to be discontent?
In ancient times, the state of Wèi had loyal ministers,
and Duke Líng was able to maintain his position.
How can we now harmonize Yin and Yang,
and dispel calamities and condemnations?
Inspectors and Administrators should investigate punishments and rectify injustices,
and care for orphans and the vulnerable.
Strive to fulfill your duties."
In the eleventh month,
Liú Yīng, King of Chǔ, plotted rebellion.
He was deposed,
his kingdom abolished,
and he was relocated to Jīngxiàn.
Thousands of people implicated were either executed or exiled.
In this year,
Liú Shí, King of Qí, died.
In the fourteenth year, spring, third month, on the day Jiǎ Xū,
Yú Yán, Sītú, was dismissed
and committed suicide.
In the summer, fourth month, on the day Dīng Sì,
Xíng Mù from Nányáng, Administrator of Jùlù, was appointed Sītú.
Former King Yīng of Chǔ committed suicide.
In the summer, fifth month,
Liú Yuánshòu, son of the former Prince Jīng of Guǎnglín, was enfeoffed as Marquis of Guǎnglín.
The construction of the Shòulíng tomb began.
In the fifteenth year, spring, second month, on the day Gēng Zǐ,
the Emperor made an eastern tour.
On the day Xīn Chǒu,
he visited Yǎnshī.
An imperial edict ordered that fugitives, from those deserving extreme punishment downwards, could redeem themselves:
for death crimes, forty rolls of fine silk; for crimes from right foot amputation to tattooing, branding, and hard labor for life, ten rolls of fine silk;
for hard labor without branding to minor crimes, five rolls of fine silk.
For those who committed crimes but were not yet discovered,
if they reported themselves on the day the edict arrived,
they would pay half the redemption amount.
Liú Fǔ, Prince of Pèi, was summoned to meet at Suīyáng.
The Emperor advanced to Péngchéng.
On the day Guǐ Hài,
the Emperor ploughed the fields at Xiàpī.
In the third month,
Liú Jīng, Prince of Lángyá, was summoned to meet at Liángchéng;
Liú Cāng, Prince of Dōngpíng, was summoned to meet at Yángdū;
and the Marquis of Guǎnglín and his three younger brothers were summoned to meet at Lǔ.
Sacrifices were offered at the tomb of King Gōng of Dōnghǎi.
Returning,
the Emperor visited Confucius's residence
and offered sacrifices to Zhòngní and his seventy-two disciples.
He personally presided over the lecture hall,
commanding the Crown Prince and various princes to expound on the classics.
He also visited Dōngpíng.
On the day Xīn Mǎo,
he advanced to Dàliáng,
then went to Dìngtáo,
where he offered sacrifices at the tomb of King Gōng of Dìngtáo.
In the summer, fourth month, on the day Gēng Zǐ,
the imperial carriage returned to the palace.
Xìndū was renamed Lèchéng Commandery,
and Lín Huái was renamed Xiàpī Commandery.
The imperial son Liú Gōng was enfeoffed as Prince of Jùlù;
Liú Dǎng as Prince of Lèchéng;
Liú Yǎn as Prince of Xiàpī;
Liú Chàng as Prince of Rǔnán;
Liú Bǐng as Prince of Chángshān;
and Liú Cháng as Prince of Jìyīn.
All men in the realm were granted noble ranks,
each raised by three grades.
Palace gentlemen and imperial attendants who had served for twenty years or more received one hundred rolls of silk;
those who had served for ten years or more received twenty rolls;
those who had served for less than ten years received ten rolls;
officials in government bureaus received five rolls;
secretaries and junior clerks received three rolls.
An order was issued for a grand five-day celebration throughout the realm.
On the day Yǐ Sì,
a general amnesty was proclaimed throughout the realm;
those who plotted rebellion, committed high treason, and other unforgivable crimes
were all pardoned.
In the winter,
chariots and cavalry engaged in a hunt in the Shànglín Park.
In the twelfth month,
Fèngchē Dūwèi Dòu Gù and Fùmǎ Dūwèi Gěng Bǐng were sent to garrison Liángzhōu.
In the sixteenth year, spring, second month,
Tàipú Jì Róng was sent out through Gāoquē;
Fèngchē Dūwèi Dòu Gù through Jiǔquán;
Fùmǎ Dūwèi Gěng Bǐng through Jūyán;
and Qí Dūwèi Lái Miáo through Píngchéng,
to attack the Northern Xiōngnú.
Dòu Gù defeated King Hūyǎn at Tiānshān,
and left troops to garrison Yīwúlú City.
Gěng Bǐng, Lái Miáo, and Jì Róng all returned without achievement.
In the summer, fifth month,
Liú Yán, Prince of Huáiyáng, plotted rebellion,
which was discovered.
On the day Guǐ Chǒu,
Sītú Xíng Mù and Fùmǎ Dūwèi Hán Guāng were imprisoned and died due to their involvement in the affair.
Many others implicated were executed or died.
On the last day, Wù Wǔ,
there was a solar eclipse.
On the sixth month, day Bǐng Yín,
Dàsīnóng Wáng Mǐn of Xīhé was appointed Sītú.
In the autumn, seventh month,
Liú Yán, Prince of Huáiyáng, was relocated and enfeoffed as Prince of Fùlíng.
In the ninth month, on the day Dīng Mǎo,
an imperial edict ordered that prisoners awaiting execution for capital crimes in commanderies, kingdoms, and central government offices should have their sentences reduced by one degree from death,
without flogging.
They were to be sent to military camps
to garrison Shuòfāng and Dūnhuáng.
Their wives and children could follow them;
parents and siblings who wished to follow were allowed to do so freely;
married women
were not to go with them.
This decree did not apply to those who plotted rebellion, committed high treason, or acted without principle.
In this year,
the Northern Xiōngnú raided Yúnzhōng.
Lián Fàn, Administrator of Yúnzhōng, attacked and defeated them.
In the seventeenth year, spring, first month,
sweet dew descended upon Gānlíng.
Liú Mù, Prince of Běihǎi, died.
In the second month, on the day Yǐ Sì,
Sītú Wáng Mǐn died.
In the third month, on the day Guǐ Chǒu,
Bào Yù, Administrator of Rǔnán, was appointed Sītú.
That year,
sweet dew still descended,
tree branches attached themselves inward,
spirit ganoderma grew before the palace,
and five-colored divine sparrows soared and gathered in Jīngshī.
The various tribes of the southwest Yi, such as Āiláo, Dān'ěr, Jiāojiāo, Pánmù, Báiláng, and Dòngnián,
came one after another, admiring righteousness and offering tribute;
the various kingdoms of the Western Regions sent their sons to serve at court.
In the fifth month of summer, on the day of Wùzǐ,
the high ministers and all officials, believing in the Emperor's majestic virtue that embraced distant lands,
and the manifest auspicious signs,
all gathered in the court hall
and presented wine to offer longevity.
An edict stated:
"Heaven produces divine objects
to respond to the king;
distant people admire transformation,
truly because of virtue.
I, with my shallow and meager self,
how can I enjoy this?
Only by the sagely virtue bestowed by Gāozǔ and Guāngwǔ,
I dare not decline.
Therefore, respectfully raise the cups,
