In the eleventh month, on the *yǐchǒu* day,
Grand Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud Zhāng Pú became Grand Commandant.
That year,
the military in Wǔlíng Commandery suppressed the Shénqìng Mán people,
who then surrendered.
Colonel Protector of the Qiāng, Guàn Yǒu, attacked the Shāodāng Qiāng,
and the Qiāng then fled.
Ānguó, the Southern *Chányú*, rebelled.
Gǔdōuhóu Xǐ beheaded him.
In the sixth year, spring, first month,
barbarians from beyond the frontier of Yǒngchāng sent envoys and interpreters to present rhinoceroses and elephants.
On the *jǐmǎo* day,
Minister of Works Dīng Hóng passed away.
In the second month, on the *yǐwèi* day,
palace attendants were dispatched to distribute grain and provide loans to the poor in the Sānhé region and Yǎn, Jì, and Qīng Provinces.
Mǎ Guāng, Marquis of Xǔyáng, committed suicide.
On the *dīngwèi* day,
Minister of Works Liú Fāng became Minister of Works,
and Grand Master of Ceremonies Zhāng Fèn became Minister of Works.
In the third month, on the *gēngyín* day,
an edict stated that all commanderies and kingdoms through which displaced people passed should provide them with grain.
Those who engaged in trade were not to be charged rent or taxes.
Furthermore, those who wished to return to their homes at a low cost
were to be exempt from land rent and *gēngfù* for one year.
On the *bǐngyín* day,
an edict stated:
"I, though insignificant,
have inherited this great enterprise.
The *yīn* and *yáng* are out of harmony,
and floods and droughts are abnormal.
In the region of the Jì River,
there is famine and displacement,
yet I have not received loyal words or profound strategies
to rectify and save the situation.
Waking and sleeping, I sigh deeply,
and my heart is greatly distressed.
I believe that officials are not properly selected by their superiors,
and the common people are not at peace below.
Those in charge do not consider leniency and harmony,
but instead compete in harshness and severity,
investigating without urgency,
thereby hindering the people's affairs.
This is certainly not how one responds to the will of Heaven above
and benefits the myriad people below.
I seek loyal and good scholars
to assist me in my deficiencies.

Let the Three Ducal Ministers, the Zhong'èrqiānshí, the èrqiānshí, and the commandery administrators and chancellors within the imperial domain each recommend one worthy and upright person, capable of direct speech and strong remonstrance.
Let them illuminate the hermits,
uncover the hidden,
and send them to the Public Carriages.
I shall listen to all of them."
The Emperor then personally interviewed and tested them,
selecting and appointing *lánglì*.
In summer, fourth month,
the Qiāng people beyond the frontier of Shǔjùn, with their tribal leaders, sent envoys to pledge allegiance.
In the fifth month,
Shú, Prince of Chéngyáng, passed away.
Having no son,
the kingdom was abolished.
In the sixth month, on the *jǐyóu* day,
for the first time, a full day's *fúbì* (period of seclusion) was ordered.
In autumn, seventh month,
there was a drought in the capital.
An edict ordered that all convicts in the *Zhōngdūguān* have half their sentences remitted,
and those whose punishments were not yet completed
since the fifth month were all to be pardoned and released.
On the *dīngsì* day,
the Emperor visited Luòyáng Temple,
recorded prisoners,
and redressed wrongful cases.
The Prefect of Luòyáng was arrested, imprisoned, and punished.
The *Sīlì Xiàowèi* and *Hénán Yǐn* were both demoted.
Before he could return to the palace, there was a heavy rain.
Bān Chāo, Protector General of the Western Regions, thoroughly defeated Yānqí and Wèilí,
and beheaded their kings.
From then on, the Western Regions submitted,
with over fifty states presenting hostages.
Féng Hóu, a nephew of Southern *Chányú* Ānguó, led rebellious Hú and fled beyond the frontier.
In the ninth month, on the *guǐchǒu* day,
Dèng Hóng, Grand Master of Guanglu, was given the acting command of General of Chariots and Cavalry.
He was dispatched with Féng Zhù, Colonel of the Yueqi Cavalry, Zhū Huī, acting General Dùliáo, and Dù Chóng, Zhonglangjiang Overseeing the Xiongnu, to attack Féng Hóu.
In winter, eleventh month,
Rèn Shàng, Colonel Protector of the Wūhuán, led Wūhuán and Xiānbēi troops
and severely defeated Féng Hóu.
Féng Zhù sent troops to pursue and attack him.
They were again defeated.
An edict ordered Bóhǎi Commandery to be subordinate to Jì Province.
The Mán people in the Lóuzhōng area of Wǔlíng rebelled,
and the commandery forces suppressed them.
In the seventh year, spring, first month,
acting General of Chariots and Cavalry Dèng Hóng, General Dùliáo Zhū Huī, and Zhonglangjiang Dù Chóng were all imprisoned and died.
In summer, fourth month, on the *xīnhài* *shuò* (first day),
there was a solar eclipse.
The Emperor summoned the Three Ducal Ministers and other high officials to discuss gains and losses,
and ordered generals, grand masters, imperial censors, palace attendants, academicians, councillors, and *lángguān* to gather in the court,
each to present their sealed memorials.
An edict stated:
"When the sovereign is not enlightened,
his influence spreads poorly,
governance fails the people,
and punishment is seen from Heaven.
Deeply reflecting on all affairs,
the five teachings emphasize leniency.
Therefore, according to ancient regulations, through the recommendation of *xiàolián*,
such individuals were sought.
Let those in charge carefully select thirty *lángguān* who are broad-minded, resourceful, and capable of governing cities."
Afterward, all selected *láng* were sent out to serve as Prefects and Chancellors.
In the fifth month, on the *xīnmǎo* day,
the kingdom of Qiānchéng was changed to the kingdom of Lè'ān.
In the sixth month, on the *bǐngyín* day,
Dìng, Prince of Pèi, passed away.
In autumn, seventh month, on the *yǐsì* day,
the ground cracked in Yìyáng.
In the ninth month, on the *guǐmǎo* day,
there was an earthquake in the capital.
In the eighth year, second month, on the *jǐchǒu* day,
Consort Yīn was established as Empress.
All men in the empire were granted noble ranks,
two grades per person.
The *Sānlǎo*, *Xiàotì*, and *Lìtián* were granted three grades.
Commoners without names or ranks, and displaced people who wished to register, were granted one grade.
Widowers, widows, orphans, childless elderly, the seriously ill, and the poor who could not sustain themselves were given grain,
five *hú* per person.
In summer, fourth month, on the *guǐhài* day,
Dǎng, Prince of Lèchéng, passed away.
On the *jiǎzǐ* day,
an edict ordered the distribution of grain and loans to the poor in the four commanderies of Bìng Province.
In the fifth month,
Hénèi and Chénliú suffered from locusts.
The Right Wēnyúdú King of the Southern Xiōngnú rebelled
and raided the frontier.
In autumn, seventh month,
General Dùliáo Páng Fèn and Colonel Yuèqí Féng Zhù were dispatched to pursue and suppress him,
and they decapitated the Right Wēnyúdú King.
The King of the Rear Division of Jūshī rebelled
and attacked its Former King.
In the eighth month, on the day Xīnyǒu,
the zhòu wine was consumed.
An edict ordered that all those detained in the capital prisons of the commanderies and kingdoms for minor offenses, such as fighting or quarreling,
be sent to garrison Dunhuáng.
Those who committed high treason
were to be castrated (recruited into the silk chamber);
their women were to have their wombs removed (suffer uterine excision).
For those whose crimes ranged from death penalty down
to common criminals and fugitives, redemption through payment was accepted,
with varying amounts.
In the ninth month,
the capital suffered from locusts.
Many officials and commoners who presented memorials
attributed the blame to the relevant authorities.
An imperial edict stated:
"The anomaly of locusts
surely does not arise without cause.
Though myriad lands may be guilty,
the fault lies with Me alone.
Those who present memorials, however, exclusively blame those below,
which is not helpful to Me.
I am distressed and compassionate, waking and sleeping,
thinking how to avert these worries and calamities.
Of old, King Yán of Chǔ feared without calamity,
and King Chéng turned back a wind by going to the outskirts.
How can I rectify My shortcomings
and avert these disasters?
All officials and supervisors should diligently perform their duties;
inspectors and two-thousand-bushel officials should carefully judge penalties,
redress grievances and oppressions,
care for the poor and widows,
pity the orphaned and weak,
and reflect on the fault that leads to calamities and the rise of locusts."
On the day Gēngzǐ,
Guǎngyáng Commandery was re-established.
In winter, tenth month, on the day Yǐchǒu,
Wēi, the King of Běihǎi, committed suicide due to a crime.
In the twelfth month, on the day Xīnhài,
Xiàn, the King of Chén, passed away.
On the day Dīngsì,
the Xuānshì Hall in the Nángōng Palace caught fire.
In the ninth year, spring, first month,
barbarians from beyond the frontier of Yǒngchāng and the Shàn kingdom sent tribute through multiple interpreters.
In the third month, on the day Gēngchén,
Lǒngxī experienced an earthquake.
On the day Guǐsì,
Kāng, the King of Jìnán, passed away.
Wáng Lín, the Chief Clerk of the Western Regions, attacked the King of the Rear Division of Jūshī,
and decapitated him.
In summer, fourth month, on the day Dīngmǎo,
Xún, a son of Dǎng, the King of Lèchéng, was enfeoffed as King of Lèchéng.
In the sixth month,
there were locusts and drought.
On the day Wùchén,
an edict stated:
"This year's autumn crops have been damaged by locusts;
therefore, all taxes of rent, corvée, and fodder shall not be collected.
If there are losses,
they shall be deducted based on the actual damage.
Of the remainder that would normally be taxed, only half shall be collected.
Regarding the rich resources of mountains and forests,
and the fishing and harvesting in ponds and lakes,
these are for the sustenance of the common people
and no temporary taxes shall be collected."
In autumn, seventh month,
locusts flew over the capital.
In the eighth month,
the Xiānbēi raided Féirú.
Jì Cān, the Administrator of Liáodōng, was imprisoned and died.
In the intercalary month, on the day Xīnsì,
Empress Dowager Dòu passed away.
On the day Bǐngshēn,
Empress Zhāngdé was buried.
The Shāodāng Qiāng raided Lǒngxī,
killing its chief officials.
General Zhēngxī Liú Shàng and Colonel Yuèqí Zhào Shì were dispatched to suppress and defeat them.
In the ninth month, on the day Gēngshēn,
Sītú Liú Fāng was dismissed from office by decree
and committed suicide.
On the day Jiǎzǐ,
Lady Liáng, the imperial mother, was posthumously honored as Empress Dowager.
In winter, tenth month, on the day Yǐyǒu,
Empress Gōnghuái Liáng was reburied in the Western Mausoleum.
In the eleventh month, on the day Guǐmǎo,
Lǚ Gài of Hénán, the Grand Master of Ceremonies, became Sītú.
In the twelfth month, on the day Bǐngyín,
Sīkōng Zhāng Fèn was dismissed.
On the day Réngshēn,
Hán Léng, the Grand Coachman, became Sīkōng.
On the day Jǐchǒu,
the Ruòlú Prison office was re-established.
In the tenth year, spring, third month, on the day Rénxū,
an edict stated:
"Dikes, embankments, and canals
are intended to conform to geographical conditions
and facilitate the flow where there are obstructions.
Now, they are neglected and lax,
not regarded as a responsibility.
Inspectors and two-thousand-bushel officials should, as appropriate, dredge and guide the waterways.
Do not exploit this for arbitrary projects
that cause trouble and disturbance,
as this will result in public punishment."
In summer, fifth month,
the capital suffered a great flood.
In autumn, seventh month, on the day Jǐsì,
Sīkōng Hán Léng passed away.
In the eighth month, on the day Bǐngzǐ,
Náo Kān of Tàishān, the Grand Usher, became Sīkōng.
In the ninth month, on the day Gēngxū,
the Lǐnxī office was re-established.
In winter, tenth month,
five provinces experienced heavy rainfall.
In the twelfth month,
Mítáng and other chieftains of the Shāodāng Qiāng led their tribesmen to the imperial court to offer tribute.
On the day Wùyín, Chàng, the King of Liáng, passed away.
In the eleventh year, spring, second month,
envoys were dispatched to inspect the commanderies and kingdoms,
providing grain and loans to those affected by disaster who could not sustain themselves.
They were allowed to fish and gather from mountains, forests, ponds, and lakes,
without paying temporary taxes.
On the day Bǐngwǔ,
an edict ordered that all capital prisoners in commanderies and kingdoms, as well as the aged, infirm, and young female prisoners, have half their sentences remitted.
Those whose remaining sentences were less than three months
were all to be freed and returned to their hometowns.
In summer, fourth month, on the day Bǐngyín,
there was a general amnesty throughout the empire.
On the day Jǐsì,
the Right Colonel office was re-established.
In autumn, seventh month, on the day Xīnmǎo,
an edict stated:
"Officials and commoners are exceeding their station,
lavishing on the dead and harming the living.
Therefore, old regulations stipulate systems of frugality.
Recently, noble relatives and close kin,
and all officials and supervisors,
have not been willing to follow them,
and the relevant authorities have not enforced them,
leading to increasing laxity.
Moreover, merchants and common people
sometimes forget the laws and prohibitions,
and curious, extravagant goods
are circulated and publicly traded.
Those in office who violate these rules
shall be corrected first.
For common people in the markets,
the constitutional principles shall merely be re-declared,
and no oppression should be added to the weak
under the guise of regulations."
In the twelfth year, spring, second month,
the Báiláng and Nièbó Yi, from beyond the frontier of Máoniú, led their tribesmen to pledge allegiance.
An edict ordered loans of seed grain to the people of the various disaster-stricken commanderies.
Aid was granted to the poor, widows, widowers, orphans, those without support,
and displaced people from commanderies and kingdoms,
allowing them to fish and gather from ponds and lakes
to supplement their vegetable food.
In the third month, on the day Bǐngshēn,
an edict stated:
"For consecutive years there has been a poor harvest,
and the common people are impoverished.
The capital saw no snow last winter,
and no soaking rain this spring.
The common folk are displaced,
struggling on the roads.
I am heartbroken and distressed,
knowing not how to help.
'Looking up to great Heaven,
what guilt do the people of today bear?'
The Sān Gōng are my closest confidants,
yet they have not found a policy to conform to Heaven and bring peace to the people.
Repeatedly I have instructed the officials concerned,
to diligently select good administrators.
Yet even now, they have not changed;
instead, they compete to be harsh and cruel,
oppressing the common folk
to seek empty fame,
delegating authority to subordinates,
who use their power to commit evil.
Thus, orders are issued, but wickedness arises;
prohibitions are enacted, but deceit emerges.
They cunningly interpret laws and analyze statutes,
embellishing texts and adding words.
Bribes are exchanged through speech,
and crimes are committed by hand.
I am deeply troubled by this.
If the Gōng Qīng do not consider helping me to clarify what is good and evil,
how can they rescue them from their transgressions and punishments?
Once transgressions and punishments arrive,
they again cause disasters to befall the common people.
If those above and below are of one mind,
perhaps there can be recovery.
Therefore, bestow noble ranks upon all men in the realm,
two grades each;
Sān Lǎo, Xiàotì, and Lìtián three grades;
and common people without official registration, as well as displaced people who wish to register, one grade each.
Widowers, widows, orphans, childless elderly, the severely ill, and the poor who cannot support themselves shall be given grain,
three hú per person."
On the day Rénzǐ,
cloth was bestowed upon the Dóushì Yuán Dìzǐ studying at the Tàixué,
three pǐ each.
In the summer, fourth month,
the Mán Yí of Xiànglín in Rìnán rebelled.
The commandery troops attacked and defeated them.
In the intercalary month,
grain was lent to the impoverished common people of Dūnhuáng, Zhāngyè, and Wǔyuán.
On the day Wùchén,
grain was provided to those affected by a mountain collapse in Guī.
In the sixth month,
Wǔyáng experienced a great flood.
Grain was bestowed upon the particularly poor victims of the flood,
three hú per person.
In the autumn, seventh month, on the day Xīnhài, the first day of the month,
there was a solar eclipse.
On the ninth month, on the day Wùwǔ,
Tàiwèi Zhāng Pú was dismissed.
On the day Bǐngyín,
Dàsīnóng Zhāng Yǔ became Tàiwèi.
In the winter, eleventh month,
the two states of Méngqí and Dōulè from the Western Regions sent envoys to pledge allegiance.
Their kings were bestowed with gold seals and purple sashes.
In this year,
the Shāodāng Qiāng rebelled again.
In the thirteenth year, spring, first month, on the day Dīngchǒu,
the Emperor visited Dōngguān,
browsed the library,
and reviewed scrolls and books.
He broadly selected men skilled in arts and crafts to fill official positions.
In the second month,
Rènchéng Wáng Fèn died.
On the day Bǐngwǔ,
provisions and loans were made to the poor people of Zhāngyè, Jūyán, Shuòfāng, and Rìnán, as well as orphans, widows, and the weak and frail who could not support themselves.
In the autumn, eighth month,
an edict commanded that the people of Xiànglín who had lost their agricultural livelihoods
be provided with seeds and grain,
and the very poor be given rations of grain.
On the day Jǐhài,
the gates and pavilions of the Běigōng's lavish banquet hall caught fire.
Hùqiāng Xiàowèi Zhōu Wěi attacked the Shāodāng Qiāng
and defeated them.
Jīngzhōu experienced heavy rainfall.
In the ninth month, on the day Rénzǐ,
an edict stated:
"Jīngzhōu has suffered from irregular weather in recent years,
and this year, excessive rain has caused harm.
Although other areas had a somewhat good harvest,
many were unevenly affected.
Deeply considering that agriculture is the foundation of the livelihood of the four classes of people,
I feel a profound pity.
Therefore, order that half of this year's land tax and fodder tribute be remitted throughout the realm;
for those cases where actual reductions are appropriate,
follow previous precedents.
Poor people who received loans of seeds and food
shall not have these collected back."
In the winter, eleventh month,
the state of Ānxī sent envoys to present lions and large birds from Tiáozhī.
On the day Bǐngchén,
an edict stated:
"The households and population of Yōu, Jì, and Liángzhōu are generally small,
and border duties are numerous and arduous.
For upright and capable officials,
the path to advancement is narrow.
In interacting with the Yídí,
people are the foundation.
Therefore, order that along the border, commanderies with a population of 100,000 or more shall recommend one Xiàolián annually;
those with less than 100,000 shall recommend one every two years;
and those with 50,000 or less shall recommend one every three years."
The Xiānbēi raided Yòuběipíng,
then entered Yúyáng.
The Prefect of Yúyáng attacked and defeated them.
On the day Wùchén,
Sītú Lǚ Gài was dismissed.
In the twelfth month, on the day Dīngchǒu,
Guānglùxūn Lǔ Gōng became Sītú.
On the day Xīnmǎo,
the Wū Mán rebelled
and raided Nánjùn.
In the fourteenth year, spring, second month, on the day Yǐmǎo,
Dōnghǎi Wáng Zhèng died.
The old Xīhǎi Commandery was repaired,
and the Wèibù Dūwèi of Jīnchéng was moved to garrison it.
In the third month, on the day Wùchén,
the Emperor visited the Píyǒng,
hosted an archery feast,
and granted a general amnesty to the realm.
In the summer, fourth month,
envoys were dispatched to lead Jīngzhōu troops to attack the Wū Mán,
defeating and subjugating them.
On the day Gēngchén,
provisions and loans of grain were made to the poor displaced people of Zhāngyè, Jūyán, Dūnhuáng, Wǔyuán, Hànyáng, and Kuàijī,
with varying amounts.
In the fifth month, on the day Dīngwèi,
the office of Xiànglín Jiāngbīng Chángshǐ was first established.
In the sixth month, on the day Xīnmǎo,
Empress Yīn Shì was deposed,
and her father, Tèjìn Gāng, committed suicide.
In the autumn, seventh month, on the day Jiǎyín,
an edict ordered the remission of the Xiànglín County's renewed taxes, land tax, and fodder for two years.
On the day Rénzǐ,
Chángshān Wáng Cè died.
This autumn,
three zhōu experienced heavy rainfall.
In the winter, tenth month, on the day Jiǎshēn,
an edict stated:
"Yǎnzōu, Yùzhōu, and Jīngzhōu this year have suffered excessive rainfall,
which has greatly harmed agricultural work.
Therefore, for those affected by four-tenths or more, half of their land tax and fodder tribute shall be remitted;
for those less affected,
reductions shall be made according to the actual damage."
On the day Xīnmǎo,
Guìrén Dèng Shì was enthroned as Empress.
On the day Dīngyǒu,
Sīkōng Cháo Kān was dismissed.
In the eleventh month, on the day Guǐmǎo,
Dàsīnóng Xú Fáng became Sīkōng.
In this year,
the system of commanderies and states recommending officials for Láng Guān positions was reinstated for the first time.
In the fifteenth year, spring, intercalary month, on the day Yǐwèi,
an edict stated that displaced people who wished to return to their hometowns but lacked food
should be provided with actual provisions at the passes,
and the sick should be given additional medical care;
those who did not wish to return
should not be compelled.
In the second month,
an edict ordered provisions and loans for the poor people of Yǐngchuān, Rǔnán, Chénliú, Jiāngxià, Liángguó, and Dūnhuáng.
In the summer, fourth month, on the day Jiǎzǐ, the last day of the month,
there was a solar eclipse.
In the fifth month, on the day Wùyín,
Nányáng experienced strong winds.
In the sixth month,
an edict allowed common people, widowers, and widows to fish and gather from ponds and lakes
without paying taxes or fees for two years.
In the autumn, seventh month, on the day Bǐngyín,
Jìnán Wáng Cuò died.
The iron officialdom of Gù'ān, Zhuōjùn, was reinstated.
In the 9th month, on the day Rénwǔ,
he went on a southern inspection tour.
Qīnghé Wáng Qìng, Jìběi Wáng Shòu, and Héjiān Wáng Kāi all accompanied him.
He bestowed money and cloth upon officials from the Two-Thousand-Picul rank and below, Sānlǎo, palace attendants, and people aged one hundred years or more in the places he passed through,
each according to their rank.
In this autumn,
there was heavy rainfall in the four *zhōu*.
In the winter, 10th month, on the day Wùshēn,
he went to Zhānglíng
and offered sacrifices at his old residence.
On the day Guǐchǒu,
he offered sacrifices at the garden temple,
gathered the imperial clan at the old dwelling,
and bestowed rewards and had music performed.
On the day Wùwǔ,
he proceeded to Yúnmèng,
overlooked the Hànshuǐ River, and then returned.
In the 11th month, on the day Jiǎshēn,
the imperial carriage returned to the palace.
He bestowed money and cloth upon the accompanying ministers and those who remained, from the ranks of *gōngqīng* and below,
each according to their rank.
In the 12th month, on the day Gēngzǐ,
Lángxié Wáng Yǔ passed away.
The relevant officials submitted a memorial,
believing that at the summer solstice, a subtle *yīn* energy arises
and soft grasses die,
which can be used to decide minor affairs.
In this year,
for the first time, *jùn* and *guó* were ordered to review minor punishments at the winter solstice.
In the 16th year, spring, 1st month, on the day Jǐmǎo,
an imperial edict stated that poor people who owned fields but were unable to cultivate them due to destitution
should be lent seeds and grain.
In the 2nd month, on the day Jǐwèi,
an imperial edict stated that in the four *zhōu* of Yǎn, Yù, Xú, and Jì, there had been excessive rain in recent years, damaging crops,
and therefore the sale of alcohol was prohibited.
In the summer, 4th month,
he dispatched clerks from the Three Departments to travel separately through the four *zhōu*.
For poor people who had nothing with which to plow,
they were to be paid the cost of an ox for plowing.
In the 5th month, on the day Rénwǔ,
Zhào Wáng Shāng passed away.
In the autumn, 7th month,
there was a drought.
On the day Wùwǔ,
an imperial edict said:
"This autumn, as crops are just heading, there is a drought,
and clouds and rain do not moisten the land.
I suspect this is caused by officials acting cruelly and harshly,
not proclaiming benevolence and favor,
arbitrarily detaining the innocent,
and imprisoning the good.
Therefore, for all prisoners whose cases are doubtful under the law, do not decide them,
in accordance with the autumn regulations.
I will investigate officials who are troublesome and harsh,
and clearly show their punishment."
On the day Xīnyǒu,
Sītú Lǔ Gōng was dismissed.
On the day Gēngwǔ,
Guānglùxūn Zhāng Pú became Sītú.
On the day Xīnsì,
an imperial edict ordered all under Heaven to pay only half of this year's land tax and fodder;
those affected by disaster
should have their taxes truthfully remitted.
Poor people who received loans of seeds and grain, as well as land tax and fodder, should not be required to repay them.
In the 8th month, on the day Jǐyǒu,
Sītú Zhāng Pú passed away.
In the winter, 10th month, on the day Xīnmǎo,
Sīkōng Xú Fáng became Sītú,
and Dàhónglú Chén Chǒng became Sīkōng.
In the 11th month, on the day Jǐchǒu,
he journeyed to Gōushì,
ascended Báipí Shān,
and bestowed cloth upon the various officials and accompanying ministers,
each according to their rank.
The Northern Xiōngnú sent envoys to declare themselves vassals and present tribute.
In the 12th month,
the office of Dūwèi of the Western Part of Liáodōng was re-established.
Yuánxīng 1st year, spring, 1st month, on the day Wùwǔ,
he summoned *sānshǔ* clerks to be interviewed in the forbidden palace,
selected and appointed seventy-five people,
to fill positions as *yèzhě*, *zhǎng*, and *xiàng*.
The Gāogōulí raided the commandery borders.
In the summer, 4th month, on the day Gēngwǔ,
a general amnesty was declared throughout the empire,
and the era name was changed to Yuánxīng.
Members of the imperial clan who had been removed from the registry due to crimes
were all restored to the household register.
In the 5th month, on the day Guǐyǒu,
the land in Yōng cracked.
In the autumn, 9th month,
Liáodōng Tàishǒu Gěng Kuí attacked the Mò people,
and defeated them.
In the winter, 12th month, on the day Xīnwèi,
the Emperor passed away in the Qiándiàn of Zhāngdé Palace,
at the age of twenty-seven.
The imperial prince Lóng was established as Crown Prince.
All men in the empire were bestowed titles of nobility,
two ranks per person;
*sānlǎo*, filial and fraternal individuals, and industrious farmers, three ranks per person;
common people without official status and vagrants wishing to register, one rank per person;
widows, widowers, orphans, the childless, the infirm, and the poor who could not support themselves were given grain,
three *hú* per person.
Since the execution of Dòu Xiàn,
the Emperor personally managed all affairs of state.
Whenever there were disasters or anomalies,
he would consult *gōngqīng*,
who would speak frankly about successes and failures.
There were eighty-one auspicious omens before and after,
but he claimed his virtue was meager,
and suppressed them all, not allowing them to be publicized.
Previously, the Nánhǎi region offered longans and lychees.
A post station was set up every ten *lǐ*,
and a lookout every five *lǐ*.
Rushing through treacherous terrain,
the dead lay one after another on the road.
At that time, Táng Qiāng of Rǔnán, the magistrate of Línwǔ,
whose county bordered Nánhǎi,
submitted a memorial explaining the situation.
The Emperor issued an edict saying:
"Rare delicacies from distant lands
were originally offered to the ancestral temples.
If it causes harm,
how can it be in line with the fundamental principle of loving the people?
Order the Tàiguān not to accept such offerings again."
From this, the practice was subsequently abolished.
A commentary states: Since the Restoration and extending to Yǒngyuán,
although there were some aggressive expansions,
they all existed without disturbing the people.
Therefore, the common people increased yearly,
and the known territory expanded generation after generation.
When a detachment of troops was sent beyond the frontier,
the land north of the desert became empty;
when the Dūhù pointed west,
forty thousand interpreters were opened up.
Was it that their Way surpassed the Three Dynasties,
and their methods exceeded previous generations?
Or was it that the submission and rebellion, coming and going,
had their own predetermined cycles?
Emperor Xiàoshāng's personal name was Lóng,
he was the youngest son of Emperor Hé.
In Yuánxīng 1st year, 12th month, on the night of Xīnwèi,
he ascended the imperial throne,
being then just over one hundred days old.
He honored the Empress as Empress Dowager,
and the Empress Dowager oversaw court affairs.
The Northern Xiōngnú sent envoys to declare themselves vassals,
going to Dūnhuáng to present tribute.
Yánpíng 1st year, spring, 1st month, on the day Xīnmǎo,
Tàiwèi Zhāng Yǔ became Tàifù.
Sītú Xú Fáng became Tàiwèi,
participating in recording the affairs of the Shàngshū,
and all officials collectively listened to him.
The imperial elder brother Shèng was enfeoffed as Píngyuán Wáng.
On the day Guǐmǎo,
Guānglùxūn Liáng Wěi became Sītú.
In the 3rd month, on the day Jiǎshēn,
Emperor Xiàohé was buried in Shènlíng,
and his ancestral temple was honored as Mùzōng.
On the day Bǐngxū,
Qīnghé Wáng Qìng, Jìběi Wáng Shòu, Héjiān Wáng Kāi, and Chángshān Wáng Zhāng first went to their respective states.
In the summer, 4th month, on the day Gēngshēn,
an imperial edict abolished sacrificial officials not included in the sacrificial canon.
The Xiānbēi raided Yúyáng.
Yúyáng Tàishǒu Zhāng Xiǎn pursued and attacked them,
and died in battle.
On the day Bǐngyín,
Hǔbēn Zhōnglángjiàng Dèng Zhì was made Chējì Jiāngjūn.
Sīkōng Chén Chǒng passed away.
In the 5th month, on the day Xīnmǎo,
the Empress Dowager issued an edict saying:
"The Emperor is young and inexperienced,
inheriting a grand enterprise.
I will temporarily assist in administering the government,
with reverence and caution,
unsure of how to succeed.
I deeply reflect on the root of ultimate governance:
moral transformation comes first,
and punishment comes after.
I intend to observe the path of harmony,
widely bestow blessings and favors,
and make a fresh start with officials and people.
Therefore, a general amnesty is declared throughout the empire.
Since Jiànwǔ, all those who incurred prohibitions and imprisonment,
even though imperial edicts have granted release,
the relevant officials have been cautious
and often failed to implement them.
Let them all be restored to commoner status."
On the day Rénchén,
Yuán Shān in Hédōng collapsed.
In the 6th month, on the day Dīngwèi,
Tàicháng Yǐn Qín became Sīkōng.
Thirty-seven commanderies and kingdoms had heavy rainfall.
On the day *jǐwèi*,
an edict stated:
"Since summer,
the incessant rain has exceeded seasonal norms.
The *qì* is not effective,
and there will be misfortune.
Sleeping and waking, I am anxious and fearful,
not knowing the cause.
In ancient times, Xià Hóu Yǔ abhorred extravagant clothing
and simple food.
Confucius said, 'I have no fault to find with him.'
Now, having recently suffered great sorrow,
and with the seasonal *qì* not yet harmonious,
reducing banquets and curtailing clothing
might be of some benefit.
Therefore, reduce the quantity of precious dishes, luxurious, and difficult-to-make items for imperial use from the Tàiguān, Dǎoguān, Shàngfāng, and Nèishǔ."
On the day *dīngmǎo*,
an edict was issued to the Sītú, Dàsīnóng, and Chánglè Shàofǔ, saying:
"I, being without virtue,
assist in governing.
Working day and night,
I fear losing the true path.
I ponder the principles of governance,
moving from near to far,
and from inner to outer.
From the beginning of Jiànwǔ to the present,
more than eighty years have passed,
and the number of palace women has increased year by year,
with the imperial chambers ever expanding.
Furthermore, those from the imperial clan who were confiscated due to involvement in affairs,
though still bearing the name of the gōngzú,
are truly pitiable.
Now, all of them shall be dismissed and sent away,
as well as the palace women from the Yètíng,
all to become commoners,
to relieve their feelings of isolation and stagnation.
For all government offices, commanderies, kingdoms, and households of kings and marquises, slaves surnamed Liú, and the infirm and elderly,
their names shall be submitted,
ensuring all are truly accounted for."
In autumn, in the seventh month, on the day *gēngyín*,
an imperial order was given to the Sīlì Xiàowèi and the Bù Cìshǐ,
saying:
"Heaven sends down calamities
in response to governance.
Recently, some commanderies and kingdoms have suffered from floods,
damaging the autumn harvest.
The court feels the blame,
anxious, grieved, and fearful.
However, commanderies and kingdoms, desiring to achieve a reputation for abundance and prosperity through false pretenses,
conceal disasters,
exaggerate the area of cultivated land,
do not consider the displaced,
compete to increase household registrations,
hide bandits,
allowing evil deeds to go unpunished,
make inappropriate appointments,
and unsuitable selections,
being greedy, harsh, cruel, and poisonous,
extending to the common people.
The Cìshǐ, with bowed heads and stopped ears,
show favoritism and collude with inferiors,
‘not fearing Heaven,
nor feeling ashamed before others.’
The grace of temporary relief
cannot be relied upon repeatedly.
From now on,
their punishments will be investigated.
The Erqiānshí chief officials shall each truly investigate the damages caused
and exempt the land tax and fodder."
In the eighth month, on the day *xīnhài*,
the Emperor passed away.
On the day *guǐchǒu*,
the coffin was placed in the front hall of Chóngdé.
He was two years old.
A eulogy says: Xiàohé was profound and resolute,
following previous principles.
His imperial authority rose from within,
bestowing strong, firm commands.
He suppressed ominous signs
and manifested timely virtue.
Why was the reign of Shāngdì so short? Píngyuán could not succeed.
Annals of Emperor Xiào'ān, Part Five.
Gōngzōng, Emperor Xiào'ān, personal name Hù,
was a grandson of Sùzōng.
His father was Qīnghé Xiàowáng Qìng,
and his mother was Lady Zuǒ.
When the Emperor was still in his residence,
divine light often illuminated his room,
and a red snake coiled between his bed and mat.
At ten years old,
he loved studying historical texts,
and Emperor Hé praised him,
frequently seeing him in the forbidden palace.
In the first year of Yánpíng,
when Qìng first proceeded to his fief,
Empress Dowager Dèng specially decreed that the Emperor remain in the Qīnghé residence.
In the eighth month,
Shāngdì passed away.
The Empress Dowager and her brother, General of Chariots and Cavalry Dèng Zhì, settled the succession in the forbidden palace.
That night,
she dispatched Dèng Zhì, bearing the imperial staff,
to welcome the Emperor in a king's cyan-canopy carriage,
and he lodged in the palace hall.
The Imperial Empress Dowager presided at Chóngdé Hall.
All officials wore ceremonial attire,
and the assembled ministers took their places.
The Emperor was introduced and appointed Marquis of Cháng'ān.
The Imperial Empress Dowager issued an edict saying:
"The late Emperor possessed sagely virtue and outstanding character,
but
early departed this world.
I, serving the Emperor,
looked up to him day and night,
hoping for his success.
How could I expect him to suddenly fall and perish,
not completing his natural lifespan,
causing heartbreaking grief?
I considered that Píngyuán Wáng suffered from a chronic illness.
Mindful of the importance of the ancestral temples
and desiring to maintain the line of succession,
only the Marquis of Cháng'ān, Hù, possesses a loyal and filial nature,
is cautious and respectful,
can understand the *Shī Jīng* and *Lún Yǔ*,
is devoted to learning and fond of antiquity,
and is benevolent and loving towards his subordinates.
He is already thirteen years old,
and has the aspirations of an adult.
For connecting virtue and continuing the lineage,
none is more suitable than Hù.
The Rites state: 'The son of a younger brother is like one's own son';
the meaning of the Spring and Autumn Annals is that one who becomes the heir of another becomes their son,
and should not reject the grandfather's command based on the father's command.
Therefore, Hù shall be made the heir of Emperor Xiàohé,
to inherit and serve the ancestors,
and the appropriate rituals and ceremonies shall be submitted."
She then composed a mandate, stating:
"On the day *guǐchǒu* of the
first year of Yánpíng,
the Imperial Empress Dowager said: 'Hear, Marquis of Cháng'ān Hù: Emperor Xiàohé's magnificent virtue
shone brightly throughout the four seas;
the late Emperor did not live out his full natural lifespan.
I consider you, Marquis, to be the direct imperial grandson of Emperor Xiàozhāng,
humble, respectful, benevolent, and compliant,
diligent even in childhood.
It is fitting that you serve at the ancestral temples
and undertake the great task of succession.
Now, I appoint you, Marquis, as the heir to Emperor Xiàohé.
May you carefully govern the Hàn state,
sincerely hold fast to the middle path,
'If one man has joy, the ten thousand people will rely on him.'
Emperor, strive diligently!'"
After the mandate was read,
the Tàiwèi presented the imperial seal and ribbon,
and he immediately ascended the imperial throne,
being thirteen years old.
The Empress Dowager still presided over the court.
In the ninth month, on the day *gēngzǐ*,
he paid respects at Gāomiào.
On the day *xīnchǒu*,
he paid respects at Gūangwǔ Miào.
Six prefectures suffered major floods.
On the day *jǐwèi*,
envoys were dispatched to investigate conditions,
report on disasters,
and provide relief to the destitute.
On the day *bǐngyín*,
Emperor Xiàoshāng was buried at Kānglíng.
On the day *yǐhài*,
a meteorite fell in Chénliú.
Various Western Regions states rebelled,
attacking the Dūhù Rèn Shàng.
Vice Colonel Liáng Jǐn was dispatched to assist Rèn Shàng,
and defeated the rebels.
In winter, in the tenth month,
four prefectures experienced major floods,
and hail fell.
An edict was issued to provide relief to the poor
because the winter wheat had not been harvested.
In the twelfth month, on the day *jiǎzǐ*,
the King of Qīnghé passed away.
The Sīkōng was dispatched, bearing the imperial staff, to offer condolences and sacrifices,
and General of Chariots and Cavalry Dèng Zhì oversaw the funeral arrangements.
On the day *yǐyǒu*,
the *Yú Lóng Màn Yán* and other hundred entertainments were abolished.
In the first year of Yǒngchū, in spring, in the first month, on the day *guǐyǒu*, the first day of the month,
a general amnesty was proclaimed throughout the empire.
The Qiāng from beyond the borders of Shǔjùn surrendered.
On the day *wùyín*,
the southern part of Jiànwéi was divided to establish a Protector of the Subject People.
Grain was provided to the poor people in the Sīlì, Yǎn, Yù, Xú, Jì, and Bìng prefectures.
In the second month, on the day *bǐngwǔ*,
the hunting grounds of Guǎngchéng
and public lands in disaster-stricken commanderies and kingdoms were temporarily granted to the poor.
On the day *dīngmǎo*,
the kingdom of Qīnghé was divided, and the Emperor's younger brother Cháng Bǎo was enfeoffed as King of Guǎngchuān.
On the day *gēngwǔ*,
Sītú Liáng Wěi passed away.
In the third month, on the day Guǐyǒu,
there was a solar eclipse.
An imperial edict was issued to the gōngqīng, the various officials internal and external, and the zhōuguó shǒuxiàng,
to recommend Xiánliáng Fāngzhèng and those with daòshù,
who understood the art of government, were conversant with ancient and modern affairs, and could speak frankly and remonstrate strongly,
one person each.
On the day Jǐmǎo,
the Jiāojiǎo tribes from outside Yǒngchāng offered tribute and submitted.
On the day Jiǎshēn,
Qīnghé Xiàowáng was buried,
and granted lóngqí and hǔbēn.
In summer, in the fifth month, on the day Jiǎxū,
Lǔ Gōng, Commandant of the Chánglè Guard, became Sītú.
On the day Dīngchǒu,
an imperial edict enfeoffed Pǔ, grandson of Běihǎi Wáng Mù and Marquis of Shòuguāng, as Běihǎi Wáng.
The Yèláng Man-Yi from outside Jiǔzhēn offered their territory and submitted.
In the sixth month, on the day Wùshēn,
the Empress Dowager's mother, Lady Yīn, was enfeoffed as Xīnyě Jūn.
On the day Dīngsì,
the ground in Hédōng collapsed.
On the day Rénxū,
the Protector-General of the Western Regions was abolished.
The Xiānlíng Qiāng rebelled,
cut off the Lǒng Pass,
and greatly plundered.
Chēqí Jiāngjūn Dèng Zhì and Zhēngxī Xiàowèi Rèn Shàng were dispatched to suppress them.
On the day Dīngmǎo,
a general amnesty was granted, pardoning those Qiāng who had conspired and rebelled by linking up with each other.
In autumn, in the ninth month, on the day Gēngwǔ,
an imperial edict ordered the Sāngōng to clearly reiterate old regulations,
prohibiting extravagance
and the making of frivolous and ingenious items,
as well as the squandering of wealth on lavish burials.
On this day,
Tàiwèi Xú Fáng was dismissed.
On the day Xīnwèi,
Sīkōng Yǐn Qín was dismissed.
On the day Guǐyǒu,
rent rice from five commanderies in Yángzhōu was allocated
to supply Dōngjùn, Jìyīn, Chénliú, Liángguó, Xiàpí, and Shānyáng.
On the day Dīngchǒu,
an imperial edict stated:
"From now on, if a zhǎnglì is subjected to an audit and the report is not yet issued,
and they leave their post without cause, except for the mourning of parents,
they will not be considered for promotion until ten years have passed for a severe county, or five years for an ordinary county.
Only then may they be considered next."
On the day Rénwǔ,
an imperial edict ordered the Tàipú and Shàofǔ to reduce the Huángmén drum and wind ensembles,
to replenish the Yǔlín troops;
stabled horses not regularly used by the emperor's carriage
were all to be fed half rations;
all constructions
not for the use of ancestral temples and imperial tombs
were all to be halted for the time being.
On the day Bǐngxū,
an imperial edict established different rates for redemption of crimes from capital punishment downwards and for fugitives.
There were varying scales.
On the day Gēngyín,
Tàifù Zhāng Yǔ became Tàiwèi,
Tàicháng Zhōu Zhāng became Sīkōng.
In winter, in the tenth month,
the Wō kingdom sent envoys to offer tribute.
On the day Xīnyǒu,
a large volume of spring water emerged from Xīnchéng Mountain.
In the eleventh month, on the day Dīnghài,
Sīkōng Zhōu Zhāng secretly plotted to depose and enthrone,
was dismissed by edict,
and committed suicide.
On the day Wùzǐ,
an imperial order was issued to the Sīlì Xiàowèi and the Cìshǐ of Jì and Bìng provinces:
"The people are spreading rumors and frightening each other,
abandoning their old homes,
the old and weak carrying each other,
suffering on the roads.
Each of you should instruct the zhǎnglì under your command
to personally explain and comfort them.
If they wish to return to their original commandery,
issue sealed long dispatches at their location;
if they do not wish to,
do not force them."
In the twelfth month, on the day Yǐmǎo,
Yǐngchuān Tàishǒu Zhāng Mǐn became Sīkōng.
In this year,
eighteen commanderies and kingdoms experienced earthquakes;
forty-one had heavy rainfall,
or sudden mountain floods;
twenty-eight had strong winds
and hail.
In the second year, in spring, in the first month,
grain was supplied to the poor people of Hénán, Xiàpí, Dōnglái, and Hénèi.
Chēqí Jiāngjūn Dèng Zhì was defeated by the Zhǒng Qiāng west of Jì.
In the second month, on the day Yǐchǒu,
Guānglù Dàfū Fán Zhǔn and Lǚ Cāng were dispatched to tour Jì and Yǎn provinces separately,
to provide grain and loans to the displaced people.
In summer, on the day Gēngxū,
there was a fire in the city of Hànyáng,
burning and killing three thousand five hundred and seventy people.
In the fifth month,
there was a drought.
On the day Bǐngyín,
the Empress Dowager visited Luòyáng Temple and Ruòlú Prison,
reviewed the prisoners,
and granted various rewards to the Hénán Yǐn, Tíngwèi, Qīng, and their subordinate officials;
rain fell that very day.
In the sixth month,
the capital and the commanderies and kingdoms experienced large floods,
strong winds,
and hail.
In autumn, in the seventh month, on the day Wùchén,
an imperial edict stated:
"In ancient times, emperors,
who governed the people under Heaven,
all relied on the xuánjī yùhéng [celestial sphere and jade transverse tube]
to regulate the seven luminaries.
I, being without virtue,
have upheld this great enterprise,
yet yin and yang are out of balance,
and various calamities appear together;
the myriad people are starving and displaced,
and the Qiāng and Mò are rebellious.
Day and night I have constrained myself,
my heart full of worry.
Recently I ordered the gōngqīng and commanderies to recommend Xiánliáng Fāngzhèng,
seeking widely and selecting broadly,
opening the path for plain speaking,
hoping to obtain excellent counsel
to remedy my shortcomings.
However, those who responded all followed superficial talk,
without any distinct and remarkable insights.
Therefore, all officials, and the officials and people of the commanderies,
who possess daòshù, are clear about disasters, anomalies, the degrees of yin and yang, and the numbers of the xuánjī,
each should point out the changes and report them.
The èrqiānshí zhǎnglì should clearly convey this imperial edict,
broadly extending it to the obscure and hidden.
I will personally examine them,
and treat them without regard to rank,
hoping to obtain excellent counsel
to respond to the warnings from Heaven."
In the intercalary month, on the day Xīnchǒu,
Guǎngchuān Wáng Chángbǎo died,
having no son,
the kingdom was abolished.
On the day Guǐwèi,
the Qiāng from outside Shǔjùn offered their territory and submitted.
In the ninth month, on the day Gēngzǐ,
an imperial edict ordered that officials of kingdoms and principalities, from those with black seals down to lányá and yèzhě,
who were proficient in the classics and served as Bóshì,
and had a reputation for integrity, purity, filial piety, and fraternal duty in their hometowns,
and whose talents qualified them to govern people,
should have their names submitted annually by the guóxiàng
along with the annual reports to the Shàngshū.
The public bureaus would openly evaluate them,
allowing them to be appointed to external posts.
In winter, in the tenth month, on the day Gēngyín,
grain was supplied to the poor people of Jìyīn, Shānyáng, and Xuántú.
Zhēngxī Xiàowèi Rèn Shàng fought the Xiānlíng Qiāng at Píngxiāng,
and Shàng's army was defeated.
In the eleventh month, on the day Xīnyǒu,
Dèng Zhì was appointed Dàjiāngjūn,
recalled to the capital,
while Rèn Shàng remained stationed in Lǒngyòu.
The Xiānlíng Qiāng Diān Líng proclaimed himself Tiānzǐ in Běidì,
and then plundered the Sānfǔ,
attacked Zhào and Wèi to the east,
and entered Yìzhōu to the south,
killing Hànzhōng Tàishǒu Dǒng Bǐng.
In the twelfth month, on the day Xīnmǎo,
grain was supplied to the poor people of Dōngjùn, Jùlù, Guǎngyáng, Āndìng, Dìngxiāng, and Pèiguó.
The Cānláng Qiāng from outside Guǎnghàn submitted,
and the northern part of Guǎnghàn was divided to form a Shǔguó Dūwèi.
In this year,
twelve commanderies and kingdoms experienced earthquakes.
In the third year, in spring, in the first month, on the day Gēngzǐ,
the Emperor came of age and received the ceremonial cap.
A general amnesty was granted to the empire.
Kings, princesses, noble ladies, dukes, gōngqīng, and others were granted gold and silk, each according to their rank;
men who were successors to their fathers,
and Sānlǎo, Xiàotì, and Lìtián were granted noble ranks,
two grades each,
and displaced people who wished to register were granted one grade each.
Qí Dūwèi Rèn Rén was dispatched to suppress the Xiānlíng Qiāng,
but was unsuccessful,
and the Qiāng then attacked and captured Líntáo.
Gāogōulí sent envoys to offer tribute.
In the third month,
the capital suffered a great famine,
and people ate each other.
On the day *Rénchén*,
the *Gōngqīng* went to the palace gate to apologize.
An imperial edict stated:
"I, being young and immature,
received this great enterprise,
but have been unable to promote and spread virtuous governance,
and instead have caused a disharmony of *yīn* and *yáng*,
leading to the present famine among the common people,
where they consume one another.
I am filled with sorrow and lamentation,
as if fallen into an abyss.
The fault lies with me,
not with the various officials;
yet you have demeaned yourselves excessively,
further demonstrating the court's lack of virtue.
You should earnestly endeavor to consider changes and reforms
to assist in my inadequacy."
On the day *Guǐsì*,
an imperial edict granted Hóngchí pond to the poor.
On the day *Rényín*,
the *Sītú*, Lǔ Gōng, was dismissed.
In summer, fourth month, on the day *Bǐngyín*,
the *Dàhónglú*, Xià Qín of Jiǔjiāng, became *Sītú*.
The Three Dukes, seeing that national resources were insufficient,
memorialized to allow officials and commoners to contribute money and grain,
thereby acquiring titles such as *Guānnèi Hóu*, *Hǔbēn Yǔlín Láng*, *Wǔ Dàfū*, official scribes, *tíqí*, and camp soldiers, each according to specific ranks.
On the day *Jǐsì*,
an imperial edict declared that the arable parts of the Shànglín and Guǎngchéng Parks
should be distributed to the poor.
On the day *Jiǎshēn*,
Qīnghé Wáng, Hǔwēi, died.
In the fifth month, on the day *Bǐngshēn*,
Yánpíng, son of the Prince of Lè'ān, Chǒng, was enfeoffed as Qīnghé Wáng.
On the day *Dīngyǒu*,
Pèi Wáng, Zhèng, died.
On the day *Guǐchǒu*,
there was a great wind in the capital.
In the sixth month,
the Wūhuán raided Dàijùn, Shànggǔ, and Zhuójùn.
In autumn, seventh month,
the sea bandit Zhāng Bólù and others plundered nine coastal commanderies.
The Imperial Censor Páng Xióng was dispatched to supervise troops and defeat them.
On the day *Gēngzǐ*,
an imperial edict commanded local officials to inspect their jurisdictions
and ensure all planted late-season wheat and vegetables,
making full use of the land's potential.
The poor were to be provided with seeds and provisions.
In the ninth month,
the Wūhuán of Yànmén and the Xiānbēi rebelled,
defeating the Wǔyuán commandery troops at Gāoqú Gǔ.
In winter, tenth month,
the Southern *Chányú* rebelled
and besieged the Commander of the Gentlemen-of-the-Household, Gěng Zhǒng, at Měijì.
In the eleventh month,
the acting General of Chariots and Cavalry, Hé Xī, was dispatched to suppress them.
In the twelfth month, on the day *Xīnyǒu*,
nine commanderies and kingdoms experienced earthquakes.
On the day *Yǐhài*,
a comet appeared in Tiānyuàn.
This year,
the capital and forty-one commanderies and kingdoms had rain and hail.
Bìng and Liáng provinces suffered a great famine,
and people ate each other.
In the fourth year, spring, first month, on the first day of the month,
the assembly was held,
but music was removed,
and the court was not filled with ceremonial carriages.
On the day *Xīnmǎo*,
an imperial edict stated that as the Three Commanderies had recently suffered from banditry and chaos,
and the populace was displaced,
three years of outstanding taxes, *guògēng*, *kǒusuàn*, and fodder were remitted;
provisions were given to the poor of Shàngjùn, each according to a specified amount.
The sea bandit Zhāng Bólù, along with the major bandits Liú Wénhé and Zhōu Wénguāng from Bóhǎi and Píngyuán, again attacked Yàncì,
killing the county magistrate.
The Imperial Household Grandee Wáng Zōng was dispatched to supervise the Inspector of Qīngzhōu, Fǎ Xióng, to suppress and defeat them.
The General Overseeing the Borders, Liáng Jǐn, and the Administrator of Liáodōng, Gěng Kuí, suppressed and defeated the Southern *Chányú* at the old city of the Dependent State.
On the day *Bǐngwǔ*,
an imperial edict ordered a reduction in the salaries of all officials, and those of the provinces and commanderies, each according to a specific scale.
In the second month, on the day *Dīngsì*,
provisions were given to the poor of Jiǔjiāng.
The Southern Xiōngnú raided Chángshān.
On the day *Yǐchǒu*,
the offices of Capital Commandant for Cháng'ān and Yōng were first established.
On the day *Yǐhài*,
an imperial edict stated that since the *Jiànchū* era,
all those who had been exiled to the borders for "ominous rumors" or other offenses
should return to their native commanderies;
those who had been confiscated by the state as slaves
were to be freed as commoners.
An imperial edict ordered the Palace Attendant Liú Zhēn and the Academicians of the Five Classics
to collate and correct the Five Classics, various philosophical works, biographies, and treatises of the Hundred Schools of Arts at the Dōngguān,
to standardize omissions and correct the text.
In the third month,
the Southern *Chányú* surrendered.
The Xiānlíng Qiāng raided Bāozhōng,
and the Administrator of Hànzhōng, Zhèng Qín, died in battle.
The Jīnchéng Commandery capital was moved to Xiāngwǔ.
On the day *Wùzǐ*,
the Dùlíng Park caught fire.
On the day *Guǐsì*,
nine commanderies and kingdoms experienced earthquakes.
In summer, fourth month,
six provinces suffered from locusts.
On the day *Dīngchǒu*,
a general amnesty was proclaimed throughout the empire.
In autumn, seventh month, on the day *Yǐyǒu*,
three commanderies suffered great floods.
On the day *Jǐmǎo*,
the Cavalry Commandant, Rèn Rén, was imprisoned and died.
In the ninth month, on the day *Jiǎshēn*,
Yìzhōujùn suffered an earthquake.
In winter, tenth month, on the day *Jiǎxū*,
the Lady of Xīnyě, Yīn Shì, died.
The *Sīkōng* was sent with a *jí* (credentials) to oversee the funeral arrangements.
The Grand General Dèng Zhì was dismissed.
In the fifth year, spring, first month, on the day *Gēngchén*, which was the first day of the month,
there was a solar eclipse.
On the day *Bǐngxū*,
ten commanderies and kingdoms experienced earthquakes.
On the day *Jǐchǒu*,
the Grand Commandant Zhāng Yǔ was dismissed.
On the day *Jiǎshēn*,
the Grand Master of Ceremonies Lǐ Xiū became Grand Commandant.
In the second month, on the day *Dīngmǎo*,
an imperial edict ordered the reduction of contributions of food for the Grand Provisioner from commanderies and kingdoms.
The Xiānlíng Qiāng raided Hédōng,
and then reached Hénèi.
In the third month,
an imperial edict ordered Lǒngxī to move to Xiāngwǔ,
Āndìng to Měiyáng,
Běidì to Chíyáng,
and Shàngjùn to Yá.
The Fúyú Yi violated the frontier,
killing and injuring officials and commoners.
In the intercalary month, on the day *Dīngyǒu*,
an amnesty was granted to the four commanderies of Héxī in Liángzhōu.
On the day *Wùxū*,
an imperial edict stated:
"I, being without virtue,
serve the ancestral temples and the altars,
and carry on this great enterprise,
but have been unable to promote harmony and bring down blessings,
or pray for good fortune for the people.
Disasters and anomalies arise in succession,
bandits and brigands roam freely,
barbarians disturb our land,
military affairs are unceasing,
the common people are impoverished,
and exhausted by levies and conscriptions.
Moreover, locusts have proliferated,
damaging the ripening wheat,
and the autumn harvest is just beginning,
which is extremely lamentable.
I, being unenlightened,
have mismanaged governance,
and have not yet found loyal and good men to assist in my deficient administration.
The *zhuàn* says: 'If one stumbles and is not helped,
or is in danger and not supported,
of what use then are his ministers?'
How will the *Gōngqīng* and *Dàfū* rectify and save this situation,
deliver us from this hardship and calamity,
and heed the warnings of Heaven?
Indeed, the foundation of governance
is nothing better than obtaining suitable men.
To commend the worthy and display the good
is what the sage system prioritizes.
'Numerous indeed are the gentlemen,
with whom Wén Wáng found peace.'
I seek loyal, upright, and honest ministers
to assist in my inadequacy.

Therefore, let the Three Dukes, Special Advanced Officials (*Tèjìn*), Marquises, Officials of Two Thousand *Dàn* (*Zhōng èr qiān dàn*), Officials of Two Thousand *Dàn* (*Èr qiān dàn*), Commandery Administrators (*Jùnshǒu*), and Chancellors to the Princes (*Zhūhóuxiàng*) each recommend one person who is贤良方正 (*xiánliáng fāngzhèng*, virtuous, upright, and righteous), possesses *dàoshù* (moral and administrative skills), is adept at governance and reform, and can speak frankly and remonstrate strongly,
as well as those who are supremely filial or stand out among the populace.
All are to be sent to the *Gōngchē* (State Carriages),
and I shall personally examine them."
In the sixth month, on the day *Jiǎchén*,
Lèchéng Wáng, Xún, died.
In autumn, seventh month, on the day *Jǐsì*,
an imperial edict commanded the Three Dukes, Special Advanced Officials, Nine Ministers (*Jiǔqīng*), and Colonels (*Xiàowèi*)
to recommend descendants of distinguished generals who are knowledgeable in battle formations and capable of serving as commanders.
In the ninth month,
Dù Qí and Wáng Xìn of Hànyáng rebelled,
and together with various Xiānlíng Qiāng tribes, they captured the city of Shàngguī.
In the twelfth month,
the Administrator of Hànyáng, Zhào Bó, sent an assassin to kill Dù Qí.
This year,
nine provinces suffered from locusts,
and eight commanderies and kingdoms had floods.
In the sixth year, spring, first month, on the day *Gēngshēn*,
an imperial edict ordered the establishment of the three parks, Chánglì, Gāowàng, and Shǐchāng, in Yuèsuí.
It also ordered Yìzhōujùn to establish the Wànsuì Park,
and Jiànwéi to establish the Hànpíng Park.
In the third month,
ten provinces suffered from locusts.
In summer, fourth month, on the day *Yǐchǒu*,
the *Sīkōng*, Zhāng Mǐn, was dismissed.
On the *jǐmǎo* day,
Liú Kǎi (劉愷), the Grand Minister of Ceremonies (Tàicháng), became Minister of Works (Sīkōng).
In the fifth month,
there was a drought.
On the *bǐngyín* day,
an imperial edict ordered all officials from the rank of Middle Two Thousand Piculs (Zhōng Èrqiānshí) down to the Yellow Sash (Huángshòu)
to have their ranks restored and their redemptions returned.
Nobility ranks were bestowed with varying differences.
On the *wùchén* day,
the Empress Dowager (Huáng Tàihòu) visited Luòyáng Sì (洛陽寺),
inspected prisoners,
and settled wrongful cases.
In the sixth month, on the *rénchén* day,
mountains collapsed in Yùzhāng (豫章), Yuánxī (員谿), and Yuánshān (原山).
On the *xīnsì* day,
a general amnesty was proclaimed throughout the empire.
A Supervising Imperial Secretary (Shìyùshǐ), Táng Xǐ (唐喜), was sent to suppress the bandit Wáng Xìn (王信) in Hànyáng (漢陽).
He defeated and executed him.
In winter, in the eleventh month, on the *xīnchǒu* day,
Wú Zhǐ (吳祉), the Protector of the Wūhuán (Hù Wūhuán Xiàowèi), was imprisoned and died.
This year,
Diān Líng (滇零), leader of the Xiānlíng Qiāng (先零羌), died,
and his son Líng Chāng (零昌) resumed the false title.
In the seventh year, spring, in the first month, on the *gēngxū* day,
the Empress Dowager, accompanied by ministers and their wives (mìngfù), paid respects at the ancestral temples (zōngmiào).
In the second month, on the *bǐngwǔ* day,
there were earthquakes in eighteen commanderies and kingdoms (jùn guó).
Summer, in the fourth month, on the *yǐwèi* day,
Shèng (勝), the King of Píngyuán (平原), passed away.
On the *bǐngshēn* day, the last day of the month,
there was a solar eclipse.
In the fifth month, on the *gēngzǐ* day,
the capital (Jīngshī) held a grand rainmaking ceremony (yú).
In autumn,
Hóu Bà (侯霸), the Protector of the Qiāng (Hù Qiāng Xiàowèi), and Mǎ Xián (馬賢), the Colonel of Cavalry (Jì Dūwèi), defeated the Xiānlíng Qiāng.
In the eighth month, on the *bǐngyín* day,
there was a great wind in the capital,
and locusts flew over Luòyáng (洛陽).
An edict bestowed nobility ranks upon the people.
If commanderies and kingdoms suffered locust damage to their crops by fifteen percent or more,
they were exempted from paying this year's land tax;
if less,
the reduction would be based on the actual damage.
In the ninth month,
rice taxes were levied from Línglíng (零陵), Guìyáng (桂陽), Dānyáng (丹陽), Yùzhāng (豫章), and Kuàijī (會稽)
to relieve the famine victims in Nányáng (南陽), Guǎnglíng (廣陵), Xiàpī (下邳), Péngchéng (彭城), Shānyáng (山陽), Lújiāng (廬江), and Jiǔjiāng (九江);
grain was also levied from riverside counties and transported to the Áocāng (敖倉) granary.
Yuánchū (元初) first year, spring, in the first month, on the *jiǎzǐ* day,
the reign title was changed to Yuánchū (元初).
Nobility ranks were bestowed upon the people,
two grades for commoners,
and three grades for those who were filial and fraternal (xiàotì) or diligent in farming (lìtián);
if the rank exceeded Gōngchéng (公乘),
it could be transferred to a son, a brother, or a brother's son;
for commoners without registered status and for vagrants (liúmín) wishing to register, one grade was bestowed;
widowers (guān), widows (guǎ), orphans (gū), the childless (dú), the seriously ill (dú), and the impoverished (pín) who could not support themselves were given grain,
three *hú* per person,
and chaste women were given silk,
one bolt per person.
In the second month, on the *jǐmǎo* day,
the earth cracked in Rìnán (日南).
In the third month, on the *guǐyǒu* day,
there was a solar eclipse.
Summer, in the fourth month, on the *dīngyǒu* day,
a general amnesty was proclaimed throughout the empire.
The capital, commanderies, and kingdoms suffered from five droughts and locusts.

An edict ordered the Three Excellencies (Sāngōng), Special Advance (Tèjìn), Marquis (Lièhóu), Middle Two Thousand Piculs (Zhōng Èrqiānshí), Two Thousand Piculs (Èrqiānshí), and Grand Administrators (Jùnshǒu) to each nominate
one person of integrity and straightforwardness.
In the fifth month,
the Xiānlíng Qiāng plundered Yōngchéng (雍城).
In the sixth month, on the *dīngsì* day,
the ground collapsed in Hédōng (河東).
Autumn, in the seventh month,
the barbarians (yí) of Shǔjùn (蜀郡) plundered Cánlíng (蠶陵)
and killed the county magistrate.
In the ninth month, on the *yǐchǒu* day,
Lǐ Xiū (李脩), the Grand Commandant (Tàiwèi), was dismissed.
The Xiānlíng Qiāng plundered Wǔdū (武都) and Hànzhōng (漢中),
blocking the Lǒngdào (隴道) road.
On the *xīnwèi* day,
Sīmǎ Bāo (司馬苞) of Shānyáng (山陽), the Grand Minister of Agriculture (Dà Sīnóng), became Grand Commandant.
Winter, in the tenth month, on the *wùzǐ* day, the first day of the month,
there was a solar eclipse.
The Xiānlíng Qiāng defeated Pí Yáng (皮陽), the Inspector of Liángzhōu (Liángzhōu Cìshǐ), at Dídao (狄道).
On the *yǐmǎo* day,
an edict exempted the Sānfǔ (三輔) region from three years of land tax, labor service (gēngfù), and poll tax (kǒusuàn).
In the eleventh month.
This year,
there were earthquakes in fifteen commanderies and kingdoms.
In the second year, spring, in the first month,
an edict ordered the distribution of grain to the vagrants and poor in Sānfǔ and the six commanderies of Liángzhōu (涼州).
The Qīngyī Dào (青衣道) barbarians of Shǔjùn offered tribute and submitted.
The branch channels of the Zhāngshuǐ (漳水) river, originally divided by Xīmén Bào (西門豹), were repaired
to irrigate the people's fields.
In the second month, on the *wùxū* day,
a Palace Attendant (Zhōng Yèzhě) was dispatched to collect and bury those who died as guests in the capital without family or whose coffins had decayed,
and offerings were made for all of them;
for those with families
who were too poor to afford a burial,
five thousand cash were granted per person.
On the *xīnyǒu* day,
an edict ordered Sānfǔ, Hénèi (河內), Hédōng (河東), Shàngdǎng (上黨), Zhàoguó (趙國), and Tàiyuán (太原) to each repair their old canals
and improve waterways
to irrigate public and private fields.
In the third month, on the *guǐhài* day,
there was a great wind in the capital.
The Xiānlíng Qiāng plundered Yìzhōu (益州),
and Zhōnglángjiàng Yǐn Jiù (中郎將尹就) was dispatched to suppress them.
Summer, in the fourth month, on the *bǐngwǔ* day,
Lady Yán (Yán Shì) was established as Empress (Huánghòu).
In the fifth month,
there was a drought in the capital,
and locusts in Hénán (河南) and nineteen commanderies and kingdoms.
On the *jiǎxū* day,
an edict stated:
"The imperial court is not enlightened,
and affairs of state are out of balance,
calamities and anomalies do not cease,
causing deep concern and dread.
It has been seven years
since the locust infestation began,
yet provinces and commanderies concealed the extent
and merely reported minor damages.
Now, swarms cover the sky,
causing widespread and far-reaching harm;
how can what is reported match what is seen?
The Three Excellencies (Sānsī) are responsible
for supervising both internally and externally,
yet they have neither reported nor corrected the situation.
Heavenly calamities are grave,
and deceit is a great crime.
Now it is mid-summer,
and we shall again grant loans
and observe what follows.
It is imperative to mitigate and relieve calamities
and bring peace to the common people."
In the sixth month, on the *bǐngxū* day,
Sīmǎ Bāo (司馬苞), the Grand Commandant, passed away.
The ground cracked in the new city of Luòyáng.
Autumn, in the seventh month, on the *xīnsì* day,
Mǎ Yīng (馬英) of Tàishān (太山), the Grand Coachman (Tàipú), became Grand Commandant.
In the eighth month,
the Xiānbēi (鮮卑) of Liáodōng (遼東) besieged Wúlǜ (無慮) county.
In the ninth month,
they also attacked Fūlíyíng (夫犂營)
and killed the county magistrate.
On the *rénwǔ* day, the last day of the month,
there was a solar eclipse.
Winter, in the tenth month,
Zhōnglángjiàng Rèn Shàng (任尚) was dispatched to garrison the Sānfǔ region.
An edict ordered that prisoners in commandery and kingdom prisons
have their death sentences reduced by one degree.
They were not to be flogged,
but sent to garrison Fēngyì (馮翊) and Fúfēng (扶風);
their wives and children were to follow them
and register their residence;
women were not to be transported.
Fugitives sentenced to death or lesser crimes were allowed to redeem themselves,
with varying differences.
For officials and commoners who gathered to become bandits
and showed remorse,
their crimes were pardoned.
On the *yǐwèi* day,

Zhòng Guāng (仲光), the Right Protector of Fúfēng (Yòu Fúfēng), Dù Huī (杜恢), the Grand Administrator of Āndìng (Āndìng Tàishǒu), and Gěng Pǔ (耿溥), the Commander of Tiger Teeth of Jīngzhào (Jīngzhào Hǔyá Dūwèi), fought the Xiānlíng Qiāng at Dīngxī Chéng (丁奚城).
Guāng and the others were utterly defeated
and all perished.
Sīmǎ Jūn (司馬鈞), the Left Protector of Fēngyì (Zuǒ Fēngyì), was imprisoned
and committed suicide.
In the eleventh month, on the *gēngshēn* day,
there were earthquakes in ten commanderies and kingdoms.
In the twelfth month,
the Man (Mán) people of Lǐzhōng (澧中) in Wǔlíng (武陵) rebelled,
and the provinces and commanderies attacked and defeated them.
On the *jǐyǒu* day,
Xià Qín (夏勤), the Grand Minister Over the Masses (Sītú), was dismissed.
On the *gēngxū* day,
Liú Kǎi (劉愷), the Minister of Works, became Grand Minister Over the Masses,
and Yuán Chǎng (袁敞), the Grand Master of Ceremonies (Guānglùxūn), became Minister of Works.
In the third year, spring, in the first month, on the *jiǎxū* day,
the old irrigation canals in Tàiyuán were repaired
to irrigate public and private fields.
An auspicious tree with interlocking branches was reported from Pínglù (平陸) in Dōngpíng (東平).
The Man and Yi (Mányí) people of Cāngwú (蒼梧), Yùlín (鬱林), and Hépǔ (合浦) rebelled.
In the second month,
a Supervising Imperial Secretary, Rèn Zhuó (任逴), was dispatched to supervise the provincial and commandery troops to suppress them.
There were earthquakes in ten commanderies and kingdoms.
In the third month, on the *xīnhài* day,
there was a solar eclipse.
On the *bǐngchén* day,
officials and commoners in Cāngwú, Yùlín, Hépǔ, and Nánhǎi (南海) who were forced by bandits were pardoned.
Summer, in the fourth month,
there was a drought in the capital.
In the fifth month,
the Wǔlíng Man rebelled again,
and the provinces and commanderies attacked and defeated them.
On the Guǐyǒu day,
Dùliáo Jiāngjūn Dèng Zūn (鄧遵) led the Southern Xiongnú (匈奴) to attack the Xiānlíng Qiāng (先零羌) at Língzhōu (靈州),
and defeated them.
The barbarians outside the borders of Yuèsuí (越巂) all brought their tribes and pledged allegiance.
In the sixth month,
Zhōnglángjiāng Rèn Shàng (任尚) dispatched troops and defeated the Xiānlíng Qiāng (先零羌) at Dīngxī Chéng (丁奚城).
In autumn, seventh month,
the Wǔlíng Mán (武陵蠻) rebelled again,
and the prefectures and commanderies pacified them.
The ground at Gōushì (緱氏) cracked.
In the ninth month, on the Xīnsì day,
Zhào Wáng Hóng (趙王宏) passed away.
In winter, eleventh month,
the Mán (蠻) barbarians of Cāngwú (蒼梧), Yùlín (鬱林), and Hépǔ (合浦) surrendered.
On the Bǐngxū day,
permission was first granted for high ministers, officials of 2,000 dàn, and Cìshǐ to observe three years of mourning.
On the Guǐmǎo day,
nine commanderies and kingdoms experienced earthquakes.
In the twelfth month, on the Dīngsì day,
Rèn Shàng (任尚) dispatched troops and defeated the Xiānlíng Qiāng (先零羌) in Běidì (北地).
In the fourth year, spring, second month, on the Yǐsì day, the first of the month,
there was a solar eclipse.
On the Yǐmǎo day,
a general amnesty was proclaimed throughout the empire.
On the Rénxū day,
the imperial armory caught fire.
In summer, fourth month, on the Wùshēn day,
Sīkōng Yuán Chǎng (袁敞) passed away.
On the Jǐsì day,
the Xiānbēi (鮮卑) raided Liáoxī (遼西),
and the Liáoxī (遼西) commandery troops and Wūhuán (烏桓) attacked and defeated them.
In the fifth month, on the Dīngchǒu day,
Tàicháng Lǐ Hé (李郃) was appointed Sīkōng.
In the sixth month, on the Wùchén day,
three commanderies experienced rain and hail.
In autumn, seventh month, on the Xīnchǒu day,
Chén Wáng Jūn (陳王鈞) passed away.
The capital and ten commanderies and kingdoms experienced floods.
An imperial edict stated:
"This year's autumn crops are flourishing and good,
almost ready for harvest,
but continuous rain has not ceased,
and it is feared they will certainly be damaged by submersion.
From dusk till dawn, I am filled with worry,
pondering the cause of this calamity.
Indeed, prolonged rain
is caused by the grievances of the people.
If military officials oppress the common people with their power and violence,
and civil officials arbitrarily impose harsh and severe measures,
and local officials commit wicked acts under the guise of public duty,
causing suffering and distress to the populace,
then the responsible authorities must clearly declare their punishments.
Furthermore, the monthly ordinance states: 'In mid-autumn, care for the elderly,
provide them with chairs and staffs,
and distribute gruel.'
At present, during the time of population registration and inspection,
many commanderies and counties do not adhere to this practice.
Even if there is gruel,
chaff and husks make up half of it;
the senior officials are negligent in their duties,
none personally attending to it,
which greatly violates the imperial decree's intent to care for the elderly.
They must diligently promote benevolence and forgiveness,
provide relief and protection to the widowed and solitary,
to accord with Our intention."
In the ninth month,
Hùqiāng Xiàowèi Rèn Shàng (任尚) sent an assassin to kill the rebellious Qiāng (羌) leader Líng Chāng (零昌).
In winter, eleventh month, on the Jǐmǎo day,
Péngchéng Wáng Gōng (彭城王恭) passed away.
In the twelfth month,
the barbarians of Yuèsuí (越巂) raided Suìjiǔ (遂久),
killing the county magistrate.
On the Jiǎzǐ day,
Rèn Shàng (任尚) and Qí Dūwèi Mǎ Xián (馬賢) fought the Xiānlíng Qiāng (先零羌) at Fùpíng Shànghé (富平上河),
and thoroughly defeated them.
The Qiánrén Qiāng (虔人羌) led their followers to surrender,
and Lǒngyòu (隴右) was pacified.
In this year,
thirteen commanderies and kingdoms experienced earthquakes.
In the fifth year, spring, first month,
the Yuèsuí (越巂) barbarians rebelled.
In the second month, on the Rénxū day,
Zhōngshān Wáng Xiàn (中山王憲) passed away.
In the third month,
the capital and five commanderies and kingdoms experienced drought,
and an imperial edict commanded grain distribution to the poor people affected by the drought.
In summer, sixth month,
Gāogōulí (高句驪) and Huì Mò (穢貊) raided Xuántú (玄菟).
In autumn, seventh month,
the Yuèsuí Mán (越巂蠻) barbarians and the Máoniú Háo (旄牛豪) rebelled,
killing the senior officials.
On the Bǐngzǐ day,
an imperial edict stated:
"The old regulations and systems
each have their classifications and categories,
intended to encourage the common people to prioritize frugality.
During the time of Yǒngchū (永初),
people were scattered and in distress,
the imperial court itself was humble and modest,
eliminating extravagance and ostentation,
eating no more than one dish per meal,
and wearing clothes of no more than two colors.
Although recent years have brought abundant harvests,
storage is still lacking,
yet the common people are thoughtless,
not planning for the long term;
for weddings and funerals,
they indulge in splendor and luxury,
to the extent that even common servants and slaves wear fine silk
and adorn themselves with pearls and jewels.
If the capital is already like this,
how can we set an example for the four directions?
We have established strict laws and prohibitions,
with earnest and clear instructions,
but the responsible authorities are negligent in their duties,
and have not implemented them.
As the autumn season has begun,
and fierce birds are about to be used (referring to the enforcement of laws),
We shall reiterate these commands,
to observe their subsequent effect."
In the eighth month, on the Bǐngshēn day, the first of the month,
there was a solar eclipse.
The Xiānbēi (鮮卑) raided Dàijùn (代郡),
killing the senior officials.
In winter, tenth month,
the Xiānbēi (鮮卑) raided Shànggǔ (上谷).
In the twelfth month, on the Dīngsì day,
Zhōnglángjiāng Rèn Shàng (任尚) committed a crime
and was executed in the marketplace.
In this year,
fourteen commanderies and kingdoms experienced earthquakes.
In the sixth year, spring, second month, on the Yǐsì day,
the capital and forty-two commanderies and kingdoms experienced earthquakes,
some with fissures,
and spring water gushed forth.
On the Rénzǐ day,
an imperial edict commanded the Three Excellencies to select five high-ranking subordinates each,
who were capable of benefiting and governing the people;
the Guānglù Xūn (光祿勳) and the Zhōnglángjiāng (中郎將) were to select fifty Xiàolián Láng (孝廉郎) who were broad-minded, resourceful,
and of high moral integrity,
to be appointed as magistrates, chiefs, assistant magistrates, and commandants.
On the Yǐmǎo day,
an imperial edict stated:
"Indeed, in governance,
the capital comes first,
then the various Chinese states.
The monthly ordinance for mid-spring states: 'Care for the young,
and provide for orphans,'
and for late spring: 'Bestow gifts upon the poor,
provide relief to the destitute,
reduce the labor of women,
and commend chaste women,'
which is to accord with the yang energy
and promote life and growth.
Therefore, grant grain to the particularly impoverished, orphaned, weak, and solitary individuals,
three hu for each person;
and ten hu to chaste women of integrity,
and commend their households,
making their virtuous conduct widely known."
In the third month, on the Gēngchén day,
the Six Zōng (六宗) were first established
and sacrificed to in the northwest of Luòchéng (洛城).
In summer, fourth month,
Kuàijī (會稽) experienced a great plague,
and a Guānglù Dàfū (光祿大夫) was dispatched with imperial physicians to inspect the sick,
grant coffins,
and abolish land tax and poll tax.
Pèiguó (沛國) and Bóhǎi (勃海) experienced strong winds
and hail.
In the fifth month,
the capital experienced drought.
In the sixth month, on the Dīngchǒu day,
Lèchéng Wáng Bīn (樂成王賓) passed away.
On the Bǐngxū day,
Píngyuán Wáng Dé (平原王得) passed away.
In autumn, seventh month,
the Xiānbēi (鮮卑) raided Mǎchéng (馬城),
and Dùliáo Jiāngjūn Dèng Zūn (鄧遵) led the Southern Chányú (單于) to attack and defeat them.
In the ninth month, on the Guǐsì day,
Chén Wáng Sǒng (陳王竦) passed away.
In the twelfth month, on the Wùwǔ day, the first of the month,
there was a total
solar eclipse.
Eight commanderies and kingdoms experienced earthquakes.
In this year,
the barbarians of Yǒngchāng (永昌) and Yìzhōu Shǔjùn (益州蜀郡) rebelled,
and with the Yuèsuí (越雟) barbarians, killed senior officials
and burned cities and towns.
Yìzhōu Cìshǐ Zhāng Qiáo (張喬) attacked and defeated them, causing them to surrender.
In Yǒngníng (永寧) first year, spring, first month, on the Jiǎchén day,
Rènchéng Wáng Ān (任城王安) passed away.
In the third month, on the Dīngyǒu day,
Jìběi Wáng Shòu (濟北王壽) passed away.
The King of Chēshī (車師) Later Kingdom rebelled,
killing the Bù Sīmǎ (部司馬).
The Shéndǐ Qiāng (沈氐羌) raided Zhāngyè (張掖).
In summer, the fourth month, on the day bǐngyín,
Imperial Prince Bǎo (保) was established as Crown Prince.
The reign title was changed to Yǒngníng (永寧).
There was a general amnesty throughout the empire.
Kings, princesses, the Three Ducal Ministers, and marquises down to palace attendants and subordinate officials were bestowed with gold and silk.
Furthermore, the common people were granted noble ranks and grain, each according to their station.
On the day jǐsì,
Chén Wáng (陳王) Xiàn’s (羨) son Chóng (崇) was re-enfeoffed as Chén Wáng.
Jǐběi Wáng (濟北王) Zhāng’s (萇) son Wú (毋) was made Lèchéng Wáng (樂成王).
Héjiān Wáng (河閒王) Yì’s (翼) son Yì (翼) was made Píngyuán Wáng (平原王).
On the day rénwǔ,
Lángxié Wáng (琅邪王) Shòu (壽) died.
In the sixth month,
the Shěndī Qiāng (沈氐羌) rebelled,
and plundered Zhāngyè (張掖).
The Protector of the Qiāng (護羌校尉), Mǎ Xián (馬賢), attacked the Shěndī Qiāng
and defeated them.
In autumn, the seventh month, on the day yǐyǒu, the first day of the month,
there was a solar eclipse.
In winter, the tenth month, on the day jǐsì,
Sīkōng (司空) Lǐ Hé (李郃) was dismissed.
On the day guǐyǒu,
Wèiwèi (衞尉) Lújiāng (廬江) Chén (陳) was made Sīkōng.
From the third month to this month,
the capital and thirty-three commanderies and kingdoms experienced severe gales
and heavy rainfall.
In the twelfth month,
the state of Dàn (撣國) from beyond the frontier of Yǒngchāng (永昌) sent envoys to offer tribute.
On the day wùchén,
Sītú (司徒) Liú Kǎi (劉愷) was dismissed.
The Xiānbēi (鮮卑) of Liáoxī (遼西) surrendered.
On the day guǐyǒu,
Tàicháng (太常) Yáng Zhèn (楊震) was made Sītú.
In this year,
twenty-three commanderies and kingdoms experienced earthquakes.
The king of Fúyú (夫餘) sent his son to the imperial court to offer tribute.
The Shāodāng Qiāng (燒當羌) rebelled.
In the first year of Jiànguāng (建光), spring, the first month,
the Inspector of Yōuzhōu (幽州刺史), Féng Huàn (馮煥), led the grand administrators of two commanderies to attack Gāogōulí (高句驪) and Huìmò (穢貊),
but was unsuccessful.
In the second month, on the day guǐhài,
there was a general amnesty throughout the empire.
Noble ladies in various imperial gardens,
kings, princesses, dukes, and ministers down to their subordinates were bestowed with money and cloth, each according to their station.
One son or younger brother of a duke, minister, commandant, or Secretariat Director was appointed as a Lang (郎) or Shèrén (舍人).
In the third month, on the day guǐsì,
Empress Dowager Dèng (鄧) passed away.
On the day bǐngwǔ,
Empress Héxī (和熹皇后) was buried.
On the day dīngwèi,
Lè'ān Wáng (樂安王) Chǒng (寵) died.
On the day wùshēn,
the deceased Imperial Father, Qīnghé Xiàowáng (清河孝王), was posthumously honored as Xiàodé Huáng (孝德皇),
and the Imperial Mother, Lady Zuǒ (左氏), as Xiàodé Huánghòu (孝德皇后).
The Imperial Grandmother, Noble Lady Sòng (宋貴人), was honored as Jìngyǐn Huánghòu (敬隱皇后).
In summer, the fourth month,
the Huìmò (穢貊) again, with the Xiānbēi (鮮卑), plundered Liáodōng (遼東).
