The Grand Administrator of Liáodōng, Cài Fěng (蔡諷), pursued and attacked them
and was killed in battle.
On the day bǐngchén,
Guǎngchuān (廣川) was merged with Qīnghé Guó (清河國).
On the day dīngsì,
Emperor Xiàodé’s (孝德皇) birth mother, Lady Gěng (耿氏), was honored as Gānlíng Dàguìrén (甘陵大貴人).
On the day jiǎzǐ,
Lèchéng Wáng (樂成王) Cháng (萇) was found guilty
and demoted to Línhú Hóu (臨湖侯).
On the day jǐsì,
dukes, ministers, Special Advance (特進), marquises, officials of two thousand *shi* (中二千石), officials of two thousand *shi*, and grand administrators and chancellors of commanderies and kingdoms
were ordered to recommend one worthy scholar each.
The widowed, lonely, orphaned, childless, and poor who could not support themselves were granted grain,
three *hu* (斛) per person.
On the day jiǎxū,
the Commandant of the Tributary State of Liáodōng (遼東屬國都尉), Páng Fèn (龐奮),
acting on a forged imperial edict, killed the Grand Administrator of Xuántú (玄菟), Yáo Guāng (姚光).
In the fifth month, on the day gēngchén,
Special Advance Dèng Zhì (鄧騭) and General Who Crosses the Liao (度遼將軍) Dèng Zūn (鄧遵)
both committed suicide due to calumny.
On the day bǐngshēn,
Píngyuán Wáng (平原王) Yì (翼) was demoted to Dūxiāng Hóu (都鄉侯).
In autumn, the seventh month, on the day jǐmǎo,
the reign title was changed to Jiànguāng (建光).
There was a general amnesty throughout the empire.
On the day rénzǐ,
Tàiwèi (太尉) Mǎ Yīng (馬英) died.
In the eighth month,
the Protector of the Qiāng (護羌校尉), Mǎ Xián (馬賢), attacked the Shāodāng Qiāng (燒當羌) in Jīnchéng (金城)
but was unsuccessful.
On the day jiǎzǐ,
former Sītú (司徒) Liú Kǎi (劉愷) was made Tàiwèi.
The Xiānbēi (鮮卑) plundered Jūyōng Guān (居庸關).
In the ninth month,
the Grand Administrator of Yúnzhōng (雲中), Chéng Yán (成嚴), attacked them
and was killed in battle.
The Xiānbēi besieged the Commandant of the Wūhuán (烏桓校尉) at Mǎchéng (馬城).
General Who Crosses the Liao (度遼將軍) Gěng Kuí (耿夔) rescued him.
On the day wùzǐ,
the emperor visited the residence of Wèiwèi (衞尉) Féng Shí (馮石).
This autumn,
the capital and twenty-nine commanderies and kingdoms experienced heavy rainfall.
In winter, the eleventh month, on the day jǐchǒu,
thirty-five commanderies and kingdoms experienced earthquakes,
some with fissures.
An edict ordered the Three Ducal Ministers and their subordinates
each to submit sealed memorials outlining gains and losses.
Grand Masters of Bright Radiance (光祿大夫) were dispatched to inspect,
and the deceased were granted money,
two thousand per person.
This year’s land tax was remitted.
Those severely affected by the disaster
were exempted from household taxes.
The Xiānbēi (鮮卑) plundered Xuántú (玄菟).
On the day gēngzǐ,
ministers of two thousand *shi* or higher were again permitted to observe three years of mourning.
On the day guǐmǎo,
an edict ordered the Three Ducal Ministers, Special Advance (特進), marquises, ministers, and commandants
each to recommend five martial and capable commanders.
On the day bǐngwǔ,
an edict ordered that in the capital and commanderies and kingdoms where crops were damaged by rain,
land tax should be reduced proportionally to the damaged area.
On the day jiǎzǐ,
troops were first stationed in Yúyáng (漁陽).
In winter, the twelfth month,
Gāogōulí (高句驪), Mǎhán (馬韓), and Huìmò (穢貊) besieged Xuántúchéng (玄菟城).
The king of Fúyú (夫餘) sent his son to join forces with the imperial army and provincial troops to attack and defeat them.
In the first year of Yánguāng (延光), spring, the second month,
the king of Fúyú (夫餘) sent his son with troops to rescue Xuántú (玄菟),
attacking Gāogōulí (高句驪), Mǎhán (馬韓), and Huìmò (穢貊),
and defeating them.
He then sent envoys to offer tribute.
In the third month, on the day bǐngwǔ,
the reign title was changed to Yánguāng (延光).
There was a general amnesty throughout the empire.
Those who had been relocated were allowed to return,
and their households and residences were restored to the registers.
The common people, and the three elders, filial and fraternal individuals, and diligent farmers were granted noble ranks,
two grades per person.
Additionally, the widowed, lonely, orphaned, childless, seriously ill, and poor who could not support themselves were granted grain,
three *hu* per person.
Chaste women were given silk,
two bolts per person.
In summer, the fourth month, on the day guǐwèi,
the capital and twenty-one commanderies and kingdoms experienced hail.
On the day guǐsì,
Sīkōng (司空) Chén (陳) was dismissed.
In the fifth month, on the day gēngxū,
Grandee of the Imperial Clan (宗正) Liú Shòu (劉授) of Péngchéng (彭城) was made Sīkōng.
On the day jǐsì,
Lèchéng Guó (樂成國) was changed to Ānpíng (安平),
and Héjiān Wáng (河閒王) Kāi’s (開) son Dé (得) was enfeoffed as Ānpíng Wáng (安平王).
In the sixth month,
commandery and kingdoms experienced locust plagues.
In autumn, the seventh month, on the day guǐmǎo,
the capital and thirteen commanderies and kingdoms experienced earthquakes.
Gāogōulí (高句驪) surrendered.
The Qiánrén Qiāng (虔人羌) rebelled,
attacking Gǔluóchéng (穀羅城).
General Who Crosses the Liao (度遼將軍) Gěng Kuí (耿夔) attacked and defeated them.
In the eighth month, on the day wùzǐ,
a fire broke out in the imperial tomb park (yuánqǐn 園寢) of Yánglíng (陽陵).
On the day xīnmǎo,
Jiǔzhēn (九真) reported a yellow dragon sighting in Wúgōng (無功).
On the day jǐhài,
an edict ordered the Three Ducal Ministers and officials of two thousand *shi*
to recommend inspectors (cìshǐ 刺史), officials of two thousand *shi*, magistrates (lìng 令), chiefs (zhǎng 長), and chancellors (xiàng 相)
who had served for one to ten years,
were upright, benevolent, and beneficial,
capable of disciplining themselves and leading their subordinates,
preventing corruption, and managing complex affairs,
and who had brought benefits to the people,
without being constrained by official records.
Inspectors were to recommend officials from their respective departments.
Grand administrators and chancellors of commanderies and kingdoms were to recommend officials holding black seals,
with careful consideration,
and not select the superficial.
In the ninth month, on the day jiǎxū,
twenty-seven commanderies and kingdoms experienced earthquakes.
In winter, the tenth month,
the Xiānbēi (鮮卑) plundered Yànmén (鴈門) and Dìngxiāng (定襄).
In the eleventh month,
the Xiānbēi plundered Tàiyuán (太原).
The chieftain of the Shāodāng Qiāng (燒當羌) surrendered.
In the twelfth month,
the barbarians beyond the frontier of Jiǔzhēn (九真) offered tribute and submitted.
In this year,
the capital and twenty-seven commanderies and kingdoms experienced heavy rainfall,
with strong winds
that caused deaths.
An edict granted money to those who died by crushing or drowning, aged seven or above,
two thousand per person.
For those whose houses were damaged or destroyed, or who lost grain and food,
grain was granted,
three *hu* per person.
Furthermore, for fields damaged by flooding,
all land tax was remitted.
If an entire family suffered disaster and only the young and weak survived,
the commanderies and counties were to provide for their care.
The Qiánrén Qiāng (虔人羌) attacked Gǔluóchéng (穀羅城).
General Who Crosses the Liao (度遼將軍) Gěng Kuí (耿夔) attacked and defeated them.
In the second year, in spring, the first month,
the Máoniú Yí rebelled,
raiding Língguān,
and killing the county magistrate.
The Inspector of Yìzhōu and Western Commandant of Shǔjùn attacked them.
An edict was issued to select one official from each of the three bureaus,
as well as one commoner, who could master the ancient script Shàngshū, Máoshī, and Gǔliáng Chūnqiū respectively.
On the day of Bǐngchén,
Hédōng and Yǐngchuān experienced strong winds.
In summer, the sixth month, on the day of Rénwǔ,
eleven commanderies and kingdoms experienced strong winds.
Jiǔzhēn reported that auspicious grain had grown.
On the day of Bǐngshēn,
Pǔ, the King of Běihǎi, died.
In autumn, the seventh month,
Dānyáng experienced a mountain collapse.
In the eighth month, on the day of Gēngwǔ,
an initial decree ordered that officials from the three bureaus who were proficient in classical studies and capable of governing the people,
after serving for three years or more,
were all eligible for recommendation and selection.
In the ninth month,
five commanderies and kingdoms experienced floods.
In winter, the tenth month, on the day of Xīnwèi,
Tàiwèi Liú Kǎi was dismissed.
On the day of Jiǎxū,
Sītú Yáng Zhèn became Tàiwèi,
and Guānglùxūn Liú Xī of Dōnglái became Sītú.
In the eleventh month, on the day of Jiǎchén,
a hunt was held in the Shànglín Park.
The Xiānbēi defeated the Southern Xiōngnú at Mánbó.
This year,
the Western Commandery of Shǔjùn was divided into a Dependent State Commandant's office.
The capital and three commanderies and kingdoms experienced earthquakes.
In the third year, in spring, the second month, on the day of Bǐngzǐ,
the emperor made an eastern tour.
On the day of Dīngchǒu,
the Grand Administrator of Chénliú was notified
to offer sacrifices to Nándùn Jūn and Emperor Guāngwǔ at Jìyáng,
and the land tax and fodder for Jìyáng were remitted for this year.
On the day of Gēngyín,
envoys were dispatched to offer sacrifices to Táng Yáo at Chéngyáng.
On the day of Wùzǐ,
Jìnán reported
that a phoenix had gathered on a tree in the residence of Huò Shōu, the county assistant magistrate of Táixiàn.
The Táizhǎng was granted fifty rolls of silk,
the assistant magistrate twenty rolls,
the commandant half that,
and each official and soldier three rolls.
The villages and districts where the phoenix passed
were exempted from this year's land tax.
Men were granted titles of nobility,
two ranks each.
On the day of Xīnmǎo,
the emperor went to Tài Shān,
and performed the 'chái' sacrifice to announce to Dài Zōng.
Wújì, the King of Qí, Yì, the King of Běihǎi, and Yán, the King of Lè'ān, came to court.
On the day of Rénchén,
ancestral sacrifices were offered to the Five Emperors at the Míngtáng in Wénshàng.
On the day of Guǐsì,
sacrifices were announced for the Two Ancestors and Six Zōng,
rewards were bestowed upon commanderies and counties,
and music was performed.
In the third month, on the day of Jiǎwǔ,
Chóng, the King of Chén, died.
On the day of Wùxū,
sacrifices were offered to Kǒngzǐ and his seventy-two disciples at Quèlǐ.
The Prime Minister, Magistrates, Assistant Magistrates, and Commandants of Lǔ, as well as Kǒng's relatives, women, and various scholars, all assembled.
Bows and silk were bestowed upon the Marquess of Bāochéng and others, each with varying amounts.
Upon returning,
the emperor visited Dōngpíng,
then arrived at Dōngjùn,
and passed through Wèijùn and Hénèi.
On the day of Rénxū,
the imperial carriage returned to the capital,
and visited the Grand Academy.
On this day,
Tàiwèi Yáng Zhèn was dismissed.
In summer, the fourth month, on the day of Yǐchǒu,
the imperial carriage entered the palace.
Offerings were made to the ancestors.
On the day of Rénxū,
Pèiguó reported that sweet dew had descended in Fēngxiàn.
On the day of Wùchén,
Guānglùxūn Féng Shí became Tàiwèi.
In the fifth month,
the Left Rìzhú King of the Southern Xiōngnú rebelled.
Mǎ Yì, the Colonel-Protector of the Xiōngnú, was dispatched to attack and defeat him.
The barbarian tribes beyond Rìnán's border submitted.
In the sixth month,
the Xiānbēi raided Xuántú.
On the day of Gēngwǔ,
Lángzhōng experienced a mountain collapse.
On the day of Xīnwèi,
Fúfēng reported that a white deer was seen in Yōng.
On the day of Xīnsì,
Imperial Censors were dispatched to inspect the disasters in Qīng and Jì provinces,
and to supervise the apprehension of bandits.
In autumn, the seventh month, on the day of Dīngyǒu,
the offices of the Right and Left Correction Magistrates were first restored.
The barbarian chieftains from beyond Rìnán's border came to the palace to offer tribute.
Féngyì reported that sweet dew had descended in Pínyáng and Yá.
Yǐngchuān reported that trees had grown with intertwined branches.
White deer and qílín were seen in Yángzhái.
The Xiānbēi raided Gāoliǔ.
Jiān, the King of Liáng, died.
In the eighth month, on the day of Xīnsì,
Dàhónglú Gěng Bǎo became Dàjiāngjūn.
On the day of Wùzǐ,
Yǐngchuān reported that one qílín and two white tigers were seen in Yángzhái.
In the ninth month, on the day of Dīngyǒu,
Crown Prince Bǎo was deposed and made King of Jìyīn.
On the day of Yǐsì,
an edict was issued for those condemned to death in the commanderies, kingdoms, and central offices to be commuted one degree,
to be sent to Dūnhuáng, Lǒngxī, and the Dùliáo camps;
those whose right foot or below were mutilated, and fugitives, were allowed to redeem themselves,
with varying rates.
On the day of Xīnhài,
Jìnán reported that a yellow dragon was seen in Lìchéng.
On the last day of the month, Gēngshēn,
there was a solar eclipse.
In winter, the tenth month,
the emperor journeyed to Cháng'ān.
On the day of Rénwǔ,
Xīnfēng reported that a phoenix had gathered at the western border post.
On the day of Dīnghài,
the governors, magistrates, and clerks of the three Fǔ were assembled in Cháng'ān,
and music was performed.
In the intercalary month, on the day of Yǐwèi,
sacrifices were offered at the High Temple,
followed by rituals at the eleven imperial tombs,
and a tour of Shànglín and Kūnmíng Lake.
Envoys were dispatched to offer sacrifices to the Grand Emperor at Wànnián,
and medium-grade sacrifices were offered to Xiāo Hé, Cáo Cān, and Huò Guāng.
In the eleventh month, on the day of Yǐchǒu,
the emperor returned from Cháng'ān.
In the twelfth month, on the day of Yǐwèi,
Lángxié reported that yellow dragons were seen in various counties.
This year,
the capital and twenty-three commanderies and kingdoms experienced earthquakes;
thirty-six experienced floods,
strong winds,
and hail.
In the fourth year, in spring, the first month, on the day of Rénwǔ,
Dōngjùn reported that two yellow dragons and one qílín were seen in Púyáng.
In the second month, on the day of Yǐhài,
Yǎn, the King of Xiàpī, died.
On the day of Jiǎchén,
the emperor made a southern tour.
In the third month, on the first day, Wùwǔ,
there was a solar eclipse.
On the day of Gēngshēn,
the emperor visited Wǎn,
where he fell ill.
On the day of Xīnyǒu,
Dàjiāngjūn Gěng Bǎo was ordered to act as Tàiwèi.
Sacrifices were offered at the Zhānglíng Garden Temple.
The Grand Administrators of Chángshā and Línglíng were notified
to offer sacrifices to Dìngwáng, Jiéhóu, and Yùlín Fǔjūn.
On the day of Yǐchǒu,
the emperor returned from Wǎn.
On the day of Dīngmǎo,
the emperor visited Yè,
and died in the imperial carriage,
at the age of thirty-two.
The death was kept secret,
and offerings and inquiries about his daily life were made as usual wherever he was.
On the day of Gēngwǔ,
the emperor's body returned to the palace.
On the evening of Xīnwèi,
the mourning was finally announced.
The empress was honored as the Empress Dowager.
The Empress Dowager entrusted her brother, Dàhónglú Yán Xiǎn, as Chējì Jiāngjūn,
and settled the succession in the forbidden palace,
installing Yī, the Marquess of Běixiāng, son of Shòu, the King Huì of Jìběi, and grandson of Emperor Zhāng.
On the day of Jiǎxū,
Xiāng, the King of Jìnán, died.
On the day of Yǐyǒu,
the Marquess of Běixiāng ascended the imperial throne.
In summer, the fourth month, on the day of Dīngyǒu,
Tàiwèi Féng Shí became Tàifù,
Sītú Liú Xī became Tàiwèi,
and the former Sīkōng Lǐ Hé, participating in recording state affairs, became Sītú.
On the day of Xīnmǎo,
Dàjiāngjūn Gěng Bǎo, Zhōngchángshì Fán Fēng, Shìzhōng Xiè Yùn, Zhōu Guǎng, and the wet nurse Yěwáng Jūn Wáng Shèng,
were accused of forming factions.
Fēng, Yùn, and Guǎng were imprisoned and died;
Bǎo committed suicide;
and Shèng was exiled to Yànmén.
On the day of Jǐyǒu,
Emperor Xiào'ān was buried at Gōnglíng.
His temple name was Gōngzōng.
In the sixth month, on the day of Yǐsì,
a general amnesty was proclaimed throughout the empire.
An edict stated that all places visited by the late emperor during his tours
were to have their land tax reduced by half for this year.
In autumn, seventh month,
Bān Yǒng, Administrator of the Western Regions,
attacked the Later King of Chēshī
and beheaded him.
On the day Bǐngwǔ,
Sù, King of Dōnghǎi, died.
In winter, tenth month, on the day Bǐngwǔ,
Mount Yuècuí collapsed.
On the day Xīnhài,
the Young Emperor died.
This winter,
the capital suffered a great plague.
A commentary states: Although Xiào'ān was revered and enjoyed the imperial throne,
power belonged to the Dèng clan.
Even though she reduced her own meals and attire,
she focused on the way of governance.
However, her orders originated from within the inner chambers,
and her authority did not reach far.
She began by losing control over the foundation,
which led to decay and ruin.
Consequently, she resorted to selling offices for gold,
allowing migrants to flee from bandits,
and shifting blame to the ministers
to respond to heavenly calamities.
Though she was called a wise woman,
she was also
"the ruin of her house."
A eulogy states: Xiào'ān's virtue did not ascend,
marring our royal principles.
He deposed the heir apparent,
giving rise to wickedness and corruption.
Féng Shí gained favor,
while Yáng Gōng met with wrath.
His days became dim,
and he brought misfortune upon the Way of Heaven.
Annals of Emperors Xiàoshùn, Xiàochōng, and Xiàozhì, Chapter Six
Emperor Xiàoshùn, whose personal name was Bǎo,
was the son of Emperor Ān.
His mother, Lady Lǐ,
was harmed by Empress Yán.
In the first year of Yǒngníng,
he was established as the Crown Prince.
In the third year of Yán'guāng,
Wáng Shèng, Emperor Ān's wet nurse, Jiāng Jīng, the Grand Chief of the Chánglè Palace,
and Fán Fēng, a Palace Regular Attendant, slandered Wáng Nán, the Crown Prince's wet nurse, and Bǐng Jí, the kitchen superintendent,
and had them killed.
The Crown Prince often sighed in lament.
Wáng Shèng and the others feared future retribution,
so they conspired with Fēng and Jīng to frame the Crown Prince.
The Crown Prince was consequently deposed as King of Jìyīn.
In the third month of the following year,
Emperor Ān died.
The Marquis of Běixiāng was enthroned.
As the King of Jìyīn had been deposed,
he was not permitted to ascend the hall to personally attend the imperial coffin.
He wept bitterly and refused to eat,
and all officials, both inside and outside the court, grieved for him.
When the Marquis of Běixiāng died,
Yán Xiǎn, General of Chariots and Cavalry, and Jiāng Jīng,
along with Palace Regular Attendants Liú Ān and Chén Dá, reported to the Empress Dowager,
secretly withholding the news of the death,
and instead sought to establish princes from other states.
They then closed the palace gates
and stationed troops to guard themselves.
On the day Dīngsì of the eleventh month,
an earthquake struck the capital and sixteen commanderies and states.
That night,
Sūn Chéng, a Yellow Gate Attendant, and nineteen others
jointly slew Jiāng Jīng, Liú Ān, Chén Dá, and others.
They welcomed the King of Jìyīn from beneath the bell west of Déyáng Hall
and enthroned him as emperor
at the age of eleven.
Close officials, from the Shangshū downwards,
followed the imperial carriage to the Southern Palace.
They ascended the Yúntái terrace
and summoned all officials.
Liú Guāng, the Director of the Shangshū, and others memorialized, saying:
"Emperor Xiào'ān, with his sagely virtue and brilliance,
began to rule the world early.
Your Majesty, being of the rightful lineage,
should serve the ancestral temples.
However, wicked ministers conspired,
causing Your Majesty to lie dormant in a feudal state,
and all officials, near and far, were disappointed.
Heaven's mandate is constant;
Běixiāng did not last long.
The virtue of Hàn flourishes brightly,
and its blessings are vast and manifest.
Close officials proposed a plan,
and those on Your Majesty's sides assisted.
With internal and external unity,
it accords with the divine will.
Your Majesty ascended the throne
to uphold the grand lineage
and serve as the lord of the suburban altars and ancestral temples,
continuing the endless achievements of your ancestors,
thus satisfying Heaven's will
and the people's expectations.
However, since the enthronement was sudden,
many rituals and regulations are lacking.
We request to systematically examine the rites
and present them in detail."
An imperial edict stated:
"Granted."
Then, the grandees and all officials were summoned,
and the Huben and Yulin guards were stationed at the gates of the Southern and Northern Palaces.
When Yán Xiǎn and his brothers heard that the emperor had been enthroned,
they led troops into the Northern Palace.
Guō Zhèn, a Shangshū, engaged them in battle
and consequently slew Yán Xiǎn's younger brother, Jǐng, the Commandant of the Palace Guard.
On the day Wǔwǔ,
envoys were sent to the palace to seize
the imperial seals and ribbons.
Then, the emperor proceeded to Jiādé Hall,
and sent an Imperial Censor with a credential to arrest Yán Xiǎn and his younger brothers, Yào, Commandant of the City Gates, and Yàn, Intendant of the Capital,
who were all imprisoned and executed.
On the day Jǐwèi,
the gates were opened,
and troops were stationed.
On the day Rénxū,
an edict was issued to the Colonel Director of Retainers:
"Only the close relatives of Yán Xiǎn and Jiāng Jīng should suffer execution.
The others should be treated with leniency."
On the day Rénshēn,
he visited the Gāomiào temple.
On the day Guǐyǒu,
he visited the Guāngwǔ temple.
On the day Yǐhài,
an edict was issued to the Inspector of Yìzhōu to close the Zǐwǔ road
and open the Bāoxié path.
On the day Jǐmǎo,
the Young Emperor was buried with the rites of a prince.
Liú Shòu, Minister of Works, was dismissed.
Money and grain were bestowed upon officials from the grandees downwards, each in varying amounts.
In the twelfth month, on the day Jiǎshēn,
Táo Dūn of Hénán, the Minor Steward, was appointed Minister of Works.
An order was issued that all commandery governors and chancellors who had served for less than a year
were permitted to recommend filial and incorruptible officials.
On the day Guǐmǎo,
the Shangshū memorialized to instruct the relevant officials
to withdraw the imperial edict of the ninth month, Dīngyǒu, in the third year of Yán'guāng, which deposed the Crown Prince as King of Jìyīn.
The memorial was approved.
The capital suffered a great plague.
On the day Xīnhài,
an edict was issued to the grandees, commandery governors, and state chancellors
to each recommend one worthy and upright scholar, capable of speaking candidly and offering strong remonstrance.
Officials from the Director of the Shangshū downwards who had followed the imperial carriage to the Southern Palace
were all promoted in rank and awarded cloth, each in varying amounts.
In the first month, Jiǎyín, of the first year of Yǒngjiàn,
an edict stated:
"The former emperor, with his sagely virtue,
did not enjoy a long reign
and departed early from his great achievements.
Wickedness arose in the interim,
and the common people harbored resentment and criticism,
disturbing the harmonious vital forces above,
causing plague and calamity.
I have inherited this great enterprise,
but have not yet been able to bring peace.
The root of ultimate governance
lies in examining private virtue and kindness,
cleansing past evils,
and making a new start with the people.
Therefore, there shall be a great amnesty throughout the empire.
Men shall be granted noble ranks,
two grades each;
those who succeeded their fathers, the Three Elders, filial and fraternal individuals, and industrious farmers, three grades each;
migrants who wish to register themselves, one grade.
Widowers, widows, orphans, childless elderly, the seriously ill, and the poor who cannot support themselves shall receive grain,
five *hú* each;
chaste women shall receive silk,
three bolts each.
Those sentenced to transportation by law
shall not be transported.
Those who have fled from arrest shall not be pursued.
Imperial clan members who were disinherited due to crimes
shall all have their family registrations restored.
Those who had dealings with Yán Xiǎn, Jiāng Jīng, and others
shall not be prosecuted.
Strive to fulfill your duties
to bring peace to our people."
On the day Xīnwèi,
Empress Dowager Yán died.
On the day Xīnsì,
Féng Shí, Grand Tutor, Liú Xī, Grand Commandant, and Lǐ Hé, Minister of the Masses, were dismissed.
In the second month, on the day Jiǎshēn,
Empress Ānsī was buried.
On the day Bǐngxū,
Huán Yān, Grand Master of Sacrifices, was made Grand Tutor;
Zhū Chǒng, Grand Herald, was made Grand Commandant
and participated in recording Shangshū affairs;
Zhū Chāng of Jiǔjiāng, Minor Steward of Chánglè Palace, was made Minister of the Masses.
Officials who followed the imperial carriage and served as guards, as well as those appointed or dismissed, were given varying amounts of cloth.
The Qiāng of Lǒngxī rebelled.
Mǎ Xián, Protector of the Qiāng, attacked and defeated them.
In summer, the fifth month, on the day Dīngchǒu,
an edict was issued to the Cìshǐ of Yōu, Bìng, and Liáng Prefectures,
ordering each to investigate officials from the two-thousand-dàn rank down to the Huángshòu (yellow ribbon) rank.
Those who were old, inferior, weak, and unfit for military service
were to have their names reported.
Strict orders were given to barricade the frontiers
and prepare garrisons.
After the beginning of autumn,
they were to inspect and train the cavalry.
In the sixth month, on the day Jǐhài,
Liú Xiǎn, son of Liú Cuò, the King of Jìnán, was enfeoffed as King of Jìnán.
In autumn, the seventh month, on the day Gēngwǔ,
Lái Lì, the Wèiwèi, was made Chēqí Jiāngjūn.
In the eighth month,
the Xiānbēi raided Dàijùn.
Lǐ Chāo, the Tàishǒu of Dàijùn, died in battle.
In the ninth month, on the day Xīnhài,
it was first ordered that the Sāngōng and Shàngshū enter to report on affairs.
In winter, the tenth month, on the day Xīnsì,
an edict was issued to commute death sentences and lesser crimes to frontier exile.
Those who were fugitives and redeemed themselves
were to be treated according to different grades.
On the day Dīnghài,
Táo Dūn, the Sīkōng, was dismissed.
The Xiānbēi violated the border.
On the day Gēngyín,
troops from the Líyáng營 were dispatched to garrison the northern border of Zhōngshān.
The Cìshǐ of Yōuzhōu was notified
to order the frontier commanderies to increase their infantry
and establish garrisons along the defensive line.
Nǔshī (crossbow masters) from the five camps were conscripted,
five men from each commandery,
to teach and practice archery.
On the day Rényín,
Zhāng Hào, the Tíngwèi, was made Sīkōng.
On the day Jiǎchén,
an edict was issued due to pestilence and floods,
ordering people to pay half of this year's land tax.
If damage was four-tenths or more,
no collection was to be enforced.
If less,
it was to be reduced according to the actual loss.
In the twelfth month, on the day Xīnsì,
the kings, princesses, noble consorts, and officials from the Gōngqīng down were bestowed cloth according to their ranks.
In the second year, spring, the first month, on the day Wùshēn,
Liú Hóng, the King of Luò'ān, came to court.
On the day Dīngmǎo,
Liú Zhāng, the King of Chángshān, passed away.
In the second month,
the Xiānbēi raided Liáodōng and Xuántú.
On the day Jiǎchén,
an edict was issued to provide food and loans to the displaced poor in Jīng, Yù, Yǎn, and Jì, the four prefectures,
and settle them where they were;
the sick were to be given medicine.
Gěng Yè, the Hùwūhuán Xiàowèi, led the Southern Chányú to attack the Xiānbēi
and defeated them.
In the third month,
there was a drought,
and envoys were sent to review prisoners.
The kingdom of Shūlè sent envoys with tribute.
In summer, the sixth month, on the day Yǐyǒu,
Empress Mother Lǐ, posthumously honored as Gōngmǐn Huánghòu,
was interred in Gōngběilíng.
Bān Yǒng, the Xīyù Chángshǐ, and Zhāng Lǎng, the Dūnhuáng Tàishǒu, campaigned against the three kingdoms of Yānqí, Wèilí, and Wēixū,
defeating them;
all subsequently sent their sons to offer tribute.
In autumn, the seventh month, on the first day Jiǎxū,
there was a solar eclipse.
On the day Réngwǔ,
Zhū Chǒng, the Tàiwèi, and Zhū Chāng, the Sītú, were dismissed.
On the day Gēngzǐ,
Liú Guāng, the Tàicháng, was made Tàiwèi
and Lù Shàngshūshì;
Xǔ Jìng, the Guānglùxūn, was made Sītú.
On the day Xīnchǒu,
Liú Chéng, the King of Xiàpī, passed away.
In the third year, spring, the first month, on the day Bǐngzǐ,
there was an earthquake in the capital,
and the ground in Hànyáng collapsed and cracked.
On the day Jiǎwǔ,
an edict was issued to thoroughly investigate the injured and damaged,
and bestow money to those aged seven and above,
two thousand per person.
If a family suffered casualties,
the commandery and county were to arrange for their burial.
On the day Yǐwèi,
an edict was issued not to collect this year's land tax and poll tax in Hànyáng.
In summer, the fourth month, on the day Guǐmǎo,
a Guānglù Dàfū was dispatched to inspect Hànyáng, as well as Hénèi, Wèijùn, Chénliú, and Dōngjùn,
and provide food and loans to the poor.
In the sixth month,
there was a drought.
Envoys were sent to review prisoners
and deal with those lightly confined.
On the day Jiǎyín,
Liú Xiǎn, the King of Jìnán, passed away.
In autumn, the seventh month, on the day Dīngyǒu,
the imperial mausoleum at Màolíng suffered a calamity.
The Emperor wore plain white mourning clothes and avoided the main hall.
On the day Xīnhài,
Wáng Gōng, the Tàicháng, was sent with a credential to announce a sacrifice at Màolíng.
In the ninth month,
the Xiānbēi raided Yúyáng.
In winter, the twelfth month, on the day Jǐhài,
Huán Yān, the Tàifù, was dismissed.
That year,
Lái Lì, the Chēqí Jiāngjūn, was dismissed.
In the fourth year, spring, the first month, on the day Bǐngyín,
an edict stated:
"I, who am placed above the kings and dukes,
have daily strayed from the Dao,
and my governance has lost its balance.
The forces of Yīn and Yáng are separated,
bandits run rampant,
and prisons are ever more crowded.
I grieve and sigh perpetually,
afflicted as if with a headache.
The Shī Jīng says: 'If the lord is blessed,
the troubles will quickly cease.'
At the court assembly of the three mornings,
on the first day of the month and the beginning of spring,
I wish with the whole country to cleanse our hearts and renew ourselves.
Therefore, pardon the empire.
Those whose ranks and registers were restored since the amnesty order of Jiǎyín
shall have their redemptions returned from the first month of the third year onwards.
The prohibitions on the associates and marriage relatives of Yán Xiǎn, Jiāng Jīng, and others
are all to be lifted.
Strive to promote leniency and harmony,
reverently comply with the seasonal commands,
follow established principles, and eliminate harshness,
to accord with my wishes."
On the day Bǐngzǐ,
the Emperor came of age (underwent the capping ceremony).
Kings, princesses, noble consorts, and officials from Gōngqīng down were bestowed gold and silk according to their ranks.
Men were granted one rank of nobility, and those seeking registration as migrants one rank;
those who were successors to fathers, Sānlǎo, Xiàotì, or Lìtián were granted two ranks.
To the widowed, solitary, orphaned, and those afflicted with severe illness [and] unable to sustain themselves,
one bolt of silk per person was given.
In the second month, on the day Wùxū,
an edict was issued concerning people digging stones in the mountains,
thereby releasing hidden energies.
Officials were ordered to investigate what should be prohibited,
following the precedents of Jiànwǔ and Yǒngpíng.
In summer, the fifth month, on the day Réngchén,
an edict stated:
"The empire has suffered numerous calamities.
The court has reformed governance,
the Tàiguān has reduced meals,
and precious ornaments are not used.
Yet Wén Lóng, the Tàishǒu of Guìyáng,
without thinking of exhausting his loyalty
and promoting the court's policies,
has sent large pearls from afar
to seek favor and flattery.
I now return them sealed."
Five prefectures experienced rain and floods.
In autumn, the eighth month, on the day Gēngzǐ,
envoys were sent to thoroughly investigate deaths,
collect the deceased, and provide sustenance and grants.
On the day Dīngsì,
Liú Guāng, the Tàiwèi, and Zhāng Hào, the Sīkōng, were dismissed.
In the ninth month,
Āndìng, Běidì, and Shàngjùn were restored to their former territories.
On the day Guǐyǒu,
Páng Cān, the Dàhónglú, was made Tàiwèi
and Lù Shàngshūshì.
Wáng Gōng, the Tàicháng, was made Sīkōng.
In winter, the eleventh month, on the day Gēngchén,
Xǔ Jìng, the Sītú, was dismissed.
The Xiānbēi raided Shuòfāng.
In the twelfth month, on the day Yǐmǎo,
Liú Qí, the Zōngzhèng, was made Sītú.
That year,
Kuàijī was divided into Wújùn.
The kingdom of Jūmí sent envoys with tribute.
In the fifth year, spring, the first month,
the King of Shūlè sent a hostage prince,
and the kings of Dàyuān and Shāchē all sent envoys with tribute.
In summer, the fourth month,
there was a drought in the capital.
On the day Xīnsì,
an edict stated that the poor in commanderies and kingdoms who suffered from calamities
were not to be pressed for overdue taxes this year.
The capital and twelve commanderies and kingdoms experienced locust plagues.
In winter, the tenth month, on the day Bǐngchén,
an edict was issued to commute the death sentences of all central and local government prisoners in commanderies and kingdoms by one degree,
to be sent to garrison Běidì, Shàngjùn, and Āndìng.
On the day Yǐhài,
Bān Shǐ, the Dìngyuǎn Hóu, was found guilty of murdering his wife, Princess Yīnchéng,
and was cut in half at the waist;
all his siblings were executed publicly.
In the sixth year, spring, the second month, on the day Gēngwǔ,
Liú Kāi, the King of Héjiān, passed away.
In the third month, on the day Xīnhài,
the military colonies at Yīwú were restored,
and one Yīwú Sīmǎ was re-established.
In the ninth month of autumn, on the *xīnsì* day,
repairs were begun on the Tàixué.
The Protector of the Wūhuán, Gěng Yè, dispatched troops to attack the Xiānbēi,
and defeated them.
On the *dīngyǒu* day,
the king of Yútián sent a hostage son to offer tribute.
In the eleventh month of winter, on the *xīnhài* day,
an imperial edict stated:
“For consecutive years, there have been floods and disasters,
especially severe in Jìbù.
While remission and exemption have indeed caused suffering,
and the poor and destitute have been assisted,
the common people still have [⿱𠫓廾]yè,
and the flow of displaced persons is unceasing.
I suspect that the commanderies and counties are negligent in their duties,
and that imperial benevolence is not being proclaimed.
The *Yì* praises '損上益下' (*sǔn shàng yì xià* - diminish the top, augment the bottom),
and the *Shū* says, '安民則惠' (*ān mín zé huì* - bring peace to the people, then there is benevolence).
Therefore, the Jìbù is ordered not to collect this year's land rent and fodder.”
In the twelfth month,
the state of Yètiáo and the state of Shàn, from beyond the frontiers of Rìnán, sent envoys to offer tribute.
On the *rénshēn* day,
a guest star appeared in Qiānniú.
The king of Yútián sent a hostage son to the imperial court to offer tribute.
In the first year of Yángjiā, in the first month of spring, on the *yǐsì* day,
Empress Liángshì was enthroned.
Titles were bestowed,
two ranks for each person;
three ranks for Sānlǎo, Xiàotì, and Lìtián.
Those whose titles exceeded Gōngchéng
were allowed to transfer them to a son, a sibling, or a sibling's son.
Commoners without official registration and displaced people who wished to register were granted one rank each.
Grain was given to the 鰥 (*guān* - widowers),寡 (*guǎ* - widows),孤 (*gū* - orphans),獨 (*dú* - childless elderly),篤 (*dǔ* - seriously ill), and those so poor they could not sustain themselves;
five *hú* per person.
In the second month,
the sea pirates Zēng Jǐng and others plundered Kuàijī,
killed the magistrates of Jùzhāng, Yín, and Màoxuàn counties,
and attacked the Eastern Commandant of Kuàijī.
An imperial edict ordered coastal counties to station troops.
On the *dīngsì* day,
the empress paid respects at the Gāomiào and Guāngwǔmiào.
An imperial edict ordered provisions for the poor people of Gānlíng,
with different amounts for adults and children.
The capital suffered from drought.
On the *gēngshēn* day,
an imperial edict commanded the Two Thousand *Shí* officials of each commandery and state to pray to the famous mountains, peaks, and rivers.
Grand Masters and Envoys were dispatched to Sōnggāo and Shǒuyángshān,
and also to offer sacrifices to the Hé and Luò rivers,
to request rain.
On the *wùchén* day,
a rain ceremony was performed.
Because Jìbù had experienced floods and waterlogging in recent years,
and the people lacked sufficient food,
an imperial edict ordered inspection and distribution of loans,
encouragement of agricultural work,
and relief for the destitute.
On the *jiǎxū* day,
an imperial edict stated:
“The government has lost its harmony,
and Yin and Yang are separated and entangled.
There has been no lingering snow in winter,
and no abundant rain in spring.
Prayers and entreaties have been offered in various places,
and no deity has been left un-sacrificed to.
I deeply fear that officials in various places have negligently disregarded the meaning of '如在' (*rú zài* - as if present).
Now, I dispatch Palace Attendants Wáng Fǔ and others,
bearing imperial credentials, to proceed separately to Dàishān, Dōnghǎi, Xíngyáng, and the Hé and Luò rivers,
to pray with all their heart.”
In the third month,
the demon賊 Zhāng Hé and others from six commanderies in Yángzhōu plundered forty-nine counties,
killing and wounding magistrates.
On the *gēngyín* day,
the emperor personally presided over a banquet and archery contest at the Bìyōng,
granted a general amnesty to the empire,
and changed the era name to Yángjiā.
An imperial edict ordered that all members of the imperial clan whose names had been removed from the registry
be reinstated;
provisions were given to the especially poor people of Jìzhōu,
and this year's *gēng*, rent, and poll tax were not to be collected.
In the fifth month of summer, on the *wùyín* day,
Fùlíng Wáng Huī passed away.
In the seventh month of autumn,
historians began to construct a bronze instrument for observing wind and detecting earthquakes.
On the *bǐngchén* day,
because the Tàixué was newly completed,
examinees who failed the "clarifying the classics" test were appointed as disciples,
and the number of members in the A and B categories was each increased by ten.
Ninety venerable scholars from commanderies and states were appointed as Langs and Sheren.
In the ninth month,
an imperial edict ordered that all prisoners in commanderies and states who were facing the death penalty should have their sentences reduced by one degree,
and fugitives could redeem themselves,
each with different regulations.
The Xiānbēi plundered Liáodōng.
In the eleventh month of winter, on the *jiǎshēn* day,
wolves in Wàngdū and Púyīn killed ninety-seven women.
An imperial edict ordered that money be granted to those killed by wolves,
three thousand *qián* per person.
On the *xīnmǎo* day,
it was first ordered that commanderies and states recommend *Xiàolián*.
The age limit was set at forty years or older.
Scholars who were proficient in chapters and verses,
and scribes who were skilled in memorials and奏 (*zòu* - reports to the throne),
were eligible for selection.
However, those with exceptional talent and extraordinary conduct,
like Yán Yuān or Zǐ Qí,
were not restricted by age.
In the twelfth month, on the *dīngwèi* day,
Dōngpíng Wáng Chǎng passed away.
On the *gēngxū* day,
the Xúantu commandery's agricultural colonies were re-established in six *bù*.
In the intercalary month, on the *dīnghài* day,
it was ordered that those who had been appointed as Langs by imperial edict,
and who were forty years or older and passed examinations according to the *Xiàolián* criteria,
could participate in the *Lián* selection,
one person to be recommended annually.
On the *wùzǐ* day,
a guest star appeared in Tiānyuàn.
On the *xīnmǎo* day,
an imperial edict stated:
“Since some time ago,
officials have not been diligent in governance,
thus disasters and calamities have repeatedly arrived,
and bandits are numerous.
Reflecting on the reasons,
all are due to elections not being true,
and officials not being the right people for the job.
Because of this, the will of Heaven has not been attained,
and the people's grievances are many.
The *Shū* praises the *gǔgōng* (ministers),
and the *Shī* criticizes the *sānsì* (three officials).
Now, the selection of Inspectors and Two Thousand *Shí* officials
is entrusted to the Sānsī.
They must carefully rank them in order,
and precisely scrutinize their merits,
considering the sequence of years,
and the suitability for civil and military roles,
striving to uphold impartiality.”
On the *gēngzǐ* day,
the hundred-zhang corridor of the Gōnglíng suffered a fire.
In this year,
the Xīyuàn was constructed,
and the imperial palaces were renovated.
In the second year, in the second month of spring, on the *jiǎshēn* day,
an imperial edict was issued, stating that due to famine in Wú commandery and Kuàijī,
people were to be loaned seeds and grain.
In the third month,
the Colonel-Protector of the Xiongnú, Wáng Chóu, led the Left Gǔdū Hóu and others to attack the Xiānbēi,
and defeated them.
On the *xīnyǒu* day,
forty-eight venerable scholars in the capital aged sixty or older were appointed as Langs, Sheren, and Langs in various kingdoms.
In the fourth month of summer,
the office of the Southern Commandant of Lǒngxī was re-established.
On the *jǐhài* day,
there was an earthquake in the capital.
In the fifth month, on the *gēngzǐ* day,
an imperial edict stated:
“I, being without virtue,
have succeeded to this great undertaking,
and am unable to serve Heaven and Earth respectfully,
or harmonize Yin and Yang.
Disasters and misfortunes have repeatedly appeared,
and ill omens have continuously arrived.
The anomaly of the earthquake,
originating from the capital,
fills me with anxious reverence,
and I do not know how to handle it.
How will the various dukes, ministers, and gentlemen assist my shortcomings,
and respond to these warning anomalies?
Anomalies are not set forth in vain;
there must be something they correspond to.
Let each of you sincerely and directly speak of the faults,
without any concealment.”
On the *wùwǔ* day,
Sīkōng Wáng Gōng was dismissed.
In the sixth month, on the *xīnwèi* day,
Tàicháng Kǒng Fú of Lǔguó became Sīkōng.
The state of Shūlè presented lions and "sealed oxen."
On the *dīngchǒu* day,
Luòyáng experienced a ground subsidence.
In this month,
there was a drought.
In the seventh month of autumn, on the *jǐwèi* day,
Tàiwèi Páng Cān was dismissed.
In the eighth month, on the *jǐsì* day,
Dàhónglú Shī Yán of Pèiguó became Tàiwèi.
The Xiānbēi plundered Dàijùn.
In the tenth month of winter, on the *gēngwǔ* day,
the ceremony was performed at Bìyōng,
the *Yìngzhōng* was played,
and the *Huángzhōng* was restored for the first time.
Musical instruments were made according to the monthly pitches.
In the third year, spring, second month, on the day Jǐchǒu,
an edict was issued due to a prolonged drought,
that in the capital, all prisons, regardless of the severity of the offense, should temporarily cease investigations and trials,
awaiting abundant rain.
In the third month, on the day Gēngxū,
bandits in Yìzhōu robbed and held hostage prefects and chiefs,
and killed a titled marquess.
In summer, fourth month, on the day Bǐngyín,
the commander of the Chēshī Later Division, leading the king of the Later Division, Jiātèní, and others, launched a surprise attack on the Xiōngnú,
thoroughly defeating them,
and capturing their younger maternal relative.
In the fifth month, on the day Wùxū,
an imperial edict proclaimed:
"In the past, our Tàizōng,
greatly displayed his virtue,
which was granted to both high and low.
Through frugality, he cared for the people,
and his governance achieved prosperity.
I have been unclear in handling affairs,
and governance has deviated from its proper course,
thus Heaven and Earth express their wrath,
and great calamities repeatedly appear.
Spring and summer have seen continuous drought,
bandits are increasingly numerous,
and the common people suffer harm.
I am deeply saddened by this.
I desire to cleanse our hearts and make a fresh start with all within the seas.
A general amnesty is hereby granted to the entire realm.
All offenses, from those deserving special execution downwards, including rebellion, high treason, and other crimes not usually eligible for pardon,
are all pardoned and remitted.
To commoners aged eighty and above, a grant of rice is given,
one hú per person,
twenty jīn of meat,
and five dòu of wine.
Those ninety and above shall additionally receive silk,
two pǐ per person,
and three jīn of floss."
In autumn, seventh month, on the day Gēngxū,
the Zhōng Qiāng raided Lǒngxī and Hànyáng.
In winter, tenth month,
the Protector-in-Chief of the Qiāng, Mǎ Xù, attacked Zhǎ Jūnd.
In the eleventh month, on the day Rényín,
the Grand Minister of Works, Liú Qí, and the Grand Excellency, Kǒng Fú, were dismissed.
On the day Yǐsì,
the Grand Minister of Agriculture, Huáng Shàng of Nányùn, became Grand Minister of Works,
and the Minister of the Imperial Household, Wáng Zhuó of Hédōng, became Grand Excellency.
On the day Bǐngwǔ,
the garrisoned Qiāng and foreign Qiāng in the Bùdū frontier attacked and broke through the garrison posts,
driving away and seizing people and livestock.
In the fourth year, spring, second month, on the day Bǐngzǐ,
it was first permitted for palace attendants to adopt sons as successors,
with hereditary enfeoffments and titles.
From the previous winter's drought,
it continued until this month.
The Imperial Messenger, Mǎ Xián, attacked the Zhōng Qiāng,
utterly defeating them.
In summer, fourth month, on the day Jiǎzǐ,
the Grand Commandant, Shī Yán, was dismissed.
On the day Wùyín,
the Commandant of the Guards, Liáng Shāng, became Grand General,
and the former Grand Commandant, Páng Cān, became Grand Commandant.
In the sixth month, on the day Jǐwèi,
Prince Kuāng of Liáng died.
In autumn, seventh month, on the day Jǐhài,
Prince Dēng of Jìběi died.
In the intercalary month, on the first day, Dīnghài,
there was a solar eclipse.
In winter, tenth month,
the Wūhuán raided Yúnzhōng.
In the eleventh month,
they besieged the General Who Crosses the Liao, Gěng Yè, at Lánchí.
Troops from various commanderies were dispatched to relieve him,
and the Wūhuán retreated.
In the twelfth month, on the day Jiǎyín,
there was an earthquake in the capital.
In the first year of Yǒnghé, spring, first month,
the King of Fúyú came to pay tribute.
On the day Yǐmǎo,
an edict proclaimed:
"I have been unclear in administering government,
and disasters and misfortunes have repeatedly occurred.
Among what is forbidden in the classics, earthquakes and eclipses are considered serious.
Today, the omen is far-reaching,
and the earth shook in the capital.
The sign of calamity is not false,
and must have a corresponding reason.
Let all the ducal ministers and numerous officials each submit sealed memorials,
pointing out successes and failures,
without any concealment."
On the day Jǐsì,
sacrifices were offered in the Míngtáng,
and the Língtái was ascended.
The era name was changed to Yǒnghé,
and a general amnesty was granted to the realm.
In autumn, seventh month,
there were locusts in Yǎnshī.
In winter, tenth month, on the day Dīnghài,
Chéngfú Hall caught fire,
and the Emperor took refuge in Yúntái.
In the eleventh month, on the day Bǐngzǐ,
the Grand Commandant, Páng Cān, was dismissed.
In the twelfth month,
the Mán and Yí of Xiànglín rebelled.
On the day Yǐsì,
the former Grand Excellency, Wáng Gōng, was appointed Grand Commandant.
In the second year, spring, first month,
the Wǔlíng Mán rebelled,
besieging Chōng county,
and also raiding Yídào.
In the second month,
the Commandant of the Guanghàn Commandery Dependent State attacked and defeated the Báimǎ Qiāng.
The Administrator of Wǔlíng, Lǐ Jìn, attacked the rebellious Mán,
defeating them.
In the third month, on the day Xīnhài,
Prince Yì of Běihǎi died.
On the day Yǐmǎo,
the Grand Excellency, Wáng Zhuó, died.
On the day Dīngchǒu,
the Minister of the Imperial Household, Guō Qián of Féngyì, became Grand Excellency.
In summer, fourth month, on the day Bǐngshēn,
there was an earthquake in the capital.
In the fifth month,
the rebellious Mán of Rìnán attacked the commandery seat.
In autumn, seventh month,
the troops of the two commanderies of Jiǔzhēn and Jiāozhǐ rebelled.
In the eighth month, on the day Gēngzǐ,
Huǒxīng encroached upon Nándǒu.
Bandits in Jiāngxià killed the chief of Zhū.
In winter, tenth month, on the day Jiǎshēn,
the Emperor traveled to Cháng'ān.
Along the way,
the widowed, orphaned, solitary, and poor who could not sustain themselves were granted grain,
five hú per person.
On the day Gēngzǐ,
the Emperor visited Wèiyāng Palace,
where he met with the administrators and commandants of the three Fǔ commanderies, as well as their officials and subordinates,
showing favor and granting rewards with music.
In the eleventh month, on the day Bǐngwǔ,
sacrifices were offered at Gāomiào.
On the day Dīngwèi,
rites were subsequently performed at the eleven mausoleums.
On the day Dīngmǎo,
there was an earthquake in the capital.
In the twelfth month, on the day Yǐhài,
the Emperor returned from Cháng'ān.
In the third year, spring, second month, on the day Yǐhài,
there were earthquakes in the capital and in Jīnchéng and Lǒngxī.
In the two commanderies, mountains and cliffs collapsed,
and the ground sank.
On the day Wùzǐ,
Tàibái encroached upon Huǒxīng.
In summer, fourth month,
the bandit Cài Bólíu of Jiǔjiāng raided the commandery borders,
and also Guǎnglín,
killing the chief of Jiāngdū.
On the day Wùxū,
a Grand Master of Imperial Splendor was dispatched to inspect Jīnchéng and Lǒngxī,
and money was granted to those crushed to death,
two thousand [qián] per person aged seven and above.
For families where all members were killed,
arrangements were made for their burial.
The land tax for this year was remitted,
and for those most severely affected, the household tax was also not collected.
In the intercalary month,
Cài Bólíu and his followers led their troops to the Inspector of Xúzhōu, Yīng Zhì, and surrendered.
On the day Jǐyǒu,
there was an earthquake in the capital.
In the fifth month,
Yáng Zhēn, the aide of Wú Commandery, rebelled,
attacking the commandery seat.
The Administrator, Wáng Héng, defeated and beheaded him.
In the sixth month, on the day Xīnchǒu,
Prince Zūn of Lángyá died.
The Administrator of Jiǔzhēn, Zhù Liáng, and the Inspector of Jiāozhǐ, Zhāng Qiáo, appeased and enticed the rebellious Mán of Rìnán,
securing their surrender,
and the area beyond the mountains was pacified.
In autumn, seventh month, on the day Bǐngxū,
Prince Duō of Jìběi died.
In the eighth month, on the day Jǐwèi,
the Grand Minister of Works, Huáng Shàng, was dismissed.
In the ninth month, on the day Jǐyǒu,
the Minister of the Imperial Household, Liú Shòu of Chángshā, became Grand Minister of Works.
On the day Bǐngxū,

an order was issued for the Grand General and the Three Excellencies to each recommend two former inspectors, officials of two thousand dàn salary, and incumbent prefects, chiefs, palace gentlemen, imperial messengers, and subordinates of the four ministries who were resolute, brave, strategic, and capable of commanding armies;
and for the Grandee of Grand Brilliance, ministers, and commandants to each recommend one.
In winter, tenth month,
the Shāodāng Qiāng raided Jīnchéng.
The Protector-in-Chief of the Qiāng, Mǎ Xián, attacked and defeated them,
but the Qiāng then incited each other to rebel.
In the twelfth month, on the first day, Wùxū,
there was a solar eclipse.
In the fourth year, spring, first month, on the day Gēngchén,
the Regular Palace Attendants Zhāng Kuí, Qú Zhèng, Yáng Dìng, and others were executed for their crimes,
implicating the Administrator of Hóngnóng, Zhāng Fèng, and the Chancellor of Ānpíng, Yáng Hào,
who were imprisoned and died.
In the third month, on the *yǐhài* day,
the capital experienced an earthquake.
In summer, in the fourth month, on the *guǐmǎo* day,
the Protector of the Qiāng, Mǎ Xián, attacked the Shāodāng Qiāng,
and thoroughly defeated them.
On the *wùwǔ* day,
a general amnesty was proclaimed throughout the empire.
The common people were granted noble ranks, millet, and silk, with varying amounts.
In the fifth month, on the *wùchén* day,
Ān, son of the late Prince Huì of Jìběi, Shòu, was enfeoffed as Prince of Jìběi.
In autumn, in the eighth month,
Táiyuán Commandery suffered a drought,
and the common people were displaced.
On the *guǐchǒu* day,
a Grand Master of Guanglu was dispatched to investigate and provide loans,
and to abolish the *gēngfù* tax.
In winter, in the tenth month, on the *wùwǔ* day,
a hunt was held in the Shànglín Park,
and the emperor returned after passing through Hángǔ Pass.
In the eleventh month, on the *bǐngyín* day,
the emperor visited the Guǎngchéng Park.
In the fifth year, in spring, in the second month, on the *wùshēn* day,
the capital experienced an earthquake.
In summer, in the fourth month, on the *gēngzǐ* day,
Prince Hóng of Zhōngshān passed away.
Gōulóng Wúsī, Chēniǔ, and others, leaders of the Left Division of the Southern Xiōngnú, rebelled,
and besieged Měijì.
In the fifth month,
General Who Crosses the Liao, Mǎ Xù, attacked Wúsī and Chēniǔ,
and defeated them.
The Colonel-Protector of the Xiōngnú, Chén Guī, forced the Southern Chányú to his death.
On the last day of the month, *jǐchǒu huì*,
there was a solar eclipse.
The Qiědòng Qiāng raided Sānfǔ,
killing magistrates and chiefs.
On the *dīngchǒu* day,
it was ordered that those guilty of capital crimes or lesser offenses, and fugitives, could redeem themselves,
with varying rates.
In the ninth month,
Fúfēng and Hànyáng were ordered to build three hundred fortified camps along the Lǒng Pass,
and to station garrison troops there.
On the *xīnwèi* day,
Grand Commandant Wáng Gōng was dismissed.
The Qiědòng Qiāng raided Wǔdū,
and burned Lǒng Pass.
On the *rénwǔ* day,
Grand Herald Huán Yān became Grand Commandant.
On the *dīnghài* day,
Xīhé Commandery was moved to Líshí,
Shàng Commandery to Xiàyáng,
and Shuòfāng to Wǔyuán.
Gōulóng Wúsī and others brought in the Wūhuán from the east,
and gathered the Qiāng and Hú from the west,
raiding Shàng Commandery,
and establishing Chēniǔ as Chányú.
In winter, in the eleventh month, on the *xīnsì* day,
Colonel-Protector of the Xiōngnú, Zhāng Dān, was sent to attack them, and Chēniǔ surrendered.
In the sixth year, in spring, in the first month, on the *bǐngzǐ* day,
General Who Attacks the West, Mǎ Xián, battled the Qiědòng Qiāng at Shègū Mountain,
Mǎ Xián's army was defeated and annihilated,
and Grand Administrator Guō Huáng of Āndìng was imprisoned and died.
An edict pardoned one year's rent for princely and marquise states.
In the intercalary month,
the Gǒngtáng Qiāng raided Lǒngxī,
and then reached Sānfǔ.
In the second month, on the *dīngsì* day,
a comet appeared in Yíngshì.
In the third month,
Grand Administrator Zhào Chōng of Wǔwēi attacked the Gǒngtáng Qiāng,
and defeated them.
On the *gēngzǐ* day,
Minister of Works Guō Qián was dismissed.
On the *yǐsì* day,
Prince Zhèng of Héjiān passed away.
On the *bǐngwǔ* day,
Grand Coachman Zhào Jiè became Minister of Works.
In summer, in the fifth month, on the *gēngzǐ* day,
Prince Wújì of Qí passed away.
Colonel-Protector of the Xiōngnú, Zhāng Dān, thoroughly defeated the Wūhuán and Qiānghú at Tiānshān.
The Gǒngtáng Qiāng raided Běidì.
In autumn, in the seventh month, on the *jiǎwǔ* day,
an edict ordered that households with property be loaned one thousand *qián*.
In the eighth month, on the *bǐngchén* day,
General-in-Chief Liáng Shāng passed away;
on the *rénxū* day,
Liáng Jì, Governor of Hénán, became General-in-Chief.
In the ninth month,
various Qiāng tribes raided Wǔwēi.
On the last day of the month, *xīnhài huì*,
there was a solar eclipse.
In winter, in the tenth month, on the *guǐchǒu* day,
Āndìng was moved to Fúfēng,
and Běidì to Fèngyì.
In the eleventh month, on the *gēngzǐ* day,
Zhāng Qiáo, bearer of the Gilded Mace, was appointed acting General of Chariots and Cavalry,
and led troops to garrison Sānfǔ.
In the first year of Hàn'ān, in spring, in the first month, on the *guǐsì* day,
the ancestral sacrifices were performed in the Míngtáng,
a general amnesty was proclaimed throughout the empire,
and the reign era was changed to Hàn'ān.
In the second month, on the *bǐngchén* day,
an edict ordered the General-in-Chief, the Three Dukes, and the Nine Ministers to each recommend one worthy and upright person, skilled in exploring the abstruse and seeking the hidden.
In autumn, in the seventh month,
the position of Chénghuá was first established.
In the eighth month,
Gōulóng Wúsī, leader of the Left Division of the Southern Xiōngnú, rebelled with Yùjiàn Táiqí and others.
On the *dīngmǎo* day,

eight people—Court Attendant Dù Qiáo, Grand Master of Guanglu Zhōu Jǔ, Acting Grand Master of Guanglu Guō Zūn, Féng Xiàn, Luán Bā, Zhāng Gāng, Zhōu Xǔ, and Liú Bān—were dispatched to tour the commanderies and provinces,
to proclaim and spread moral transformation,
and to report on actual merits and faults.
In the ninth month, on the *gēngyín* day,
Zhāng Yīng and other bandits from Guǎnglíng raided commanderies and counties.
In winter, in the tenth month, on the *xīnwèi* day,
Grand Commandant Huán Yān and Minister of the Masses Liú Shòu were dismissed.
On the *jiǎxū* day,
Acting General of Chariots and Cavalry Zhāng Qiáo was dismissed.
In the eleventh month, on the *rénwǔ* day,
Colonel Director of Retainers Zhào Jùn became Grand Commandant,
and Grand Minister of Agriculture Hú Guǎng became Minister of the Masses.
On the *guǐmǎo* day,
an edict ordered the General-in-Chief and the Three Dukes to each select one martial and fierce person, test their effectiveness, and appoint them as a general or officer.
In this year,
Zhāng Yīng and other bandits from Guǎnglíng surrendered to Grand Administrator Zhāng Gāng.
In the second year, in spring, in the second month, on the *bǐngchén* day,
the state of Shànshàn sent envoys to pay tribute.
In summer, in the fourth month, on the *gēngxū* day,
Protector of the Qiāng Zhào Chōng, with Grand Administrator Zhāng Gòng of Hànyáng, attacked the Shāohé Qiāng at Cānyú,
and defeated them.
In the sixth month, on the *yǐchǒu* day,
Mars infringed upon Saturn.
On the *bǐngyín* day,
Dōulóuchú, the Prince Who Guards Righteousness of the Southern Xiōngnú, was enthroned as Southern Chányú.
In winter, in the tenth month, on the *xīnchǒu* day,
it was ordered that prisoners in the capital jails of the commanderies and states, from capital crimes downwards, could redeem themselves with silk,
with varying rates;
those who could not afford the redemption
were sent to Língqiāng County for two years of labor.
On the *jiǎchén* day,
the stipends of all officials were reduced.
On the *bǐngwǔ* day,
the sale of wine was prohibited,
and one year's rent for princely and marquise states was again pardoned.
In the intercalary month,
Zhào Chōng attacked the Shāodāng Qiāng at Āyáng,
and defeated them.
In the eleventh month,
Colonel-Protector of the Xiōngnú, Mǎ Shí, sent someone to assassinate Gōulóng Wúsī.
In the twelfth month,
bandits from Yáng and Xú attacked and burned cities and temples,
and killed and plundered officials and common people.
In this year,
Liángzhōu experienced one hundred eighty earthquakes.
In the first year of Jiànkāng, in spring, in the first month, on the *xīnchǒu* day,
an imperial edict stated:
"Lǒngxī, Hànyáng, Zhāngyè, Běidì, Wǔwēi, and Wǔdū,
since the ninth month of last year,
have experienced one hundred eighty earthquakes,
mountains and valleys have cracked,
cities and temples have been destroyed,
and common people have been killed.
Barbarians have rebelled,
taxes and levies have increased,
and there is widespread resentment within and without.
We sigh with sorrow over these faults.
Therefore, a Grand Master of Guanglu is dispatched to investigate,
to spread our grace and favor,
to benefit these common people,
and not to trouble them."
In the third month, on the *gēngzǐ* day,
Prince Guǎng of Pèi passed away.
Wèi Jū, acting Protector of the Qiāng, pursued and attacked the rebellious Qiāng,
and defeated them.
Bandits from Nán Commandery and Jiāngxià raided cities and towns,
and the provinces and commanderies attacked and pacified them.
In summer, in the fourth month,
Colonel-Protector of the Xiōngnú, Mǎ Shí, attacked the Left Division of the Southern Xiōngnú,
and defeated them.
Thereupon, the Hú, Qiāng, and Wūhuán all surrendered to Mǎ Shí.
On the *xīnsì* day,
Imperial Prince Bǐng was established as Crown Prince,
the reign year was changed to Jiànkāng,
and a general amnesty was proclaimed throughout the empire.
People were granted noble ranks, with varying amounts.
In autumn, in the seventh month, on the *bǐngwǔ* day,
Prince Yánpíng of Qīnghé passed away.
In the eighth month,
Fàn Róng, Zhōu Shēng, and other bandits from Yáng and Xú raided cities and towns,
and Censor-in-Chief Féng Shè was dispatched to oversee the provincial and commandery troops in attacking them.
On the *gēngwǔ* day,
the emperor passed away in the front hall of the Yùtáng,
at the age of thirty.
His dying edict stipulated no construction of a sleeping temple,
burial in his old clothes,
and no pearls, jade, or cherished objects were to be interred.
Discussion: In ancient times, there were rulers
who, having been exiled to obscurity, restored their dynastic fortunes.
None of them failed to rectify past transgressions,
discern true from false,
and never forgot the hardships endured in exile;
thus, they were able to revive their enterprises.
But is the administration of the Shùn dynasty
not quite like that?
Why are its deviations so numerous?
Emperor Xiàochōng, personal name Bǐng,
was the son of Emperor Shùn.
His mother was Consort Yú.
In the first year of Jiànkāng, he was established as Crown Prince.
In the eighth month of that year, on the day Gēngwǔ,
he ascended the imperial throne
at the age of two.
The Empress was honored as Empress Dowager.
The Empress Dowager presided over the court.
On the day Dīngchǒu,
Grand尉 Zhào Jùn was made Grand Tutor;
Grand Minister of Agriculture Lǐ Gù was made Grand尉,
participating in the recording of Imperial Secretariat affairs.
In the ninth month, on the day Bǐngwǔ,
Emperor Xiàoshùn was buried at Xiānlíng,
and his temple name was Jìngzōng.
On this day,
the capital and Tàiyuán, Yànmén experienced earthquakes,
and in these three commanderies, water surged and the earth cracked.
On the day Gēngxū,
an edict ordered the Sān Gōng, Special Advance, marquises, ministers, and commandants
each to recommend one worthy and upright, reclusive and cultivated scholar.
All officials were to submit sealed memorials.
On the day Jǐwèi,
Qiū Téng, the Administrator of Jiǔjiāng, was found guilty,
imprisoned, and died.
Yǐn Yào, the Inspector of Yángzhōu, and Dèng Xiǎn, the Administrator of Jiǔjiāng, attacked the bandit Fàn Róng and others at Lìyáng.
Their army was defeated,
and Yào and Xiǎn were killed by the bandits.
In the tenth month of winter,
the barbarians of Rìdòng attacked and burned cities and towns.
Xià Fāng, the Inspector of Jiāozhǐ, enticed them to surrender.
On the day Rénshēn,
Yí, Prince of Chángshān, passed away.
On the day Jǐmǎo,
Liú Kāng, the Administrator of Línglíng, was convicted of killing innocent people,
imprisoned, and died.
In the eleventh month,
the bandits Xú Fèng and Mǎ Miǎn and others of Jiǔjiāng proclaimed themselves
"Supreme Generals"
and attacked and burned cities and towns.
On the day Jǐyǒu,
an order was issued that prisoners in all commanderies and kingdoms, in the central government prisons, whose crimes were not capital offenses and whose cases were not yet concluded,
should all have their sentences reduced by one degree and be exiled to the frontier;
those guilty of rebellion or high treason
were not to be subject to this order.
In the twelfth month,
the Jiǔjiāng bandit Huáng Hǔ and others attacked Héféi.
In this year,
groups of bandits plundered Xiānlíng.
Zhào Chōng, the Commandant of the Protectorate of the Qiāng, pursued and attacked the rebellious Qiāng at Zhānyīnhé,
and died in battle.
In the first month of spring of the first year of Yǒngxǐ (originally Jiā), on the day Wùxū,
the Emperor passed away in the front hall of Yùtáng
at the age of three.
Sùn, Prince of Qīnghé, was summoned to the capital.
Emperor Xiàozhì, personal name Zuǎn,
was the great-great-grandson of Sùzōng.
His great-grandfather was Kàng, Virtuous Prince of Qiānchéng;
his grandfather was Chǒng, Peaceful Prince of Lè'ān;
his father was Hóng, Filial Prince of Bóhǎi;
and his mother was Lady Chén.
When Emperor Chōng was unwell,
Jiǎmín Liáng Jì summoned the Emperor to the Dūtíng in Luòyáng.
After Emperor Chōng passed away,
the Empress Dowager and Jì decided on the succession within the Forbidden Palace.
On the day Bǐngchén,
Jì was sent with imperial credentials
to welcome the Emperor into the Nángōng with a blue-canopied carriage.
On the day Dīngsì,
he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Jiànpíng,
and on that same day, he ascended the imperial throne
at the age of eight.
On the day Jǐwèi,
Emperor Xiàochōng was buried at Huáilíng.
Zhāng Yīng and other bandits of Guǎnglín rebelled again,
attacking and killing the chiefs of Tángyì and Jiāngdū.
Xú Fèng and other bandits of Jiǔjiāng attacked and killed the chiefs of Qǔyáng and Dōngchéng.
On the day Jiǎshēn,
a visit was made to Gāomiào.
On the day Yǐyǒu,
a visit was made to Guāngwǔmiào.
In the second month,
Yú Xù, the Administrator of Yùzhāng, was imprisoned and died for bribery.
On the day Yǐyǒu,
a general amnesty was granted to all under heaven,
and people were granted noble ranks and bestowed with varying amounts of grain and silk.
The household and land previously confiscated from princes and marquises were restored.
Dào, Prince of Péngchéng, passed away.
The rebellious Qiāng submitted and surrendered to Liáng Bìng, Left Administrator of Fēngyì.
In the third month,
Mǎ Miǎn, a bandit from Jiǔjiāng, declared himself
"Yellow Emperor".
Téng Fǔ, the Commandant of Jiǔjiāng, attacked Mǎ Miǎn, Fàn Róng, and Zhōu Shēng,
greatly defeating and beheading them.
In the fourth month of summer, on the day Rénshēn,
there was a prayer for rain.
On the day Gēngchén,
Ān, Prince of Jìběi, passed away.
Lù Gōng and other bandits from Dānyáng besieged cities
and burned rest stops and temples.
Jiāng Hàn, the Administrator of Dānyáng, attacked and defeated them.
In the fifth month, on the day Jiǎwǔ,
an edict stated:
"I, though without virtue,
have been entrusted with governing the world,
and my administration has been unclear,
often missing the mark.
From spring to summer,
there has been a great drought and scorching heat,
causing my heart deep worry.
I have therefore performed prayers and bright sacrifices,
hoping to receive moistening favor.
Although rain was received before,
the winter wheat was somewhat damaged;
recently, the overcast clouds
have again cleared.
Waking and sleeping, I sigh endlessly,
burdened by sorrow.
Is it perhaps because the officials of two thousand *shí* and the prefects and chiefs have not upheld benevolence and harmony,
but have acted with cruelty and harshness?
Let all prisoners in the central government prisons whose crimes are not capital offenses and whose examinations are not yet concluded
be released without exception,
pending the autumn equinox.
For commanderies and kingdoms that have famous mountains and great marshes capable of generating clouds and rain,
let the officials of two thousand *shí* and the chief magistrates each purify themselves and offer prayers,
presenting their sincerity and performing all rites.
Moreover, military conscription has been continuous for years,
leading to deaths and displacement.
Some bodies remain uncollected,
while some coffins await burial.
I deeply lament this.
In ancient times, King Wén buried dry bones,
and people benefited from his virtue.
Now, I send envoys to investigate.
If there are no family members or if the poor lack resources,
let them be granted relief as appropriate,
to comfort the lonely souls."
In this month,
Xiè Ān from Xiàpéi volunteered to attack Xú Fèng and others,
and beheaded them.
On the day Bǐngchén,
an edict stated:
"Although Emperor Xiàoshāng did not long enjoy his reign,
he was enthroned for over a year,
and the rites between ruler and minister were established.
Emperor Xiào'ān succeeded to the unified enterprise,
yet previous generations arranged for Gōnglíng to be above Kānglíng,
inverting the proper sequence,
thus losing its order.
This is not how the solemnity of the ancestral temple should be observed,
nor how an eternal system should be passed down.
In ancient times, Duke Dìng corrected the order of sacrifices,
which the *Spring and Autumn Annals* lauded.
Therefore, let Gōnglíng be placed after Kānglíng,
and Xiānlíng after Gōnglíng,
to sequence their familial ranks
as a law for ten thousand generations."
In the sixth month,
the Xiānbēi raided Dàijùn.
In the seventh month of autumn, on the day Gēngyín,
Dài, Prince of Fùlíng, passed away.
Bandits from Lújiāng attacked Xúnyáng,
and then attacked Xūtái.
Téng Fǔ dispatched the Cavalry Commander Wáng Zhāng to attack and defeat them.
In the ninth month, on the day Gēngxū,
Grand Tutor Zhào Jùn passed away.
In the eleventh month of winter, on the day Jǐchǒu,
Hán Zhāo, the Administrator of Nányáng, was imprisoned and died for bribery.
On the day Bǐngwǔ,
Téng Fǔ, the Commandant of the Household, attacked the Guǎnglín bandit Zhāng Yīng,
and defeated him.
On the day Dīngwèi,
Zhào Xù, the Commandant of the Household, was executed in the marketplace for his crimes.
Huá Mèng, a bandit from Lìyáng, declared himself
"Black Emperor,"
and attacked and killed Yáng Cén, the Administrator of Jiǔjiāng.
Téng Fǔ led various generals to attack Mèng and others,
greatly defeating and beheading them.
In the first year of Běnchū, in the spring, first month, on the day bǐngshēn,
an edict stated:
“In ancient times, Yáo commanded the Four Sages
to revere the way of Heaven.
In the Great Plan’s nine divisions,
good and bad fortune had their signs.
Indeed, auspicious omens descend with harmony,
while anomalies arise from opposition and provocation.
Suppressing the subtle in response to the great
was esteemed by the former sages.
Recently,
the commanderies and kingdoms have been contemptuous and negligent of constitutional safeguards,
competing in cruelty and violence,
establishing their own regulations,
and ensnaring the innocent.
Some, swayed by personal likes and dislikes, expel senior officials,
indulging their favorites,
and unjustly punishing those with whom they harbor grudges,
leading to an endless stream of people
waiting at court to lodge complaints.
As old officials are sent off and new ones welcomed,
people are suffering from their harms,
and the accumulated grievances injure harmony,
leading to disasters and calamities.
The *Shū* says: ‘Illustrate virtue, be cautious in punishment.’
As spring begins and eastern work proceeds,
nurture the subtle and respect the beginning.
Therefore, instruct the officials concerned
that for crimes not warranting special death,
they should temporarily not investigate them,
so as to promote leniency.”
On the day rénzǐ,
Wáng Xǐ, the Grand Administrator of Guǎnglín, was imprisoned and died
for lingering during a bandit suppression campaign.
In the second month, on the day gēngchén,
an edict stated:
“The two commanderies of Jiǔjiāng and Guǎnglín have repeatedly suffered from banditry,
and their devastation is most severe.
The living have lost their livelihoods,
and the dead lie abandoned in the wilderness.
In ancient governance,
if even one thing did not find its proper place,
it was as if the ruler himself had caused it.
How much more so now, that our people
are enduring such hardship and poison.
This spring, a season for restraint,
is also the time to provide relief to the needy and distressed,
and to cover the bones and bury the corpses.
Therefore, mobilize grain from neighboring commanderies,
distribute provisions to the poor and weak,
collect and bury the desiccated remains,
and make every effort to provide burial and comfort,
to accord with Our intention.”
In the summer, fourth month, on the day gēngchén,
an order was issued for commanderies and kingdoms to recommend erudites of the classics,
aged fifty to seventy, to proceed to the Grand Academy.
From the Grand General down to those of six hundred *dàn* salary,
all were to send their sons to study.
After one year, they would be tested.
The top five would be appointed as Gentlemen,
the next five as Palace Attendants to the Crown Prince.

Furthermore, officials of one thousand *dàn* and six hundred *dàn*, clerks of the four bureaus, gentlemen of the three agencies, and younger marquises of the four influential families who already understood the classics
were to follow their respective family traditions.
Those with high merits would have their names submitted
and would be rewarded and promoted in due course.
In the fifth month, on the day gēngyín,
Liè'ān Wáng was transferred to become Bóhǎi Wáng.
The sea overflowed.
On the day wùshēn,
an imperial envoy was dispatched to inspect,
collect and bury those from Liè'ān and Běihǎi who had drowned in the flood,
and also to provide provisions to the poor and weak.
On the day gēngxū,
Táibái encroached upon Yínghuò.
In the sixth month, on the day dīngsì,
a general amnesty was proclaimed throughout the empire,
and the people were granted ranks, grain, and silk according to different grades.
In the intercalary month, on the day jiǎshēn,
Grand General Liáng Jì secretly poisoned and assassinated the Emperor.
The Emperor passed away in the front hall of the Yùtáng,
aged nine.
On the day dīnghài,
Grand Commandant Lǐ Gù was dismissed.
On the day wùzǐ,
Sītú Hú Guǎng became Grand Commandant,
Sīkōng Zhào Jiè became Sītú,
and they, along with Liáng Jì, jointly managed the affairs of the Imperial Secretariat.
Grand Servant Yuán Tāng became Sīkōng.
A eulogy states: “Upon Xiàoshùn’s initial enthronement,
talented men truly gathered.
Neither reforming nor rectifying,
they ultimately sank into favoritism.
Guardians passed on their authority,
and the empress’s family gained hereditary power.
Chōng, who died young and was unaware,
was assassinated for his intelligence.
The imperial line was broken and twisted by fate,
the heavenly succession ended thrice.”
Annals of Emperor Xiàohuán, Seventh
Emperor Xiàohuán, personal name Zhì,
was the great-grandson of Sùzōng.
His grandfather was Kāi, King Xiào of Héjiān;
his father was Yì, Marquis of Líwú;
his mother was Lady Yǎn.
When Yì died,
the Emperor inherited his title as Marquis.
In the first year of Běnchū,
Empress Dowager Liáng summoned the Emperor to the Xiàmén Tíng,
intending to marry him to her younger sister.
It happened that Emperor Zhì died,
so the Empress Dowager and her brother, Grand General Jì, decided upon a plan within the forbidden palace.
In the intercalary month, on the day gēngyín,
Jì was sent with an imperial staff,
with a royal blue canopy carriage,
to welcome the Emperor into the Nángōng.
On that same day, he ascended the imperial throne,
then aged fifteen.
The Empress Dowager still presided over court affairs.
In autumn, seventh month, on the day yǐmǎo,
Emperor Xiàozhì was buried at Jìnglíng.
Qí Wáng Xǐ died.
On the day xīnsì,
reverence was paid at the Gāomiào and Guāngwǔmiào.
On the day bǐngxū,
an edict stated:
“Filial and Incorrupt, and Incorrupt Officials, are all meant to govern cities and shepherd the people,
suppressing evil and promoting good,
which are the foundations of transforming customs,
and must always be followed.
Edicts have been repeatedly issued,
clearly and earnestly,
yet local officials treat them lightly,
thus becoming negligent and slow,
making wrong choices in selection,
harming the common people.
Although some corrections have been made recently,
they have not yet served as a warning or led to reform.
Currently, the Huái barbarians are not yet pacified,
and military expeditions are frequent,
the common people are weary and exhausted,
suffering from conscription and levies.
We hope that all officials
will show kindness to our toiling people,
cleanse themselves of corruption and impurity,
to pray for auspicious fortune.
Therefore, let it be commanded that only those who have completed their tenure of one hundred *dàn* salary,
for ten years or more,
and possess extraordinary talent and exceptional conduct,
may participate in selections.
Children and grandchildren of corrupt officials
shall not be nominated or recommended.
Block the source of evil and false recommendations,
so that those who are honest and uphold the Dao may be trusted in their integrity.
Let each clearly guard their responsibilities;
We shall observe the consequences.”
In the ninth month, on the day wùxū,
the imperial ancestor Kāi, King Xiào of Héjiān, was posthumously honored as Emperor Xiàomù,
and his consort, Lady Zhào, as Empress Xiàomù.
His imperial father, Yì, Marquis of Líwú, was honored as Emperor Xiàochóng.
In winter, tenth month, on the day jiǎwǔ,
his imperial mother, Lady Yǎn, was honored as Noble Lady of the Bóyuán Palace, Xiàochóng.
In the first year of Jiànhé, in the spring, first month, on the day xīnhài, the new moon,
there was a solar eclipse.
An edict commanded the Three Excellencies, Nine Ministers, and Commandants to each state what was gained or lost.
On the day wùwǔ,
a general amnesty was proclaimed throughout the empire.
Officials were granted one year of salary;
men were granted two ranks of nobility;
those who succeeded their fathers, and the Three Elders, Filial and Fraternal, and Industrious Farmers, were granted three ranks;
widows, widowers, orphans, the solitary, the severely ill, and the poor who could not support themselves were given grain,
five *hú* per person;
chaste women were given silk,
three bolts per person.
For areas where disasters had damaged forty percent or more,
the land tax was not to be collected;
for those with less damage,
the reduction was to be made according to the actual loss.
In the second month,
many people in Jīng and Yáng provinces starved to death.
Four bureau clerks were dispatched to travel separately and distribute relief.
Pèiguó reported that a yellow dragon was seen in Qiáo.
In summer, fourth month, on the day gēngyín,
there was an earthquake in the capital.
An edict commanded the Grand General, Excellencies, Ministers, and Commandants to each recommend one worthy and upright person, capable of speaking frankly and offering strong remonstrance.
It also ordered Marquises, Generals, Grandees, Imperial Censors, Envoys, officials of one thousand *dàn* and six hundred *dàn*,
Erudites, Counselors, and Gentlemen to each submit sealed memorials,
pointing out gains and losses.
Another edict commanded the Grand General, Excellencies, Ministers, commanderies, and kingdoms to each recommend one person of extreme filial piety and earnest conduct.
On the day réchén,
an edict stated that commanderies and kingdoms were not to coerce or expel senior officials.
If a senior official embezzled thirty *wàn* cash and was not reported,
the Inspector and officials of two thousand *dàn* salary would be guilty of condoning and avoiding punishment.
If anyone unauthorizedly lent seals of office to another,
they would be judged as committing murder
and executed publicly.
On the *bǐngwǔ* day,
an edict was issued to the commanderies and kingdoms that prisoners condemned to death should have their sentences reduced by one degree,
and not be flogged.
Only those plotting rebellion and great treason
were not to be subject to this decree.
Another edict stated:
