"Compared to the imperial tombs,
the time elapsed has been long,
the labor extensive,
and the penal laborers particularly toiled.
Recently, the rain has not fallen,
and dense clouds have dispersed again,
perhaps due to this.
Let those penal laborers working on the tombs have their sentences reduced by six months each."
In this month,
Fùlíng Wáng Dài's elder brother, Bóqiú Tínghóu Biàn, was established as Fùlíng Wáng.
Six places in the commanderies and kingdoms experienced ground fissures,
with water gushing and wells overflowing.
*Zhīcǎo* grew in the imperial treasury (*Zhōnghuáng Zàngfǔ*).
In the sixth month,
Grand Commandant Hú Guǎng was dismissed,
and Grand Minister of Agriculture Dù Qiáo became Grand Commandant.
In autumn, seventh month,
Bóhǎi Wáng Hóng died.
The emperor's younger brother, Líwú Hóu Kuí, was established as Bóhǎi Wáng.
In the eighth month, on the *yǐwèi* day,
Empress Liáng was established.
In the ninth month, on the *dīngmǎo* day,
the capital experienced an earthquake.
Grand Commandant Dù Qiáo was dismissed.
In winter, tenth month,
Minister of Works Zhào Jiè became Grand Commandant,
Minister of Education Yuán Tāng became Minister of Works,
and former Grand Commandant Hú Guǎng became Minister of Education.
In the eleventh month,
Jìyīn reported that a large five-colored bird was seen in Jǐshì.
On the *wùwǔ* day,
all death sentences in the empire were reduced by one degree,
and the convicts were sent to guard the borders.
Liú Wén of Qīnghé rebelled,
killing the Chancellor of the Kingdom, Shè Gǎo,
intending to establish Qīnghé Wáng Suàn as Son of Heaven;
the plot was discovered and he was executed.
Suàn was implicated, demoted to Wèishì Hóu,
exiled to Guìyáng,
and committed suicide.
Former Grand Commandants Lǐ Gù and Dù Qiáo were both imprisoned and died.
Lǐ Jiān, a bandit from Chénliú, proclaimed himself emperor,
and was executed.
In the second year, spring, first month, on the *jiǎzǐ* day,
the emperor underwent his capping ceremony.
On the *gēngwǔ* day,
a general amnesty was granted to the empire.
The kings of Héjiān and Bóhǎi were each granted one hundred *jīn* of gold,
and the kings of Péngchéng and other kingdoms were each granted fifty *jīn*;

princesses, Grand General, Three Excellencies, Special Advance, marquises, officials of two thousand *shí* and above, officials of two thousand *shí*, generals, grand masters, court gentlemen, minor officials, imperial retinue, the Four Clans, and the minor marquises of Liáng and Dèng, and below, were granted silk,
each according to their rank.
Those eighty years or older were granted rice, wine, and meat,
and those ninety years or older were given an additional two bolts of silk
and three *jīn* of cotton.
In the third month, on the *wùchén* day,
the emperor, accompanied by the Empress Dowager, visited the residence of Grand General Liáng Jì.
The Báimǎ Qiāng raided Guǎnghàn Shǔguó,
killing its chief officials.
The Inspector of Yìzhōu led the Bǎnshùn Mán to suppress and defeat them.
In summer, fourth month, on the *bǐngzǐ* day,
the emperor's younger brother, Shuò, was enfeoffed as Píngyuán Wáng,
to maintain the sacrifices to the Reverent Emperor.
The Reverent Emperor's consort, Lady Mǎ, was honored as Reverent Garden Noble Lady (*Xiàochóng Yuán Guìrén*).
Auspicious grain grew in the treasury of the Grand Minister of Agriculture.
In the fifth month, on the *guǐchǒu* day,
the Déyáng Hall and the Left Yèmén Gate in the Northern Palace's Yètíng caught fire,
and the imperial carriage moved to the Southern Palace.
In the sixth month,
Qīnghé was renamed Gānlíng,
and Ānpíng Wáng Dé's son, Jīng Hóu Lǐ, was established as Gānlíng Wáng.
In autumn, seventh month,
the capital experienced severe flooding.
Hédōng reported that trees were intertwined.
In winter, tenth month,
Chén Jǐng of Chángpíng styled himself
"Son of the Yellow Emperor" and
appointed officials;
also, Guǎn Bó of Nándùn called himself
"True Man."
Both plotted to raise an army
and were all executed.
In the third year, spring, third month, on the *jiǎshēn* day,
Péngchéng Wáng Dìng died.
In summer, fourth month, on the *dīngmǎo* day, the last day of the month,
there was a solar eclipse.
In the fifth month, on the *yǐhài* day,
an edict stated:
"It is heard that Heaven gave birth to the common people,
who are unable to govern themselves,
so it established rulers for them,
to shepherd them.
If the way of the ruler is upheld below,
then auspicious signs appear above;
if affairs lose their order,
then ominous portents are seen in the heavens.
Recently,
the sun was eclipsed and damaged,
its light obscured and dimmed.
I am reverent and fearful, contemplating in silence,
with no time to rest.
Does not the tradition say: 'When the sun is eclipsed, cultivate virtue;
when the moon is eclipsed, cultivate punishments'?
In the past, Emperor Xiàozhāng, pitying the prohibitions and exiles of previous generations,
in the first year of Jiànchū,
extended his benevolence to all,
allowing exiles to return to their former commanderies,
and those confiscated to be released as commoners.
How can we not emulate the virtuous governance of the former emperor!
Therefore, from the first year of Yǒngjiàn until this year,
all those involved in various evil deeds,
their relatives implicated,
and officials and common people whose death sentences were reduced to exile,
are all to return to their native commanderies;
only those who were confiscated are not subject to this order."
In the sixth month, on the *gēngzǐ* day,
an edict commanded the Grand General, Three Excellencies, Special Advance, and marquises,
along with ministers and colonels, to each recommend one worthy and upright person, capable of outspoken and extreme remonstrance.
On the *yǐmǎo* day,
the roof of the Xiànlíng mausoleum was struck by lightning.
In autumn, seventh month, on the *gēngshēn* day,
it rained meat in Lián Xiàn.
In the eighth month, on the *yǐchǒu* day,
a comet appeared in *Tiānshì*.
The capital experienced severe flooding.
In the ninth month, on the *jǐmǎo* day,
there was an earthquake.
On the *gēngyín* day,
the earth shook again.
An edict ordered that those sentenced to death and below, as well as fugitives, could redeem themselves,
each according to specific rates.
Five mountains in the commanderies and kingdoms collapsed.
In winter, tenth month,
Grand Commandant Zhào Jiè was dismissed.
Minister of Works Yuán Tāng became Grand Commandant,
and Grand Minister of Agriculture Zhāng Xīn of Hénèi became Minister of Works.
In the eleventh month, on the *jiǎshēn* day,
an edict stated:
"I have governed improperly,
with continuous disasters and calamities,
the three luminaries unclear,
and *yīn* and *yáng* in disarray.
Awake and asleep, I sigh,
feeling as if my head aches from illness.
Now in the capital's alleys,
the dead lie one upon another,
and in the commanderies and counties' fields,
this is seen everywhere,
greatly violating the principle of King Wén of Zhōu to cover exposed corpses.
For those with families who are too poor to bury their dead,
provide funds,
three thousand [cash] per person,
and three bolts of cloth for the chief mourner;
if there are no relatives,
they may be buried on state land,
with their names marked and identified,
and sacrifices offered for them.
Furthermore, penal laborers in work details,
if ill, should be provided with medicine,
and if they die, be buried with proper care.
Common people unable to support themselves or those displaced
should be given grain according to regulations.
All officials are urged to inspect
and diligently promote benevolent policies
to bring peace to our people."
In the first year of Hépíng, first month, on the *jiǎzǐ* day,
a general amnesty was granted to the empire,
and the reign era was changed to Hépíng.
On the Yǐchǒu day,
an imperial edict stated:
"Formerly, Our house met with misfortune,
and the Late Emperor (Xiāndì) passed away young.
Always considering the gravity of the main imperial lineage,
and deeply contemplating the blessing of a successor,
We consulted with the chief ministers,
and examined the omens and divinations.
Having appointed a sagacious and wise one,
We were able to establish the imperial enterprise,
and Heaven and man are in harmony,
all nations are peaceful.
The coming-of-age cap has already been donned,
and We were about to immediately entrust (the rule to him),
but in all directions there were bandits and rebels,
and it was still somewhat unsettled.
Therefore, We temporarily prolonged Our oversight of the government,
in order to await peace and tranquility.
Fortunately, relying on the assistance of Our trusted ministers in resisting aggression,
the remaining villains have been swept away,
the people are harmonious, and the year has been abundant.
Throughout the entire realm,
near and far are in accord.
Looking to the ancient principle of 'restoring the son to the enlightened ruler,'
and emulating the recent example of the former empress returning and handing over power,
now is an auspicious time.
The Emperor shall now formally assume rule.
All dukes, ministers, and officials,
reverently attend to your positions,
unite your efforts with one mind,
and strive together with the unity that can break metal.
'Then indeed great achievements will be made,'
is what is hoped for."
In the second month, the Fúfēng (Fúfēng) demonic rebel Péi Yōu (裴優) proclaimed himself Emperor,
and was executed.
On the Jiǎyín (Jiǎyín) day,
Empress Dowager Liáng (Liáng shì) passed away.
In the third month,
the imperial carriage moved to the Northern Palace (Běi Gōng).
On the Jiǎwǔ (Jiǎwǔ) day,
Empress Shùnliè (Shùnliè Huánghòu) was buried.
In summer, in the fifth month, on the Gēngchén (Gēngchén) day,
Noble Lady Yǎn (Yǎn Guìrén) of Bóyuán (Bóyuán) was honored as Empress Xiàochóng (Xiàochóng Huánghòu).
In autumn, in the seventh month,
a mountain in Zǐtóng (Zǐtóng) collapsed.
In winter, in the eleventh month, on the Xīnsì (Xīnsì) day,
the death penalty throughout the realm was reduced by one degree,
and (those convicted) were exiled to border garrisons.
In spring, in the first month of the first year of Yuánjiā (Yuánjiā),
there was an epidemic in the capital,
and the Grand Master of Brightness (Guānglù Dàfū) was sent with doctors and medicine to investigate and patrol.
On the Guǐyǒu (Guǐyǒu) day,
a general amnesty was declared throughout the realm,
and the reign era was changed to Yuánjiā (Yuánjiā).
In the second month,
there was a severe epidemic in Jiǔjiāng (Jiǔjiāng) and Lújiāng (Lújiāng).
On the Jiǎwǔ (Jiǎwǔ) day,
Jiàn (Jiàn), Prince of Héjiān (Héjiān Wáng), passed away.
In summer, in the fourth month, on the Jǐchǒu (Jǐchǒu) day,
Dé (Dé), Prince of Ānpíng (Ānpíng Wáng), passed away.
There was a drought in the capital.
There was famine in Rènchéng (Rènchéng) and the kingdom of Liáng (Liáng Guó),
with people resorting to cannibalism.
The Minister of the Masses (Sītú) Zhāng Xīn (Zhāng Xīn) was dismissed,
and the Superintendent of the Imperial Household (Guānglùxūn) Wú Xióng (Wú Xióng) became Minister of the Masses (Sītú).
In autumn, in the seventh month,
the Mán (Mán) people of Wǔlíng (Wǔlíng) rebelled.
In winter, in the tenth month,
the Minister of Works (Sīkōng) Hú Guǎng (Hú Guǎng) was dismissed.
In the eleventh month, on the Xīnsì (Xīnsì) day,
there was an earthquake in the capital.
In the intercalary month, on the Gēngwǔ (Gēngwǔ) day,
Chóng (Chóng), Prince of Rènchéng (Rènchéng Wáng), passed away.
The Grand Herald (Tàicháng) Huáng Qióng (Huáng Qióng) became Minister of Works (Sīkōng).
In spring, in the first month of the second year,
Wáng Jìng (Wáng Jìng), Chief Clerk (Zhǎngshǐ) of Xīchéng (Xīchéng), was killed by the Kingdom of Yútián (Yútián Guó).
On the Bǐngchén (Bǐngchén) day,
there was an earthquake in the capital.
In summer, in the fourth month, on the Jiǎyín (Jiǎyín) day,
Empress Xiàochóng (Xiàochóng Huánghòu) Yǎn (Yǎn shì) passed away.
On the Gēngwǔ (Gēngwǔ) day,
Bào (Bào), Prince of Chángshān (Chángshān Wáng), passed away.
In the fifth month, on the Xīnmǎo (Xīnmǎo) day,
Empress Xiàochóng (Xiàochóng Huánghòu) was buried at Bólíng (Bólíng).
In autumn, in the seventh month, on the Gēngchén (Gēngchén) day,
there was a solar eclipse.
In the eighth month,
Jìyīn (Jìyīn) reported that a yellow dragon was seen at Gōuyáng (Gōuyáng),
and Jīnchéng (Jīnchéng) reported that a yellow dragon was seen at Yǔnjiē (Yǔnjiē).
In winter, in the tenth month, on the Yǐhài (Yǐhài) day,
there was an earthquake in the capital.
In the eleventh month,
the Minister of Works (Sīkōng) Huáng Qióng (Huáng Qióng) was dismissed.
In the twelfth month,
the Special Advanced Official (Tèjìn) Zhào Jiè (Zhào Jiè) became Minister of Works (Sīkōng).
Hé Mín (Hé Mín), Grand Administrator (Tàishǒu) of Yòuběipíng (Yòuběipíng), was found guilty of corruption,
imprisoned, and died.
In spring, in the second month of the first year of Yǒngxīng (Yǒngxīng),
Zhāngyè (Zhāngyè) reported that a white deer was seen.
In the third month, on the Dīnghài (Dīnghài) day,
(the Emperor) visited Hóngchí (Hóngchí).
In summer, in the fifth month, on the Bǐngshēn (Bǐngshēn) day,
a general amnesty was declared throughout the realm,
and the reign era was changed to Yǒngxīng (Yǒngxīng).
On the Dīngyǒu (Dīngyǒu) day,
Guǎng (Guǎng), Prince of Jìnán (Jìnán Wáng), passed away.
He had no heir,
so his kingdom was abolished.
In autumn, in the seventh month,
there were locust infestations in thirty-two commanderies and kingdoms.
The Yellow River overflowed.
The common people were starving and destitute,
starving people wandering on the roads,
amounting to hundreds of thousands of households,
with Jìzhōu (Jìzhōu) being especially severe.
An edict ordered local authorities to provide relief to the destitute,
and comfort and settle them in their livelihoods.
In winter, in the tenth month,
the Grand Commandant (Tàiwèi) Yuán Tāng (Yuán Tāng) was dismissed,
and the Grand Herald (Tàicháng) Hú Guǎng (Hú Guǎng) became Grand Commandant (Tàiwèi).
The Minister of the Masses (Sītú) Wú Xióng (Wú Xióng) was dismissed,
and the Minister of Works (Sīkōng) Zhào Jiè (Zhào Jiè) was dismissed;
the Grand Coachman (Tàipú) Huáng Qióng (Huáng Qióng) became Minister of the Masses (Sītú),
and the Superintendent of the Imperial Household (Guānglùxūn) Fáng Zhí (Fáng Zhí) became Minister of Works (Sīkōng).
In the eleventh month, on the Dīngchǒu (Dīngchǒu) day,
an imperial edict reduced the death penalty throughout the realm by one degree,
and (those convicted) were exiled to border garrisons.
This year,
Yīng Fèng (Yīng Fèng), Grand Administrator (Tàishǒu) of Wǔlíng (Wǔlíng), enticed and persuaded the rebellious Mán (Mán) people,
and they submitted.
In spring, in the first month of the second year, on the Jiǎwǔ (Jiǎwǔ) day,
a general amnesty was declared throughout the realm.
In the second month, on the Xīnchǒu (Xīnchǒu) day,
Inspectors (Cìshǐ) and high-ranking officials (Èrqiānshí) were for the first time permitted to observe a three-year mourning period.
On the Guǐmǎo (Guǐmǎo) day,
there was an earthquake in the capital,
and an imperial edict ordered dukes, ministers, and commandants (Xiàowèi) each to recommend one person who was virtuous, upright, and able to speak frankly and offer strong remonstrance.
The edict stated:
"Recently, the stars have moved irregularly,
and the spirit of the earth has been shaken.
The descent of disasters and anomalies
is certainly not without reason.
We must admonish Ourselves and reform the government,
hoping for some improvement.
As for those carriages and clothing regulations that are extravagant or overly ornate,
all should be reduced and simplified.
Commanderies and counties must practice frugality and restraint,
reaffirming old regulations,
following the precedents of the Yǒngpíng (Yǒngpíng) era."
In the sixth month,
the Sì River (Sìshuǐ) in Péngchéng (Péngchéng) swelled and flowed upstream.
An imperial edict to the Colonel Director of the Retainers (Sīlì Xiàowèi) and the regional Inspectors (Cìshǐ) stated:
"Locust disasters have caused harm,
water calamities have arrived again,
the five grains have failed,
and people have no reserves.
Therefore, order the affected commanderies and kingdoms to plant turnips (wújīng) to help feed the people."
There were locusts in the capital.
Mount Qú (Qúshān) in Dōnghǎi (Dōnghǎi) collapsed.
In the ninth month, on the Dīngmǎo (Dīngmǎo) day, the new moon,
there was a solar eclipse.
An imperial edict stated:
"The court administration has lost its balance,
Heaven has caused droughts,
river spirits have sent forth floods,
locusts have bred and spread,
destroying all Our grains.
The sun has lost its light,
and famines have repeatedly arrived.
As for the commanderies and counties not harmed by disaster,
they ought to store (grain) for the starving.
The world is one family;
that which quickly does not rot,
is a national treasure.
Therefore, forbid commanderies and kingdoms from selling alcohol,
and for sacrifices, use just enough."
The Grand Commandant (Tàiwèi) Hú Guǎng (Hú Guǎng) was dismissed,
and the Minister of the Masses (Sītú) Huáng Qióng (Huáng Qióng) became Grand Commandant (Tàiwèi).
In the intercalary month,
the Superintendent of the Imperial Household (Guānglùxūn) Yǐn Sòng (Yǐn Sòng) became Minister of the Masses (Sītú).
The death penalty throughout the realm was reduced by one degree,
and (those convicted) were exiled to border garrisons.
Lǐ Bó (Lǐ Bó) of Shǔjùn (Shǔjùn) falsely claimed to be of the imperial clan,
and was to be established as
"Emperor Tàichū" (Tàichū Huángdì).
He was executed.
In winter, in the eleventh month, on the Jiǎchén (Jiǎchén) day,
a grand hunt was held in the Shànglín Imperial Park (Shànglín Yuàn),
and then (the Emperor) proceeded to Hángǔ Pass (Hángǔ Guān).
Money was bestowed upon people aged ninety and above along the roadside (where the imperial procession passed),
with varying amounts.
Rebels, including Gōngsūn Jǔ (Gōngsūn Jǔ) from Tàishān (Tàishān) and Lángyá (Lángyá), rebelled,
and killed chief officials.
In spring, in the first month of the first year of Yǒngshòu (Yǒngshòu), on the Wùshēn (Wùshēn) day,
a general amnesty was declared throughout the realm,
and the reign era was changed to Yǒngshòu (Yǒngshòu).
In the second month,
Sīlì and Jìzhōu suffered from famine;
people devoured each other.
An edict commanded provinces and commanderies to provide relief to the poor and weak.
If kings, marquises, officials, or commoners had accumulated grain,
three-tenths of it would be taken,
to assist in lending;
for commoners and officials,
this would be purchased with 현錢 (xiànqián, existing money).
Kings and marquises would be repaid only with new rent.
In summer, the fourth month,
a white crow appeared in Qíguó.
In the sixth month,
the Luò River overflowed,
destroying the Hóngdé Yuàn.
Nányáng experienced severe floods.
Sīkōng Fáng Zhí was dismissed,
and Tàicháng Hán Yǎn became Sīkōng.
An imperial edict declared that those in Tàishān and Lángyá who had encountered bandits
should be exempt from paying rent and taxes,
and be excused from corvée labor and poll tax for three years.
Another edict commanded that for those whose bodies were lost or swept away by floods,
commandery and county officials should search for and bury them;
and for those who died due to being crushed or drowned in the sudden disaster,
those aged seven and above would be granted money,
two thousand per person.
For destroyed homes
and lost grain,
the extremely poor would be given grain rations,
two *hú* per person.
Mountains collapsed in Bā Jùn and Yìzhōu Jùn.
In autumn, the seventh month,
the offices of Tàishān and Lángyá Dūwèi were first established.
The Southern Xiōngnú Zuǒ Yùjiān Táiqí and Jùqú Bódé rebelled,
raiding Měijì.
Āndìng Shǔguó Dūwèi Zhāng Huàn attacked and suppressed them.
In the second year, spring, the first month,
eunuchs were first permitted to observe three years of mourning.
In the second month, on the *jiǎshēn* day,
Dōnghǎi Wáng Zhēn passed away.
In the third month,
the Yí of Shǔjùn Shǔguó rebelled.
In autumn, the seventh month,
the Xiānbēi raided Yúnzhōng.
Bandits from Tàishān, Gōngsūn Jǔ and others, raided Qīng, Yǎn, and Xú, the three provinces.
Zhōnglángjiàng Duàn Jiǒng was dispatched to suppress them;
he defeated and beheaded them.
In winter, the eleventh month,
the office of Tàiguān Yòujiānchéng was established.
In the twelfth month,
the capital experienced an earthquake.
In the third year, spring, the first month, on the *jǐwèi* day,
a general amnesty was proclaimed throughout the empire.
In summer, the fourth month,
the Mán Yí of Jiǔzhēn rebelled.
Tàishǒu Ér Shì attacked them,
and was killed in battle;
Jiǔzhēn Dūwèi Wèi Lǎng was dispatched to strike and defeat them.
They then re-established their stronghold in Rìnán.
In the intercalary month, on the last day of *gēngchén*,
there was a solar eclipse.
In the sixth month,
Xiǎohuángmén were first appointed as Shǒugōng Lìng,
and the office of Nǔcóng Yòupúyè was established.
The capital suffered from locusts.
In autumn, the seventh month,
Hedōng experienced an earthquake.
In winter, the eleventh month,
Sītú Yǐn Cháng passed away.
The Mán of Chángshā rebelled,
raiding Yìyáng.
Sīkōng Hán Yǎn became Sītú,
and Tàicháng Běihǎi Sūn Lǎng became Sīkōng.
In the first year of Yánxī, spring, the third month, on the *jǐyǒu* day,
the office of Hóngdé Yuàn Lìng was first established.
In summer, the fifth month, on the *jǐyǒu* day,
a grand assembly was held for high officials and below,
and rewards were distributed according to rank.
On the last day of *jiǎxū*,
there was a solar eclipse.
The capital suffered from locusts.
In the sixth month, on the *wùyín* day,
a general amnesty was proclaimed throughout the empire,
and the era name was changed to Yánxī.
On the *bǐngxū* day,
Bólíng Jùn was established by partitioning Zhōngshān,
to serve the imperial mausoleums of Xiàochóng.
A great rain sacrifice was performed.
In autumn, the seventh month, on the *jǐsì* day,
Yúnyáng experienced an earthquake.
On the *jiǎzǐ* day,
Tàiwèi Huáng Qióng was dismissed,
and Tàicháng Hú Guǎng became Tàiwèi.
In winter, the tenth month,
a hunting expedition was held in Guǎngchéng,
then the emperor proceeded to the Shànglín Yuàn.
In the twelfth month,
the Xiānbēi raided the border.
Shǐ Xiōngnú Zhōnglángjiàng Zhāng Huàn led the Southern Chányú to attack and defeat them.
In the second year, spring, the second month,
the Xiānbēi raided Yànmén.
On the *jǐhài* day,
Fùlíng Wáng Biàn passed away.
The Yí of Shǔjùn raided Cánlíng,
killing the county magistrate.
In the third month,
the observation of three years of mourning by Cìshǐ and 2000-Picul officials was again prohibited.
In summer,
the capital experienced heavy rain.
In the sixth month,
the Xiānbēi raided Liáodōng.
In autumn, the seventh month,
the Xiǎnyáng Yuàn was first constructed,
and an Assistant (chéng) was appointed.
On the *bǐngwǔ* day,
Empress Liáng passed away.
On the *yǐchǒu* day,
Empress Yìxiàn was buried at Yìlíng.
Dàjiāngjūn Liáng Jì plotted rebellion.
In the eighth month, on the *dīngchǒu* day,
the Emperor presided in the front palace,
and issued an edict for Sīlì Xiàowèi Zhāng Biāo to lead troops to surround Liáng Jì's mansion,
and seize the Dàjiāngjūn's seal and sash.
Liáng Jì and his wife both committed suicide.
Wèiwèi Liáng Shú, Hénányǐn Liáng Yìn, Túnqí Xiàowèi Liáng Ràng, Yuèqí Xiàowèi Liáng Zhōng, Chángshuǐ Xiàowèi Liáng Jǐ,
and dozens of their relatives, both internal and external,
were all executed.
Tàiwèi Hú Guǎng was dismissed due to his association.
Sītú Hán Yǎn and Sīkōng Sūn Lǎng were imprisoned.
On the *rénwǔ* day,
Empress Dèng was enthroned,
and Yìlíng was posthumously reduced to a concubine's tomb.
The imperial edict stated:
"Liáng Jì was treacherous and tyrannical,
corrupting the imperial court.
Emperor Xiàozhì was intelligent and precocious,
which filled Liáng Jì's heart with jealousy and fear,
leading him to secretly poison him.
Empress Dowager Yǒnglè was of supreme reverence, second to none,
yet Liáng Jì also obstructed her,
forbidding her return to the capital,
thus separating me from my mother's love,
and severing the bond of parental care.
His calamities were profound and great,
his crimes accumulated daily.
Relying on the spiritual power of the ancestral temples,
and with the fervent advice of Zhōngchángshì Shàn Chāo, Xú Huáng, Jù Yuàn, Zuǒ Guàn,
Táng Héng, and Shàngshū Lìng Yǐn Xūn,
with internal and external cooperation,
within a moment,
the tyrannical rebel was executed.
This truly is a blessing from the altars of soil and grain,
and the strength of my ministers,
and suitable for distributing celebrations and rewards,
to repay loyal service.
Therefore, Shàn Chāo and the other five men are enfeoffed as county marquises,
and Yǐn Xūn and the other seven men are enfeoffed as *tínghóu* (marquises of a post-station)."
Thus, old favors and private connections
led to many receiving enfeoffments and noble titles.
Dàsīnóng Huáng Qióng became Tàiwèi,
Guānglù Dàfū Zhōngshān Zhù Tián became Sītú,
and Dàhónglú Liángguó Shèng Yǔn became Sīkōng.
The office of Mìshū Jiān was first established.
In winter, the tenth month, on the *rénshēn* day,
the emperor made a tour to Cháng'ān.
On the *yǐyǒu* day,
he visited Wèiyáng Gōng.
On the *jiǎwǔ* day,
sacrifices were offered at the Gāomiào.
In the eleventh month, on the *gēngzǐ* day,
he then performed rites at the eleven imperial mausoleums.
On the *rènyín* day,
Zhōngchángshì Shàn Chāo was made Chējì Jiāngjūn.
In the twelfth month, on the *jǐsì* day,
the emperor returned from Cháng'ān.
The commoners of Cháng'ān were granted ten *hú* of grain per person,
those in the mausoleum districts five *hú* per person,
and those in counties traversed by the imperial retinue three *hú* per person.
The Shāodāng and eight other types of Qiāng rebelled,
raiding Lǒngyòu.
Hùqiāng Xiàowèi Duàn Jiǒng pursued and attacked them at Luótíng,
defeating them.
The kingdom of Tiānzhú came to offer tribute.
In the third year, spring, the first month, on the *bǐngshēn* day,
a general amnesty was proclaimed throughout the empire.
On the *bǐngwǔ* day,
Chējì Jiāngjūn Shàn Chāo passed away.
In the intercalary month,
the Shāohé Qiāng rebelled,
raiding Zhāngyè.
Hùqiāng Xiàowèi Duàn Jiǒng pursued and attacked them at Jīshí,
utterly defeating them.
Báimǎ Lìng Lǐ Yún was imprisoned and died
for his frank remonstrance.
In the summer, fourth month,
Shàngjùn reported that sweet dew had fallen.
In the fifth month, on the day Jiǎxū,
a mountain in Hàngzhōng collapsed.
In the sixth month, on the day Xīnchǒu,
Sītú Zhù Tián passed away.
In autumn, seventh month,
Sīkōng Shèng Yǔn became Sītú,
and Tàicháng Yú Fàng became Sīkōng.
The Mán of Chángshā plundered the commandery borders.
In the ninth month,
the bandits Láo Bǐng and others from Tàishān and Lángxié rebelled again,
plundering the common people.
Yùshǐ Zhōngchéng Zhào Mǒu
was sent with a staff of authority to supervise the commanderies and prefectures in suppressing them.
On the day Dīnghài,
an edict ordered that officials with no duties should temporarily have their stipends cut,
but in years of abundance, it would be as before.
In winter, eleventh month,
the Mán chieftain from Rìnán led his people to the commandery and surrendered.
The Lèjiě Qiāng besieged Yúnjiē,
and Duàn Jiǒng attacked and defeated them.
The Tàishān bandit Shūsūn Wúfàng attacked and killed the Dūwèi Hóu Zhāng.
In the twelfth month,
Zhōnglángjiàng Zōng Zī was sent to attack and defeat him.
The Wǔlíng Mán plundered Jiānglíng.
Chēqí Jiāngjūn Féng Gǔn attacked them,
and they all surrendered and dispersed.
Jīngzhōu Cìshǐ Dù Shàng attacked the Chángshā Mán,
and pacified them.
In the fourth year, spring, first month, on the day Xīnyǒu,
the Jiādé Diàn in Nángōng caught fire.
On the day Wùzǐ,
the Bǐng Shǔ caught fire.
There was a great plague.
In the second month, on the day Rénchén,
the Wǔkù caught fire.
Sītú Shèng Yǔn was dismissed,
and Dàsīnóng Zhǒng Gǎo became Sītú.
In the third month,
the office of Yòupúshè was abolished.
Tàiwèi Huáng Qióng was dismissed.
In summer, fourth month,
Tàicháng Liú Jǔ became Tàiwèi.
On the day Jiǎyín,
Bó, son of Hèjiān Wáng Kāi, was enfeoffed as Rènchéng Wáng.
In the fifth month, on the day Xīnyǒu,
a comet appeared in the constellation Xīn.
On the day Dīngmǎo,
the Chángshòumén of Yuánlíng caught fire.
On the day Jǐmǎo,
it hailed in the capital.
In the sixth month,
Jīngzhào, Fúfēng, and Liángzhōu experienced earthquakes.
On the day Gēngzǐ,
Dàishān and Bóyòuláishān both collapsed and split.
On the day Jǐyǒu,
a general amnesty was proclaimed throughout the empire.
Sīkōng Yú Fàng was dismissed,
and former Tàiwèi Huáng Qióng became Sīkōng.
The Yi from Jiànwéi Shǔguó plundered the common people.
Yìzhōu Cìshǐ Shān Yù attacked and defeated them.
The Língwú Qiāng, along with various Xiānlíng tribes, rebelled,
plundering Sānfǔ.
In autumn, seventh month,
there was a rain-making ceremony in the capital.
The stipends of Gōng, Qīng, and below were reduced,
and half the rent was levied from kings and marquises.
Money for the sale of Guānnèi Hóu titles, Hǔbēn, Yǔlín, Tíqí camp soldiers, and Wǔdàfū ranks varied.
In the ninth month,
Sīkōng Huáng Qióng was dismissed,
and Dàhónglú Liú Chǒng became Sīkōng.
In winter, tenth month,
the kingdom of Tiānzhú came to present tribute.
Huáng Wǔ of Nányáng, along with Huì Dé of Xiāngchéng and Lè Jìyǎo of Kūnyáng, were accused of making false statements,
and were all executed.
The Xiānlíng Shéndī Qiāng, along with various Qiāng tribes, plundered Bìng and Liáng provinces.
In the eleventh month,
Zhōnglángjiàng Huángfǔ Guī attacked and defeated them.
In the twelfth month,
the king of Fúyú sent an envoy to present tribute.
In the fifth year, spring, first month,
the office of Tàiguān Yòujiānchéng was abolished.
On the day Rénwǔ,
the Bǐng Shǔ in Nángōng caught fire.
In the third month,
the Shéndī Qiāng plundered Zhāngyè and Jiǔquán.
On the day Rénwǔ,
Jìběi Wáng Cì passed away.
In summer, fourth month,
bandits arose in Chángshā,
plundering Guìyáng and Cāngwú.
Startled horses and runaway elephants charged into the palace.
On the day Yǐchǒu,
the eastern tower gate of Gōnglíng caught fire.
On the day Wùchén,
the Hǔbēn Yèmén caught fire.
On the day Jǐsì,
the western gate of Tàixué collapsed on its own.
In the fifth month,
the garden and private residence of Kānglíng caught fire.
Bandits arose in Chángshā and Línglíng,
attacking Guìyáng, Cāngwú, Nánhǎi, and Jiāozhǐ.
Yùshǐ Zhōngchéng Shèng Xiū was sent to supervise the commanderies and prefectures in suppressing them,
but failed.
On the day Yǐhài,
there was an earthquake in the capital.
An edict ordered Gōng and Qīng to each submit memorials on affairs of state.
On the day Jiǎshēn,
the Chénglù Shǔ in the Zhōngcángfǔ caught fire.
In autumn, seventh month, on the day Jǐwèi,
the Chéngshàntà in Nángōng caught fire.
The Niǎowú Qiāng plundered Hànyáng, Lǒngxī, and Jīnchéng.
Troops from the various commanderies attacked and defeated them.
In the eighth month, on the day Gēngzǐ,
an edict ordered that Hǔbēn and Yǔlín personnel who resided in temples but were not on duty should have half their stipends reduced,
and not be given winter clothes;
Gōng, Qīng, and below should be given half their winter clothes.
Bandits from Ài Xiàn burned and plundered the commandery and counties of Chángshā,
plundered Yìyáng,
and killed its magistrate.
Moreover, the Línglíng Mán also rebelled,
plundering Chángshā.
On the day Jǐmǎo,
the office of Lángxié Dūwèi was abolished.
In winter, tenth month,
the Wǔlíng Mán rebelled,
plundering Jiānglíng.
Nánjùn Tàishǒu Lǐ Sù was dismissed for fleeing and abandoning the market.
On the day Xīnchǒu,
Tàicháng Féng Gǔn was made Chēqí Jiāngjūn
to suppress them.
Stipends for Gōng, Qīng, and below were borrowed.
Also, the rent from kings and marquises was exchanged to aid military provisions,
and money from the Zhuólóng Zhōngcángfǔ was issued to return it.
In the eleventh month,
Féng Gǔn greatly defeated the rebellious Mán in Wǔlíng.
Jīngzhào Hǔyá Dūwèi Zōng Qiān was imprisoned and died for corruption.
The Diānnà Qiāng plundered Wǔwēi, Zhāngyè, and Jiǔquán.
Tàiwèi Liú Jǔ was dismissed,
and Tàicháng Yáng Bǐng became Tàiwèi.
In the sixth year, spring, second month, on the day Wùwǔ,
Sītú Zhǒng Gǎo passed away.
In the third month, on the day Wùxū,
a general amnesty was proclaimed throughout the empire.
Wèiwèi Yǐngchuān Xǔ Xǔ became Sītú.
In summer, fourth month, on the day Xīnhài,
the eastern bureau of Kānglíng caught fire.
In the fifth month,
the Xiānbēi plundered Liáodōng Shǔguó.
In autumn, seventh month, on the day Jiǎshēn,
the garden and private residence of Pínglíng caught fire.
The bandits Lǐ Yán and others from Guìyáng plundered the commandery borders.
The Wǔlíng Mán rebelled again.
Tàishǒu Chén Fèng engaged them in battle,
greatly defeating and forcing them to surrender.
Lǒngxī Tàishǒu Sūn Qiāng attacked the Diānnà Qiāng
and defeated them.
In the eighth month,
Chēqí Jiāngjūn Féng Gǔn was dismissed.
In winter, tenth month, on the day Bǐngchén,
a hunting expedition was held in Guǎngchéng.
They then proceeded to Hángǔguān and Shànglínyuàn.
In the eleventh month,
Sīkōng Liú Chǒng was dismissed.
Bandits from Nánhǎi plundered the commandery borders.
In the twelfth month,
Wèiwèi Zhōu Jǐng became Sīkōng.
In the seventh year, spring, first month, on the day Gēngyín,
Pèi Wáng Róng passed away.
In the third month, on the day Guǐhài,
a meteorite fell in Hù.
In summer, fourth month, on the day Bǐngyín,
Liáng Wáng Chéng passed away.
In the fifth month, on the day Jǐchǒu,
it hailed in the capital.
In autumn, seventh month, on the day Xīnmǎo,
Zhào Wáng Gān passed away.
On Yěwángshān, there was a dead dragon.
Jīngzhōu Cìshǐ Dù Shàng attacked the bandits and Mán Yi of Línglíng and Guìyáng,
greatly defeating and pacifying them.
In winter, tenth month, on the day Rénýín,
the Emperor made a southern tour.
On the day Gēngshēn,
he visited Zhānglíng,
offered sacrifices at the old residence,
and then performed rites at the ancestral temple in the park,
bestowing gifts of varying amounts upon the guards, magistrates, and those below.
On the day Wùchén,
he visited Yúnmèng,
overlooking the Hànshuǐ.
Returning,
he visited Xīnyě,
and offered sacrifices at the temples of Húyáng,
Xīnyě Gōngzhǔ, Lǔ Āiwáng, and Shòuzhāng Jìnghóu.
Hùqiāng Xiàowèi Duàn Jiǒng attacked the Dāngjiān Qiāng,
and defeated them.
On the *xīnchǒu* day of the twelfth month,
the imperial carriage returned to the palace.
In the first month of spring of the eighth year,
the emperor dispatched Zhōng Chángshì Zuǒ Huàn to Kǔ Xiàn
to sacrifice to Lǎozǐ.
Bóhǎi Wáng Kuī plotted rebellion,
and was demoted to Yǐngtáo Wáng.
On the *bǐngshēn* day, the last day of the month,
there was a solar eclipse.
An edict ordered dukes, ministers, and commandants to recommend men of talent and uprightness.
In the second month, on the *jǐyǒu* day,
a yellow dragon was seen at the Jiādé Bureau of the Nángōng.
A fire broke out at the Qiānqiū Wànsuì Palace.
Tàipú Zuǒ Chēng committed suicide due to his crimes.
On the *guǐhài* day,
Empress Dèng was deposed.
Hénán Yǐn Dèng Wànshì
and Hǔbēn Zhōnglángjiāng Dèng Huì were imprisoned and died.
Hùqiāng Xiàowèi Duàn Jiǒng attacked the Hǎnjiě Qiāng,
and defeated them.
On the *xīnsì* day of the third month,
a general amnesty was proclaimed throughout the empire.
In the fourth month of summer, on the *jiǎyín* day,
a fire broke out at the Ānlíng Imperial Garden and Ancestral Temple.
On the *dìngsì* day,
the local shrines in commanderies and states were demolished.
The Yellow River ran clear in Jìyīn, Dōngjùn, and Jìběi.
In the fifth month, on the *rénshēn* day,
the office of Tàishān Dūwèi was abolished.
On the *bǐngxū* day,
Tàiwèi Yáng Bǐng passed away.
In the sixth month, on the *bǐngchén* day,
the ground cracked in Gōushì.
Hú Lán and Zhū Gài from Guìyáng rebelled again,
attacking and seizing commanderies and counties,
and then plundering Línglíng.
Línglíng Tàishǒu Chén Qiú resisted them.
Zhōnglángjiāng Dù Shàng and Chángshā Tàishǒu Kàng Xiá Mǔ Suān Yīng Bǐng Gài were sent,
and they were utterly defeated and beheaded.
Cāngwú Tàishǒu Zhāng Wèi was captured by bandits,
and Guìyáng Tàishǒu Rèn Yìn betrayed the enemy out of cowardice.
Both were executed in the market.
In the intercalary month, on the *jiǎwǔ* day,
fires broke out at the Gōuxùn behind the Chángqiū Héhuān Palace in the Nángōng, the Yètíng, and the Shuòpíng Bureau.
In the sixth month,
Duàn Jiǒng attacked the Dāngjiān Qiāng in Huángzhōng,
and utterly defeated them.
In the seventh month of autumn,
Tàizhōng Dàfū Chén Fán became Tàiwèi.
In the eighth month, on the *wùchén* day,
an order was first issued for commanderies and states to collect a tax of money per *mǔ* from landowners.
In the ninth month, on the *dìngwèi* day,
there was an earthquake in the capital.
In the tenth month of winter,
Sīkōng Zhōu Jǐng was dismissed,
and Tàicháng Liú Mào became Sīkōng.
On the *xīnsì* day,
the noble lady Dòu was established as empress.
Bóhǎi demon bandits Gài Dēng and others
proclaimed
"Tàishàng Huángdì" (Supreme Emperor),
possessing jade seals, *guī*, *bì*, and iron tallies.
They appointed each other to various positions,
but all were executed.
In the eleventh month, on the *rénzǐ* day,
fires broke out at the western gallery of Déyáng Hall and the northern temple of Huángmén,
extending to the Guǎngyì and Shénhǔ Gates,
burning and killing people.
Zhōng Chángshì Guǎn Bà was sent to Kǔ Xiàn
to sacrifice to Lǎozǐ.
In the first month of spring of the ninth year, on the *xīnmǎo* day, the first day of the month,
there was a solar eclipse.
An edict ordered dukes, ministers, commandants, and commanderies and states to recommend filial sons.
Dài Yì from Pèiguó found a golden seal
with no inscription.
He then, together with Lóng Shàng and others from Guǎnglíng, jointly worshipped a well
and made talismans and writings,
proclaiming
"Tàishàng Huáng" (Supreme Emperor).
They were all executed.
On the *jǐyǒu* day,
an edict stated:
"For consecutive years, harvests have been poor,
and the people are mostly hungry and impoverished,
further suffering from floods, droughts, epidemics, and diseases.
Banditry and conscription are especially severe in the southern provinces.
Calamities and eclipses repeatedly warn us.
The disorder of governance lies with me,
and I have incurred these ominous signs.
Therefore, order the Dà Sīnóng to cease all requisitions and collections for this year,
and for those from previous years that have not yet been completed,
do not demand them further.
For commanderies afflicted by disasters, droughts, or bandits,
do not collect rent;
for the remaining commanderies, collect only half."
In the third month, on the *guǐsì* day,
there was a moving light in the capital,
causing people to be alarmed and agitated.
Four or five tenths of the population in Sīlì and Yùzhōu died of starvation,
some even leading to the extermination of entire households.
Officials from the Three Bureaus were dispatched to provide relief and provisions.
Chénliú Tàishǒu Wéi Yì committed suicide due to bribery.
In the fourth month of summer,
the Yellow River ran clear in Jìyīn, Dōngjùn, Jìběi, and Píngyuán.
Sītú Xǔ Xǔ was dismissed.
In the fifth month,
Tàicháng Hú Guǎng became Sītú.
In the sixth month,
the Southern Xiōngnú, along with the Wūhuán and Xiānbēi, plundered the nine border commanderies.
In the seventh month of autumn,
the Shěndī Qiāng plundered Wǔwēi and Zhāngyè.
An edict ordered the recommendation of military strongmen:
two from each of the Three Ducal Ministers,
and one from each of the Ministers and Commandants.
Tàiwèi Chén Fán was dismissed.
On the *gēngwǔ* day,
sacrifices were made to Huáng and Lǎo at Zhuólóng Palace.
The Envoy to the Xiōngnú, Zhōnglángjiāng Zhāng Huàn, was sent to attack the Southern Xiōngnú, Wūhuán, and Xiānbēi.
In the ninth month,
Guānglùxūn Zhōu Jǐng became Tàiwèi.
Nányáng Tàishǒu Chéng Líng and Tàiyuán Tàishǒu Liú Zhì
were both executed in the market due to slanders.
Sīkōng Liú Mào was dismissed.
The king of the state of Dàqín sent envoys to offer tribute.
In the twelfth month of winter,
bamboos and cypresses beside Luòchéng withered and were damaged.
Guānglùxūn Rúnán Xuān Fēng became Sīkōng.
The Southern Xiōngnú and Wūhuán, leading their forces, surrendered to Zhāng Huàn.
Sīlì Xiàowèi Lǐ Yīng and over two hundred others were falsely accused as "party members,"
and were all imprisoned.
Their names were recorded in the royal registry.
In the first month of spring of Yǒngkāng First Year,
the Xiānlíng Qiāng plundered Sānfǔ.
Zhōnglángjiāng Zhāng Huàn defeated and pacified them.
The Dāngjiān Qiāng plundered Wǔwēi.
Hùqiāng Xiàowèi Duàn Jiǒng pursued and attacked them at Luánniǎo,
and utterly defeated them.
All the Western Qiāng were pacified.
The king of Fúyú plundered Xuántú.
Tàishǒu Gōngsūn Yù fought with him,
and defeated him.
In the fourth month of summer,
the Xiānlíng Qiāng plundered Sānfǔ again.
In the fifth month, on the *bǐngshēn* day,
the ground cracked in the capital and Shàngdǎng.
Bandits arose in Lújiāng,
plundering the commandery's borders.
On the *rénzǐ* day, the last day of the month,
there was a solar eclipse.
An edict ordered dukes, ministers, and commandants to recommend men of talent and uprightness.
In the sixth month, on the *gēngshēn* day,
a general amnesty was proclaimed throughout the empire,
all "party proscriptions" were lifted,
and the era name was changed to Yǒngkāng.
On the *bǐngyín* day,
Fùlíng Wáng Tǒng passed away.
In the eighth month of autumn,
Wèijùn reported the growth of auspicious grain
and the descent of sweet dew.
Bājùn reported the sighting of a yellow dragon.
In the sixth month, there was a flood,
and the sea overflowed in Bóhǎi.
An edict ordered provinces and commanderies to grant money to those who drowned, aged seven and above,
two thousand coins per person.
For families where all members perished,
their bodies were to be collected and buried.
For those who lost grain and food,
three *hú* of provisions were given per person.
In the tenth month of winter,
the Xiānlíng Qiāng plundered Sānfǔ again.
The Envoy to the Xiōngnú, Zhōnglángjiāng Zhāng Huàn, was sent to attack and defeat them.
In the eleventh month,
Xīhé reported the sighting of a white rabbit.
In the twelfth month, on the *rénshēn* day,
Yǐngtáo Wáng Kuī was restored as Bóhǎi Wáng.
On the *dīngchǒu* day,
the emperor passed away in the front hall of Déyáng,
aged thirty-six.
On the *wùyín* day,
the empress was honored as empress dowager,
and the empress dowager presided over court.
In this year,
Bólíng and Héjiān commanderies were restored,
comparable to Fēng and Pèi.
A commentary states: Former historians said that Emperor Huán (Huán Dì) enjoyed music,
was skilled at the qín and shēnɡ.
He adorned the Fānglín Park and inspected the Chuólónɡ Palace,
and erected elaborate canopies to sacrifice to Fútú (Buddha) and Lǎozǐ.
This is perhaps what is meant by
"listening to the spirits"
When Liánɡ Jì was executed,
his awe-inspiring wrath was aroused,
and the world still yearned for a respite.
However, the Five Evils then perpetuated tyranny,
spreading it in all directions.
Had it not been for loyal and virtuous officials strenuously contending,
repeatedly blunting the edges of treachery,
even the desire to rely on the advice of Zhēnlíuzhì
would have been impossible to achieve.
A eulogy states: Huán, from a collateral branch of the imperial family,
ascended to the heavenly throne.
His government shifted to the Five Favorites;
punishments became excessive in the Three Prisons.
Though palaces were extensively built,
the emperor himself had no successor.
Annals of Emperor Xiàolínɡ, Eighth
Emperor Xiàolínɡ, personal name Hónɡ,
was the great-great-grandson of Sùzōnɡ.
His great-grandfather was Kāi, King Xiào of Héjiān;
his grandfather was Shú;
his father was Chánɡ.
For generations, they were enfeoffed as Marquis of Jiědú Tínɡ,
and the Emperor inherited this marquisate.
His mother was Lady Dǒnɡ.
When Emperor Huán died,
he had no son.
The Empress Dowager and Dòu Wǔ, Commandant of the City Gate, jointly decided on a plan in the Forbidden Palace,
and sent Liú Shū, supervising Grand Master of Guanglù, with an imperial credential,
to lead the Left and Right Yǔlín Guards to Héjiān to welcome the new emperor.
In the first year of Jiànníng, spring, first month, on the day Rénwǔ,
Dòu Wǔ, Commandant of the City Gate, was appointed Grand General.
On the day Jǐhài,
the Emperor arrived at Xiàmén Tínɡ.
He sent Dòu Wǔ with an imperial credential
to welcome him into the palace in a king's green canopied carriage.
On the day Gēnɡzǐ,
he ascended the imperial throne,
at the age of twelve.
The era name was changed to Jiànníng.
Chén Fān, former Grand Commandant, was appointed Grand Tutor,
and along with Dòu Wǔ and Hú Guǎnɡ, Minister of Education, participated in recording matters of the Imperial Secretariat.
Duàn Jiǒnɡ, Commandant Protector of the Qiānɡ, was sent to suppress the Xiānlínɡ Qiānɡ.
Second month, on the day Xīnyǒu,
Emperor Xiàohuán was buried in Xuānlínɡ,
and his temple name was Wēizōnɡ.
On the day Gēnɡwǔ,
he paid respects at the Grand Ancestral Temple.
On the day Xīnwèi,
he paid respects at the temple of Shìzǔ.
A general amnesty was proclaimed throughout the empire.
People were granted爵 and silk, with varying amounts.
Duàn Jiǒnɡ heavily defeated the Xiānlínɡ Qiānɡ at Fēnɡyì Shān.
Intercalary month, on the day Jiǎwǔ,
the imperial grandfather was posthumously honored as Emperor Xiàoyuán,
and Lady Xià as Empress Xiàoyuán;
the father was honored as Emperor Xiàorén,
and Lady Dǒnɡ as Honored Lady of Shènyuán.
Summer, fourth month, on the day Wùchén,
Zhōu Jǐnɡ, Grand Commandant, died.
Xuān Fēnɡ, Minister of Works, was dismissed.
Wánɡ Chànɡ, Commandant of Chánɡlè Guards, was appointed Minister of Works.
Fifth month, on the first day Dīnɡwèi,
there was a solar eclipse.
An imperial edict ordered all officials from the Grand Ministers down to submit sealed memorials,
and the governors and administrators of commanderies and states to recommend one worthy scholar each;
also, former regional inspectors and officials receiving a salary of two thousand bushels who were pure, noble, and left behind good deeds,
and were respected by the populace,
were all to proceed to the Gōngchē.
Liú Jǔ, Grand Master of Tài Zhōnɡ, was appointed Grand Commandant.
Sixth month,
there was heavy rainfall in the capital.
Autumn, seventh month,
Duàn Jiǒnɡ, General Who Breaks the Qiānɡ, again defeated the Xiānlínɡ Qiānɡ at Jīnɡyánɡ.
Eighth month,
Wánɡ Chànɡ, Minister of Works, was dismissed.
Liú Chǒnɡ, Imperial Clan Court Administrator, was appointed Minister of Works.
Ninth month, on the day Xīnhài (originally Dīnɡ),

Cáo Jié, Regular Palace Attendant, falsely issued an imperial edict to execute Chén Fān, Grand Tutor; Dòu Wǔ, Grand General; Yǐn Xūn, Director of the Imperial Secretariat; Liú Yú, Palace Attendant; and Fénɡ Shù, Colonel of Cavalry.
Their clans were all exterminated.
The Empress Dowager was moved to the Nánɡōnɡ Palace.
Hú Guǎnɡ, Minister of Education, was appointed Grand Tutor,
recording matters of the Imperial Secretariat.
Liú Chǒnɡ, Minister of Works, was appointed Minister of Education.
Xǔ Xǔ, Grand Master of Ceremonies, was appointed Minister of Works.
Winter, tenth month, on the last day Jiǎchén,
there was a solar eclipse.
An order was issued that all prisoners whose cases had not been decided could redeem themselves with silk,
with varying amounts.
Eleventh month,
Liú Jǔ, Grand Commandant, was dismissed.
Wénrén Xí of Pèiguó, Grand Coachman, was appointed Grand Commandant.
Twelfth month,
the Xiānbēi and Huìmò raided Yōu and Bīnɡ provinces.
Second year, spring, first month, on the day Dīnɡchǒu,
a general amnesty was proclaimed throughout the empire.
Third month, on the day Yǐsì,
Honored Lady Dǒnɡ of Shènyuán was honored as Empress Xiàorén.
Summer, fourth month, on the day Kuǐsì,
there was a great wind
and hail.
An imperial edict ordered all officials from the Grand Ministers down to submit sealed memorials.
Fifth month,
Wénrén Xí, Grand Commandant, was removed.
Xǔ Xǔ, Minister of Works, was dismissed.
Sixth month,
Liú Chǒnɡ, Minister of Education, was appointed Grand Commandant.
Xǔ Xùn, Grand Minister of Rites, was appointed Minister of Education.
Liú Xiāo of Chánɡshā, Grand Coachman, was appointed Minister of Works.
Autumn, seventh month,
Duàn Jiǒnɡ, General Who Breaks the Qiānɡ, heavily defeated the Xiānlínɡ Qiānɡ in a valley outside Shèhǔ Sài.
The Eastern Qiānɡ were all pacified.
Ninth month,
the Mán of Jiānɡxià rebelled,
and the provinces and commanderies pacified them.
The Shānyuè bandits of Dānyánɡ besieged Chén Yín, the Administrator.
Yín attacked and defeated them.
Winter, tenth month, on the day Dīnɡhài,

Hóu Lǎn, Regular Palace Attendant, prompted the relevant authorities to memorialize that Yú Fànɡ, former Minister of Works; Dù Mì, Grand Coachman; Lǐ Yīnɡ, Minor Prefect of Chánɡlè; Zhū Jí (originally Yǔ), Colonel Director of Retainers; Bā Sù, Administrator of Yǐnɡchuān; Xún Yù (originally Yì), Chancellor of Pèi; Wèi Lǎnɡ, Administrator of Hénèi; and Zhái Chāo, Administrator of Shānyánɡ, were all members of a faction (gōudǎnɡ).
They were imprisoned,
over a hundred people died,
and their wives and children were exiled to the border.
All those affiliated with them were barred from office and their families for five generations.
An imperial edict commanded provinces and commanderies to broadly search for members of the gōudǎnɡ faction.
Consequently, all heroes and scholars of upright conduct throughout the empire
were branded as partisans.
On the last day Wùxū (originally Gēnɡzǐ),
there was a solar eclipse.
Eleventh month,
Liú Chǒnɡ, Grand Commandant, was dismissed.
Guō Xǐ, Grand Coachman, was appointed Grand Commandant.
The Xiānbēi raided Bīnɡ Province.
In this year,
Cáo Jié of Chánɡlè, Grand Coachman, was appointed General of Chariots and Cavalry,
but was dismissed after more than a hundred days.
Third year, spring, first month,
a woman in Hénèi ate her husband;
a man in Hénán ate his wife.
Third month, on the last day Bǐnɡyín,
there was a solar eclipse.
Summer, fourth month,
Guō Xǐ, Grand Commandant, was removed.
Wénrén Xí, Grand Master of Tài Zhōnɡ, was appointed Grand Commandant.
Autumn, seventh month,
Liú Xiāo, Minister of Works, was removed.
Eighth month,
Qiáo Xuán, Grand Master of Ceremonies, was appointed Minister of Works.
Ninth month,
Dǒnɡ Chǒnɡ, Commandant of the Capital, was imprisoned and died.
Winter,
bandits arose in Jìnán,
attacking Dōnɡpínɡlínɡ.
The Wūhǔ people of Yùlín collectively submitted.
Fourth year, spring, first month, on the day Jiǎzǐ,
the Emperor underwent the capping ceremony,
and a general amnesty was proclaimed throughout the empire.
Officials from the Grand Ministers down were granted varying amounts,
but partisans were not pardoned.
Second month, on the day Kuǐmáo,
there was an earthquake,
the sea overflowed,
and the Yellow River ran clear.
Third month, on the first day Xīnyǒu,
there was a solar eclipse.
Wénrén Xí, Grand Commandant, was dismissed.
Lǐ Xián, Grand Coachman, was appointed Grand Commandant.
An imperial edict ordered all officials from the Grand Ministers down to those with a salary of six hundred bushels to submit sealed memorials.
There was a great plague,
and palace attendants were sent to tour and provide medicine.
Xǔ Xùn, Minister of Education, was dismissed.
Qiáo Xuán, Minister of Works, was appointed Minister of Education.
Summer, fourth month,
Lái Yàn, Grand Minister of Rites, was appointed Minister of Works.
Fifth month,
the ground cracked in Hédōng,
there was hail,
and mountain waters burst forth.
Autumn, seventh month,
Lái Yàn, Minister of Works, was dismissed.
On the day Kuǐchǒu,
Honored Lady Sònɡ was established as Empress.
Qiáo Xuán, Minister of Education, was dismissed.
Zōnɡ Jù, Grand Minister of Rites, was appointed Minister of Works.
Xǔ Xǔ, former Minister of Works, was appointed Minister of Education.
Winter,
the Xiānbēi raided Bīnɡ Province.
Xīpínɡ first year, spring, third month, on the day Rénxū,
Hú Guǎnɡ, Grand Tutor, died.
Summer, fifth month, on the day Jǐsì,
a general amnesty was proclaimed throughout the empire,
and the era name was changed to Xīpínɡ.
Hóu Lǎn (侯覽), Grand Coachman of Chánglè (長樂), committed a crime
and committed suicide.
In the sixth month,
the capital experienced heavy rain.
On the guǐsì day,
Empress Dowager Dòu (竇) passed away.
In autumn, seventh month, on the jiǎyín day,
Empress Huán-sī (桓思) was buried.
The eunuchs prompted Duàn Jiǒng (段熲), Colonel Director of Retainers, to arrest and imprison over a thousand imperial academy students.
In winter, tenth month,
Lǐ Kū (悝), Prince of Bóhǎi (渤海), was falsely accused of rebellion.
On the dīnghài day,
Lǐ Kū (悝) and his wife and children all committed suicide.
In the eleventh month,
Xǔ Shēng (許生) from Kuàijī (會稽) proclaimed himself
"King of Yuè (越),"
and raided commanderies and counties.
Yáng Zhōu (楊州) Inspector Zāng Mín (臧旻) and Dānyáng (丹陽) Administrator Chén Yín (陳夤) were dispatched to suppress and defeat him.
In the twelfth month,
Sītú Xǔ Xǔ (許栩) was dismissed.
Dàhónglú Yuán Weǐ (袁隗) became Sītú.
The Xiānbēi (鮮卑) raided Bìng Zhōu (并州).
That year,
Lǐ Huī (恢), Prince of Gānlíng (甘陵), passed away.
In the second year, spring, first month,
there was a great plague.
Envoys were dispatched to tour and provide medicine.
On the dīngchǒu day,
Sīkōng Zōng Jù (宗俱) passed away.
In the second month, on the rénwǔ day,
a general amnesty was proclaimed throughout the empire.
Yáng Cì (楊賜), Grand Master of Brightness, was appointed Sīkōng.
In the third month,
Tàiwèi Lǐ Xián (李咸) was dismissed.
In summer, fifth month,
Duàn Jiǒng (段熲), Colonel Director of Retainers, was appointed Tàiwèi.
Shī Qiān (師遷), Chancellor of Pèi (沛), was imprisoned and died for falsely accusing the king.
He was imprisoned and died.
In the sixth month,
Běihǎi (北海) experienced an earthquake.
In Dōnglái (東萊)
and Běihǎi (北海), the sea overflowed.
In autumn, seventh month,
Sīkōng Yáng Cì (楊賜) was dismissed.
Táng Zhēn (唐珍) of Yǐngchuān (潁川), Grand Astrologer, was appointed Sīkōng.
In winter, twelfth month,
foreign states beyond Rìnán (日南)'s borders offered tribute through multiple translations.
Tàiwèi Duàn Jiǒng (段熲) was dismissed.
The Xiānbēi (鮮卑) raided Yōu (幽) and Bìng (并) two prefectures.
On the guǐyǒu day, the last day of the month,
there was a solar eclipse.
In the third year, spring, first month,
the kingdom of Fúyú (夫餘) sent envoys to offer tribute.
In the second month, on the jǐsì day,
a general amnesty was proclaimed throughout the empire.
Chén Dān (陳耽), Grand Astrologer, was appointed Tàiwèi.
In the third month,
Liú Chàng (暢), Prince of Zhōngshān (中山), passed away.
Having no son,
his state was abolished.
In summer, sixth month,
Lǐ Kāng (康), son of Lǐ Lì (利), Prince of Héxián (河閒), was enfeoffed as Prince of Jìnán (濟南)
to maintain the sacrifices for Emperor Xiàorén (孝仁).
In autumn,
the Luò (洛) River overflowed.
In winter, tenth month, on the guǐchǒu day,
an edict ordered that all prisoners throughout the empire whose cases were undecided
could redeem themselves with silk.
In the eleventh month,
Yáng Zhōu (楊州) Inspector Zāng Mín (臧旻) led Dānyáng (丹陽) Administrator Chén Yín (陳寅)
to greatly defeat Xǔ Shēng (許生) at Kuàijī (會稽)
and behead him.
Liú Bó (博), Prince of Rènchéng (任城), passed away.
In the twelfth month,
the Xiānbēi (鮮卑) raided Běidì (北地).
Běidì (北地) Administrator Xià Yù (夏育) pursued and defeated them.
The Xiānbēi (鮮卑) again raided Bìng Zhōu (并州).
Sīkōng Táng Zhēn (唐珍) was dismissed.
Xǔ Xùn (許訓), Prefect of Yǒnglè (永樂), was appointed Sīkōng.
In the fourth year, spring, third month,
an imperial edict ordered scholars to rectify the characters of the Five Classics
and engrave them on stone steles to be erected outside the Imperial Academy gate.
Lǐ Tuó (佗), son of Lǐ Jiàn (建), Prince of Héxián (河閒), was enfeoffed as Prince of Rènchéng (任城).
In summer, fourth month,
seven commanderies and kingdoms experienced great floods.
In the fifth month, on the dīngmǎo day,
a general amnesty was proclaimed throughout the empire.
The Yánlíng (延陵) park suffered a disaster.
Envoys were dispatched with credentials to offer sacrifices at Yánlíng (延陵).
The Xiānbēi (鮮卑) raided Yōu Zhōu (幽州).
In the sixth month,
Hóngnóng (弘農) and the Sānfǔ (三輔) suffered from locusts.
The Superintendent of the Imperial Household was dispatched to oversee salt production,
digging canals to benefit the people.
Commandments were issued that for commanderies and kingdoms affected by disaster,
field taxes should be halved;
and for those whose damage was fourteen parts or more,
no repayment should be collected.
In winter, tenth month, on the dīngsì day,
an edict ordered that all prisoners throughout the empire whose cases were undecided
could redeem themselves with silk.
Consort Yú (虞), mother of Emperor Chōng (沖), was appointed Guìrén (貴人) of Xiànyuán (憲園).
Lady Chén (陳), mother of Emperor Zhì (質), was appointed Empress of Bóhǎi (渤海) Xiàowáng (孝王).
Píngzhǔn (平準) was renamed Zhōngzhǔn (中準).
Eunuchs were appointed as its chiefs
and listed within the inner court.
From then on, all inner departments appointed eunuchs as their vice-chiefs and chiefs.
In the fifth year, summer, fourth month, on the guǐhài day,
a general amnesty was proclaimed throughout the empire.
The Yi (夷) of Yìzhōu (益州) Commandery rebelled.
Administrator Lǐ Yǒng (李顒) suppressed and pacified them.
Mount Chónggāo (崇高) was renamed Mount Sōnggāo (嵩高).
A great rain sacrifice was held.
Imperial Household Recorders were sent to inspect imperial prisons and courier stations
to rectify injustices,
release those with minor charges,
and pardon prisoners.
In the fifth month,
Tàiwèi Chén Dān (陳耽) was dismissed.
Sīkōng Xǔ Xùn (許訓) was appointed Tàiwèi.
In the intercalary month,
Cáo Luán (曹鸞), Administrator of Yǒngchāng (永昌), was executed in the marketplace
for pleading on behalf of the partisans.
An imperial edict ordered that all partisans, their disciples, former officials, fathers, elder brothers, sons, and younger brothers who held office
were to be dismissed and banned from holding office.
In the sixth month, on the rénxū day,
Liú Yì (劉逸) of Nányáng (南陽), Grand Astrologer,
was appointed Sīkōng.
In autumn, seventh month,
Tàiwèi Xǔ Xùn (許訓) was dismissed.
Liú Kuān (劉寬), Grand Master of Brightness, was appointed Tàiwèi.
In winter, tenth month, on the rénwǔ day,
a locust tree behind the imperial palace uprooted itself and fell inverted.
Sītú Yuán Weǐ (袁隗) was dismissed.
In the eleventh month, on the bǐngxū day,
Yáng Cì (楊賜), Grand Master of Brightness, was appointed Sītú.
In the twelfth month,
Liú Dìng (定), Prince of Gānlíng (甘陵), passed away.
Over a hundred imperial academy students aged sixty or above were tested
and appointed as Langzhong (郎中), Crown Prince's Retainers, King's Household Retainers, or literary officials in commanderies and kingdoms.
That year,
the Xiānbēi (鮮卑) raided Yōu Zhōu (幽州).
Pèi (沛) Commandery reported that a yellow dragon was seen at Qiáo (譙).
In the sixth year, spring, first month, on the xīncchǒu day,
a general amnesty was proclaimed throughout the empire.
In the second month,
the Píngchéng (平城) Gate of Nángōng (南宮) and the eastern wall roof of the arsenal collapsed on their own.
In summer, fourth month,
there was a great drought,
and locusts in seven prefectures.
The Xiānbēi (鮮卑) raided the three frontiers.
Dozens of merchants and commoners who claimed to be filial sons of Xuānlíng (宣陵)
were all appointed as Crown Prince's Retainers.
In autumn, seventh month,
Sīkōng Liú Yì (劉逸) was dismissed.
Chén Qiú (陳球), Commandant of the Guards, was appointed Sīkōng.
In the eighth month,
Tián Yàn (田晏), Colonel Who Breaks the Xiānbēi (鮮卑), was dispatched from Yúnzhōng (雲中).
Zāng Mín (臧旻), Colonel Who Commands the Xiongnu, was dispatched with the Southern Chányú from Yànmén (鴈門).
Xià Yù (夏育), Protector-Colonel of the Wūhuán (烏桓), was dispatched from Gāoliǔ (高柳).
They all attacked the Xiānbēi (鮮卑),
but Tián Yàn (田晏) and the others suffered a great defeat.
In winter, tenth month, on the guǐchǒu day, the first day of the month,
there was a solar eclipse.
Tàiwèi Liú Kuān (劉寬) was dismissed.
The Emperor presided over the Bìyōng (辟雍).
On the xīnchǒu day,
the capital experienced an earthquake.
On the xīnhài day,
an edict ordered that all prisoners throughout the empire whose cases were undecided
could redeem themselves with silk.
In the eleventh month,
Sīkōng Chén Qiú (陳球) was dismissed.
In the twelfth month, on the jiǎyín day,
Mèng Kāi (孟キ) of Hénán (河南), Grand Astrologer, was appointed Tàiwèi.
On the gēngchén day,
Sītú Yáng Cì (楊賜) was dismissed.
Chén Dān (陳耽), Grand Astrologer, was appointed Sīkōng.
The Xiānbēi (鮮卑) raided Liáoxī (遼西).
Wáng Mín (王旻), Grand Coachman of Yǒng'ān (永安), was imprisoned and died.
In the first year of Guānghé (光和), spring, first month,
the Wūhǔ (烏滸) barbarians of Hépǔ (合浦) and Jiāozhǐ (交阯) rebelled,
attracting the people of Jiǔzhēn (九真) and Rìnán (日南) to attack and occupy commanderies and counties.
Tàiwèi Mèng Kāi (孟キ) was dismissed.
In the second month, on the xīnhài day, the first day of the month,
there was a solar eclipse.
On the guǐchǒu day,
Yuán Pāng (袁滂) of Chén Guó (陳國), Grand Master of Brightness, was appointed Sītú.
On the jǐwèi day,
there was an earthquake.
Students of Hóngdūmén (鴻都門) were first established.
In the third month, on the xīnchǒu day,
a general amnesty was proclaimed throughout the empire,
and the reign era was changed to Guānghé (光和).
Tài-cháng Zhāng Hào of Chángshān became Tàiwèi.
In the summer, in the fourth month, on the day Bǐngchén,
there was an earthquake.
In the Shìzhōng-sì, a hen transformed into a rooster.
Sīkōng Chén Dān was dismissed,
and Tài-cháng Lái Yàn became Sīkōng.
In the fifth month, on the day Rénwǔ,
a person in white clothing entered the Dèyáng-diàn gate,
fled, and was not captured.
In the sixth month, on the day Dīngchǒu,
a black vapor fell into the courtyard of the Wēndé-diàn, where the emperor resided.
In the autumn, in the seventh month, on the day Rénzǐ,
a blue rainbow appeared in the courtyard behind the Yùtáng, where the emperor sat.
In the eighth month,
a comet appeared in the constellation Tiānshì.
In the ninth month,
Tàiwèi Zhāng Hào was dismissed,
and Tài-cháng Chén Qiú became Tàiwèi.
Sīkōng Lái Yàn passed away.
In the winter, in the tenth month,
Túntí-xiàowèi Yuán Féng became Sīkōng.
Empress Sòng was deposed,
and her father, Zhíjiīn-wǔ Fēng, was imprisoned and died.
On the day Bǐngzǐ, which was the last day of the month,
there was a solar eclipse.
In the eleventh month,
Tàiwèi Chén Qiú was dismissed.
In the twelfth month, on the day Dīngsì,
Guānglù-dàfū Qiáo Xuán became Tàiwèi.
In this year,
the Xiānbēi raided Jiǔquán.
In the capital, a horse gave birth to a human.
The Xī-dì was opened for the first time to sell official positions.
From Guānnèi-hóu, Hǔbēn, and Yǔlín,
each required a different amount of money to be paid.
The emperor secretly ordered his attendants to sell positions of Gōng and Qīng.
A Gōng cost ten million,
and a Qīng five million.
In the second year, in spring,
there was a great plague.
Chángshì and Zhōngyèzhě were sent to inspect and provide medicine.
In the third month,
Sītú Yuán Pāng was dismissed,
and Dàhónglú Liú Hé became Sītú.
On the day Yǐchǒu,
Tàiwèi Qiáo Xuán was dismissed,
and Tàizhōng-dàfū Duàn Jiǒng became Tàiwèi.
There was an earthquake in Jīngzhào.
Sīkōng Yuán Féng was dismissed,
and Tài-cháng Zhāng Jì became Sīkōng.
In the summer, in the fourth month, on the day Jiǎxū, which was the first day of the month,
there was a solar eclipse.
On the day Xīnsì,
Zhōngchángshì Wáng Fǔ and Tàiwèi Duàn Jiǒng were both imprisoned and died.
On the day Dīngyǒu,
there was a general amnesty throughout the realm,
and all members of the factions who had been banished and whose mourning obligations were less than "little mourning" (xiǎogōng) were pardoned.
Dōngpíng-wáng Duān passed away.
In the fifth month,
Wèiwèi Liú Kuān became Tàiwèi.
In the autumn, in the seventh month,
the mission of Xiōngnú Zhōnglángjiàng Zhāng Xiū was found guilty,
and he was imprisoned and died.
In the winter, in the tenth month, on the day Jiǎshēn,
Sītú Liú Hé, Yǒnglè-shàofǔ Chén Qiú, Wèiwèi Yáng Qiú, and Bùbīng-xiàowèi Liú Nà conspired to execute the eunuchs.
The plot was exposed,
and they were all imprisoned and died.
The Bǎndùn-mán of Bājùn rebelled.
Yùshǐ-zhōngchéng Xiāo Yuàn was dispatched to oversee the Yìzhōu-cìshǐ to suppress them,
but failed.
In the twelfth month,
Guānglùxūn Yáng Cì became Sītú.
The Xiānbēi raided Yōu and Bìng two zhōus.
In this year,
Héjiān-wáng Lì passed away.
In Luòyáng, a woman gave birth to a child
with two heads and four arms.
In the third year, in spring, in the first month, on the day Guǐyǒu,
there was a general amnesty throughout the realm.
In the second month,
the covered corridor where the imperial carriage stopped at the Gōng-fǔ collapsed on its own.
In the third month,
Liáng-wáng Yuán passed away.
In the summer, in the fourth month,
the Jiāngxià-mán rebelled.
In the sixth month,
an imperial edict ordered Gōng and Qīng to each recommend one person skilled in the ancient texts of the Shàngshū, Máoshī, Zuǒshì, and Gǔliáng-chūnqiū,
and all were appointed as Yìláng.
In the autumn,
a memorial reported an earthquake,
from which water surged forth.
In the eighth month,
an order was issued that prisoners whose cases were not yet decided
could pay silk to redeem themselves,
with amounts varying.
In the winter intercalary month,
a comet appeared in the constellations Láng and Hú.
The Xiānbēi raided Yōu and Bìng two zhōus.
In the twelfth month, on the day Jǐsì,
Noble Lady Hé was established as Empress.
In this year,
the Bìguī and Língkūn-yuàn were constructed.
In the fourth year, in spring, in the first month,
the office of Lùjì-cèng was first established
to be in charge of receiving tribute horses from commanderies and kingdoms.
Powerful magnates engaged in extortion,
and a single horse cost up to two million.
In the second month,
commanderies and kingdoms presented Zhīyīng grass.
In the summer, in the fourth month, on the day Gēngzǐ,
there was a general amnesty throughout the realm.
Jiāozhǐ-cìshǐ Zhū Jùn attacked the Wūhǔ-mán of Jiāozhǐ and Hépǔ,
and defeated them.
In the sixth month, on the day Gēngchén,
it hailed.
In the autumn, in the seventh month,
Hénán reported that a Fenghuáng was seen in Xīnchéng,
followed by a flock of birds;
the Xīnchéng-lìng and the Sānlǎo and Lìtián were granted silk,
with varying amounts.
In the ninth month, on the day Gēngyín, which was the first day of the month,
there was a solar eclipse.
Tàiwèi Liú Kuān was dismissed,
and Wèiwèi Xǔ Gǒng became Tàiwèi.
In the intercalary month, on the day Xīnyǒu,
the Yǒngxiàng-shǔ in the east wing of the Běigōng-yètíng caught fire.
Sītú Yáng Cì was dismissed.
In the winter, in the tenth month,
Tài-cháng Chén Dān became Sītú.
The Xiānbēi raided Yōu and Bìng two zhōus.
In this year, the emperor established markets in the rear palace,
where his concubines sold goods,
and engaged in mutual theft and quarrels.
The emperor wore merchant clothes
and enjoyed banquets.
He also played with dogs in the Xīyuán,
dressing them in jìnxián-guān
and ribbons.
He also drove a four-donkey carriage,
personally holding the reins,
driving around and circling;
the capital residents followed suit.
In the fifth year, in spring, in the first month, on the day Xīnwèi,
there was a general amnesty throughout the realm.
In the second month,
there was a great plague.
In the third month,
Sītú Chén Dān was dismissed.
In the summer, in the fourth month,
there was a drought.
Tài-cháng Yuán Wěi became Sītú.
In the fifth month, on the day Gēngshēn,
there was a fire at Yǒnglè-gōng.
In the autumn, in the seventh month,
a comet appeared in Tàiwēi.
The Bǎndùn-mán of Bājùn surrendered to Tàishǒu Cáo Qiān.
On the day Guǐyǒu,
an order was issued that prisoners whose cases were not yet decided
could pay silk to redeem themselves.
In the eighth month,
a four-hundred-foot tower was built on the Ātíng road.
In the winter, in the tenth month,
Tàiwèi Xǔ Gǒng was dismissed,
and Tài-cháng Yáng Cì became Tàiwèi.
There was a hunting expedition in the Shànglín-yuàn,
passing through Hángǔ-guān,
and then touring Guǎngchéng-yuàn.
In the twelfth month,
returning,
the emperor visited the Tàixué.
In the sixth year, in spring, in the first month,
foreign countries from beyond Rìnán, through multiple translations, offered tribute.
In the second month,
Chánglíng county was restored,
comparable to Fēng and Pèi.
In the third month, on the day Xīnwèi,
there was a general amnesty throughout the realm.
In the summer,
there was a great drought.
In the autumn,
the Héshuǐ river in Jīnchéng overflowed.
The mountain bank in Wǔyuán collapsed.
The Pǔyòu-shǔ was first established,
with eunuchs as its superintendents.
In the winter,
in Dōnghǎi, Dōnglái, and Lángxié, the ice in the wells was more than a foot thick.
It was a year of great harvest.
In the first year of Zhōngpíng, in spring, in the second month,
Zhāng Jiǎo of Jùlù proclaimed himself
"Huáng Tiān" (Yellow Heaven).
His thirty-six divisions
all wore yellow turbans,
and rebelled on the same day.
People from Ānpíng and Gānlíng each seized their respective kings to join them.
In the third month, on the day *wùshēn*,
Hé Jìn, the Prefect of Hénán, was appointed Grand General,
and led troops to garrison Dūtíng.
The office of the Eight Passes Commandant was established.
On the day *rénzǐ*,
a general amnesty was granted to all members of the *dǎng* factions,
and all those who had been banished were allowed to return,
with the sole exception of Zhāng Jiǎo.
An imperial edict ordered the high officials to contribute horses and crossbows,
and to recommend descendants of distinguished generals, as well as officials and commoners with a clear grasp of battle tactics,
to report to Gōngchē.
Lú Zhí, the Northern Commandant, was dispatched to suppress Zhāng Jiǎo,
while Huángfǔ Sōng, the Left Commandant, and Zhū Jùn, the Right Commandant, were sent to suppress the Yellow Turbans in Yǐngchuān.
On the day *gēngzǐ*,
Zhāng Mánchéng, a Yellow Turban from Nányáng, attacked and killed Chǔ Gòng, the Grand Administrator of the commandery.
In the summer, fourth month,
Grand尉 Yáng Cì was dismissed.
Dèng Shèng of Hóngnóng, Grand Coachman, became Grand尉.
Sīkōng Zhāng Jì was dismissed.
Zhāng Wēn, Grand Minister of Agriculture, became Sīkōng.
Zhū Jùn was defeated by Bō Cái of the Yellow Turbans.
Shìzhōng Xiàng Xǔ and Zhāng Jūn were imprisoned and executed
for speaking about eunuchs.
The Rǔnán Yellow Turbans defeated Zhào Qiān, the Grand Administrator, at Shàolíng.
The Guǎngyáng Yellow Turbans killed Guō Xūn, the Inspector of Yōuzhōu, and Liú Wèi, the Grand Administrator.
In the fifth month,
Huángfǔ Sōng and Zhū Jùn again fought Bō Cái and others at Chángshè,
and utterly routed them.
In the sixth month,
Qín Xié, the Grand Administrator of Nányáng, attacked Zhāng Mánchéng,
and beheaded him.
The garrison troops in Jiāozhǐ seized the Inspector and Lái Dá, the Grand Administrator of Hépǔ,
and declared themselves
"Zhùtiān Jiāngjūn."
Jiǎ Cóng, the Inspector of Jiāozhǐ, was dispatched to suppress and pacify them.
Huángfǔ Sōng and Zhū Jùn utterly defeated the Rǔnán Yellow Turbans at Xīhuá.
An edict ordered Huángfǔ Sōng to suppress Dōngjùn,
and Zhū Jùn to suppress Nányáng.
Lú Zhí defeated the Yellow Turbans
and besieged Zhāng Jiǎo at Guǎngzōng.
The eunuchs falsely impeached Lú Zhí,
and he was punished.
Dǒng Zhuó, a Commandant, was dispatched to attack Zhāng Jiǎo,
but did not succeed.
In Luòyáng, a woman gave birth to a child
with two heads sharing one body.
In the autumn, seventh month,
Zhāng Xiū, a demonic sorcerer from Bājùn, rebelled,
and plundered the commanderies and counties.
Xú Guàn, the Prefect of Hénán, was imprisoned and died.
In the eighth month,
Huángfǔ Sōng fought the Yellow Turbans at Cāngtíng,
and captured their leader.
On the day *yǐsì*,
an edict ordered Huángfǔ Sōng to march north to suppress Zhāng Jiǎo.
In the ninth month,
Ānpíng Wáng Xù was executed for a crime,
and his state was abolished.
In the winter, tenth month,
Huángfǔ Sōng fought the Yellow Turbans at Guǎngzōng,
and captured Zhāng Liáng, Zhāng Jiǎo's younger brother.
Zhāng Jiǎo had died previously,
so his corpse was dismembered.
Huángfǔ Sōng was appointed General of the Left Chariots and Cavalry.
In the eleventh month,
Huángfǔ Sōng again defeated the Yellow Turbans at Xiàqǔyáng,
and beheaded Zhāng Bǎo, Zhāng Jiǎo's younger brother.
Běigōng Bóyù of the Yìcóng Hú in Huángzhōng, along with the Xiānlíng Qiāng, rebelled,
and appointed Biān Zhāng and Hán Suì of Jīnchéng as their military commanders.
They attacked and killed Líng Zhēng, the Colonel Protector of the Qiāng, and Chén Yì, the Grand Administrator of Jīnchéng.
On the day *guǐsì*,
Zhū Jùn captured Wǎnchéng
and beheaded Sūn Xià, a separate Yellow Turban leader.
An edict ordered the reduction of delicacies from the Grand Provisioner,
allowing only one meat dish per imperial meal.
Horses from the stables not used for suburban sacrifices
were all to be given to the army.
In the twelfth month, on the day *jǐsì*,
a general amnesty was granted throughout the realm,
and the era name was changed to Zhōngpíng.
In this year,
Xiàpī Wáng Yì died.
Having no son,
his state was abolished.
In commanderies and states, strange plants grew,
assuming the forms of dragons, snakes, birds, and beasts.
In the second year, spring, first month,
there was a great plague.
Lángyá Wáng Jù died.
In the second month, on the day *jǐyǒu*,
a great fire broke out in the Nángōng palace,
burning for half a month before it was extinguished.
On the day 【guǐ】hài,
the outer buildings of Guǎngyángmén spontaneously collapsed.
A tax of ten cash per *mǔ* was levied
on all land in the empire.
Zhāng Niújiǎo and more than ten other Black Mountain bandits rose up simultaneously,
plundering everywhere.
Sītú Yuán Wěi was dismissed.
In the third month,
Cuī Liè, the Grand Minister of Justice, became Sītú.
Běigōng Bóyù and others plundered Sānfǔ.
Huángfǔ Sōng, the General of the Left Chariots and Cavalry, was dispatched to suppress them,
but did not succeed.
In the summer, fourth month, on the day *gēngxū*,
there was a great wind
and a hailstorm.
In the fifth month,
Grand尉 Dèng Shèng was dismissed. Zhāng Yán of Hénèi, Grand Coachman, became Grand尉.
In the autumn, seventh month,
Sānfǔ was infested with locusts.
Huángfǔ Sōng, the General of the Left Chariots and Cavalry, was dismissed.
In the eighth month,
Sīkōng Zhāng Wēn was appointed General of the Chariots and Cavalry
to suppress Běigōng Bóyù.
In the ninth month,
Yáng Cì, who held the special rank of *Tèjìn*, became Sīkōng.
In the winter, tenth month, on the day *gēngyín*,
Sīkōng Yáng Cì died.
Xǔ Xiàng, Grand Master of Guanglu, became Sīkōng.
Chén Dān, the former Sītú, and Liú Táo, the Grand Master Remonstrant, were imprisoned and executed
for speaking frankly.
In the eleventh month,
Zhāng Wēn defeated Běigōng Bóyù at Měiyáng,
and then dispatched Zhōu Shèn, the General who Attacks the Robbers, to pursue and attack them,
besieging Yúzhōng.
He also dispatched Dǒng Zhuó, a Commandant, to suppress the Xiānlíng Qiāng.
Neither Shèn nor Zhuó succeeded.
The Xiānbēi raided Yōu and Bìng provinces.
In this year,
the Wànjīntáng was built in the Xīyuán.
In Luòyáng, a commoner gave birth to a child
with two heads and four arms.
In the third year, spring, second month,
Zhào Cí, a soldier from Jiāngxià, rebelled,
and killed Qín Xié, the Grand Administrator of Nányáng.
On the day *gēngxū*,
a general amnesty was granted throughout the realm.
Grand尉 Zhāng Yán was dismissed.
Zhāng Wēn, the General of the Chariots and Cavalry, became Grand尉.
Zhào Zhōng, a Central Regular Attendant, became General of the Chariots and Cavalry.
The Yùtángdiàn palace was repaired,
and four bronze figures were cast,
four *huángzhōng* bells,
as well as Tiānlù and Háma,
and also coins with four-outward designs.
In the fifth month, on the last day, *rénchén*,
there was a solar eclipse.
In the sixth month,
Wáng Mǐn, the Inspector of Jīngzhōu, suppressed Zhào Cí
and beheaded him.
Zhào Zhōng, the General of the Chariots and Cavalry, was dismissed.
In the autumn, eighth month,
tens of thousands of sparrows gathered on Huáilíng,
crying mournfully,
then fought and killed each other.
In the winter, tenth month,
the Wǔlíng Mán rebelled,
plundering the commandery's borders.
The commandery troops suppressed and defeated them.
Zhāng Yán, the former Grand尉, was slandered by eunuchs,
imprisoned and died.
In the twelfth month,
the Xiānbēi raided Yōu and Bìng provinces.
In the fourth year, spring, first month, on the day *jǐmǎo*,
a general amnesty was granted throughout the realm.
In the second month,
thieves in Xíngyáng killed the Magistrate of Zhōngmóu.
On the day *jǐhài*,
the *fúbì* in the inner palace of Nángōng spontaneously collapsed.
In the third month,
Hé Miáo, the Prefect of Hénán, suppressed the Xíngyáng thieves,
defeated them,
and was appointed General of the Chariots and Cavalry.
In the summer, fourth month,
Gěng Bǐ, the Inspector of Liángzhōu, suppressed Hán Suì, a thief from Jīnchéng.
Bǐ's troops were utterly defeated.
Suì then plundered Hànyáng.
Fù Xiè, the Grand Administrator of Hànyáng, died in battle.
Mǎ Téng of Fúfēng and Wáng Guó of Hànyáng both rebelled,
and plundered Sānfǔ.
Grand尉 Zhāng Wēn was dismissed.
Cuī Liè, the Sītú, became Grand尉.
In the fifth month,
Xǔ Xiàng, the Sīkōng, became Sītú.
Dīng Gōng of Pèiguó, Grandee Secretary, became Sīkōng.
In the sixth month,
in Luòyáng, a commoner gave birth to a boy
with two heads sharing one body.
Zhāng Chún of Yúyáng and Zhāng Jǔ of the same commandery raised an army and rebelled,
attacking and killing Liú Zhèng, the Grand Administrator of Yòuběipíng, Yáng Zhōng, the Grand Administrator of Liáodōng, Gōngqí Chóu, the Colonel Protector of the Wūhuán, and others.
Zhāng Jǔ declared himself Son of Heaven
and plundered Yōu and Jì provinces.
In autumn, the ninth month, on the *dīngyǒu* day,
an order was issued to the whole empire that prisoners whose crimes were undecided
could redeem themselves with silk.
In winter, the tenth month,
a man from Línglíng, Guānchèng,
proclaimed himself
"General Pacifying Heaven" (*Píngtiān Jiāngjūn*),
and plundered Guìyáng.
The Grand Administrator of Chángshā, Sūn Jiān, attacked and beheaded him.
In the eleventh month,
the Grand Commandant Cuī Liè was dismissed,
and the Grand Minister of Agriculture Cáo Sōng became Grand Commandant.
In the twelfth month,
the Xiūtúgē Hú rebelled.
In this year,
the title of Guānnèi Hóu was sold.
Holders were granted a gold seal with a purple cord,
which was hereditary,
for a payment of five million cash.
In the fifth year, spring, the first month,
the Xiūtúgē Hú plundered Xīhé,
killing the Commander of the Commandery, Xíng Jì.
On the *dīngyǒu* day,
a general amnesty was proclaimed throughout the empire.
In the second month,
a comet appeared in the Purple Palace constellation.
Guō Tài and other remaining Yellow Turban rebels rose up in the Baíbō Valley of Xīhé,
and plundered Tàiyuán and Hédōng.
In the third month,
the Xiūtúgē Hú attacked and killed the Inspector Zhāng Yì,
and then joined with the Hú of the Southern Xiōngnú's Left Faction,
killing their Chányú.
In summer, the fourth month,
the Yellow Turbans of Gépí in Rǔnán attacked and captured commanderies and counties.
The Grand Commandant Cáo Sōng was dismissed.
In the fifth month,
the Administrator of Yǒnglè Lesser Treasury, Fán Líng, became Grand Commandant.
In the sixth month, on the *bǐngyín* day,
there was a great wind.
The Grand Commandant Fán Líng was dismissed.
The Yìzhōu Yellow Turbans, led by Mǎ Xiāng, attacked and killed the Inspector Xī Jiǎn,
proclaimed himself Son of Heaven,
and then plundered Bājùn,
killing the Commander of the Commandery, Zhào Bù.
The Yìzhōu Aide, Jiǎ Lóng, attacked Mǎ Xiāng
and beheaded him.
Seven commanderies and kingdoms suffered great floods.
In autumn, the seventh month,
