Note: It is suspected to be a corruption of the character
Tiānwén (天文) Part 1: Wáng Mǎng (王莽) 3, Guāngwǔ (光武) 12.
The Yì (易) says:
"Heaven manifests images,
and the sages emulate them.
When Páoxīshì (庖犧氏) ruled the world,
he looked up to observe images in Heaven,
and looked down to observe laws on Earth."
Observing images in Heaven refers to the sun, moon, and stars.
Observing laws on Earth refers to water, land, and divisions of regions.
Forms are established below,
and images appear above.
Therefore, it is said that Heaven is the North Star,
which combines the primordial brilliance to establish the imperial form,
operates the cosmic mechanism, grants measures, and spreads out the hundred spirits.
The Three Ranks and Nine Columns,
the twenty-seven great officials,
the eighty-one prime ministers,
the Dipper, the Scales, Táiwēi (太微), Shèntí (攝提), and their subordinates, a hundred and twenty officials,
and the twenty-eight Mansions are all arrayed,
corresponding below to the twelve branches.
Heaven and Earth are established in their positions,
and the images of the stars are complete.
The Three Sovereigns (Sānhuáng) expanded their transforming influence,
harmonizing with the divine purity and simplicity.
It is said that the five planets were like a string of pearls,
and the sun and moon were like a conjoined jade disk.
Transformation proceeded naturally,
and the people committed no transgressions.
It was not until the rise of written records
that the Five Emperors (Wǔdì) created them.
Xuānyuán (軒轅) first received the Hétú dòubāo shòu (河圖鬬苞授),
which regulated the images of the sun, moon, and stars.
Therefore, books on celestial officials began with the Yellow Emperor (Huángdì).
Up to Gāoyángshì (高陽氏),
he commanded Nán Zhèng Chóng (南正重) to manage Heaven,
and Běi Zhèng Lí (北正黎) to manage Earth.
In the time of Táng (唐) and Yú (虞), there were Xī Zhòng (羲仲) and Hé Zhòng (和仲).
In Xià (夏), there was Kūn Wú (昆吾).
Tāng (湯) had Wū Xián (巫咸).
Zhōu (周) had Shǐ Yì (史佚) and Cháng Hóng (萇弘).
Sòng (宋) had Zǐ Wéi (子韋).
Chǔ (楚) had Táng Miè (唐蔑).
Lǔ (魯) had Zǐ Shèn (梓慎).
Zhèng (鄭) had Pí Zào (裨竈).
Wèi (魏) had Shí Shēnfū (石申夫).
Qí (齊) had Gān Gōng (甘公).
All were officials in charge of astronomy.
They looked up to observe and looked down to examine,
to assist in the governance of the time.
They traced changes, detected subtleties,
penetrated deeply and thoroughly,
explored the origins of fortune and misfortune,
and foresaw the trends of success and failure.
Qín (秦) burned the books of poetry and history
to make the common people ignorant.
The classics of the Six Arts
were reduced to ashes and charcoal,
but the books of celestial officials
were preserved and not destroyed.
Therefore, the Qín historian recorded that during the time of Shǐhuáng (始皇),
a comet appeared in Dàjiǎo (大角),
and Dàjiǎo (大角) perished.
A large star fought with a small star within the palace,
which was a sign of its downfall and demise.
When Hàn (漢) arose,
during the reigns of Jǐng (景) and Wǔ (武),
Sīmǎ Tán (司馬談),
and Tán's (談) son Qiān (遷),
as descendants of the Lǐ (黎) clan for generations,
served as Tài Shǐ Lìng (太史令).
Qiān (遷) compiled the Shǐjì (史記)
and wrote the Tiānguān Shū (天官書).
In the time of Emperor Chéng (成),
Zhōnglěi Xiàowèi Liú Xiàng (中壘校尉劉向)
expanded the "Hóngfàn Zāitiáo" (洪範災條) and wrote the "Wǔjì Huángjí" (五紀皇極) treatise,
to compare with past events.
Emperor Xiàomíng (孝明) commanded Bān Gù (班固) to compile the Hàn Shū (漢書),
and Mǎ Xù (馬續) narrated the Tiānwén Zhì (天文志).
Now Shào (紹) compiles the Hàn Shū (漢書) as the Tiānwén Zhì (天文志),
starting from the first year of Wáng Mǎng's (王莽) regency
until the twenty-fifth year of Jiàn'ān (建安) under Emperor Xiàn (孝獻帝),
covering two hundred and fifteen years.
It speaks of the changes in the stars during that time,
and the corresponding manifestations,
to reveal Heaven's warnings
and illuminate the affairs of kings.
In the eleventh month of the third year of Dìhuáng (地皇) under Wáng Mǎng (王莽),
a comet appeared in Zhāng (張),
moving southeast for five days before disappearing.
A comet
is born from evil qi,
signifying rebel soldiers.
Its appearance is due to the decline of virtue.
The decline of virtue
is a sign of chaos,
an indication of obscurity.
Also, Cān (參) shone brightly like a comet,
which is a type of soldier,
hence it is called a "bèi" (孛).
The word "bèi" (孛)
implies harm
and obstruction.
Some call it a "huìxīng" (彗星, broom star),
which is meant to sweep away filth and usher in the new.
Zhāng (張) is the land of Zhōu (周).
A comet appearing in Zhāng (張)
and moving southeast is in the region of Yì (翼) and Zhěn (軫).
Yì (翼) and Zhěn (軫) represent Chǔ (楚).
This means there will be military unrest in the Zhōu (周) and Chǔ (楚) lands.
One year later, in the first month,
Guāngwǔ's (光武) army was in Chūnlíng (舂陵).
The bandits from Xiàjiāng (下江) and Xīnshì (新巿), Zhāng Áng (張卬) and Wáng Cháng (王常),
and the army of Gēngshǐ (更始) also arrived.
Together they attacked and captured Nányáng (南陽),
beheading Zhēn Fù (甄阜), Wáng Mǎng's (王莽) former vanguard commander, and Liángqiū Cì (梁丘賜), his subordinate,
killing tens of thousands of their soldiers.
Gēngshǐ (更始) became emperor,
made Luòyáng (雒陽) his capital,
went west into Cháng'ān (長安),
and was defeated and died.
Guāngwǔ (光武) rose in Héběi (河北),
again made Luòyáng (雒陽) his capital,
residing in the land of Zhōu (周),
symbolizing the sweeping away of filth and ushering in the new.
In the sixth month of the fourth year,
Hàn troops rose from Nányáng
and reached Kūnyáng.
Wáng Mǎng sent the Sītú Wáng Xún and the Sīkōng Wáng Yì to lead the troops from various commanderies,
proclaiming them to be a million strong,
with 420,000 having already arrived;
sixty-three families skilled in military strategy
all served as generals and commanders,
carrying their maps, documents, and equipment.
The army marched out east of the passes,
leading along groups of elephants, tigers, wolves, and fierce beasts,
releasing them on the roads
to display wealth and strength
and to terrify those east of the mountains.
Upon reaching Kūnyángshān,
they set up over a hundred camps,
encircling the city several times;
some used battering rams to strike the city walls,
and built cloud ladders ten zhàng high to overlook the city from above.
Crossbow bolts fell like rain,
and people in the city fetched water by covering their doors.
Requests for surrender were not heeded,
and pleas to exit were denied.
The troops of the two dukes believed they were certain to win,
neglecting military affairs
and failing to coordinate their strategies.
A portent of Wáng Mǎng's defeat and destruction appeared.
During the day, there was a cloudy vapor like a collapsing mountain,
falling upon the army;
all the soldiers were suppressed,
this was what is called the 'Yíngtóu star.'
The divination said:
"Wherever the Yíngtóu falls,
the army beneath it will be destroyed,
and blood will flow for three thousand lǐ."
At this time, Guāngwǔ led several thousand troops to relieve Kūnyáng,
rushing to attack the troops of the two dukes.
With combined strength and sudden fury,
their shouts and cries shook heaven and earth;
tigers and leopards were terrified and scattered.
Coincidentally, there was a great wind,
blowing off roof tiles,
and rain poured down like water.
The two dukes' troops were thrown into chaos and defeated,
slaughtering each other,
with tens of thousands dying.
They rushed frantically to the Zhǐshuǐ River;
the dead piled up,
and the Zhǐshuǐ River ceased to flow because of it.
The Sītú Wáng Xún was killed.
All the armies dispersed and fled back to their original commanderies.
Wáng Yì returned to Cháng'ān;
Wáng Mǎng was defeated,
and both were executed.
The Yíngtóu portent
was the manifestation of the army's destruction and the flowing of blood.
In the autumn of the fourth year,
Tàibái (Venus) was in the center of Tàiwēi,
illuminating the ground like moonlight.
Tàibái represents soldiers,
and Tàiwēi represents the Celestial Court.
When Tàibái gains strength and enters Tàiwēi from the north,
this signifies a great army will enter the Son of Heaven's court.
At this time, Wáng Mǎng had sent the troops of the two dukes to Kūnyáng,
but they had already been defeated by Guāngwǔ.
Wáng Mǎng then appointed nine men as generals,
all of whom used "Tiger" in their titles.
The Jiǔhǔ Jiāngjūn (Nine Tiger Generals) reached Huàyīn
and were all defeated by the Hàn generals Dèng Yè and Lǐ Sōng.
They advanced to attack the capital;
the Cāng Jiāngjūn Hán Chén reached Chángmén.
On the wùshēn day of the tenth month,
Hàn troops entered through the Xuānpíng Chéngmén gate.
Two days later, on the jǐyǒu day,
several thousand young men in the city, including Zhū Dì and Zhāng Yú, rose up to attack Wáng Mǎng,
burning the Zuòshì gate
and hacking at the Jìngfǎ Tà gate.
The merchant Dù Wú killed Wáng Mǎng atop the Jiāntái,
and the Xiàowèi Gōngbīn Jiù cut off Wáng Mǎng's head.
Large armies trampled within the palace.
Then Gēngshǐ entered Cháng'ān;
the Chìméi (Red Eyebrow) rebels established Liú Pénzi as Son of Heaven,
and all entered the palace with large armies;
this was the manifestation of that portent.
In the ninth year of Jiànwǔ, in the seventh month, on the yǐchǒu day,
Jīn (Venus) encroached upon the great star of Xuānyuán.
In the eleventh month, on the yǐchǒu day,
Jīn (Venus) again encroached upon Xuānyuán.
Xuānyuán represents
the officials of the imperial harem;
the great star represents the empress,
and Jīn (Venus) encroaching upon it signifies a loss of power.
At this time, Empress Guō had already lost power and fallen out of favor,
and was later deposed as Zhōngshān Tàihòu (Empress Dowager of Zhōngshān),
while Noble Lady Yīn was established as empress.
In the tenth year, in the third month, on the guǐmǎo day,
a meteor, like the moon,
issued from Tàiwēi
and entered the sixth star of the Běidǒu Kuí (Dipper's Bowl);
its color was white.
Beside it, there were over ten small shooting stars;
when it extinguished, there was a sound like thunder,
and it stopped after about the time it takes to eat a meal.
Meteors represent noble envoys;
a large star means a great envoy,
a small star means a minor envoy.
Tàiwēi is the Son of Heaven's court,
and Běidǒu Kuí presides over killing.
A star issuing from Tàiwēi
and reaching Běidǒu Kuí
means that the Son of Heaven's great envoy will depart
to carry out an attack and killing.
In the twelfth month, on the jǐhài day,
a large meteor, like a jar,
issued from Liǔ (Willow), traveled southwest, and entered Zhěn (Chariot).
When it was about to extinguish,
it split into more than ten pieces,
like scattered fire.
Shortly after, there was a sound,
faintly like thunder.
Liǔ represents Zhōu,
and Zhěn represents Qín and Shǔ.
A large meteor issuing from Liǔ and entering Zhěn
signifies a great envoy departing from Zhōu and entering Shǔ.
At this time, Emperor Guāngwǔ sent the Dàsīmǎ Wú Hàn to dispatch thirty thousand Nányáng soldiers,
to sail upstream along the river
and attack Gōngsūn Shù at Báidì in Shǔ.
He also ordered generals Mǎ Wǔ, Liú Shàng, Guō Bà, Cén Péng, and Féng Jùn to pacify Wǔdū and Bājùn.
In the tenth month of the twelfth year,
Hàn advanced its troops to attack Shù's cousin, Wèiwèi Yǒng,
then reached Guǎngdū
and killed Shù's son-in-law Shǐ Xīng.
The Wēilǔ Jiāngjūn Féng Jùn captured Jiāngzhōu
and beheaded Shù's general Tián Róng.
Wú Hàn then attacked Shù's Dàsīmǎ Xiè Fēng,
beheading over five thousand.
Zāng Gōng broke through Fú
and killed Shù's brother, the Dàsīkōng Huī.
On the dīngchǒu day of the eleventh month,
the Hàn Hùjūn Jiāngjūn Gāo Wǔ stabbed Gōngsūn Shù through,
and he died that night.
The next day,
Hàn entered and massacred the city of Shǔ,
executing Shù's great generals Gōngsūn Huǎng, Yán Cén, and others,
killing tens of thousands of people,
and annihilating Shù's wife's clan and over ten thousand people.
This was the manifestation of the great envoy going forth to attack and kill.
As for the small shooting stars,
and the division into over ten pieces like scattered fire,
these were all symbols of minor generals following along.
The sound faintly like thunder
was a sign of the soldiers' rage.
In the first month of the year, on the jǐwèi day,
over a hundred small stars flowed,
some northwest,
some due north,
some northeast,
and ceased after two nights.
In the morning of the wùxū day of the sixth month,
over a hundred small meteors
traveled in all four directions.
Small stars represent
the common people.
Their flowing represents
the omen of migration.
Some northwest,
some northeast,
or traveling in all four directions,
are all signs of the common people migrating.
At this time, Gōngsūn Shù was being attacked in the northwest,
and Lú Fāng was being campaigned against in the north.
The Xiōngnú assisted Lú Fāng in invading the border;
Hàn sent General Mǎ Wǔ and Cavalry Commandants Liú Nà and Yán Xīng with troops to Qǔyáng, Línpíng, and Hūtuó
to guard against the Hú.
The Xiōngnú entered Hédōng;
Zhōngguó was not yet peaceful;
rice and grain were scarce and expensive,
and some people scattered and migrated.
Three years later,
Wú Hàn and Mǎ Wǔ again relocated over sixty thousand officials and common people from Yànmén, Dàijùn, Shànggǔ, and Guānxī counties,
settling them east of Chángshān Guān and Jūyōng Guān
to avoid Húkòu (barbarian raiders).
This was the manifestation of the common people's migration.
In the fifteenth year, in the first month, on the *dìngwèi* day,
a comet was seen in the Mǎo (Pleiades) constellation.
It moved slightly northwest into the Yíngshì (Encampment) constellation,
offending the Lí Gōng (Detached Palace).
In the third month, on the *yǐwèi* day,
it reached the Dōngbì (Eastern Wall) and vanished,
having been visible for forty-nine days.
A comet is for troops entering to eliminate filth.
Mǎo is for border troops,
so the appearance of a comet there means troops are arriving.
In the eleventh month,
Yīn Chéng, the Commandant of Dìngxiāng, rebelled,
and the Grand Administrator pursued and executed him.
Lú Fāng entered Gāoliǔ from among the Xiongnu.
By the tenth month of the sixteenth year, he surrendered,
presenting his seals and ribbons.
Another interpretation:
The Mǎo constellation is for legal affairs.
At this time, Ōuyáng Shè, the Grand Minister over the Masses, was imprisoned for an offense
and died more than a year later.
Yíngshì is
the Emperor's constant palace;
Lí Gōng is
where the imperial consorts reside.
A comet entering Yíngshì
and offending Lí Gōng
signifies the removal of a palace resident.
At this time, Empress Guō was already estranged.
By the tenth month of the seventeenth year,
she was deposed and made Empress Dowager of Zhōngshān,
and Noble Lady Yīn was established as Empress.
This was the omen of removing a palace resident.
In the thirtieth year, in the intercalary month, on the *jiǎwǔ* day,
a *shuǐ* (water-like vapor) at twenty degrees in the Dōngjǐng (Eastern Well) constellation
emitted a white vapor,
pointing southeast.
Its flame was five feet long,
forming a comet.
It moved northeast
and stopped at the western fence of the Zǐgōng (Purple Palace).
In the fifth month, on the *jiǎzǐ* day, it disappeared,
having been visible for thirty-one days in total.
Water is normally released from Dōngjǐng at the summer solstice.
The intercalary month was in the fourth month.
It appeared before it was due to be seen,
which means it was excessive and advanced.
Dōngjǐng is the Superintendent of Water,
so water emerging from it means great floods.
In the fifth month of this year and the following year,
there were great floods in the commanderies and kingdoms,
destroying cities and walls,
damaging crops,
and killing people.
White vapor signifies mourning.
A flame forming a comet,
a comet is for eliminating filth.
Zǐgōng is
the Emperor's palace.
A comet reaching its fence
is an omen of removing a palace resident.
Three years later,
Emperor Guāngwǔ passed away.
In the thirty-first year, in the seventh month,
on the *wǔwǔ* day,
Huǒ (Mars) was at one degree in the Yúguǐ (Ghost Cart) constellation,
entering the center of Guǐ.
It emerged half a degree south of the Shī Xīng (Corpse Star).
In the tenth month, on the *jǐhài* day,
it offended the great star of Xuānyuán.
Also, between the Qī Xīng (Seven Stars), there was a guest star,
with a flame about two feet long,
moving southwest.
By the twenty-second day of the second month of the following year,
it disappeared about six feet northeast of Yúguǐ,
having been visible for one hundred thirteen days in total.
Yínghuò (Mars) signifies misfortune and decline.
The Shī Xīng in Yúguǐ governs death,
so Yínghuò entering it means a great mourning.
Xuānyuán is for the imperial harem.
The Qī Xīng are
the territory of Zhōu.
A guest star dwelling there means death and mourning.
Two years later,
Emperor Guāngwǔ passed away.
In the Zhōngyuán
second year, in the eighth month, on the *dìngsì* day,
Huǒ (Mars) offended the southwest corner star of Tàiwēi,
separated by two *cun*.
In the tenth month, on the *wùzǐ* day,
a large meteor traveled from southwest to northeast,
with a sound like thunder.
Huǒ (Mars) offending the southwest corner star of Tàiwēi
is for generals and prime ministers.
Later, Grand Commandant Zhào Xǐ and Minister over the Masses Lǐ Xīn were dismissed from office for offenses.
A large meteor is for envoys.
This refers to Colonel Dòu Gù, Marquis of Yángxū Mǎ Wǔ, and Marquis of Yángxiāng Wáng Shǎng leading troops to conquer the west.
Astronomical Records, Chapter Twelve, Section Five. Hépíng 33, Shāng 1, Ān 46, Shùn 23, Zhì 3.
In the first year of Xiàomíng Yǒngpíng, in the fourth month, on the *dìngyǒu* day,
a meteor as large as a dipper
originated from the Tiānshìlóu (Celestial Market Tower),
moving southwest,
its light illuminating the ground.
A meteor is for foreign troops.
Moving southwest is for the southwestern barbarians.
At this time, Yìzhōu dispatched troops to attack the Gūfù Man-Yi Dàmóutì tribe and annihilate Líng,
beheading them and sending the heads to Luòyáng.
In the third year, in the sixth month, on the *dìngmǎo* day,
a comet appeared north of Tiānchuán (Celestial Boat),
about two feet long,
moving slightly north to the south of Kàng,
and departed after being visible for thirty-five days.
Tiānchuán is for water.
A comet appearing there signifies great floods.
In this year, the Yī and Luò rivers overflowed,
reaching the Jīnchéng Gate,
and destroying the Yī Bridge.
Seven commanderies and thirty-two counties all suffered great floods.
In the fourth year, in the eighth month, on the *xīnyǒu* day,
a guest star appeared in Gěnghé (River Guard),
pointing northwest to Guànsuǒ (Coiled Thong),
and departed after seventy days.
Gěnghé is for Hú (northern barbarian) troops.
By the eleventh month of the fifth year,
seven thousand cavalry of the Northern Xiongnu entered the Wǔyuán pass.
In the twelfth month, they again entered Yúnzhōng,
reaching Yuányáng.
Guànsuǒ is
a prison for noble persons.
In that twelfth month,
Liáng Sōng, Marquis of Língxīang, was imprisoned and died for resentful thoughts, secretly sending anonymous letters to slander the court.
His wife, children, and household were exiled to Jiǔzhēn.
In the seventh year, in the first month, on the *wùzǐ* day,
a meteor as large as a cup
traveled west from Zhīnǚ (Weaving Girl),
its light illuminating the ground.
Zhīnǚ is
the true maiden of Heaven.
A meteor appearing there
signifies the empress's sorrow.
In that month, on the *guǐmǎo* day,
Empress Guāngliè passed away.
In the eighth year, in the sixth month, on the *rénwǔ* day,
a long star appeared at thirty-seven degrees in Liǔ (Willow) and Zhāng (Extended Net),
offending Xuānyuán,
piercing Tiānchuán,
and overrunning Tàiwēi.
Its vapor reached the Upper Steps,
and it departed after being visible for fifty-six days in total.
Liǔ is
the territory of Zhōu.
This year had much rain,
damaging crops in fourteen commanderies.
In the ninth year, in the first month, on the *wùshēn* day,
a guest star appeared in Qiānniú (Cowherd),
eight feet long,
passing Jiànxīng (Establishing Star) to the south of Fáng,
and disappeared after being visible for fifty days.
Qiānniú governs Wú and Yuè.
Fáng and Xīn are for Sòng.
Later, Jīng, Prince of Guǎnglíng, with Shěn Liáng,
and Yīng, Prince of Chǔ, with Yán Zhōng, each plotted rebellion.
Their plots were discovered,
and they all committed suicide.
Guǎnglíng belonged to Wú,
Péngchéng was ancient Sòng territory.
In the thirteenth year, in the intercalary month, on the *dīnghài* day,
Huǒ (Mars) offended Yúguǐ,
signifying a great mourning.
The Zhì Xīng (Quality Star) is for high officials being executed.
In that twelfth month,
Yīng, Prince of Chǔ, with Yán Zhōng and others, fabricated sinister writings and plotted rebellion.
Their plot was discovered,
Yīng committed suicide,
and Zhōng and the others were all executed.
In the fourteenth year, in the first month, on the *wùzǐ* day,
a guest star appeared in Mǎo,
for sixty days,
and gradually disappeared at the right horn of Xuānyuán.
Mǎo governs border troops.
One year later,

the Hàn dispatched Dòu Gù, Marquis of Xiǎnqīn and Commandant of Attendant Chariots; Gěng Bǐng, Commandant of Mounted Escorts; Gěng Zhōng, Commandant of Cavalry; Qín Péng, Prefect of Kāiyáng City Gate; and Jì Róng, Grand Coachman,
leading troops to attack the Xiongnu.
Another interpretation:
The right horn of Xuānyuán is for noble ministers.
Mǎo is for legal affairs.
A guest star guarding it signifies a great imprisonment.
At this time, the investigation into the Chǔ affair was not yet concluded.
Sītú Yú Yán was found to be in contact with Huáng Chū and Gōngsūn Hóng, members of Prince Yīng of Chǔ's faction.
They all committed suicide,
or were imprisoned and executed.
In the fifteenth year, in the eleventh month, on the *yǐchǒu* day,
Tàibái (Venus) entered the moon,
signifying the execution of a great general,
and the death of the sovereign,
within three years.
Three years later,
Emperor Xiàomíng passed away.
In the sixteenth year, in the first month, on the *dīngchǒu* day,
the Jupiter star encroached upon the right outer flank of Fángxiù.
The northernmost of its three stars disappeared
and was only seen again on the *xīnsì* day.
The right outer flank of Fángxiù represents high officials;
Jupiter encroaching upon it indicates their execution.
Subsequently, the Minister of Works, Xíng Mù,
was implicated in illicit communication with Yán, Prince of Fùlíng, and in treasonous plotting, and committed suicide.
In the fourth month, on the *guǐwèi* day,
Venus encroached upon Bìxiù.
Bìxiù represents border troops.
Later, the Northern Xiōngnú raided the border,
entered Yúnzhōng,
and reached Yúyáng.
The envoy Gāo Hóng dispatched troops from three commanderies to pursue and attack them,
but achieved nothing.
The Grand Coachman, Jì Róng, was imprisoned for failing to advance.
In the eighteenth year, in the sixth month, on the *jǐwèi* day,
a comet appeared in Zhāngxiù,
three *chǐ* long,
then moved to Lángjiāng,
and entered Tàiwēi to the south,
all belonging to Zhāngxiù.
Zhāngxiù
is the territory of Zhōu
and represents the eastern capital.
Tàiwēi
is the Emperor's court.
A comet encroaching upon them signifies war and death.
In the eighth month of that year, on the *rénzǐ* day,
Emperor Xiàomíng died.
In the first year of Jiànchū under Emperor Xiàozhāng,
in the first month, on the *dīngsì* day,
Venus was one *chǐ* west of Mǎoxiù.
In the eighth month, on the *gēngyín* day,
a comet appeared in Tiānshì,
about two *chǐ* long,
gradually moved three degrees into Qiānniú,
and slowly disappeared after forty days.
Venus in Mǎoxiù represents border troops,
a comet appearing in Tiānshì represents foreign armies,
and Qiānniú represents Wú and Yuè.
At this time, the Man barbarians Chén Zòng and others, as well as Lèi, King of Āiláo, rebelled,
attacking Kuítáng city.
Wáng Xún, the Administrator of Yǒngchāng, fled to Diéyú,
and Sòng Yán, the Chief of Ānyí, was killed by the Qiāng.
Fù Yù, the Administrator of Wǔwēi, was appointed Colonel Protector of the Qiāng,
and Mǎ Fáng served as General of Chariots and Cavalry,
to campaign against the Western Qiāng.
Furthermore, Yán, Prince of Fùlíng, plotted rebellion with his son Máo Fáng,
committing high treason and heinous acts,
but was not executed.
He was demoted to a marquis.
In the second year, in the ninth month,
on the *jiǎyín* day,
a meteor passed through Zǐgōng,
several *zhàng* long,
scattered into three,
and vanished.
In the twelfth month, on the *wùyín* day,
a comet appeared three degrees in Lóuxìu,
eight or nine *chǐ* long,
gradually entered Zǐgōng,
and slowly disappeared after one hundred and six days.
A meteor passing
and entering Zǐgōng
always portends harm to great personages.
Four years later, in the sixth month, on the *guǐchǒu* day,
Empress Míngdé died.
In the second year of Yuánhé, in the fourth month, on the *dīngsì* day,
a guest star appeared in the east in the morning,
eight degrees in Wèixiù,
three *chǐ* long,
passed through Gédào and entered Zǐgōng,
stayed for forty days and then vanished.
Gédào and Zǐgōng
are the palaces of the Son of Heaven.
A guest star encroaching and staying for a long time indicates a great funeral.
Four years later,
Emperor Xiàozhāng died.
In the first year of Yǒngyuán under Emperor Xiàohé, in the first month, on the *xīnmǎo* day,
a meteor rose from Shēnxìu,
four *zhàng* long,
with light,
yellowish-white in color.
In the second month,
a meteor rose from Tiānbàng,
traveled northeast for about three *zhàng* and vanished,
bluish-white in color.
On the *rénshēn* day,
at night, a meteor rose from the eastern wall of Tàiwēi,
three *zhàng* long.
In the third month,
on the *bǐngchén* day,
a meteor rose from Tiānjīn.
On the *rénxū* day,
a meteor rose from Tiānjiāngjūn,
traveling northeast.
Shēnxìu represents border troops,
Tiānbàng represents troops,
Tàiwēi is the celestial court,
Tiānjīn represents water,
Tiānjiāngjūn represents troops;
meteors rising from them all signify troops.
In the sixth month of that year,
the Hàn dispatched Dòu Xiàn, General of Chariots and Cavalry, and Gěng Bǐng, Keeper of the Gilded Seal,
along with Dèng Hóng, General Who Crosses the Liao, to depart from Shuòfāng,
advancing troops to the shores of Sīqú Běidīhai,
beheading over ten thousand enemy heads,
and capturing one million livestock including people, cattle, horses, and sheep.
Eighty-one tribes, including the Rìzhú King, surrendered,
totaling over three hundred thousand people.
The Chányú was pursued to the Western Sea.
In the seventh month of that year,
there were also floods that swept away people,
which was the corresponding omen.
In the second year, in the first month, on the *yǐmǎo* day,
Venus and Jupiter were both in Kuíxiù.
On the *bǐngyín* day,
Mercury was also in Kuíxiù.
Kuíxiù governs armories and weapons,
and the conjunction of three stars also indicates war and death.
On the *xīnwèi* day,
Mercury, Venus, and Jupiter were in Lóuxiù,
also signifying war,
and also secret plotting.
In the second month, on the *dīngyǒu* day,
a meteor as large as a peach
rose from the eastern wall of Zǐgōng,
traveled northwest for five *zhàng* and slowly vanished.
In the fourth month, on the *bǐngchén* day,
a meteor as large as a melon
rose from the northeast of Wénchāng,
traveled southwest until it vanished west of Shàowēi.
Shortly after, a sound like thunder was heard,
and then Venus was about two *chǐ* northeast of the great star of Xuānyuán.
In the eighth month, on the *dīngwèi* day,
a meteor like a hen's egg
rose from the west of Tàiwēi,
traveled southeast for four *zhàng* and disappeared.
In the tenth month, on the *guǐwèi* day,
a meteor as large as a peach
rose from Tiānjīn,
traveled west for six *zhàng* and disappeared.
In the eleventh month, on the *xīnyǒu* day,
a meteor as large as a fist
rose from Zǐgōng,
traveled west to Wèixiù and disappeared.
In the third year, in the ninth month, on the *dīngmǎo* day,
a meteor as large as a hen's egg
rose from Zǐgōng,
traveled southwest and disappeared between the handle of the Northern Dipper.
Zǐgōng is the Emperor's palace,
Wénchāng and Shàowēi represent high officials,
Tiānjīn represents water,
and the Northern Dipper presides over killing.
Meteors rising,
passing through Zǐgōng, Wénchāng, Shàowēi, and Tiānjīn,
Wénchāng representing the Emperor's envoys,
indicate military campaigns and executions.
Dòu Xiàn was the General-in-Chief.
Xiàn's younger brothers Dǔ and Jǐng were all ministers and colonels.
Xiàn's younger sister's husband, Guō Jǔ, was a Palace Attendant and Colonel of Archery,
and with Yuán, the mother of Dèng Dié, the Commandant of the Guards, frequently entered and exited the palace,
plotting rebellion.
By the fourth year, in the sixth month, on the *bǐngchén* day, their plot was discovered.
Emperor Hé visited the Northern Palace,
and issued an edict to the Keeper of the Gilded Seal and the Five Colonels to mobilize troops and garrison the Southern and Northern Palaces,
close the city gates,
and arrest Jǔ.
Jǔ's father, Huáng, the Chief of Chánglè for the Minor Treasury, and Dié,
Dié's younger brother Lěi, the Colonel of Infantry,
and their mother Yuán,
were all imprisoned and executed.
Xiàn's younger brothers Dǔ and Jǐng all committed suicide.
Venus encroaching upon Xuānyuán signifies the loss of power for the empress.
The Dòu clan was executed,
and the Empress Dowager lost her influence.
In the fifth year,
on the guǐ-sì day of the fourth month,
Tài Bái, Yíng Huò, and Chén Xīng were all in Dōng Jǐng.
On the rén-wǔ day of the seventh month,
Suì Xīng trespassed against the great star of Xuān Yuán.
In the ninth month,
Jīn was within the head of Nán Dǒu.
Huǒ trespassed against the first northern star of Fáng.
Dōng Jǐng
is the land of Qín,
representing law.
When three stars conjoin,
there are internal and external military conflicts,
and it also signifies decrees and water.
When Jīn enters the mouth of Dǒu,
it means a great general will die.
When Huǒ trespasses against the first northern star of Fáng,
it refers to a general or chancellor.
In the first month of the sixth year,
Sī Tú Dīng Hóng passed away.
In the seventh month, there were floods,
which caused great devastation, killing people,
and damaging the five grains.
Hǔ Mǎ Guāng, Marquis of Xǔ, committed suicide due to crimes.
In the ninth month,
Xíng Chē Jì Jiāng Jūn Shì Dèng Hóng and Yuè Qí Xiào Wèi Féng Zhù dispatched the Zǔo Yòu Yǔ Lín, Běi Jūn Wǔ Xiào soldiers, and archers from eight commanderies, Wū Huán, and Xiān Bēi,
a total of forty thousand cavalry,
together with Dù Liáo Jiāng Jūn Zhū Zhēng, Hù Wū Huán Xiào Wèi Rén Shàng, and Zhōng Láng Jiāng Dù Chóng, to campaign against the rebellious Hú.
In the twelfth month,
Chē Jì Jiāng Jūn Hóng was imprisoned and executed for failing in the pursuit of the captives;
Dù Liáo Jiāng Jūn Zhēng and Zhōng Láng Jiāng Chóng were both found guilty.
On the dīng-wèi day of the first month of the seventh year,
a shooting star rose from Tiān Jīn
and extinguished in Zǐ Gōng.
Its color was bluish-yellow,
and it emitted light.
On the guǐ-yǒu day of the second month,
Jīn and Huǒ were both in Cān.
On the wù-yín day,
Jīn and Huǒ were both in Dōng Jǐng.
On the jiǎ-yín day of the eighth month,
Shuǐ, Tǔ, and Jīn were all in Zhěn.
On the jiǎ-xū day of the eleventh month,
Jīn and Huǒ were both in Xīn.
On the jǐ-mǎo day of the twelfth month,
a shooting star rose from Wén Chāng
and vanished in Zǐ Gōng.
On the bǐng-chén day,
Huǒ, Jīn, and Shuǐ were all in Dǒu.
A shooting star entering Zǐ Gōng,
and Jīn and Huǒ being in Xīn,
all signify great mourning.
Three stars conjoining in Zhěn signifies a gathering of commoners.
Jīn and Huǒ being both in Cān and Dōng Jǐng
all signify external military conflicts,
with a general dying.
Three stars all in Dǒu
signify the execution of a general,
or the death of a chancellor.
In the fourth month of the eighth year, Yuè Chéng Wáng Dǎng,
and in the seventh month, Yuè Chéng Wáng Zōng, both passed away.
Jiāng Bīng Cháng Shǐ Wú Shēn was summoned for a crime, imprisoned, and executed.
In the tenth month,
Běi Hǎi Wáng Wēi committed suicide.
In the twelfth month,
Chén Wáng Xiàn passed away.
In the intercalary month of the ninth year,
Empress Dowager Dòu passed away.
The Xiān Bēi of Liáo Dōng rebelled.
Tài Shǒu Jì Cān failed to pursue the captives,
was summoned, imprisoned, and executed.
In the ninth month,
Sī Tú Liú Fāng was dismissed from office for a crime
and committed suicide.
The Qiāng of Lǒng Xī rebelled.
Zhí Jīn Wǔ Liú Shàng was dispatched to act as Zhēng Xī Jiāng Jūn Shì,
and Yuè Qí Xiào Wèi Jié Xiāng Hóu Zhào Shì dispatched the Běi Jūn Wǔ Xiào, Límíng, Yōng, and border Hú soldiers, numbering thirty thousand cavalry,
to campaign against the Western Qiāng.
On the bǐng-wǔ day of the fifth month of the eleventh year,
a shooting star as large as a melon
rose from Dī,
moving southwest,
gradually emitting light,
and was white in color.
The prognostication stated:
"A white shooting star
signifies a visiting envoy,
large means a great envoy,
small means a minor envoy.
A swift period means swift action.
Likewise.
As large as a melon means a close minor official.
Moving with gradually increasing light means it will succeed.
Moreover, on the King's rightful day,
there will be someone on the frontier who receives the King's mandate."
In the second month of the following year,
the kings Táng Zēng and others of the Bái Láng Lóu Báo tribes, from the indigenous people outside the Máoniú bastion in Shǔ Jùn, numbering 170,000, submitted and became subjects,
and were granted gold seals, purple ribbons, money, and silk.
On the guǐ-yǒu day of the eleventh month of the twelfth year,
at night, there was a pale blue aura,
thirty feet long,
rising from Tiān Yuán,
pointing northeast towards Jūn Shì,
estimated to last ten days.
The prognostication stated:
"War will break out,
the ten-day period refers to a year."
In the eleventh month of the following year,
two thousand Xiān Bēi cavalry from Liáo Dōng raided Yòu Běi Píng.
In the thirteenth year,
on the yǐ-chǒu day of the eleventh month,
a small guest star, bluish-yellow in color, appeared between the fourth star of Xuān Yuán.
Xuān Yuán represents the imperial harem.
A star appearing there
signifies loss of power.
In the sixth month of the fourteenth year, on the xīn-mǎo day,
Empress Yīn was deposed.
On the dīng-wèi day of the fourth month of the sixteenth year,
white qi like powder and floss was generated in Zǐ Gōng.
On the wù-wǔ day,
a guest star appeared in Zǐ Gōng, moved west to Áng,
and extinguished on the rén-shēn day of the fifth month.
On the gēng-wǔ day of the seventh month,
Shuǐ was in Yú Guǐ.
On the xīn-hài day of the tenth month,
a shooting star rose from Gōu Chén,
moved thirty feet north,
emitting light,
and was yellow in color.
White qi appearing in Zǐ Gōng signifies mourning.
A guest star moving west from Zǐ Gōng to Áng refers to Zhào.
Yú Guǐ signifies death and mourning.
Gōu Chén represents the empress,
and a shooting star appearing from it signifies a palace envoy.
A year later,
in the twelfth month of Yuán Xīng first year (second day),
Emperor Hé passed away,
Emperor Shāng ascended the throne for one year and then also passed away,
without an heir.
Empress Dowager Dèng sent an envoy to welcome the son of Qīng Hé Xiào Wáng to ascend the throne,
who became Emperor Xiào Ān,
which was the fulfillment of these portents.
Qīng Hé
is the land of Zhào.
On the gēng-chén day of the second month of Yuán Xīng first year,
a shooting star rose about five zhàng from Jiǎo and Kàng.
On the xīn-hài day of the fourth month,
a shooting star rose from Dǒu,
moving northeast to Xū Nǚ.
On the jǐ-sì day of the seventh month,
a shooting star rose about five zhàng from Tiān Shì,
its light reddish.
On the xīn-hài day of the intercalary month,
Shuǐ and Jīn were both in Dī.
A shooting star rising from Dǒu
and moving northeast to Xū Nǚ.
Xū Nǚ
is the land of Yān.
Tiān Shì represents external armies.
The conjunction of Shuǐ and Jīn signifies military punishment.
In that year,
the Mò people of Liáo Dōng rebelled,
raiding six counties.
Wū Huán troops from Shàng Gǔ, Yú Yáng, Yòu Běi Píng, and Liáo Xī were dispatched to attack them.
On the dīng-yǒu day of the first month of Xiào Shāng Dì Yán Píng first year,
Jīn and Huǒ were in Lóu.
The conjunction of Jīn and Huǒ signifies a flash,
and foretells distress for a great person.
In the eighth month of that year, on the xīn-hài day,
Emperor Xiào Shāng passed away.
In the fifth month, on the day *wùyín*, in the first year of Yǒngchū of [Emperor] Xiào'ān,
Mars retrograded and guarded the Front Star of Xīn.
In the eighth month, on the day *wùshēn*,
a guest star appeared in Dōngjǐng and to the southwest of Hú.
Xīn represents the Mingtang of the Son of Heaven.
Mars retrograding and guarding it
signifies rebellious officials.
A guest star in Dōngjǐng
signifies great floods.
At this time,
Emperor Ān had not yet taken charge of the court,
Empress Dowager Dèng was regent,
Dèng Zhì was General of Chariots and Cavalry,
and his younger brothers Hóng, Kuí, and Chāng were all enfeoffed as marquises as Commandants,
holding the reins of national power.
Sīkōng Zhōu Zhāng was displeased,
and conspired with Wáng Zūn, Shū Yuánmào, and others,
intending to close the palace gates,
arrest the General and his brothers,
execute the regular attendants Zhèng Zhòng and Cài Lún,
abduct and assassinate the Shangshū,
depose the Empress Dowager,
and enfeoff the Emperor as a king of a distant state.
The plot was discovered,
and Zhāng committed suicide.
Dōngjǐng and Hú are both territories of Qín.
At this time, the Qiāng rebelled,
cutting off the Lǒng path.
Hàn dispatched Zhì to lead the Left and Right Yǔlín, the Five Bureaus of the Northern Army, and troops from various commanderies to suppress them.
In this year, 315 counties in 41 commanderies experienced heavy rain.
The Four Rivers overflowed,
damaging the autumn crops,
destroying cities,
and killing people,
which was the omen's fulfillment.
In the first month, on the day *wùzǐ*, of the second year,
Venus was visible during the day.
In the first month, on the day *gēngxū*, of the third year,
the Moon violated the Rear Star of Xīn.
On the day *jǐhài*,
Venus entered Dǒu.
In the twelfth month,
a comet appeared south of Tiānwǎn,
pointing northeast,
six or seven *chǐ* long,
and pale white in color.
Venus being visible during the day
signifies powerful officials.
At this time, the Dèng clan was flourishing.
The Moon violating the Rear Star of Xīn
was unfavorable to children.
Xīn represents Sòng.
In the fifth month, on the day *dīngyǒu*,
the King of Pèi, [Liú] Zhèng, passed away.
Venus entering Dǒu
signifies ill fortune for noble generals.
Tiānwǎn represents the outer army,
and a comet appearing south of it signifies external troops.
Subsequently, the Qiāng and Dī were dispatched to suppress the bandit Lǐ Guì,
the Wūhuán were dispatched to attack the Xiānbēi,
and Zhongláng Jiāng Rèn Shàng and Hù Qiāng Xiàowèi Mǎ Xián were dispatched to attack the Qiāng,
and they all surrendered.
In the fourth year,
in the sixth month, on the day *jiǎzǐ*,
a guest star as large as a plum,
pale white,
with an aura two *chǐ* long,
pointed southwest towards the Shàngjiē stars.
On the day *guǐyǒu*,
Venus entered Yúguǐ.
Pointing to Shàngjiē
signifies the Three Dukes.
Later, Grand Commandant Zhāng Yǔ and Sīkōng Zhāng Mǐn were both dismissed from office.
Venus entering Yúguǐ
signifies ill fortune for generals.
Later, Zhongláng Jiāng Rèn Shàng was implicated in embezzlement of ten million [cash],
brought in a cage-cart,
and executed in the marketplace.
In the sixth month, on the day *xīnchǒu*, of the fifth year,
Venus was visible during the day,
traversing the sky.
In the third month, on the day *guǐyǒu*, of the first year of Yuánchū,
Mars entered Yúguǐ.
In the ninth month, on the day *xīnyǒu*, of the second year,
Mars entered the center of Yúguǐ.
In the third month of the third year,
Mars entered the center of Yúguǐ.
In the fifth month, on the day *bǐngyín*,
Venus entered Bìkǒu.
In the seventh month, on the day *jiǎyín*,
Jupiter entered Yúguǐ.
In the intercalary month, on the day *jǐwèi*,
Venus violated Zuǒzhífǎ of Tàiwēi.
In the eleventh month, on the day *jiǎwǔ*,
a guest star was seen in the west,
on the day *jǐhài* it was in Xū and Wēi,
extending south to Wèi and Mǎo.
In the first month, on the day *bǐngxū*, of the fourth year,
Jupiter lingered in the center of Yúguǐ.
On the day *yǐwèi*,
Venus was visible during the day above Bǐng.
In the fourth month, on the day *rénxū*,
Venus entered the center of Yúguǐ.
On the day *jǐsì*,
Mercury entered the center of Yúguǐ.
In the fifth month, on the day *jǐmǎo*,
Mercury violated Jupiter.
In the sixth month, on the day *bǐngshēn*,
Mars entered the center of Yúguǐ,
on the day *wùxū*,
it violated the Great Star of Yúguǐ.
In the ninth month, on the day *xīnsì*,
Venus entered the center of Nándǒu.
In the third month, on the day *bǐngshēn*, of the fifth year,
Saturn violated Yuèxīng of Dōngjǐng.
In the fifth month, on the day *gēngwǔ*,
Mercury violated Zhìxīng of Yúguǐ.
On the day *bǐngxū*,
Venus violated Yuèxīng.
In the fourth month, on the day *guǐchǒu*, of the sixth year,
Venus entered Yúguǐ.
In the sixth month, on the day *bǐngxū*,
Mars was in the center of Yúguǐ.
On the day *dīngmǎo*,
Saturn was in the center of Yúguǐ.
〔一０〕On the day *xīnsì*,
Venus violated Zuǒzhífǎ.
From the fifth year of Yǒngchū to Yǒngníng,
within these ten years,
Venus was visible during the day traversing the sky once,
entered Yúguǐ twice,
guarded Bì once,
violated Zuǒzhífǎ twice,
entered Nándǒu,
and violated Yuèxīng.
Mars entered Yúguǐ five times.
Saturn violated Yuèxīng of Dōngjǐng once,
and entered Yúguǐ once.
Jupiter and Mercury entered Yúguǐ twice.
All five planets entering the center of Yúguǐ
signifies deaths and mourning.
Mars and Venus severely violating Yuè and Zhì stars signifies executions.
Dǒu represents noble generals.
Zuǒzhífǎ represents close officials.
A guest star in Xū and Wēi signifies mourning,
and weeping.
〔一一〕Mǎo and Bì represent border troops,
and also prison affairs.
Then, in the third month, on the day *guǐsì*, of the first year of Jiànguāng,
Empress Dowager Dèng passed away;
in the fifth month, on the day *gēngchén*, the Empress Dowager's brother, General of Chariots and Cavalry Dèng Zhì, and six other marquises were all dismissed from office,
and committed suicide,
which was the fulfillment of the omens.
In the second year of Yánguāng
(123 CE), in the eighth month, on the day Jǐhài,
Mars appeared at the Dānmén of Tàiwēi.
In the third year (124 CE), in the second month, on the day Xīnwèi,
Venus encroached upon Mǎo.
In the fifth month, on the day Guǐchǒu,
Venus entered Bì.
In the ninth month, on the day Rényín,
Saturn encroached upon Zuǒzhífǎ.
In the fourth year (125 CE),
Venus entered Yúguǐ.
In the sixth month, on the day Rénchén,
Venus emerged from Tàiwēi.
In the ninth month, on the day Jiǎzǐ,
Venus entered Dǒukǒu.
In the eleventh month,
a guest star was seen in Tiānshì.
Mars appearing from Tàiwēi
signifies rebellious officials.
Venus encroaching upon Mǎo and Bì
signifies border troops;
one interpretation is that a great person will bear the consequences.
Saturn encroaching upon Zuǒzhífǎ
signifies the execution of officials.
Venus entering Yúguǐ
signifies a great mourning.
Venus emerging from Tàiwēi
signifies troops in the central palace;
entering Dǒukǒu
signifies that noble generals and chancellors will be executed.
A guest star appearing in Tiānshì
signifies a noble's death.

At this time, Grand General Gěng Bǎo, Palace Attendants Jiāng Jīng and Fán Fēng, and Junior Palace Attendant Liú Ān, along with Wet Nurse Wáng Shèng and her children Zǐ Yǒng and others, conspired to slander Crown Prince Bǎo.
They also disliked the Crown Prince's wet nurse Nán and the kitchen supervisor Bǐng Jí.
In the third year, in the ninth month, on the day Dīngyǒu,
Crown Prince Bǎo was deposed as King of Jìyīn,
and Hóu Yì of Běixiāng was installed in his place.
Nán and Jí were killed,
and their parents, wives, and children were exiled to Rìnán.
In the fourth year, in the third month, on the day Dīngmǎo,
Emperor Ān, while on an imperial tour,
returned from Nányáng.
On the way, he fell ill
and collapsed upon reaching Yè. Empress Yán, her brother Commander of the Guard Yán Xiǎn, Palace Attendant Jiāng Jīng, and others
jointly concealed the emperor's death,
not allowing the officials to know of the emperor's demise.
They sent Minister of Works Liú Xǐ and others to go separately to the suburban temples
to announce to Heaven and plead for his life,
and then carried him into the Běigōng.
On the evening of Gēngwǔ, his death was announced,
and Lady Yán was honored as Empress Dowager.
Hóu Yì of Běixiāng fell ill and died.
Jiāng Jīng and others again did not wish to enthrone Bǎo.
They reported to the Empress Dowager
and sought to summon other princes to choose a successor.
However, Palace Attendants Sūn Chéng, Wáng Guó, Wáng Kāng, and nineteen others
conspired to execute Yán Xiǎn, Jiāng Jīng, and others,
and enthroned Bǎo as the Son of Heaven.
This was Emperor Xiàoshùn.
All these treacherous people and powerful officials brought chaos to the imperial house,
leading to deaths and executions,
and troops rising within the palace.
This was their consequence.
In the second year of Yǒngjiàn (127 CE) of Emperor Xiàoshùn, in the second month, on the day Guǐwèi,
Venus was visible during the day for thirty-nine days.
In the intercalary month, on the day Yǐyǒu,
Venus was visible during the day in the southeast for forty-one days.
In the eighth month, on the day Yǐsì,
Mars entered Yúguǐ.
Venus visible during the day
signifies powerful officials.
Mars signifies misfortune.
Yúguǐ signifies death and mourning.
Zhìxīng signifies executions.

At this time, Palace Attendants Gāo Fàn and Zhāng Fáng, Grand Master of Works Zhái Pú, Minister of the Imperial Secretariat Gāo Tángzhī, Palace Assistant Supervisor Zhāng Dūn, Minister Yǐn Jiù, Gentleman Jiāng Shù, Yáng Fèng, and others,
as well as Inspector of Yǎnzhōu Bào Jiù, Commandant-Protector of the Southern Xiongnú Zhāng Guó, Administrator of Jīnchéng Zhāng Dǔ, and Administrator of Dūnhuáng Zhāng Lǎng,
engaged in mutual illicit communication,
which was leaked.
Jiù and Shù were executed in the marketplace,
and Fàn, Fáng, Pú, Zhī, Dūn, Fèng, Jiù, and Guó were all condemned for their crimes.
Furthermore, Bān Shǐ, Marquis of Dìngyuǎn, married Princess Yīnchéng Jiāndé.
They quarreled, and Bān Shǐ killed Jiāndé.
For this crime, he was summarily executed by decapitation in the horse market,
and all his siblings were also executed in the marketplace.
In the sixth year (131 CE), in the fourth month,
Mars entered Tàiwēi,
encroaching upon Zuǒzhífǎ and Yòuzhífǎ by about six inches to the northwest.
In the tenth month, on the day Yǐmǎo,
Venus was visible during the day.
In the twelfth month, on the day Rényīn,
a guest star with a luminous vapor more than two feet long
pointed southwest,
its color grayish-white,
located six degrees from Qiānniú.
A guest star with white luminous vapor signifies military conflict.
Qiānniú signifies Wú and Yuè.
A year later,
pirates from Kuàijī, led by Céng Yú and over a thousand others, burned Gōuzhāng,
killed the chief administrator,
and also killed the chief administrators of Yín and Mào.
They seized government troops,
captured and killed officials and common people,
and attacked the Eastern Commandant's office.
In Yángzhōu, the rebellious bandits Zhāng Hé and others, claiming the title of general,
attacked forty-nine counties,
extensively plundering officials and common people.
In the first year of Yángjiā (132 CE), in the intercalary month, on the day Wùzǐ,
a guest star with white vapor,
two feet wide and five zhàng long,
arose from the southwest of Tiānwǎn.
It presides over horses and cattle,
signifying foreign armies.
White color signifies military conflict.
At this time,
Administrator of Dūnhuáng Xú Bái dispatched troops of King Pán of Shūlè and others, totaling twenty thousand men, to enter Yútián territory,
where they plundered and decapitated over three hundred people.
Commandant of Wūhuán Gěng Huá sent Wūhuán pro-Hàn Colonel Róng Mòhuì and others out of the pass
to raid the Xiānbēi,
decapitating some and
capturing living captives and valuables.
The Xiānbēi, resentful,
raided Liáodōng and Dàijùn,
killing and injuring officials and common people.
After this,
the Western Róng and Northern Dí became marauders,
initiating military actions involving horses and cattle.
Horses and cattle also died and were injured in the conflict,
which did not cease for over ten years.
In the second year of Yǒnghé (137 CE), in the fifth month, on the day Wùshēn,
Venus was visible during the day.
In the eighth month, on the day Gēngzǐ,
Mars encroached upon Nándǒu.
Dǒu signifies Wú.
In the following year, in the fifth month,
Yáng Zhēn, acting as Chief Clerk to the Administrator of Wú County, along with his brother Yè from the Yuè army, and officials and common people such as Wú Tóng, totaling over two hundred people,
rose in rebellion,
killing officials and common people,
burning official lodges and civilian houses,
and attacking the Administrator's office.
Administrator Wáng Héng defended the office,
and his officials and soldiers fought and killed Zhēn and others.
Furthermore, the bandits from Jiǔjiāng, Cài Bóliú and several hundred others, attacked Guǎnglíng and Jiǔjiāng,
burned cities and outer walls,
and killed the chief administrator of Jiāngdū.
In the second month of the third year, on the day *Xīnsì*,
Tàibái was seen in daylight.
On the day *Wùzǐ*,
it was in the southwest of Yínghuò,
its rays clashing.
On the day *Xīnchǒu*,
there was a shooting star as large as a *dǒu*,
traveling from the northwest to the east,
eight or nine *chǐ* long,
reddish-yellow in color,
with a rumbling sound like thunder.
In the third month, on the day *Rénzǐ*,
Tàibái was seen in daylight.
In the sixth month, on the day *Bǐngwǔ*,
Tàibái was seen in daylight.
In the eighth month,
on the day *Yǐmǎo*,
Tàibái was seen in daylight.
In the intercalary month, on the day *Jiǎyín*,
Chénxīng entered Yúguǐ.
On the day *Jǐyǒu*,
Yínghuò entered Tàiwēi.
On the day *Yǐmǎo*,
Tàibái was seen in daylight.
Tàibái [Venus] is
the official of generals,
and also represents the western regions.
When seen in daylight,
it signifies the ascendancy of *yīn* energy,
competing with the ruler for brightness.
Yínghuò [Mars] clashing with Tàibái [Venus]
portends warfare and mourning.
A shooting star signifies an envoy.
Its rumbling sound
is a sign of anger.
Chénxīng [Mercury] entering Yúguǐ [28 mansions of the Chinese zodiac]
means that a high minister will die.
Yínghuò [Mars] entering Tàiwēi [Grand Palace constellation]
means rebellious officials are in the court.
At this time,
the Grand General Liáng Shāng and his son wielded power,
hence Tàibái [Venus] was frequently seen in daylight.
In the first month of the fourth year,
when sacrifices were made to the southern suburbs,
and the sacrificial animals were prepared in the evening,

the palace attendants Zhāng Kuí, Qú Zhèng, Yáng Dìng, the Director of the Inner Bureau Shí Guāng, the Director of the Imperial Workshops Fù Fú, and others contended for power with the palace attendants Cáo Téng and Mèng Bēn.
They falsely reported to the emperor that Téng and Bēn were plotting rebellion with Shāng,
and fabricated an imperial edict to arrest Téng and Bēn.
Bēn explained himself,
and Emperor Shùnwàng became aware [of the truth],
releasing Téng and Bēn from their bonds.
Kuí and the others, knowing their scheme had failed,
each fled,
some stabbing themselves,
discarding their *diāochán* [official headgear] and hiding in the grass to escape,
but all managed to get away.
In the sixth year,
the General Who Conquers the West Mǎ Xián attacked the Western Qiāng at the foot of Shègū Shān in Běidì.
He and his son were killed by the Qiāng.
This was the fulfillment of the omen.
In the seventh month of the fourth year, on the day *Rénwǔ*,
Yínghuò [Mars] entered Nándǒu [Southern Dipper] and clashed with the third star.
In the fourth month of the fifth year, on the day *Wùwǔ*,
Tàibái [Venus] was seen in daylight.
In the eighth month, on the day *Jǐyǒu*,
Yínghuò [Mars] entered Tàiwēi.
Dǒu [Dipper] represents high-ranking officials
and Yángzhōu.
Yínghuò [Mars] clashing with and entering it portends warfare and mourning.
In the sixth year,
Grand General Shāng died.
Bandits Zhōu Shēng and Mǎ Miǎn from Jiǔjiāng and Dānyáng raised troops and attacked and captured prefectures and counties.
The Liáng clan again monopolized power in the imperial court.
In the second month of the sixth year, on the day *Dīngsì*,
a comet was seen in the east,
six or seven *chǐ* long,
bluish-white in color,
pointing southwest towards Yíngshì and Fénmù stars.
On the day *Dīngchǒu*,
the comet was at one degree of Kuí,
six *chǐ* long.
On the day *Guǐwèi*, it was seen at dusk,
passing northwest through Mǎo and Bì.
On the day *Jiǎshēn*,
it was in Dōngjǐng,
then passed through Yúguǐ, Liǔ, Qīxīng, Zhāng,
its fiery glow reaching Sāntái,
and extinguished in Xuānyuán.
Yíngshì [Encampment] is
the permanent palace of the Son of Heaven.
Fénmù [Tombs] governs death.
When a comet appears in Yíngshì and Fénmù,
within five years,
there will be a great mourning throughout the realm.
Four years later,
Emperor Xiàoshùn died.
Mǎo [Pleiades] represents border troops
and also Zhào.
The Qiāng, Zhōu, and Mǎ father and son later indeed became bandits.
Also, Liú Wén kidnapped the Administrator of Qīnghé, Shè Gǎo,
wanting to enthrone Wáng Suàn as the Son of Heaven.
Gǎo refused to comply
and was killed.
The King [Suàn] shut his gates and resisted Wén.
Government troops captured and executed Wén.
Suàn, having been kidnapped by a wicked person,
was demoted to Marquis of Wèishì,
then transferred to Marquis of Jiànyáng Dūxiāng.
He died
and his state was extinguished.
Passing through Dōngjǐng [East Well] and Yúguǐ [Ghost Carriage] represents Qín,
all plundered by the Qiāng.
The flames reaching Sāntái [Three Terraces]
represent the Three Ducal Ministers.
At this time,
Grand Commandant Dù Qiáo and the former Grand Commandant Lǐ Gù were entrapped by Liáng Jì,
and died due to official documents.
And as for Zhù and Zhāng representing Zhōu,
extinguishing in Xuānyuán represents the imperial harem.
Subsequently, Empress Yìxiàn died of sorrow,
and the Liáng clan was executed.
This was the fulfillment of the omen.
Hàn'ān
second year,
first month, on the day *Jǐhài*,
Tàibái [Venus] was seen in daylight.
Fifth month, on the day *Dīnghài*,
Chénxīng [Mercury] clashed with Yúguǐ.
Sixth month, on the day *Yǐchǒu*,
Yínghuò's [Mars'] rays clashed with Zhènxīng [Saturn].
Seventh month, on the day *Jiǎshēn*,
Tàibái [Venus] was seen in daylight.
Chénxīng [Mercury] clashing with Yúguǐ portends a great mourning.
Yínghuò [Mars] clashing with Zhènxīng [Saturn] portends harm to a great person.
In the eighth month of the next year,
Emperor Xiàoshùn died.
Emperor Xiàochōng
died again in the first month of the next year.
Emperor Xiàozhì, first year of Běnchū,
third month, on the day *Guǐchǒu*,
Yínghuò [Mars] entered Yúguǐ.
Fourth month, on the day *Xīnsì*,
Tàibái [Venus] entered Yúguǐ.
Both portend a great mourning.
Fifth month, on the day *Gēngxū*,
Tàibái [Venus] clashed with Yínghuò [Mars],
portending a rebellious plot.
On the first day of the intercalary month,
Emperor Xiàozhì was poisoned by Liáng Jì
and died.
Astronomy, lower part: Huán 38, Líng 20, Xiàn 9. Meteorites.
First year of Jiànhé of Emperor Xiàohuán, eighth month, on the day *Rén'yín*,
Yínghuò [Mars] clashed with the Zhì star in Yúguǐ.
Second year, second month, on the day *Xīnmǎo*,
Yínghuò [Mars] was within Yúguǐ.
Third year, fifth month, on the day *Jǐchǒu*,
Tàibái [Venus] entered the Right Flank Gate of Tàiwēi,
stayed for fifteen days,
and exited the Duānmén gate.
On the day *Bǐngshēn*,
Yínghuò [Mars] entered Dōngjǐng.
Eighth month, on the day *Jǐhài*,
Zhènxīng [Saturn] clashed with the southern star within Yúguǐ.
On the day *Yǐchǒu*,
a comet with a tail five *chǐ* long
was seen in Tiānshì,
pointing southeast,
yellowish-white in color.
It disappeared on the day *Wùchén* in the ninth month.
Yínghuò [Mars] clashing with Yúguǐ portends death and mourning.
The Zhì star portends executed ministers.
Entering Tàiwēi portends rebellious ministers.
Zhènxīng [Saturn] clashing with Yúguǐ portends mourning.
A comet seen in Tiānshì portends a noble person.
By the first year of Hépíng, second month, on the day *Jiǎyín*,
Empress Dowager Liáng died.
Liáng Jì became even more arrogant and disruptive.
First year of Yuánjiā, second month, on the day *Wùzǐ*,
Tàibái [Venus] was seen in daylight.
Second year of Yǒngxīng, intercalary month, on the day *Dīngyǒu*,
Tàibái [Venus] was seen in daylight.
At this time, the Emperor favored the palace lady Dèng Měng.
The next year,
Měng's brother Yǎn was enfeoffed as Marquis of Nándùn.
Four years later,
Empress Liáng died,
Liáng Jì was executed,
and Měng was installed as Empress,
receiving immense favor and affection.
In the first year of Yǒngshòu, in the third month, on the day Bǐngshēn,
Zhènxīng retrograded into Tàiwēi,
and after seventy-four days, departed from the Zuǒyèmén.
In the seventh month, on the day Jǐwèi,
Chénxīng entered Tàiwēi,
and after eighty days, departed from the Zuǒyèmén.
In the eighth month, on the day Jǐsì,
Yínghuò entered Tàiwēi,
and after twenty-one days, exited the Duānmén.
Tàiwēi
is the Heavenly Son's court.
Zhènxīng represents esteemed officials and imperial consorts;
its retrograde motion signifies secret plots.
Chénxīng entering Tàiwēi forebodes great floods;
one interpretation is that the imperial harem will face worries.
In this year, the Luòshuǐ overflowed to the Jīnmén,
and there was a great flood in Nányáng.
Yínghuò remaining in Tàiwēi
also signifies rebellious officials.
At this time, the Liáng clan held sole power.
In the ninth month, on the day Jǐyǒu,
a meteor, about two feet long, was seen in daytime,
its color yellowish-white.
On the day Guǐsì,
Yínghuò trespassed against Suìxīng,
which signifies treacherous officials plotting,
and the execution of a great general.
In the second year, in the sixth month, on the day Jiǎyín,
Chénxīng entered Tàiwēi,
then became hidden and unseen.
Chénxīng signifies water,
military affairs,
and imperial consorts.
In the eighth month, on the day Wùwǔ,
Tàibái trespassed against the great star of Xuānyuán,
which represents the empress.
In its third year, in the fourth month, on the day Wùyín,
Yínghuò entered the mouth of Dōngjǐng,
which signifies ministers being executed.
In its seventh month, on the day Dīngchǒu,
Tàibái trespassed against the front star of Xīn,
which represents ministers.
Two years later, in the [seventh] month,
Empress Yìxiàn died of grief.
Grand General Liáng Jì ordered Tàicāng Ling Qín Gōng to assassinate the Imperial Counselor Bǐng Zūn,
and also wanted to kill Empress Dèng's mother, Xuān.
When the plot was discovered,
Emperor Huán seized Jì and his wife Shòu Xiāngchéng Jūn's official seals and ribbons,
and they both committed suicide.
The clans of Zhūliáng and Sūnshì were executed,
or exiled to the frontier.
This was their karmic retribution.
In the fourth year of Yánxī, in the third month, on the day Jiǎyín,
Yínghuò trespassed against the principal star of Yúguǐ.
In the fifth month, on the day Xīnyǒu,
a guest star appeared in Yíngshì,
gradually moving forward,
emitting a light about five feet long,
until it reached one degree from Xīn,
and transformed into a comet.
Yínghuò trespassing against the principal star of Yúguǐ
signifies ministers being executed.
In the tenth month of the fifth year,
the Administrator of Nánjùn, Lǐ Sù, was accused of allowing barbarians and bandits to attack and plunder commanderies and counties,
seizing over one hundred million in wealth,
and entering the prefecture to take the bronze tiger tallies.
Sù fled from the enemy,
and failed to save the cities;
also, the Yèzhě of Líyáng, Yàn Qiáo, was accused of corruption;
the Magistrate of Chóngquán, Péng Liáng, killed innocent people.
All were executed in the marketplace.
The Hǔyá Dūwèi of Jīngzhào, Sòng Qiān, was accused of corruption
and died in prison.
A guest star appearing in Yíngshì and transforming into a comet when it reached Xīn
signifies a great funeral.
Four years later,
Empress Dèng died of grief.
In the sixth year, in the eleventh month, on the day Dīnghài,
Tàibái was seen in daylight.
At this time, Empress Dèng's family was powerful and prosperous.
In the seventh year, in the seventh month, on the day Wùchén,
Chénxīng trespassed against Suìxīng.
In the eighth month, on the day Gēngxū,
Yínghuò trespassed against the principal star of Yúguǐ.
On the day Gēngshēn,
Suìxīng trespassed against the great star of Xuānyuán.
In the tenth month, on the day Bǐngchén,
Tàibái trespassed against the northern star of Fáng.
On the day Dīngmǎo,
Chénxīng trespassed against Tàibái.
In the twelfth month, on the day Yǐchǒu,
Yínghuò trespassed against the second star of Xuānyuán.
Chénxīng trespassing against Suìxīng signifies warfare.
Yínghuò trespassing against the principal star signifies executed officials.
Suìxīng trespassing against Xuānyuán signifies worries for the empress.
Tàibái trespassing against the northern star of Fáng signifies the imperial harem.
In its eighth year, in the second month,
the Grand Coachman, Nánxiāng Hóu Zuǒ Shèng, was granted death for his crimes;
Shèng's younger brothers, the Palace Attendants Cáo Shàngcài Hóu Tàipíng and Běixiāng Hóu Dǎng, both committed suicide.
On the day Guǐhài,
Empress Dèng was deposed for practicing heterodox doctrines,
and was moved to Tónggōng where she died.

Her relatives, including Palace Attendant Bìyáng Hóu Dèng Kāng, Hénán Yǐn Dèng Wàn, Yuèqí Xiàowèi Dèng Bì, Hǔbēn Zhōngláng Jiàng Ānyáng Hóu Dèng Huì, Palace Attendant Supervisor Yǔlín Zuǒqí Dèng Dé, Yǔlín Yòuqí Dèng Shòu, Kūnyáng Hóu Dèng Tǒng, Yùyáng Hóu Dèng Bǐng, and Imperial Counselor Dèng Xún, were all imprisoned in the Baòshì.
Wàn and Huì died;
Kāng and the others were dismissed from office.
Also, the Inspector of Jīngzhōu, Zhī, and the Inspector of Jiāozhǐ, Gé Zhǐ, were both captured by bandits;
the Administrator of Guìyáng, Rèn Yìn, fled from the enemy.
All were executed in the marketplace.
This was the retribution for Yínghuò trespassing against the principal star of Yúguǐ.
In the eighth year, in the fifth month, on the day Guǐyǒu,
Tàibái trespassed against the principal star of Yúguǐ.
On the day Rénwǔ,
Yínghuò entered Tàiwēi's Right Law Enforcer.
In the intercalary month, on the day Jǐwèi,
Tàibái trespassed against the front star of Xīn.
In the tenth month, on the day Guǐyǒu,
Suìxīng trespassed against the Left Law Enforcer.
In the eleventh month, on the day Wùwǔ,
Suìxīng entered Tàiwēi,
and trespassed against the Left Law Enforcer.
In the ninth year, in the first month, on the day Rénchén,
Suìxīng entered Tàiwēi,
and after fifty-eight days, exited the Duānmén.
In the sixth month, on the day Rénxū,
Tàibái moved into Yúguǐ.
In the seventh month, on the day Yǐwèi,
Yínghuò moved through Yúguǐ,
and trespassed against the principal star.
In the ninth month, on the day Xīnhài,
Yínghuò entered Tàiwēi's west gate,
and remained for fifty-eight days.
In the first year of Yǒngkāng, in the first month, on the day Gēngyín,
Yínghuò retrograded into Tàiwēi's east gate,
remained in Tàiwēi,
and after one hundred and one days, exited the Duānmén.
In the seventh month, on the day Bǐngxū,
Tàibái was seen in daylight traversing the sky.
Tàibái trespassing against the front star of Xīn,
and Tàibái trespassing against the principal star of Yúguǐ signify executed officials.
Yínghuò entering Tàiwēi signifies treacherous officials.
Tàibái trespassing against the front star of Xīn signifies military conflict and funerals.
Suìxīng entering Tàiwēi and trespassing against the Left Law Enforcer
signifies generals and prime ministers being executed.
Suìxīng remaining in Tàiwēi for fifty days
presages the ruler.
Tàibái and Yínghuò entering Yúguǐ
both signify death and mourning,
and trespassing against the principal star signifies executed officials.
Yínghuò remaining in Tàiwēi for one hundred and one days
presages the ruler.
Tàibái seen in daylight traversing the sky signifies warfare,
and worries for important figures.
In its ninth year, in the eleventh month,
the Administrator of Tàiyuán, Liú Kā, and the Administrator of Nányáng, Chéng Gē, were both accused of killing innocent people;
the Inspector of Jīngzhōu, Lǐ Kuí, was captured by bandits;
the Shangshū Láng, Mèng Dāng, was accused of accepting bribes and leaking information.
All were executed in the marketplace.
In the first year of Yǒngkāng, in the twelfth month, on the day Dīngchǒu,
Emperor Huán collapsed.
Grand Tutor Chén Fān, Grand General Dòu Wǔ, Shàngshū Lìng Yǐn Xūn, Huángmén Lìng Shān Bīng, and others all died unjustly.
This was the retribution for Tàibái trespassing against Xīn
and Yínghuò remaining in Tàiwēi.
In the sixth month of the first year of Jiànníng, during the reign of Emperor Xiàolíng,
Tàibái was in the west,
entered Tàiwēi,
and trespassed against the southern head star of the western outer wall.
Tàiwēi
is the Heavenly Court.
Tàibái moving through it
means the palace gates will be closed,
great generals will don armor,
and ministers will be executed.
In its eighth month,
Grand Tutor Chén Fān and Grand General Dòu Wǔ conspired to eliminate all eunuchs;
in its ninth month, on the day Xīnhài,
the Palace Attendants Cáo Jié and Chánglè Wǔguān Shǐ Zhū Yǔ discovered the plot,
fabricated an imperial edict to kill Fān and Wǔ,
and their families were exiled to Bǐjǐng in Rìnán.
In the tenth month of the first year of Xīpíng,
Yínghuò entered the Nándǒu.
The divination says:
"Where Yínghuò remains, there will be military conflict."
Dǒu represents Wú.
In its eleventh month,
the bandit Xǔ Zhāo of Kuàijī gathered a crowd and proclaimed himself Grand General;
Zhāo's father, Shēng, was made King of Yuè,
and attacked and broke through commanderies and counties.
In the second year, fourth month,
a star emerged from Wénchāng,
entered the Zǐgōng,
moved like a snake,
with a head and tail but no body,
red in color,
and shone with light upon the city walls.
In the eighth month, on the day of Bǐngyín,
Tàibái transgressed the star in front of Xīn.
On Xīnwèi,
a white vapor, like a bolt of white silk,
collided with the fourth star of the Běidǒu.
The prognostication stated:
"Wénchāng is for a high-ranking general and a noble minister.
Tàibái transgressing the star in front of Xīn
is for a high minister."
Six years later,
Sītú Liú Hé was slandered by Zhōngchángshì Cáo Jié,
imprisoned, and died.
White vapor colliding with the Běidǒu signifies a major battle.
In the winter of the following year,
Yángzhōu Cìshǐ Zāng Mín and Dānyáng Tàishǒu Chén Yín
attacked the bandit Jū Kāng,
beheading several thousand.
On the day of Guǐchǒu in the fourth month of Guānghé first year,
a meteor transgressed the second star of Xuānyuán,
traveling northeast and entering the kuí of the Běidǒu.
In the eighth month,
a comet emerged north of Kàng,
entered the Tiānshì,
was several feet long,
gradually grew to five or six zhàng,
was red in color,
passed through more than ten constellations,
for over eighty days,
and then vanished in the Tiānwǎn.
A meteor is for a noble envoy,
Xuānyuán is for the inner palace,
and the kuí of the Běidǒu presides over killing.
A meteor moving from Xuānyuán to the kuí of the Běidǒu
means that the Son of Heaven's great envoy will go out,
and there will be a punitive killing.
By Zhōngpíng first year,
the Huángjīn bandits arose,
and the emperor dispatched Zhōnglángjiāng Huángfǔ Sōng, Zhū Jùn, and others to suppress them,
beheading over one hundred thousand.
A comet clearing the Tiānshì means
the Celestial Emperor will relocate,
the Emperor will change his capital.
By Chūpíng first year,
Xiàndì moved the capital to Cháng'ān.
In the winter of the third year,
a comet emerged from Láng and Hú,
traveled east to Zhāng and then departed.
Zhāng is the land of Zhōu,
a comet transgressing it signifies military chaos.
Four years later,
the capital mobilized a large army to attack the Huángjīn bandits.
In the fourth month of the fifth year,
Yínghuò was in Tàiwēi,
guarding Píng.
In the seventh month,
a comet emerged below Sāntái,
traveled east into Tàiwēi,
reaching Tàizǐ and Xìngchén,
and vanished after more than twenty days.
In the tenth month,
Suìxīng, Yínghuò, and Tàibái converged at Xū,
each five or six inches apart.
Like a string of pearls.
The prognostication stated:
"Yínghuò in Tàiwēi is for rebellious ministers."
At this time, Zhōngchángshì Zhào Zhōng, Zhāng Ràng, Guō Shèng, Sūn Zhāng, and others
all committed treasonous acts.
A comet entering Tàiwēi means
the world will change its ruler.
By Zhōngpíng sixth year,
the imperial carriage made its final journey.
Suìxīng, Yínghuò, and Tàibái converging at Xū is for a great funeral.
Xū is
the land of Qí.
The following year,
Lángyé Wáng Jù passed away.
During Guānghé,
the Guóhuáng star, in its southeast corner, was one or two zhàng from the ground,
resembling a torch,
and disappeared after more than ten days.
The prognostication stated:
"The Guóhuáng star is for internal chaos,
with military misfortunes both internal and external."
Afterward, the Huángjīn bandit Zhāng Jiǎo burned down commanderies and states,
and the imperial court dispatched generals to pacify them,
beheading over one hundred thousand.
In Zhōngpíng sixth year,
the imperial carriage made its final journey,
Dàjiāngjūn Hé Jìn ordered Sīlì Xiàowèi Yuán Shào to secretly recruit over a thousand soldiers,
covertly stationed outside Luòyáng city,
and secretly summoned Bìngzhōu Mù Dǒng Zhuó to bring troops to the capital,
together to execute the eunuchs.
They battled below the southern and northern palace gates,
several thousand died,
the palaces were burned,
and the capital was moved to Xījīng.
When Sītú Wáng Yǔn and Jiāngjūn Lǚ Bù executed Dǒng Zhuó,
Dǒng Zhuó's generals Guō Sì and Lǐ Quē turned their troops to attack Cháng'ān,
nearly ten thousand high officials, civil servants, and common people died in battle.
The chaos in the world
all originated internally.
In the tenth month, on the day of Guǐhài, of Zhōngpíng second year,
a guest star appeared in Nánmén,
as large as half a mat,
with five colors of joy and anger, gradually shrinking,
and vanished by the sixth month of the following year.
The prognostication stated:
"This is for warfare."
By the sixth year,
Sīlì Xiàowèi Yuán Shào annihilated the eunuchs,
and Dàjiāngjūn's general Wú Kuāng attacked and killed Chēqí Jiāngjūn Hé Miáo,
several thousand died.
In the fourth month of the third year,
Yínghuò moved retrogradely to guard the star behind Xīn.
In the tenth month, on the day of Wùwǔ,
the moon eclipsed the star behind Xīn.
The prognostication stated:
"This is for a great funeral."
Three years later, Emperor Líng collapsed.
In the second month of the fifth year,
a comet emerged from Kuí,
moved retrogradely into Zǐgōng,
reappeared three times,
and vanished after more than sixty days.
In the sixth month, on the day of Dīngmǎo,
a guest star, like a three-shēng bowl,
appeared from Guànsuǒ,
traveled southwest into Tiānshì,
and vanished at Wěi.
The prognostication stated:
"A comet clearing Zǐgōng means
the world will change its ruler.
A guest star entering Tiānshì
is for the death of a noble person."
In the fourth month of the following year,
the imperial carriage made its final journey.
In the summer of Zhōngpíng,
a meteor, red like fire,
three zhàng long,
rose from Hégǔ,
entered Tiānshì,
collided with the Huànzhě star,
was white in color,
two or three zhàng long,
its tail bent twice,
and extinguished after a meal's time,
resembling a crooked arrow.
The prognostication stated:
"A crooked arrow flying out,
shooting at its palace,
means that the arrow should be straight but is crooked,
the person holding the arrow is deviant and crooked."
In Zhōngpíng sixth year,
Dàjiāngjūn Hé Jìn plotted to exterminate all eunuchs,
but the eunuchs found out,
and killed Hé Jìn in the provincial office: both sides were destroyed,
and the world consequently fell into great chaos.
In the eighth month, on the day of Bǐngyín, of the sixth year,
Tàibái transgressed the star in front of Xīn,
and on Wùchén, transgressed the great star in the center of Xīn.
On that day, four *kè* before dusk,
Dàjiāngjūn Hé Jìn was killed in the provincial office by the various huángmén.
On Jǐsì,
Chēqí Jiāngjūn Hé Miáo was killed by Hé Jìn's general Wú Kuāng.
In the ninth month of Xiàoxiàn's Chūpíng second year,
the Chīyóu Qí appeared,
over ten zhàng long,
white in color,
emerging south of Jué and Kàng.
The prognostication stated:
"When the Chīyóu Qí appears,
the king will campaign and conquer the four directions."
Afterward, Chéngxiàng Cáo Gōng campaigned and conquered the world for nearly thirty years.
In the tenth month of the fourth year,
a bò star appeared between Liǎngjué,
traveled northeast into Tiānshì and then extinguished.
The prognostication stated:
"A comet clearing Tiānshì means
the Celestial Emperor will relocate,
the Emperor will change his capital."
At this time, the Emperor was in Cháng'ān,
two years later he moved east,
in the seventh month of the following year,
he arrived at Luòyáng,
and in the eighth month,
Cáo Gōng welcomed the Emperor to Xu.
In the fifth year of Jiàn'ān, in the tenth month, on the day Xīnhài,
a comet appeared in Dàliáng,
the division of Jìzhōu.
At that time, Yuán Shào was in Jìzhōu.
In the eleventh month of that year,
Shào's army was defeated by Cáo Gōng.
In the summer of the seventh year,
Shào died,
and later Cáo Gōng then took Jìzhōu.
In the eleventh month of the ninth year,
a comet appeared in Dōngjǐng and Yúguǐ,
entering Xuānyuán and Tàiwēi.
In the first month of the eleventh year,
a comet appeared in Běidǒu,
its head in Dǒu,
its tail piercing through Zǐgōng
and Běichén.
The prognostication said:
"If a comet sweeps through Tàiwēi Palace,
the lord of men will change position."
Thereafter, Wèi Wéndì received the abdication.
In the tenth month of the twelfth year, on the day Xīnmǎo,
a comet appeared in Qúnwěi.
This was the division of Jīngzhōu.
At that time, Liú Biǎo, the Governor of Jīngzhōu, occupied Jīngzhōu.
Zhōu Qún, an assistant in Yìzhōu, believed that the Governor of Jīngzhōu was about to die and lose territory.
In the autumn of the following year,
Biǎo died,
and his younger son Cóng succeeded him.
When Cáo Gōng was about to attack Jīngzhōu,
Cóng was afraid
and led his army to surrender to Gōng.
In the twelfth month of the seventeenth year,
a comet appeared in Wǔzhūhóu.
Zhōu Qún believed that all those who exclusively held territory in the west
would lose their land.
At this time, Liú Zhāng, the Governor of Yìzhōu, occupied Yìzhōu;
Zhāng Lǔ, the Administrator of Hànzhōng, separately occupied Hànzhōng;
Hán Suì occupied Liángzhōu;
Zōng Jiàn separately occupied Páohǎn.
In the winter of the following year,
Cáo Gōng dispatched a partial general to attack Liángzhōu.
In the nineteenth year,
Zōng Jiàn was captured;
Hán Suì fled to the Qiāng regions
and died of illness.
In the autumn of that year,
Zhāng lost Yìzhōu.
In the autumn of the twentieth year,
Gōng attacked Hànzhōng,
and Lǔ surrendered.
In the autumn of the eighteenth year,
Suìxīng, Zhènxīng, and Yínghuò all entered Tàiwēi,
moving retrograde and staying guarding the Imperial Seat for over a hundred days.
The prognostication said:
"If Suìxīng enters Tàiwēi,
the lord of men will change."
In the third month of the twenty-third year,
a comet was seen in the morning in the east for over twenty days,
and appeared in the evening in the west,
transgressing Wǔchē, Dōngjǐng, Wǔzhūhóu, Wénchāng, Xuānyuán, Hòufēi, and Tàiwēi.
Its fiery tip pointed at the Imperial Seat.
The prognostication said:
"This is the omen of removing the old and establishing the new."
In the ninth month of Yánpíng first year of Shāngdì, on the day Yǐhài,
four meteorites fell in Chénliú.
In the sixteenth year of Xīgōng of the Chūnqiū period,
five meteorites fell in Sòng.
Tradition says these were falling stars.
Dǒng Zhòngshū believed it to be an omen of going from high to low.
Some believed that commoners are represented by stars,
and falling
is an omen of the people's distress.
In the seventh year of Yánxī of Emperor Huán, in the third month, on the day Guǐhài,
a meteorite fell in Yòufúfēng;
and two more meteorites fell in Hù,
all with sounds like thunder.
Collation Note, page 3255, line 7: "A comet was seen in Tiānshì, signaling a (質) [貴] person." This is revised according to Lú Jiào.
Page 3255, line 7: "Until the first year of Hépíng, in the second month, on the day Jiǎyín, Empress Dowager Liáng passed away." The collected explanations cite Qián Dàxīn's commentary,
stating that Emperor Huán's Chronicle places it in the second month,
and that the character
is superfluous here.
It is now deleted accordingly.
Page 3256, line 4: "In the second year, in the sixth month, on the day Jiǎyín." Note: The first day (朔) of the sixth month in the second year of Yǒngshòu was Dīngsì.
There was no Jiǎyín,
so the text of the Treatise has an error.
Page 3256, line 6: "Two years later, in the [七]th month, Empress Yìxiàn died of grief." The collected explanations cite Hóng Liàngjí's commentary,
stating that
"四月" (fourth month)
should be
"七月" (seventh month),
and that the Treatise has an error.
It is now revised accordingly.
Page 3256, line 9: "In the fourth year of Yánxī, in the third month, on the day Jiǎyín." Note: The first day (朔) of the third month in the fourth year of Yánxī was Jǐwèi.
There was no Jiǎyín,
so the text of the Treatise has an error.
Page 3256, line 12: "Sòng Qiān, the Huǒyá Commandant of Jīngzhào." Note: The collected explanations cite Qián Dàxīn's commentary,
stating that in Emperor Huán's Chronicle,
"Sòng Qiān"
is written as
"Zōng Qiān".
Page 3256, line 15: "In the seventh year, in the seventh month, on the day Wùchén." Note: The first day (朔) of the seventh month in the seventh year of Yánxī was Gēngwǔ.
There was no Wùchén,
so the text of the Treatise has an error.
Page 3257, line 3: "Zuǒ Shèng, Grand Coachman and Marquis of Nánxiāng." Note: The collected explanations cite Qián Dàxīn's commentary,
stating that
"Zuǒ Shèng"
is written as
"Zuǒ Chēng"
in both Emperor Huán's Chronicle and the Biography of the Eunuchs.
The Biography of Zhào Qí writes
"Zuǒ Shèng",
which is consistent with this text.
Page 3257, line 3: "Empress Dèng, for practicing heterodox arts, was deposed and moved to (祠) [桐] Palace, where she died." The collected explanations cite Chén Jǐngyún's commentary,
stating that
should be
The matter of Empress Yīn of Emperor Hé being deposed and moved to Tóng Palace is recorded in the Chronicle of Empresses, and can be mutually corroborated.
It is now revised accordingly.
